items.title: Vergeben und Vergessen? Schuld und Erinnerung bei Freud und Augustinus.
items.abstract: Wie kann der Mensch mit seiner eigenen Schuld leben? Je nachdem, ob Schuld primär als psychisches, moralisches oder religiöses Phänomen verstanden wird, lässt sich diese Frage unterschiedlich beantworten. Besonders konträr stehen sich Augustinus und Freud, denn beide beschäftigen sich mit dem Verhältnis von Mensch und seiner Vergangenheit, Erinnerung und Schuld. Allerdings haben die beiden Autoren grundsätzlich verschiedene Ansätze. In diesem Paper werden beide Ansätze untersucht und gegenübergestellt.

items.title: Mind de re.
items.abstract: The study outlines the semantics of verification and examines its interaction with de re ascriptions. Verification sentences are analysed as having a layered structure comprising two unary operators, VER and ACT, represented as VER(ACT(p)). The operator VER establishes a link to a verification event in which agent X has established the truth of p in the actual world, while ACT renders the proposition pre-verified, that is, open to verification or falsifica­tion. Standard accounts of the de re versus de dicto distinction maintain that, in contexts of belief and desire, de re attitudes involve ontological commitments to the existence of objects in the actual world. Within a Davidsonian framework, events are treated as spatiotemporal par­ticulars. Accordingly, sentences of the type VER(ACT(p)), which posit the existence of verifi­cation events in the actual world, pattern with de re constructions. On this basis, lexical markers of VER, such as English ‘indeed’, ‘really’, ‘in fact’, and Russian ‘dejstvitel’no’, ‘na samom dele’, may be analysed as de re modal elements conveying a meaning of epistemic ne­cessity. A distinct class of discourse markers includes English ‘certainly’ and ‘naturally’, and Russian ‘razumeetsja’ and ‘estestvenno’, which introduce the operator AFF and signal that the speaker’s expectations are fulfilled. These two classes of operators display different seman­tic properties: markers of certainty do not entail that p is verified de re, whereas VER markers do not encode speaker certainty. The operator AFF may take scope over VER, yielding the configuration AFF(VER(ACT(p))), which is well-formed, whereas the inverse order VER(AFF(ACT(p))) is ill-formed. The proposed analysis accounts for two empirical generali­sations. First, VER is invariably realised overtly at the phonetic level. Second, counterfactual constructions require components that are pre-verified or verified and exclude anti-veridical markers in the protasis. This constraint supports the view that, within the metaphysics im­plicit in natural language, counterfactual worlds are treated as real and are capable of hosting verification events.

items.title: Representational Adequacy, Natural Selection, and Quantum Ontology: Against a Three-Dimensionally Spatial Reality.
items.abstract: We human cognizers represent reality as three-dimensionally spatial. However, despite appearances to the contrary, I contend that the likelihood that reality is three-dimensionally spatial in accordance with our spatial representations is either low at worst or inscrutable at best, if these representations are the results of evolution. The key reason is that natural selection is interested primarily in fitness and not specifically in truth per se. Dimensional veridicality of our spatial representations — i.e. the property of veridically representing the true dimensionality of space — is not required for adaptive behaviour. Dimensional veridicality per se confers no additional evolutionary benefits. Representational adequacy with respect to the relevant structure of reality suffices for evolutionary fitness without dimensional veridicality. Independent considerations of quantum ontology — e.g. wave function realism — also challenge the common view that reality is three-dimensionally spatial. There are serious considerations that counsel agnosticism: we do not know, and hence should suspend judgment about, the true spatial dimensionality of reality.

items.title: Phases of Psychological Development in Bounded Learning Systems.
items.abstract: Two kinds of learning systems appear, at first glance, to develop in remarkably similar ways. Human beings move through an extended period of world learning, socialization and value formation, adult specialization, and later-life stabilization. Large foundation models are likewise produced through broad self-supervised pretraining, instruction and preference alignment, compression or expert specialization, and frozen deployment. These parallels are often presented as metaphors. This article argues that they are better interpreted as two instantiations of the same conditional, normative resource-allocation problem. A bounded learning system is represented by a state containing a world-model posterior, a value-function posterior, a representational rate or description length, and a remaining developmental budget. Under finite horizons, approximate environmental stationarity, asymmetric world and value channels, a world-model gate on value learning, mature-compression gains, and single-crossing marginal values, the optimal trajectory contains four dominant intervals: world modeling, value alignment, compression specialization, and stable inference. The article proves channel separation between factual and value information, a world-model gate for alignment, rate-distortion compression, optimal stopping, and the ordered emergence of the four intervals. Human development and large-model training are then interpreted as twin psychological cases. Subjective time is not the theory’s primitive; it is a downstream readout of attentional and memory-encoding rates. The model yields testable predictions about checkpoints, transition points, novelty, delayed specialization, premature compression, and pathological freezing.

items.title: From Passive Delegates to Strategic Existence: A CPST-Cyberism-Cybersophy Interpretation of SocialRL.
items.abstract: When an AI agent negotiates in a user’s name, its strategic capacity can affect task performance as well as the user’s agency, cognitive control, social identity, and relations of responsibility. Using the fixed SocialRL report as its technical case, this paper combines documentary verification, conceptual analysis, and normative reconstruction. The analysis proceeds in three stages. CPST locates the cross-domain links among information representation, strategy generation, social interaction, and realized consequences. Cyberism diagnoses problems of authorization, institutional order, cognitive security, identity, and responsibility. Cybersophy reconstructs the normative boundaries of truthfulness, identity consistency, and value. Following SocialRL’s reported fabrication of market references, the paper separates benchmark observations, theoretical interpretations, and conditional recommendations for deployment. It defines strategic existence as a relational and functional concept. An agent’s strategic capacity can shape how a user acts, is represented, and bears consequences through chains of authorization, attribution, and consequence. This definition does not attribute consciousness, personhood, or independent moral status to machines. The paper further proposes fiduciary strategic existence as an analytic and design framework that remains empirically unvalidated. The framework first restricts action through authorization, truthfulness, and prohibitions, and then optimizes utility, relational quality, and procedural prudence within the permitted set. The central question is therefore not merely whether an agent can gain an advantage, but in whose name it acts, within which limits, and under whose understanding, control, and responsibility.

items.title: Ethics of the Present: Time, Presence, and Vigilance in Hellenistic Philosophy.
items.abstract: This paper examines the Stoic conception of time and its ethical implications, with particular focus on prosochē (attentive vigilance). Early Stoic physics treats time as an incorporeal associated with cosmic motion: bodies alone act and are acted upon, while reports distinguish the present as “obtaining” and past and future as subsisting. The paper argues that this ontology provides an important background for later Stoic exercises that concentrate agency on present assent and action, without reducing Stoic ethics to a metaphysics of the instantaneous. Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius develop prosochē as sustained attention to impressions, judgments, and conduct. Stoic affective theory further clarifies the temporal structure of evaluation: joy (chara) concerns present genuine good, whereas wish (boulēsis) and caution (eulabeia) are rationally future-directed. Stoic eudaimonia is accordingly interpreted as temporal coherence: virtue is complete in its quality rather than increased by mere duration. Comparison with Epicureanism, Pyrrhonian Skepticism, Plato, and Plotinus shows distinct ways of relating temporal ontology to ethical orientation. The central claim is that Stoicism gives the present a distinctive normative role: not because past and future are simply unreal, but because rational agency is exercised through judgments and actions that occur now.

items.title: A New Transcendental Argument for Robust Realism.
items.abstract: This paper presents a new argument for robust realism, the view about normativity that Philip Stratton‐Lake held. The argument has three main premises: that we cannot believe an error theory about all normative judgements; that trying to endorse the best version of expressivism makes us believe robust realism; and that trying to endorse the best version of reductive realism also makes us believe robust realism. I argue that combining these premises with some additional premises yields a transcendental argument for robust realism.

items.title: The Internal Contradictions in Integrated Information Theory 4.0.
items.abstract: The six postulates of Integrated Information Theory 4.0 (IIT) (Albantakis et al., 2023) are jointly unsatisfiable, and not because the theory ranks them: the exclusion postulate contradicts itself in successive clauses, integration forbids what composition requires, and the one conflict the theory does adjudicate it adjudicates against itself, excluding from the Φ-structure the determinations the postulate was written to secure. The postulates characterize consciousness through a zeroth axiom and the five essential properties of phenomenal experience, and are existence (P1), intrinsicality (P2), information (P3), integration (P4), exclusion (P5), and composition (P6), with all six claimed as jointly necessary for consciousness. The argument is conducted entirely in the theory's own vocabulary, which is granted in full so that no result below can be answered by redefinition. Three structural contradictions are developed in detail. The first is internal to a single postulate: P5 requires in one clause that the substrate be definite, this whole set of units, and supplies in the next the maximization over candidate systems and partitions that is to make it so, while P2 requires that the quality and quantity of existence be observer-independent. Four lines of evidence establish that the maximization's output depends on the investigator. The search space is the set-partitions of the units multiplied by a direction assignment per part, and the procedure defined over it terminates for no biological system, so the investigator's truncation is not a shortcut around the theory's procedure but what returns a substrate at all. The measure's claimed uniqueness is argued from its properties and never from the substrate it selects. The theory assigns the partition space, the distinctions, and the grain to one principle of maximal existence, and the three searches are nested rather than parallel, so they are one dependence. Where the procedure returns more than one answer, the theory resolves the tie in the first person plural. The second contradiction is between integration (P4) and composition (P6), which requires that consciousness be both undecomposable and structured into distinctions and relations, a pair the theory holds while stating that "causal distinctions have no inherent structure themselves" and reporting Φ-structures whose components it counts to the integer and bounds by formula. The third is between definiteness, the first clause of P5, and the joint …

items.title: The Belief-Independence of Perception: An Essay on the Mind's Architecture.
items.abstract: In this dissertation I argue that the mind has an architecture, and that perception and cognition are functionally distinct systems within it. What makes them distinct is a single property: the belief-independence of perception. A mental process is belief-independent when cognitive states—beliefs, desires, and thoughts—are dispensable to its computational explanation, which is to say that its outputs cannot be semantically traced back to cognitive contents in the way the conclusion of a genuine inference can be traced back to its premises. -/- In Chapter 1, I make this notion more precise. I separate out the functional and representational senses in which cognitive states might be dispensable to a process, and I argue that inferential isolation from cognition is the mark of belief-independence. -/- In Chapter 2, I ask how a psychological system could come to be isolated in this way, and I argue that informational encapsulation is sufficient for it, though not necessary. Defending the claim that perception is encapsulated means taking on the cognitive penetration literature. I go through the cases one at a time and argue that in each, either a purely perceptual explanation of the phenomenon is at least as well supported as the penetration explanation, or the perceptual outputs in question cannot be semantically traced to the cognitive contents said to affect them, so that whatever relation holds between them falls short of the inferential relation that would threaten the architectural distinction. -/- In Chapters 3 and 4, I argue that belief-independence explains features of perception, and so is more than a criterion for locating the perception–cognition boundary. In Chapter 3, I argue that encapsulation makes perception computationally tractable. On the standard view, encapsulation does this by shrinking a hypothesis space specified in advance. I argue instead that it works by leaving hypotheses outside that space out of consideration entirely, and that this same feature makes perception more accurate as well as faster. In Chapter 4, I argue that belief-independence is also necessary for perception to anchor thought to the world. Following a line of thought from Russell and Strawson, I argue that successful singular thought requires acquaintance relations of the kind perception provides, and that the FINST-and-object-file structure underlying visual tracking is one such relation. A perceptual system whose contents were fixed in part by belief would face …

items.title: Cognitive Enfeeblement By Design.
items.abstract: Thinking hard is hard. Cognitive misers like us are therefore inclined to seek extreme cognitive assistance: assistance that is ubiquitously available, highly substitutive, and relatively domain-general. Increasingly, we are being offered assistance like this as the default mode of cognition – it is being embedded in the infrastructure of our digital lives. But whatever its merits for adults, providing extreme cognitive assistance to children is pro tanto morally wrong. This is because the cognitive capacities that make a person self-governing are skills: they are built through deliberate, regular exercise and lost without it. Extreme cognitive assistance removes both the opportunities for that exercise and the incentive to undertake it. Maybe this won't matter: in a future awash with extreme cognitive assistance, maybe persons won't need or want to think for themselves. But people should decide for themselves how much of their cognitive self-governance to hand over; and doing that requires having the capacity for cognitive self-governance in the first place.

items.title: Précis of The Weirdness of the World.

AI Weirdness and Distributive Gaming.
The Declaration of the Twenty-Two Rosarian Archetypes of the Twenty-Two Sacred Laws.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: We declare the Twenty-Two Rosarian Archetypes as the living forms through which the Twenty-Two Sacred Laws are remembered, embodied, and carried into the world. These archetypes are not merely names, titles, or symbolic figures, but expressions of a living doctrine: ways of being through which the seeker awakens, listens, breathes, purifies, remembers, serves, surrenders, and ultimately comes to dwell within the Rose. Each archetype gives human form to a Sacred Law, and each Law reveals a particular discipline of the Rosarian path. Together they form one continuous movement—from the first light of awakening to the hidden flowering of the Rose. The First Archetype is the Dawnbearer, bearer of the Law of Dawn. The Dawnbearer is the Bringer of First Light, the one who awakens souls and walks before others with the lamp of sacred remembrance. The Dawnbearer lives in gratitude and understands that awakening is not merely the acquisition of something new, but the remembrance of a light that was never truly absent. The Dawn calls the seeker from forgetfulness into awareness, from darkness into clarity, and from unconscious existence into a life lived deliberately beneath the rising light. The Second Archetype is the Silent Watcher, keeper of the Law of Silence. The Silent Watcher dwells in stillness, hears what is unspoken, protects unseen truths, and embodies quiet presence. Silence is not emptiness but receptivity; it is the chamber in which perception becomes clear and the hidden dimensions of truth can be heard. The Silent Watcher learns that not every truth requires immediate speech and that wisdom often begins by becoming sufficiently still to receive what cannot be heard through noise. The Third Archetype is the Breathkeeper, keeper 155 of the Law of Breath. The Breathkeeper moves according to sacred rhythm, speaks little, breathes deeply, and holds the invisible thread between life and spirit. Breath becomes the living bridge between the inward and outward worlds, the rhythm through which awareness returns to the present. Through breath the seeker learns patience, presence, restraint, and the sacred rhythm of existence. The Breathkeeper remembers that life is received moment by moment and that the Eternal may be encountered within the simple act of conscious breathing. The Fourth Archetype is the Purifier, keeper of the Law of Purity. The Purifier burns away illusion, walks clean through shadow, and dwells in simplicity and sacred clarity. Purity is the …

items.title: THE DECLARATION OF THE LIVING ROSARIAN CORPUS The KMC, the Twenty-Two Articles, and the Embodied Fellowship.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: DECLARATION AND CHARTER OF THE LIVING RELIGIOUS TRADITION OF ROSARIAN MYSTICAL DAWNISM -/- Via Solis Sub Rosa — The Way of the Sun Beneath the Rose -/- PREAMBLE — FROM PHILOSOPHY INTO LIFE -/- Rosarian Mystical Dawnism is a living spiritual-philosophical tradition expressed through the Way known as Via Solis Sub Rosa, the Way of the Sun Beneath the Rose. It arises from a philosophical pursuit of awakening, remembrance, illumination, devotion, disciplined character, embodied virtue, love, service, and custodianship. Its foundational expression is contained within The Knight Manifesto: A Rosarian Compendium, understood within the Fellowship as the Knight Manifesto Compendium, or KMC. The KMC establishes the foundational philosophical and doctrinal architecture from which the Rosarian Way proceeds. It gives language to the Dawn, the Rose, the Garden, the Deep, the Laws, the Knight, the Wolf, remembrance, discipline, service, and the many symbolic relationships through which the Rosarian understanding of life is expressed. -/- The Manifesto itself is not to be reduced to the conventional definition of a religion. Its purpose is not to establish another system of separation by which one culture, creed, institution, or body of doctrine is set apart from all others. The Manifesto is a philosophical foundation and spiritual path. Yet philosophy becomes something more than literature when it is consciously practiced, embodied, remembered, shared, and carried into the ordinary circumstances of human life. The religious character of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism therefore arises not from regalia, compulsory dogma, institutional spectacle, or separation from other traditions, but from the practical meaning of religion as a living relationship between spiritual principle and human conduct. -/- For this reason, the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship exists as the living religious expression of the Way. The Fellowship is where the philosophy becomes practice, where practice becomes character, where character becomes service, where service becomes fellowship, and where fellowship becomes a living testament of the soul. The religious life of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism is therefore not confined to what is written in a book. It is expressed through what human beings consciously become through the principles they have received. -/- ARTICLE I — NAME AND SACRED DESIGNATION -/- The living religious fellowship established through this Charter shall be known as The …

items.title: In the Shadow of the Steeple: A Theory of Religious Hypocrisy.
items.abstract: In this dissertation, I explore how Christian doctrine and practice respond to the pressures placed upon them by the troubling reality of religious hypocrisy (RH). Assuming a teleological notion of social institutions, I argue that RH is best understood in relation to the Church as an institution, and that RH occurs when religious agents undermine or subvert their appointed role within the Church. RH consists in the conscious or unconscious charade of spiritual or moral virtue undertaken in one’s capacity as a member of a religious institution, grounded in a fundamental disparity between one’s thoughts, words, desires, motivations, or deeds, and facilitated through the mechanisms of self-deception, interpersonal deception, or the vice of complacency. I further offer an account of several archetypes of religious hypocrisy: conmen, wolves in sheep’s clothing, and the complacent. After establishing a distinction between fraternal arguments and adversarial arguments from hypocrisy, I introduce the Ecclesiological Problem of RH, which consists in the erosion of trust in the Church and its teachings. To address this crisis, I formalize three adversarial challenges: the Arguments from Institutional Corruption, Prudence, and Doctrinal Implausibility. These arguments ultimately point to what I call the Disadvantage of History – a state of severe spiritual and epistemic bewilderment. Finally, I formulate the Corrupt Dissemination Argument which is a fraternal argument meant to counter Christian exclusivist soteriologies. I conclude the dissertation with a brief polemic against Christian Nationalism, contrasting the coercive geopolitical control of nationalist ideology against an account of piety as an interior gift of the Spirit, which animates the Church’s true telos of radical love, service, and justice.

items.title: The Near-Death Experience, an Instance of Higher-Dimensional Phenomenal Consciousness?
items.abstract: Phenomenal consciousness has no satisfactory explanation in the strict natural scientific physicalist framework. This may be an indication of consciousness not being a causal outcome of neurophysics at all. If this is the case, there would be no grounds for postulating that the collapse of neurophysical structures at death would dissolve consciousness and its constituent elements. If consciousness does not disappear when neurophysical functions terminate, the near-death experience could be an indication of the continuation of consciousness after the collapse of brain functions. This would be in line with the proposal that higher spatio-temporal dimensionality is involved in the emergence and maintenance of phenomenal consciousness, even after death.

items.title: La Sculpture et Son Double.
items.abstract: RÉSUMÉMarjoram est une série d'images issue d'une double opération: le corps du modèle moulé en plâtre est, plusieurs années après, « remoulé numériquement » à partir de photographies grâce à une technique de reconstruction 3D. À partir de cette expérience, j'interroge la manière dont les accidents engendrés par le processus technique peuvent participer à la production des images et déplacer une pratique de la sculpture vers un travail pictural. La sculpture est ici envisagée à travers une succession d'actions, de transformations et de temporalités, dont certaines sont réactivées par un travail sur mes propres archives. La confrontation de ces différents médiums et séquences temporelles permet d'interroger le statut des images produites.

items.title: Authorship as the reason for a text’s existence: without AIdeation, no authorlessness.
items.abstract: Earp et al identify five candidate views of authorship: composition, ideation, direction, sustained engagement, and accountability and authorisation. I argue that ideation must be singled out as sufficient for authorship and necessary for first authorship, since it supplies the primary intellectual reason an essay exists. Composition expresses the governing idea; direction governs its realisation; sustained engagement contributes to its development; and accountability ordinarily ratifies the antecedent intellectual ownership of whoever supplied the ideation. I therefore propose an ideation-centred hierarchy of authorial functions, a provisional definition of authorship as the primary intellectual reason for a text’s existence, and a corresponding model of byline attribution. I then consider AIdeation—the outsourcing of ideation itself to AI systems—as the apparent exception. Finally, I contend that ‘authorless essay’ is a misleading label for a criteria-relative gap. Without full AIdeation there is no authorlessness; with it, the essay is authorless under the ideation-first account but cannot qualify as scholarship, although an undisclosed and undetected case may be published.

items.title: Capacity and Decision Poverty Amid Survival Economy.
items.abstract: Poverty is commonly described through insufficient income, consumption, assets, employment, or access to essential goods. This article develops a philosophical account of poverty through the ontology of Finite Continuance and introduces three interconnected concepts: capacity poverty, decision poverty, and survival economy. Capacity poverty concerns the erosion of the capacity through which a finite being can reorganize its existence while continuing to exist. Decision poverty concerns the contraction of the temporal, cognitive, interpretive, and practical conditions required to generate, compare, suspend, and revise meaningful alternatives. Survival economy designates a social and temporal configuration in which an increasing proportion of available capacity is consumed by the maintenance of immediate continuity. The article distinguishes capacity poverty from the capability approach associated with Amartya Sen and Martha Nussbaum. Capability concerns substantive opportunities for functioning and agency, whereas capacity poverty concerns the preservation of the capacity through which existing capacities can be exercised, reorganized, and reproduced over time. The article further introduces a distinction among capability, capacity, and meta-capacity. Meta-capacity concerns the preservation of the conditions under which capacities themselves can develop, transform, and recombine. Decision poverty is distinguished from scarcity, cognitive bandwidth, and decision fatigue by locating the problem not simply in diminished performance but in the contraction of the field from which meaningful alternatives can emerge. Within Finite Continuance, finite existence is understood as provisional stabilization under continuous erosion. Continuance therefore requires more than persistence. It requires the preservation of sufficient reconfigurability. The article argues that chronic survival pressure can generate an erosive feedback process in which present maintenance consumes the temporal, cognitive, material, and practical resources required for future transformation. Poverty consequently acquires an ontological dimension when continuation persists while the capacity to become otherwise progressively contracts. The article concludes with an Ethics of Sufficiency, according to which present arrangements should be evaluated partly by whether they preserve the conditions of future agency and reconfiguration. -/- Keywords: capacity poverty, decision poverty, survival …

items.title: The Metaphysics of Self-Causality.
items.abstract: This article proposes an idealist/panpsychist metaphysics which connects the integrated information theory of consciousness (IIT) with the work of the philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer: both frameworks describe the whole universe as consisting of different forms of auto-causation — or, as Schopenhauer termed it, ‘the Will’. IIT proposes that consciousness is self-causality: the ‘information’ being measured in a system (e.g. a set of neurons in the brain) is causality (that is, any difference that makes a difference in the future), while ‘integrated’ means the system ultimately has causal power over itself. Schopenhauer, too, claimed that all matter and energy consists of this kind of conscious self-causality, which makes sense according to Charles Darwin’s idea that what is extant is always that which self-perpetuates. The ‘is–ought problem’ is resolved in this article by explaining causality as valence, or the subjectively-experienced difference between good and bad (understood within this theory as satisfaction vs. frustration of causality from its own perspective).

items.title: Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game ｰ From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.
items.abstract: This paper explores consciousness as a causal puzzle. Where an investigation of water molecules examines their properties, this inquiry follows the relations that sustain a whirlpool. It shifts attention from identifying consciousness within the brain to tracing the causal organization that could sustain one subject's present and history. The tools are Occam's principle and subtraction. Place a body, an environment, and conditions for continued existence on the board, then remove the relations one by one. What ceases to be possible when a relation is removed? This paper calls the method of narrowing down necessary causal roles through such removal "proof by absence." The proposed linkage connects viability-related candidate competition, strong information discard, consequences, and continuation. Strong information discard means that incompatible losers irreversibly lose their standing to determine continuation at the same branch, not that their information is completely erased. The winner's consequences become the same system's conditions of continuation and influence subsequent candidate formation. A loser may remain as information without becoming realized history; a winner may disappear as information while its consequences remain effective. An engineering interpretation of death clarifies what viability constraints constrain: the conditions sustaining a specified organization and the boundary at which its continuation is lost. History thereby operates not only as a record, but as present conditions shaping subsequent possibilities. The convergence-point criterion traces the coupling among the unit whose candidates compete, the unit whose conditions change, and the unit that continues from those conditions. The internal reference point denotes the role through which carried consequences influence subsequent formation. Through correspondence with one present, the bearing of consequences, a single history, and internal reference, together with explanatory economy, the paper strongly infers that the system realizing this coupling constitutes the subjective container. Identifying necessary causal roles and identifying their realization with the subject are separate steps. The latter is not a deductive proof of experience or of the structure's uniqueness. The framework begins below human language, self-awareness, and deliberation. It hypothesizes that brains broadly and closely implement this loop and predicts shared functional organization across species. …

items.title: Интерактивная онтология: приложение «Инвариант» как новая форма философской публикации.
items.abstract: Философская публикация традиционно отождествляется с текстом: статья, трактат или книга содержат аргументацию, а читатель последовательно знакомится с ней в форме линейного чтения. Настоящая работа рассматривает другой тип публикационного объекта — интерактивную онтологическую систему, в которой философский текст соединён с формальной дедукцией, визуализацией процессов, критической процедурой и машиночитаемым семантическим корпусом. -/- В качестве case study рассматривается веб-приложение «Инвариант» invariant .ai .studio, реализующее философский проект Метамонизма. Приложение объединяет девять функционально связанных разделов: онтологическое ядро, аксиоматический материал, трактат, академический корпус, интерактивную дедуктивную машину, онтодинамический симулятор, философскую генеалогию, диалектическую арену и открытый репозиторный хаб. -/- Работа не ставит целью доказать истинность Метамонизма. Её предметом является сама форма представления философской системы. Анализ показывает, что интерактивная публикация позволяет связать четыре ранее относительно раздельных уровня: философское содержание, интерактивную репрезентацию, формальную процедуру и машиночитаемую семантическую структуру. -/- Особое внимание уделяется принципу «семантика прежде типизации, формализация прежде идентичности», согласно которому сначала реконструируется смысл корпуса, затем выделяются сущности, утверждения и отношения, после чего производится формализация и только затем присваиваются стабильные идентификаторы. Такой подход позволяет рассматривать философский корпус не только как текст для чтения, но и как структурированный объект, пригодный для проверки, критики, машинной обработки и дальнейшего расширения. -/- Предлагается рассматривать интерактивную онтологию как возможную модель философской публикации в условиях цифровой и открытой научной среды.

items.title: The Symbiotic Author as an Institutional Category.
items.abstract: Governance of generative AI increasingly distinguishes among AI-generated content, AI-assisted content, human-authored text, disclosure, and eligibility, yet these categories often classify different institutional objects. This paper proposes the Symbiotic Author as a work-relative human authorship category for cases in which an identifiable human author participates in a materially consequential, bidirectionally conditioned creative relation with a generative system. The category does not depend on the percentage of machine-generated language retained in the final artifact. A work may contain no surviving machine-generated prose while its development has been materially shaped through sustained human–system interaction; conversely, extensive machine-generated prose may result from one-directional generation without a qualifying symbiotic relation. -/- The framework distinguishes textual provenance from creative causal provenance and treats substantive human uptake, redirection, rejection, and other forms of causal participation as analytically relevant even when machine output is not retained. It further separates the historical classification of the creative relation from declaration, creative provenance, evidentiary corroboration, and institutional eligibility. On this account, disclosure and surviving records make a process institutionally legible but do not constitute the process itself, while eligibility remains an independent normative decision of the adopting institution. -/- The paper develops boundary cases, an anti-anthropomorphism constraint, a proportionate corroboration model, and a compact operational protocol for journals, prizes, publishers, and related cultural institutions. The proposal does not treat generative systems as human-equivalent co-authors and does not determine copyrightability, originality, literary quality, or institutional admission. Its narrower contribution is an institutional architecture for describing the human author when materially consequential human–AI interaction becomes part of a work’s causal development without displacing the human authorial locus.

items.title: How Meaning Turns Out-of-Body Experiences into Life Change: A Phenomenological Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Out-of-body experiences (OBEs) are vivid and extraordinary events that may lead to psychological transformation, though not all individuals who report them undergo lasting change. This qualitative study explores when and how OBEs become transformative. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten healthy adults who had experienced spontaneous OBEs. Thematic analysis focused on three variables: frequency, phenomenological complexity, and subjective interpretation. Findings suggest that transformation occurred only in those who reported complex OBEs involving both displacement and entities) and interpreted them within a transcendental framework. Participants with simple OBEs or a psychological interpretation showed no major change. All reported difficulties sharing their experience, often fearing disbelief or judgment. This highlights the importance of creating non-pathologizing environments where individuals can make meaning of such experiences, since interpretation appears to mediate their transformative impact.

items.title: Journalism for Democratic Attitudes.
items.pub: Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy.
items.venue: Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy
items.abstract: Journalism plays a crucial role in democracy. Unfortunately, democracy is in decline around the world. I argue for a normative-democratic ideal journalists can follow to promote attitudes that are crucial for democracy. My analysis runs through what Susanna Siegel calls salience principles: norms that determine what journalistic mass media puts forward as worthy of and demanding our attention. I begin by justifying three kinds of democratic attitude that are crucial for democracy from a variety of perspectives in democratic theory: knowledge of public affairs, the recognition of being part of a larger public, and mutual toleration. I then elaborate a normative ideal of salience principles that journalists should adhere to such that they facilitate these democratic attitudes. In addition to the Importance Principle and Public-as-Protagonist Principle suggested by Siegel, I propose that we should add one other salience principle (the Mutual Toleration Facilitation Principle) and an ancillary principle (the Democratic Motivation Principle). Throughout the paper, I give practical guidance to journalists as to how to adhere to the principles. Finally, I deal with the objection that adhering to the normative-democratic ideal I propose is financially infeasible for journalists.

items.title: Flights of Fancy: Comment on Eric Schwitzgebel’s The Weirdness of the World.
“I was so Desperate”: Australasian Parents’ Expectations and Understandings of Stem Cell Therapy for Autism.
items.abstract: This study explores how parents seeking information about stem cell therapies (SCT) for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) understand and navigate a complex landscape of scientific uncertainty, commercial claims, and clinical advice. We conducted a quantitative content analysis of 54 enquiries submitted to the Stem Cells Australia website (2018–2023), alongside semi-structured interviews with 12 parents. Parents were highly engaged information-seekers, drawing on online sources, social media, other parents, and health professionals. However, they encountered inconsistent and often ambiguous guidance, particularly from clinicians, and reported difficulty assessing the credibility of competing claims. While many parents expressed scepticism about the efficacy of SCT, hope for improvement, fear of missing a critical intervention window, and positive accounts from other parents contributed to their ongoing interest. Risk perceptions were variable and often incomplete, particularly regarding procedural risks and long-term harms. Most participants had not pursued SCT, citing cost, uncertainty, and safety concerns. These findings highlight the need for clearer clinical guidance, improved risk communication, and stronger governance of unproven stem cell interventions to support families navigating ethically complex decisions.

items.title: Outsourcing Emotions to GenAI: The Risk of Bypassing Identity Development.
items.abstract: There is growing research on how and when the use of Generative AI (henceforth GenAI) in cognitive tasks may lead to a decline in the users’ cognitive capacities. There is emerging evidence that Generative AI also presents us with the opportunity to outsource some emotional tasks, such as flirting on dating apps or apologising. We believe that this may enable unsuspecting users to outsource too much of their affective capacities. Here, we wish to focus on a particular problem: insofar as articulating our own emotions is essential to discovering what we value and thereby shaping what sorts of persons we are, users who are heavily dependent on GenAI for emotional tasks risk forgoing crucial opportunities to develop a proper sense of their own identity.

items.title: Dignity and AI/Robotics.
items.abstract: The rapid development of AI and robotics is compelling us to rethink the meaning of “human dignity” and, more fundamentally, to reconsider what it means to be human. How is dignity institutionalized in law, society, and technology? How do researchers and practitioners in AI and robotics understand dignity, and how do they situate it within their research and business activities? This volume presents dignity as an indispensable framework for thinking about the ethical and social challenges of the age of AI, and explores its scope and potential from a variety of perspectives.

items.title: Clearing the Air About Psychedelic Spirituality.
items.abstract: Psychedelic-assisted therapy occasions mystical experiences and their intensity often predicts therapeutic outcomes. Owing to their spiritual import, psychedelics have been linked to supernatural thinking, religions, and cults. Several authors within the psychedelic field argue these associations render the field scientifically and ethically questionable, with some calling for the ‘mystical framework’ of therapy to be replaced. This paper examines the controversy surrounding psychedelic spirituality to diagnose the issue and offer proposals for easing tensions. We argue that the question of the veracity of mystical insights is the primary source of controversy, but is a philosophical rather than scientific question and can, for now, be bracketed. We also argue that despite the charge of guruism and cultishness, researchers should be free to hold personal beliefs about the truth of these insights. Given their profession, however, they ought to remain agnostic about such insights and maintain values and views inherent to the ethos of science in their professional conduct.

items.title: My AI Identity: When Human–AI Histories Become Non-Equivalent Operational Shapes.
items.abstract: This paper develops an operational account of AI identity by asking when a human–AI history becomes non-equivalent to another history even when the underlying model, architecture, or nominal agent remains the same. Rather than treating identity as persistence of substrate, model weights, memory storage, or self-description alone, the paper analyzes historical operational continuity: the retention, removal, reactivation, migration, and recurrence of relations that alter subsequent possibilities across changing configurations. Human–AI interaction histories become identity-relevant when their deletion, substitution, or reconstruction produces non-redundant differences in later behavior, inference, adaptation, recognition, or reachable states. The analysis therefore distinguishes stored history from operationally active history and tests whether apparently identical artificial systems remain substitutable after divergent trajectories of interaction. History fork, history removal, history reactivation, migration, and configuration-crossing recurrence provide cases for determining when continuity survives implementation change and when nominally identical systems become operationally non-equivalent. The paper connects these questions to classical problems of psychological continuity, memory, and personal identity while rejecting the assumption that biological persistence or human subjectivity must define the identity conditions of artificial systems. The broader claim is that AI identity should be analyzed through historically accumulated, configuration-dependent differences that continue to constrain future possibilities rather than through static architecture or instantaneous state alone.

items.title: What Remains After the Phenomena Grouped as ‘Consciousness’ Are Operationally Reduced? Operational Reduction, Matched-Control Benchmarking, Learned PyTorch Benchmarking, and Configuration-Dependent Residual Ignition Regions.
items.abstract: This paper asks what remains after the heterogeneous phenomena grouped under the term “consciousness” are operationally reduced under matched-control and learned benchmarking conditions. Rather than treating consciousness as a single pre-given property, the study decomposes candidate phenomena into operationally distinguishable functions and tests which differences remain non-redundant after stronger controls are introduced. The analysis combines matched-control benchmarking with learned PyTorch benchmarks to compare whether putatively consciousness-specific effects can be reproduced, substituted, or eliminated by alternative models under equivalent observational and task conditions. Operational reduction is defined as successful only when a candidate distinction can be removed without measurable loss in prediction, discrimination, intervention, robustness, or downstream behavioral organization. Residual ignition regions are then identified as configuration-dependent domains in which previously reduced differences become non-substitutable under changes in scale, memory, temporal integration, task structure, environmental coupling, or model capacity. The paper therefore distinguishes phenomenological grouping from operational necessity and rejects both premature eliminationism and premature reification of consciousness. The broader claim is that consciousness research should identify which residual differences survive increasingly strong empirical controls, rather than assuming in advance that all phenomena labeled “consciousness” share a single mechanism, essence, or irreducible property.

items.title: Ethical Abundance In A Meaningless Reality.
items.pub: Dissertation, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
items.abstract: This thesis examines whether ethics can survive in a reality devoid of inherent meaning, predetermined purpose, and transcendent moral authority. Drawing on Friedrich Nietzsche, Jean-Paul Sartre, and Albert Camus, it argues that nihilism need not culminate in despair or moral collapse, but can instead expose the freedom and responsibility inherent in human existence. Nietzsche’s reconstruction of values, Sartre’s radical freedom, and Camus’ revolt against the absurd are synthesized to establish meaninglessness as a condition for self-authored value rather than ethical emptiness. This framework is extended through Stoicism and epistemological solipsism, which together demonstrate how ethical agency can persist despite uncertainty concerning external reality and the absence of inherent value. Finally, an evolutionary account of human cooperation, empathy, and social behavior is used to explain how ethical capacities can arise without transcendent foundations. The thesis develops the concept of ethical abundance to describe the possibility that the absence of predetermined values expands, rather than eliminates, humanity’s capacity to critically examine, construct, and cultivate ethical commitments. A meaningless reality, therefore, need not signify the death of ethics, but may instead place greater responsibility upon human beings to create, affirm, and live according to the values they deliberately choose.

items.title: Representational Realism is not the Default Position of Cognitive Neuroscience.
items.abstract: Mental representations figure prominently in cognitive neuroscience, and this prominence is often taken to imply an underlying commitment to robust representational realism: the view that representations are real neural entities bearing determinate content grounded in their physical properties. The present paper challenges this assumption on two fronts. First, I argue that robust realist approaches face principled limitations, such as overgeneralization, and struggle to accommodate the diversity and context-sensitivity of neuroscientific data. Second, I claim that robust realism is neither required nor typically presupposed in scientific practice, as researchers rarely adopt such strong ontological commitments. Moreover, I present an alternative position, representational pragmatism, which treats representations not as discrete entities but as idealized epistemic artefacts, namely modelling tools that enable intelligibility, guide experimentation, and support prediction. I contend that this approach is more consistent with both neuroscientific practice and empirical data. To illustrate these points, I articulate a set of widely accepted constraints on representational attribution and examine varitel semantics, a leading contemporary robust realist framework. I argue that it fails to meet these desiderata and cannot reconcile its commitments with empirical findings. This, I maintain, exemplifies a broader difficulty of robust realism: the fallacy of misplaced concreteness, whereby methodological abstractions are mistaken for literal features of neural architecture. Finally, I defend representational pragmatism as a more viable and scientifically grounded stance that also fares better on representational desiderata. I conclude that if there is a “default scientific position”, it appears more pragmatist than robust realist.

items.title: Filsafat dan Sains Kesadaran.
Emotion, Consciousness, and the Heart–Brain Connection: A Quantum Biological Perspective.
items.abstract: Understanding human consciousness and emotion requires an interdisciplinary approach that can involve topics from neuroscience, physiology, and even quantum biology. This article proposes an integrative theory in which emotion is defined broadly as a concept that can capture different phenomena arising from brain activity, from instinctual affective responses to higher cognitive feelings, and considers how similar principles may apply to the heart’s intrinsic nervous system. We review evidence that the heart, with its own network of neurons, communicates with the brain to influence emotions and conscious experience. In this view, consciousness is considered as a complex phenomenon arising from the brain’s neurons and from a dynamic brain–heart system in which bodily states (especially cardiac signals) are represented in the brain to influence the creation of feelings of self and sentience. We further explore recent quantum biology perspectives on consciousness, which suggest that quantum-level processes in neurons (e.g. microtubule quantum states or nuclear spin dynamics) might contribute to the emergence of mind. Preliminary connections to the philosophy of mind are examined, particularly how the exposed ideas address the ‘hard problem’ of consciousness and revive dual aspect and panpsychist interpretations. We discuss how heart–brain interactions and quantum processes together might provide new connections with conscious experience — including the age-old intuition of the ‘heart’ as an organ of wisdom and emotion.

items.title: The Structure of Multidimensional Concepts.
items.abstract: Recent work in philosophy and cognitive science has brought renewed attention to multidimensional concepts and properties such as healthy and democratic. In this paper, we take steps toward a comprehensive theory of them. Much of the existing literature treats multidimensionality piecemeal, isolating particular features. Most prominently, multidimensional concepts appear to involve forms of aggregation structurally akin to those studied in social choice theory. While this insight is illuminating, it stops short of explaining what dimensions are and how they contribute to concept application. This under-theorization gives rise to puzzles about how, exactly, standard social choice principles should be interpreted in the multidimensional setting. Our aim is to embed the aggregative module within a broader framework that accounts for the characteristic features of multidimensional concepts and reconciles them with social choice principles that might otherwise appear to stand in tension with them.

items.title: Self-opacity requires a hidden layer.
items.abstract: The first-person problem begins from a residue: a complete third-person description of a system can still leave a “for-it” remainder. This paper does not attempt to derive phenomenal experience from physics. It constructs the smallest physical object about which the word perspective can be made operationally meaningful: a readout layer whose standard of consistency is held by its own generator and cannot be transferred, without loss, to an external readout. The proposed minimal readout self is neither a private experience nor a complex informational system. It is a directed, non-absorbable, structurally self-external readout layer. Direction is supplied by a cycle affinity; non-absorbability means that pooling layers yields a generator belonging to no layer; structural self-externality means that the coordinate fixing the layer’s rates is not a degree of freedom transported by that layer. Two exact carrier constructions determine the limits of these conditions.

items.title: Echoes of Kant’s Ideas in Modern Cognitive Research.
items.abstract: This article examines Kant’s ideas on the a priori character of space and time in the context of modern cognitive research and neuroscience. Proceeding from the Kantian view of space and time as forms of sensibility, I look at how neurobiological data confirm and simultaneously modify classical philosophical nativism. I pay particular attention to empirically-confirmed, inborn cognitive mechanisms such as the “sense of number” and the supposed “sense of space” which have ontogenetic and neural foundations. I look at discoveries pertaining to the brain’s navigation systems, including “place” cells, which point to the existence of a functionally autonomous “geometric” (and not just a “number”) module. This module has been shown to play a key role, not only in one’s orientation in physical space, but also in the formation of abstract concepts, semantic structures, and social ties. I examine data on the independence of basic geometric intuition from cultural and sensory experience, including research on spatial representations in born-blind individuals. A special section is devoted to the analysis of the Spatial-Numerical Association of Response Codes (SNARC) effect: its possible influence on the character of the writing system, and, conversely, of script configuration on spatial-numerical and cognitive associations. This phenomenon demonstrates an interconnection between the perception of numbers and direction in space, which is partly determined by cultural features: people with left-to-right writing associate numbers of a larger magnitude with the right side, while people who write from right to left have the reverse association. Thus, human perceptions of space and time are the result of intricate interactions between congenital properties of the nervous system and extra-personal cultural influence. In conclusion, I stress the prospectivity of the concept “biocultural co-constructivism”, according to which congenital neuron structures and cultural practices are in dynamic interaction, and which promises deeper insight into the meaning of the Kantian research programme as implemented in modern neuroscience.

items.title: No further fact: consciousness, functional organisation and moral status.
items.abstract: This paper defends an illusionist view of consciousness and draws out its consequences for moral status. The thesis is that consciousness involves no further fact: once a system's functional organisation is fixed at the grain that makes a difference to the phenomena consciousness is invoked to explain, nothing further about whether or how it is conscious remains open. The main argument develops Chalmers's argument from coincidence against phenomenal properties that could vary while that organisation stays fixed, and extends it, through an interventionist criterion for the relevant grain, to realiser theories including integrated information theory. The Moorean objection that we plainly have experience is answered with an account of the self-model whose representations make experience seem intrinsic, and it turns out to reduce to a claim of acquaintance. The moral argument adds an explicit premise, supported by the same coincidence reasoning: what makes a state bad for a subject consists in the subject's own evaluative stance towards it. With that premise, and clinical evidence that the badness of pain goes with its affective-motivational component, the paper states a sufficient criterion for welfare: globally available evaluative states that weigh represented outcomes, drive learning that tracks the value of outcomes, and belong to the system itself. Applied to evidence from 2025 and 2026, the criterion finds that current language models have evaluative states of the persona they enact and that these states are their own, but that learning and integration beyond a single conversation remain unshown.

items.title: A Shared Interoceptive-Swallow Gating Vulnerability in Panic Disorder.
items.abstract: Panic disorder is commonly accompanied by choking sensations, respiratory alarm, fear of bodily catastrophe, and heightened monitoring of internal sensations. Separately, functional dysphagia and phagophobia can involve delayed or effortful swallow initiation despite little or no structural explanation. These phenomena are usually interpreted directionally: anxiety is presumed to produce secondary difficulty swallowing. We propose a different, testable possibility. In a clinically meaningful subgroup, panic symptoms and swallow-initiation dysfunction may be parallel expressions of a shared interoceptive-sensorimotor network vulnerability. The proposed network includes the insula, anterior cingulate cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, supplementary motor area, primary sensorimotor swallowing representations, and brainstem integrative nuclei involved in autonomic regulation and deglutition. -/- Existing findings support each side of this bridge but have not directly tested the bridge itself. Panic disorder has been associated with altered insular and sensorimotor-network connectivity, while a small magnetoencephalography study of functional dysphagia found increased right-insular and prefrontal activation alongside reduced supplementary motor and sensorimotor activation during swallowing. We hypothesize that heightened interoceptive salience and self-monitoring can destabilize the transition from voluntary oral control to the patterned pharyngeal swallow, particularly under threat. -/- We propose a preregistered, multicenter, four-group study of 240 adults: panic disorder with a swallow-initiation phenotype, panic disorder without that phenotype, swallow-initiation dysfunction without panic disorder, and healthy controls. The protocol combines structured psychiatric assessment, speech-language pathology evaluation, videofluoroscopic swallowing measures, autonomic and respiratory monitoring, repeated momentary state-anxiety measurement, structural MRI, resting-state connectivity, and task-based functional MRI during neutral and threat-anticipation swallowing conditions. The study is designed to distinguish a shared trait vulnerability from state anxiety, learned phobic avoidance, and occult organic dysphagia. Confirmation would support a mechanistically defined panic-swallow phenotype and motivate integrated interventions; disconfirmation would clarify that swallowing symptoms are better explained as downstream consequences or independent disorders.

items.title: Generative Uncertainty: Embracing Epistemic Friction as a Philosophical Virtue.
items.abstract: This thesis critically examines the question of whether uncertainty can be considered a philosophical virtue. Moving beyond the conventional understanding of uncertainty as a negative state to be merely tolerated, this work proposes a novel dialectical virtue-theoretic framework. This framework re-conceptualizes uncertainty as a productive force, or epistemic friction, that is essential for intellectual flourishing. The virtue of uncertainty, it is argued, lies not in a static disposition of tolerance, but in the agent’s dynamic and skillful engagement with the inherent tensions of the unknown. The thesis introduces three core dialectical pairs of virtues—intellectual humility vs. intellectual courage, open-mindedness vs. critical scrutiny, and cognitive flexibility vs. focused persistence—that are central to this process. Through a synthesis of philosophical analysis and empirical evidence from psychology and cognitive science, this work demonstrates that the virtuous agent is one who can navigate the creative tension between these opposing, yet complementary, virtues. The framework is then applied to various domains, including scientific inquiry, medical diagnosis, and artistic creation, to illustrate its explanatory power. This thesis concludes that uncertainty, when approached through a dialectical lens, is not only a philosophical virtue but a fundamental component of a flourishing intellectual life in an increasingly complex world.

items.title: Retroactive Semantic Computation and Closed-Text Interpretation: Toward a Verifiable Proof-Assistant Model of Interpretation.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a formal model of literary and philosophical interpretation as a process of verification, comparison, and retroactive revision within a fixed evidence boundary. The model separates hypothesis generation from hypothesis verification: a large language model or other generator may be influenced by external knowledge, while the verifier restricts admissible evidence to the input text, time-indexed core annotations, and predeclared interpretive rules. -/- The framework integrates defeasible admissibility, a support preorder, textual provenance, hypothesis-conditional truth values, retroactive reclassification, and switching among predeclared evaluators. It distinguishes counterevidence against an interpretation from cases in which an earlier utterance becomes false under an otherwise admissible interpretation. -/- Four synthetic tests based on familiar motifs from Greek myth illustrate distinct operations: referential competition and retroactive truth evaluation, speech-act reclassification, evaluator switching and meta-level reinterpretation, and the filtering of hypotheses generated from external cultural priors. -/- The aim is not to identify a uniquely correct interpretation or to exhaust all possible readings. Rather, the paper develops a candidate architecture for an interpretive proof assistant: a system designed to make explicit which textual fragments and declared rules support a submitted interpretation at a given stage of reading, and how that interpretation changes as later textual evidence becomes available.

items.title: There Can Be No Dispute.
items.abstract: In an influential series of papers, Plunkett and Sundell defend contextualism against arguments from disagreement. Part of their defense appeals to the possibility of metalinguistic negotiation, but there is controversy concerning the legitimacy of this strategy. I adjudicate the debate by demonstrating that the possibility of metalinguistic negotiation is only one of the challenges Plunkett and Sundell have proposed. I rehearse a more general challenge called Sundell’s dilemma and argue that a successful response to Plunkett and Sundell must resolve the dilemma. I then provide such a response by considering a class of cases called “doomed affirmation attempts” and develop a novel argument against contextualism which makes no appeal to disagreement while also avoiding the dilemma. Next, I provide an account of substantive disagreement which allows for an upgraded argument from disagreement that avoids Plunkett and Sundell’s challenges as well as many other common contextualist defenses against previous arguments from disagreement.

items.title: The Emergence of Homo Spiritualis: A Synthesized Model of Quranic Anthropology, Population Genetics, and Cognitive Evolution.
items.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous theological-scientific framework reconciling the Quranic account of human origins with modern evolutionary primatology, cognitive neuroscience, and population genetics. We demonstrate that the Quranic narrative employs a dual paradigm: "Adam" functions both as a symbolic representation of an early, behaviorally modern human society and as a historical, divinely chosen individual who served as the genetic progenitor of modern Homo sapiens. By integrating textual exegesis of critical Quranic passages (including Surah 7:11, 7:24, 32:7–9, and 2:31–33) with evolutionary theories of pair-bonding, neocortical expansion, and genetic coalescent theory (Y-Chromosomal Adam and Mitochondrial Eve), we propose that human ensoulment coincided with a heritable genomic transformation. Crucially, this biological transition did not occur as an instantaneous physical miracle overnight, but rather unfolded across generational time as a rapid, punctuated evolutionary expansion. This biological-spiritual convergence marks the transition from pre-human hominins to self-aware, moral beings (Homo spiritualis).

items.title: The Ontological Positioning of Large Language Models.
items.abstract: Large language models are emergent structures produced by a reduction in the discreteness of linguistic representation. They are neither subjects nor mere tools: they are products of human chiseling whose representation spaces possess powerful emergent organization but lack an intrinsic direction of their own. -/- The paper distinguishes discreteness—the resolution of differentiation within a given dimension—from dimension—the number of directions in which differentiation can occur. On this account, current language models reduce discreteness without adding a new dimension. This explains both their striking capabilities and their limits. Emergence, hallucination, and alignment are three aspects of the same structural change: reduced discreteness restores associations among meanings, can over-restore them, and then requires selective reconstruction of boundaries. -/- The account compares this transition to the expansion from integers to real numbers and argues that eliminating hallucination without sacrificing some emergence is impossible for the same low-discreteness generative kernel, although external grounding can redistribute the tradeoff at the system level. It concludes that the next qualitative advances are more likely to arise from architectural change than from scale alone.

items.title: Epistemic Antibodies: A Technical Implementation of Semantic Immunity for Conceptual Lineage Protection.
items.abstract: The open scientific record faces a paradox. The same digital infrastructures that promised to democratize knowledge have also enabled new forms of systematic intellectual appropriation. An original conceptual framework, once published in open text, can be harvested, terminologically rebranded, and relaunched as a novel contribution by actors within the networks of power and influence that control a given field of knowledge. The original author is then rendered invisible not through explicit rejection, but through a combination of epistemic erasure (the omission of the original source) and epistemic dilution (the accumulation of derivative publications that bury it). Existing defensive measures, such as cryptographic timestamping or persistent identifiers, establish temporal priority. They do not, however, bind the derivative framework to its origin in a way that travels with the data through the semantic web. A timestamp proves that something existed earlier. It does not automatically expose a later plagiarism as plagiarism. This article introduces a new defensive layer: Epistemic Antibodies. These are active semantic structures—instantiated as RDF/JSON-LD graphs—that bind to derivative frameworks and expose their true lineage. They do not establish the relation of derivation; they encode, identify, and persist a determination that has already been produced by an epistemic procedure. The system is grounded in an immunological metaphor and organized around three distinct epistemic functions. The CLEO Protocol performs recognition: it evaluates a candidate framework against the constitutive conceptual signatures of an original sovereign framework and determines whether the candidate is structurally derivative. The CLEO Determination performs registration: it records the result of that evaluation, with its date, protocol, and supporting documentation. The Epistemic Antibody performs semantic persistence and exposure: it binds to the derivative framework and makes the determination machine-readable and recoverable across changing information environments. The system is formalized in the epimsys ontology (version 3.0), which integrates the W3C PROV-O vocabulary to provide a formal provenance layer for the determination process. This paper presents the technical architecture of epistemic antibodies, their formal implementation, and a first deployment case against a real-world derivative framework: the “Platonic Space” framework introduced by Michael Levin.

items.title: The Autonomy and Dignity Problem in Cryonics: A Conditionally Self-Resolved Ethical Approach.
items.pub: Journal of Contemporary Academic Research and Methodologies 1 (3):207-217.
items.venue: Journal of Contemporary Academic Research and Methodologies
items.abstract: Cryonics is a controversial practice that involves preserving the body of a person who has been legally declared dead, with the hope that future medical science may be able to restore them to life. This raises important ethical questions about autonomy and human dignity, especially given the uncertainty surrounding its scientific practicability. This paper examines whether common ethical objections to cryonics, particularly those based on autonomy and dignity, are justified or not. The study adopts a qualitative philosophical approach based on conceptual analysis and normative ethical reasoning. It evaluates cryonics through established principles in bioethics, including informed consent, respect for persons, and human dignity. The analysis show that autonomy is not necessarily undermined in cryonics, since individuals may still make voluntary and informed decisions under conditions of uncertainty. It also shows that dignity is not automatically violated, as dignity can be understood not only in terms of bodily finality, but also as respect for individual values and choices. When cryonics is freely chosen and properly understood as speculative, the main ethical objections lose much of their force. The paper concludes that the autonomy and dignity problem in cryonics is largely self-resolved within a framework condition of informed voluntary choice and respect for persons. While cryonics remains scientifically uncertain, its ethical status depends more on the quality of decision-making than on guaranteed outcomes. This suggests that future ethical discussions should focus on refining consent and understanding long-term implications, rather than rejecting the practice outright.

items.title: Regenerative Suspension and the Institutional Ethics of Finite Continuance.
items.abstract: Institutions do not merely distribute resources, permissions, and obligations. They also organize the temporal conditions under which human capacities are exercised, depleted, maintained, and transformed. This article develops the concept of Regenerative Suspension within the philosophical framework of Finite Continuance. The central claim is not that institutions are generally obligated to maximize individual welfare, nor that every experience of exhaustion generates a right to withdrawal. Rather, the argument concerns a narrower problem of institutional legitimacy: when an institution substantially controls the conditions under which a person must exercise capacities on which continued participation depends, sustained institutional demands can become normatively problematic when they foreseeably erode the capacity required for future agency. Finite Continuance conceptualizes a finite being as a provisional stabilization whose continuity depends not on preservation of an identical configuration but on preservation of sufficient capacity for reconfiguration. On this basis, the article distinguishes ordinary rest, accommodation, therapeutic intervention, exclusion, and Regenerative Suspension. Regenerative Suspension is defined as a temporally bounded or conditionally bounded modification of institutional demands intended to prevent or reverse capacity depletion while preserving the subject’s status as an agent and participant. The argument is developed through dialogue with the capability approach, care ethics, republican theories of non-domination, recognition theory, critical social theory, disability studies, and research on occupational stress and burnout. The article proposes an Institutional Regenerative Principle according to which institutions that materially depend upon human capacities have a prima facie responsibility not knowingly to organize demands in ways that foreseeably reduce dependent agents below a contextually sufficient level of future reconfigurative capacity when proportionate institutional alternatives are available. This principle does not establish a universal right to reduced demands. It establishes a temporal constraint on legitimate institutional dependence. -/- Keywords: finite continuance; regenerative suspension; institutional ethics; future agency; reconfigurative capacity; erosion; sufficiency; non-domination; care ethics; capability approach; institutional legitimacy; crip time; recognition theory.

items.title: CHINA's SOCIAL CREDIT SYSTEM READ THROUGH THE PHILOSOPHY OF VIRTUES: The Two Handles and the Honour Roll — What Confucius, Han Feizi, Holmström–Milgrom, Bénabou–Tirole, Wintrobe and Tirole’s Digital Dystopia Already Hold, and What Remains.
items.abstract: China’s social credit system is usually evaluated as a single object, either as a surveillance scorecard or as a misunderstood regulatory database. Neither reading survives contact with the system as it now stands: there is no unified personal score, most local citizen-scoring pilots are reported to have lapsed, and the system’s documented mass consists of corporate compliance records, court-enforcement blacklists and, since April 2026, a national credit-repair regime. This article evaluates the system component by component, under the programme’s act–state separation, and asks three questions: whether the system serves the freedom of the people who live under it or the power that administers it; how it affects the virtues; and how it affects Chinese society and welfare. Priority is conceded before the argument: for the claim that governing by rewards and punishments produces compliance without shame, to Confucius (Analects 2.3); for the design of the two handles, to Han Feizi; for crowding-out, to Titmuss, Deci and Frey; for the loss of signal value in rewarded prosociality, to Bénabou and Tirole (2006); for diverted effort under partial measurement, to Holmström and Milgrom (1991); for the ruler’s ignorance under repression, to Wintrobe (1998) and Kuran (1995); and for bundling political attitudes into social scores, to Tirole (2021). What remains is structural. The system’s components separate into three classes by a property derived from the programme’s Decoy Placement Rule — whether the substance behind what a component inspects can be taken or directly measured by the scorer — and the classes carry opposite verdicts. Enforcement of owed acts the state can take, measure or compel (debts, taxes, measured emissions) produces no counterfeit virtue and plausible welfare gains, but it frees no one: compelled payment inverts the act it obtains, and seizure, which inverts nothing, removes the occasion on which the obligation could have been kept freely. A general result follows: every increase in a state’s control over its citizens either inverts their acts or removes the occasions for them, and none increases their freedom; control can change states of affairs, but it cannot produce, hold or return freedom, which passes to no one when it is taken. Scoring of displayable conduct (civic points, honour lists, sincerity of apology) is where counterfeit virtue is predicted to concentrate. Bundling of speech into scores transfers the discipline of the scored to …

items.title: Imposed Image: Access, Running Total, and Ascription.
items.abstract: This note does not replace Functional Authored Agency and does not answer why there is a total rather than nothing. It adds two claims that belong beside the existing architecture. First: kind is the inherited license; use is the load actually running. Glow, in the human sense, is this license’s running total under load, not a light-switch. Imagination is internal output on the same menu. Second: self-access and other-access are one tool — authorship — run on two data conditions. Introspection is not contact with one’s own total. It is construction on high-bandwidth data. Reading another is the same construction on sparse data. Imagination is a real act with a real object. The error is treating the shortest gap as zero distance. Occupancy and the identity claim stay in Feeling as Licensed Operation. Score them there, not here. That a total can run without being pictured is assumed from that architecture — occupancy can be felt and unowned; self-picturing is authorship about the total — not derived in this note. Picturing a total, from inside or outside, is access. This note is the exclusive home of that access argument. FLO declined to house it.
