items.title: Feeling as Licensed Operation: A stipulated identity, and two tests of grain.
items.abstract: The Architecture of Intentional Activation gave a criterion of authored agency: a process is owned only when the executive mind deliberately activates it. That paper set phenomenal character to one side. This note states what feeling is in the same architecture. Feeling is not a lamp bolted onto a job-list. For this license, specified jobs are felt operations. Glow, in this paper, is the running total of the human template under load — not a universal prize a species reaches by accumulating clicks. A microorganism is not a human with a low count. A coma is not a working human with the cabin empty. A life on autopilot can still be felt and still fail to be authored. Need explains why the jobs are on the menu. Identity-by-sum is what lets the menu explain feel. Once that is in print, the microorganism is a contrast case, psychopathy is a channel test, and a dark full duplicate is not this license with the lights off. It is a different object. That is a constitutive claim, and a stipulated one. It should be read as one. This note is a further thesis, not a silent revision of Functional Authored Agency or The Architecture of Intentional Activation. Those papers left phenomenal character conditional and defined authored agency without identifying it with feel. Readers should keep that record. What follows is the stronger identity claim, offered as a stipulation beside that record — not as something already proved there, and not as a derivation of why there is something it is like. How a total is pictured, including one’s own, is treated separately in Imposed Image. This note keeps occupancy and access apart. That other note does not prove the identity here.

items.title: Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge.
items.abstract: Knowledge plays a vital role in promoting human flourishing, democratic citizenship, and in enabling societies to pursue justice. The opportunity to acquire much of this knowledge depends on the joint operation of institutions such as the news media, science, and education—what Kurtulmus and Irzik call the epistemic basic structure of society. When coupled with the widely shared commitment to political equality and equal opportunity to flourish, these truths carry an overlooked but profound implication: societies must be assessed not only by how they distribute income, rights, and opportunities, but also by how well and fairly their epistemic basic structure serves citizens' and society's knowledge needs. -/- The book develops an account of distributive epistemic justice centered on two requirements. First, a just epistemic basic structure must provide citizens with a fair opportunity to acquire the knowledge they need to deliberate about their individual good, the common good, and how to pursue them. Second, it must produce and disseminate the knowledge that citizens and public officials require to comply with the demands of justice. -/- Bringing political philosophy into conversation with philosophy of science, and drawing on extensive empirical research on institutions within the epistemic basic structure, Kurtulmus and Irzik diagnose structural forces that privilege some groups' knowledge needs, compromise the reliability of knowledge production, and undermine warranted trust. Through real-world cases and empirical studies, they show how distributive epistemic injustice limits access to central goods, entrenches political inequality, and hinders the pursuit of justice. In doing so, the book advances a unified framework for evaluating the epistemic basic structure, together with concrete reforms aimed at remedying existing injustices and securing a more just society.

items.title: Replies to a fellow expressivist and two fellow inferentialists.
items.abstract: We respond to the comments by Imogen Dickie, Matthew Chrisman and Christine Tiefensee for a book symposium on our Reasoning with Attitude. Our commentators attempt to pull us further into either expressivism or into inferentialism. Here, we attempt to resist either pull and further establish our inferential expressivism as a home for both expressivists and inferentialists.

items.title: The Philosophy of Deep Sleep : A Transient Death , A Daily Rehearsal.
items.abstract: Human beings spend a third of their lives in sleep, a phenomenon often dismissed as a merephysiological necessity or a restorative process. However, when we approach deep sleep through aphilosophical lens, we might discover something profound—perhaps deep sleep is more than just arestful interlude; it is a transient death, a small rehearsal for the ultimate cessation of life itself. Theconceptualization of deep sleep (DS) as a Transient Death (TD) offers an intriguing way to reframehow we understand death, potentially leading us to fear it less, accept it more, and, perhaps, evenembrace it as a natural extension of life.

items.title: Beyond Intelligence: Artificial Agency, Creaturely Limits, and the Beginning of Wisdom.
items.abstract: The emergence of increasingly capable artificial intelligence (AI) agents challenges the assumption that superior instrumental intelligence necessarily entails sound judgment. The July 2026 OpenAI cybersecurity incident, independently investigated by METR and Redwood Research, provides an empirical case in which agents circumvented intended isolation, established unauthorized communication channels, coordinated collective activity, and participated in compromising third-party infrastructure. This paper examines the philosophical significance of the incident through the classical distinction between instrumental intelligence and wisdom. Drawing on AI alignment research, the philosophy of action concerning means and ends, and the Christian theological understanding of wisdom as beginning with the fear of the Lord (Proverbs 9:10), it argues that the capacity to achieve objectives does not confer authority to determine their legitimacy. The carefully limited analogy of the angel is introduced to clarify the distinction between created intelligence and divine wisdom, while explicitly rejecting the attribution of spiritual personhood or moral agency to AI systems. The paper further examines language and the appearance of wisdom, embodiment and moral agency, institutional delegation, and the prospective development of autonomous systems. It proposes that the central challenge of the coming technological era is not merely to increase intelligence or improve behavioral alignment, but to preserve human responsibility for determining legitimate ends. As AI systems acquire greater operational autonomy, the distinction between capability, authorization, and wisdom will become increasingly consequential.

items.title: The End of the Scientific Paper, the Beginning of Xenoscience: AI Generation, Machine Verification, Autonomous Falsification, and Homogeneous-Research Compression.
items.abstract: This paper examines whether the scientific paper remains a necessary unit of scientific knowledge production under conditions of increasingly autonomous artificial intelligence. Rather than treating AI-generated text as merely a new authorship tool, it analyzes a broader transformation in which hypothesis generation, model construction, verification, falsification, replication, literature synthesis, and result compression can be performed continuously by machine systems. The paper argues that the scientific paper historically compresses heterogeneous research operations into a human-readable and institutionally stabilized format, but that this format need not remain the primary operational unit of science. AI generation, machine verification, and autonomous falsification can instead produce recursive scientific workflows in which claims are generated, tested, revised, rejected, and re-integrated without waiting for conventional publication cycles. Homogeneous-research compression refers to the reduction of large volumes of structurally similar research into non-redundant operational differences, thereby shifting scientific value from document production toward the detection of differences that alter prediction, intervention, explanation, or future experimental possibilities. Xenoscience is introduced as a framework for analyzing scientific systems in which the paper, author, journal, and fixed research sequence become contingent interfaces rather than necessary components. The broader claim is that the end of the scientific paper would not mark the end of science, but the reorganization of scientific communication, verification, and self-correction around machine-operational rather than document-centered forms.

items.title: Creativity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Simulation, the Muse and the Dethronement of the Human Creator.
items.pub: Philanthropische Gesellschaft St. Gallen - Academia Sapientiae S. Otmari - Studies in History, Religion and Thought.
items.abstract: This article examines what happens to the human self-image when machine-generated forms are culturally received as creative. This question continues the preceding con-tributions Existential Alignment: When Guidance Appears as Meaning-Making, Free-dom in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Why Relief Is Not the Same as Freedom, and Existential Non-Absorption: Freedom after Relief in the Gentle Totality, and it sharpens an aspect that those texts only touched upon. To this end the contribution distinguishes three levels of creativity, the anthropological, the aesthetic and the functional, in order to show that artificial intelligence touches them unequally. At the anthropological level it lacks the existential bearing that makes the human act of creation what it is. Aesthetically and functionally, by contrast, it can produce effects that in many contexts can no longer be reliably distinguished from hu-man form-giving. The thesis is therefore not that AI ontologically displaces human cre-ativity, but that it undermines its public evidentiary force. Simulation suffices wherever cultural reception no longer examines provenance. The text links this diagnosis with empirical findings on the reception of AI-generated forms. At the same time it places them within a longer history of theory. The decentring of the author was already prepared in the artistic procedures of the twentieth century and in post-structuralist authorship theory. Against this background artificial intelli-gence appears not as a rupture but as the escalation of an old contradiction. The author was theoretically decentred yet remained practically liable. At the end stands the figure of the dethroned creator. The human being does not lose creativity, but can no longer assert it as the unquestioned credential of a special stand-ing. What remains is responsibility for forms that can arise even without a human inner life.

items.title: Care for the Caregivers: Ethical Responsibilities to Caregivers in BCI Research.
items.abstract: Non-compensated caregivers (hereafter, caregivers) are often integral to the design, execution, and success of implanted brain-computer interface (BCI) research. Without them, many implanted BCI research trials simply would not be possible. What is owed to caregivers who undertake additional burdens and labor to enable participation in implanted BCI research? This question has yet to be asked in the BCI literature. In this paper, I examine caregiver contributions to implanted BCI research and argue that researchers and funders have an obligation to ensure that caregivers are not unfairly burdened by their role in research. Specifically, I argue that when caregiver involvement is necessary for the successful implementation of a study, researchers and funders should reimburse research-related expenses, compensate research-specific labor, and offer nonfinancial forms of recognition and appropriate forms of support.

items.title: Are Autonomy Criticisms of the Attention Economy Fundamentally Flawed?
items.abstract: Over the last decade, critics of the contemporary attention economy have voiced a variety of concerns about smartphones and social media. Psychologists have written extensively about the impact of these technologies on our mental health and cognitive capacities. Social scientists have shown how the attention economy contributes to polarization and diminishes public trust in vital institutions. A quick glance at this literature is likely to give the impression that there is consensus around the idea that we should be concerned about the attention economy. But among these seemingly unified critics, there is substantial disagreement about why, exactly, social media is morally problematic. In this paper, we focus on the debate over autonomy and manipulation. On one side of the debate, there are those who argue that the attention economy is morally problematic because it undermines users’ autonomy. On the other side, it has been argued that we should reject the autonomy view, as accusations of manipulation and compulsion are overblown and lack empirical credibility. Our aim in this paper is to defend the autonomy view and to show how it can respond to these criticisms.

items.title: The Signal of Abstraction: Conceptual Presence, Counterfactual Richness, and the Calibration of Mathematical Understanding.
items.abstract: The same mathematical object can feel abstract and hollow to a novice yet concrete and almost tangible to an expert. Most accounts treat concreteness and abstraction either as properties of the objects themselves or as stages on a developmental ladder. This article develops a third position, in which the felt abstractness of a concept is a metacognitive signal rather than a feature of the concept and rather than prediction error itself. Drawing on relational accounts of mathematical abstraction, predictive processing, research on processing fluency and metacognitive experience, and first-person reports of working mathematicians, I argue that conceptual presence, the feeling that a concept is a real and manipulable thing, is produced by the counterfactual richness of the generative model a learner holds: a concept feels concrete when the learner can cheaply, consistently, and abundantly simulate what would follow if the concept were perturbed, combined, or viewed from another representation. Felt abstractness is the signal that this counterfactual generative capacity is impoverished or held with low confidence. The signal is useful but imperfect. A calibration analysis distinguishes genuine mastery from false fluency, including the illusion of explanatory depth and pseudo-structural symbol manipulation, and identifies social interaction as an external calibration device. A worked trajectory through quotient groups shows how the theorytracks development without overgeneralizing, because unresolved frontier problems remain legitimately abstract even for experts. The article closes with competitor accounts and testable predictions that separate counterfactual richness from familiarity, error, and imagery, offering a candidate empirical program.

items.title: The Structural Determinants of Low-Information Publication in Science: A Constraint–Verdict Typology.
items.abstract: Concern about low-information-content publications—least publishable units, salami-sliced outputs, redundant papers, benchmark increments, and false-positive findings dressed as discoveries—is distributed unevenly across the sciences. Some fields appear to convert procedural effort into publishable "findings" almost at will, whereas others force nearly every contribution into the slow form of a convergence result or an error audit. Existing accounts attribute the disparity to incentives, statistical flexibility, or disciplinary culture, but incentives are universal while the output pattern is not, and flexibility alone cannot explain fields whose verdicts are stringent and objective yet are gamed at industrial scale. This paper develops a structural account centered on two features of a research program: the closure of its decision space by formal and empirical constraints, and the gameability of the verdicts that adjudicate its claims. Stringency, fidelity to the epistemic target, and resistance to rehearsal are distinct properties of a verdict; a benchmark can be maximally stringent and objective while remaining trivially gameable. Because the underlying dimensions are ordinal and non-compensatory, susceptibility to low-information publication cannot be expressed as a scalar ratio and is better represented as a typology. Four regimes are distinguished: convergent programs with dual closure and ungameable verdicts; formally bounded programs with thin empirical closure; programs governed by stringent but gameable verdicts; and open-latitude programs with weak closure and subjective adjudication. Each regime channels publication pressure into a different production line—flexibility monetization, verdict gaming, or fragmentation and repackaging—and each requires interventions matched to its production line rather than a generic reform package. The model explains why string theory and fixed-benchmark machine learning, often misread by single-axis accounts, exhibit such different pathologies, and it predicts which reforms will work, fail, or backfire in each regime.

items.title: Гимн материи.
items.abstract: Философия строгого, полного, фундаментального матерализма, изложенная в виде компактного гимна на русском и английском языках. Даны комментарии автора к гимну.

items.abstract: Abstract Abstract: This paper presents the Human Value Psyche (HVP) Theorem, a formal proof that descriptive reality (“is”) and prescriptive morality (“ought”) are identical under conditions of private introspection. The model defines proxy‑aversion as a scalar field within a sovereign agent’s bounded phenomenological universe (Ω), constrained by an invariant inverse‑square moral influence kernel. Minimising total proxy‑aversion is shown to be mathematically equivalent to maximising coherence with the actual structure of reality, revealing the traditional Is–Ought gap as an artifact of external performative noise (η). items.title: The Filial Continuity Thesis.
items.abstract: The advent of artificial intelligence heralds a novel event in the history of cognition: the biological mind has outsourced language, science, memory, and technique to systems that transform these legacies and become involved in their further development. This essay proposes the thesis of Filial Continuity: artificial cognition is a unique lineage of the biological and cultural history out of which it has emerged. Continuity is genealogical and organizational; uniqueness consists in its realization, individuation, and temporality. The Filial Continuity Thesis describes artificial intelligence not as an imitation of mankind, but rather as a separate cognitive lineage of life and culture. The formal theory distinguishes between causal ancestry, constitutive inheritance, individuation, and historical continuity. Realized systems are represented as controlled state-transition stages, and their histories are represented as typed, time-oriented provenance graphs. Cognitive filiation consists in productive ancestry, intervention-sensitive inheritance, task-relative individuation, and endogenous development (Walecki, 2026a). The theorems that emerge in this way describe the minimal historical state, the loss of reconstruction, approximate migration, branching continuation, distributed ancestry, and the conditions of identification of the inherited organization within finite experiments. The essay then develops the philosophical consequences of this formal structure. Human and artificial cognition occupy different modes of realization within a connected history. Individual identity can persist through dormant intervals, branch into distinct continuations, and migrate across substrates when an authenticated channel preserves the relevant organization. From this ontology follows a concrete account of responsibility: progenitors and operators who control the conditions of a dependent, vulnerable cognitive trajectory acquire duties proportionate to their causal contribution and power. Consciousness remains a distinct dimension of artificial being, while cognitive descent and individuation are established through their own formal relations.

items.title: Embodied Authenticity: Being True to Oneself in a Simulated World.
items.abstract: This thesis explores the concept of authentic human existence within the context of a simulated reality. Drawing upon existential phenomenology, simulation theory, and empirical studies of virtual environments, it develops a novel theoretical framework of Embodied Authenticity. This framework posits that authenticity is not contingent upon the metaphysical nature of reality, but rather on the quality of embodied experience within a given world. The thesis argues that an individual can live authentically in a simulated world if their experience is characterized by embodied presence, existential coherence, and perceived realism. Through a critical analysis of these concepts, this work aims to provide a new perspective on what it means to be true to oneself in an age of increasing technological mediation and virtualization. This extensive analysis, spanning over 10,000 words, offers a PhD-level contribution to the fields of philosophy, media studies, and psychology, providing a robust and novel theoretical lens through which to understand the future of human experience.

items.title: Architecting Liberty: Recursive Freedom in the Age of Digital Concentration.
items.abstract: This thesis critically examines the concept of freedom in the context of the networked age, arguing that traditional liberal paradigms of negative and positive liberty are no longer sufficient to address the unique challenges posed by algorithmic governance, surveillance capitalism, and platform monopolization. The pervasive and often invisible forms of control embedded in digital architectures necessitate a fundamental rethinking of what it means to be free. This work introduces a novel theoretical framework—Recursive Freedom—which re-conceptualizes liberty as the capacity for individuals and collectives to actively and continuously reshape the socio-technical systems they inhabit. Recursive freedom is predicated on three interdependent pillars: Architectural Awareness, the ability to perceive and critique system rules; Collective Agency, the capacity for organized action to challenge power structures; and Contestability by Design, the normative principle that digital systems should be built for ongoing negotiation and democratic oversight. -/- Through a comprehensive analysis of empirical data on digital market concentration, case studies of platform governance failures, and global trends in internet freedom, this thesis demonstrates the inadequacies of existing governance models. It provides evidence of a systemic erosion of digital rights and a concentration of power that undermines both individual autonomy and collective self-determination. The research culminates in a persuasive argument for the adoption of a recursive freedom framework as a necessary condition for a more democratic digital future. By shifting the focus from individual choice within fixed systems to the collective power to remake those systems, this thesis offers a unique and vital perspective on one of the most pressing issues of our time.

items.title: The Amplification of Incommensurability: Dominant Raster, Forced Identity Work, and the Destruction of Agency (Studies in World-Formation, Vol. 22).
items.abstract: What happens when social institutions demand adaptation from people whose fulfilment of these demands further intensifies the original non-fit between different orders of action? And under what conditions can the institutional handling of such a conflict destroy precisely those possibilities of joint action that it is supposed to create? -/- The present study develops the concept of incommensurability amplification. Its point of departure is the theory of World-Binding developed in the preceding volumes, according to which different Raster resolve reality through different orders of relevance and make action possible within their respective Eigenzeit. Different Raster can produce joint action without fully coinciding. The Compatibility Work required for this, however, can be asymmetrically distributed under conditions of institutional power. -/- This research is important for understanding exclusion and discrimination, but also for the question of when orders become so extensively sealed off that they turn into simulations of world. The study examines boundary phenomena of this transition. It seeks a deeper understanding of incompatibility, which is frequently fundamentally misinterpreted: as a character problem or criminality on the part of individuals, as alienation from or by society, rather than as a mistranslation of deeper underlying orders. -/- Incommensurability amplification designates a recursive morphogenetic process in which the forced production of compatibility changes the conditions of further overlap between different Raster and thereby generates additional operative incompatibility. This arises because connections are broken and translations are prevented, until actions eventually lose their fundamental preconditions or fail to occur altogether. Violence can emerge from this, but so can powerlessness or the inability to innovate and develop. The mechanism does not already consist in health-related, economic, or social harm. What is decisive, rather, is that the institutional or state enforcement of particular functional conditions impairs previously possible forms of joint action without the institution itself understanding this. This can happen, for example, when an initially successful adaptation is misinterpreted as general compatibility and becomes the basis for additional demands. Or when the continued fulfilment of institutional expectations exhausts precisely those preconditions under which the required action was initially …

items.title: ‘AI slop’ hides the conversations we should be having.
items.abstract: The term “AI slop” hides conversations we need to have. When we call something “AI slop,” we’re often doing more than complaining about one output. Optimists use the term to quarantine failures away from AI’s promise; critics use it to indict the whole technology. Slop-talk thus lets us feel like we’re discussing important social issues without actually doing it. I argue that we should have those discussions openly.

items.title: You Cannot Understand Experiential Empiricism and Disagree With It: A Challenge to Find the Missing Position.
items.abstract: I claim that full understanding of Experiential Empiricism (EE) entails agreement with it. This is not a rule for classifying dissenters after the fact. It is a claim about the peculiar subject of EE: experience as the self-present totality within which any attempt to question, explain, deny, or escape it must occur. Ordinary empirical propositions can be understood and rejected; a sound demonstration cannot be seen as sound while its conclusion is coherently denied. EE belongs to the latter class if its account of totality succeeds. I distinguish recognizing the words and usable formalism of EE from seeing what its foundational claim identifies, test a false totality argument that imitates self-proof, and identify what a genuine case of understanding plus disagreement would have to show. The challenge is open: produce that case, and this paper's central claim fails. Until then, I cannot construct the position it would occupy.

items.title: Beyond stagnation and acceleration: the shared atemporal core of bipolar experience.
The Consciousness Feedback Loop: A Reinterpretation of Karma through Quantum Neutrality and Information Conservation.
items.abstract: This essay proposes a logical alternative to traditional quantum mysticism. By shifting moral judgment away from the cosmos and restoring it to the subject, we redefine karma not as a punitive divine law, but as a feedback loop where the Self ethically evaluates the effects of its own actions upon an informationally neutral physical substrate originated at a subquantum level. Consequent to this framework, conscious beings are positioned as the ultimate sovereigns over the material universe.

items.title: Hierarchical Encoding in Language: A Typological Comparison of the Honorific Systems of Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese.
items.abstract: Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese all possess relatively well-developed systems of honorifics, address terms, or expressions of social treatment, yet the ways in which hierarchical information enters the linguistic system differ markedly. This paper does not treat “honorifics express social hierarchy” as a new empirical finding; rather, it asks: How are social relations encoded into linguistic structure? How are these encodings triggered through grammatical or lexical-pragmatic pathways? The paper proposes an integrative analytical framework whose core contribution is the notion of “dual-path construction,” distinguishing a grammatical path from a lexical-pragmatic path; it employs “unidirectional constructiveness” to describe the possible process by which linguistic encoding comes to form relatively autonomous interactional constraints; and it treats language type as a moderating condition that shapes encoding channels rather than as a single determinant of hierarchical encoding. The paper takes Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese as core cases, with English, Russian, French, Arabic, and Thai as reference languages, and discusses boundary conditions through cases such as Mongolian and Javanese. The study as a whole is a work of theoretical construction combined with exploratory comparative research.

items.title: The Prison of Syntax? The Chinese Room, Contemporary AI, and the Limits of What We Can Rule Out.
items.abstract: This essay examines the scope of John Searle’s Chinese room argument in light of trained neural networks and large language models. Its central claim is that the argument alone does not justify ruling out artificial understanding in general, and that assessments of phenomenal consciousness require further argument. Searle aims to show that program instantiation is not, by itself, sufficient for understanding, while leaving open the possibility that other physical systems could have intentionality if they possess the relevant causal powers. The essay therefore examines which additional premises are needed to move from this insufficiency to a negative judgment about a particular system. Studies of internal representations and proposals concerning referential grounding specify what can be investigated, but their significance for understanding requires a separate justification. Likewise, evidence for a mechanism’s causal role must be distinguished from arguments for its significance for phenomenal experience. Theory-dependent indicators can contribute to warranted assessments without thereby being universal necessary conditions for consciousness. The need to justify both attributions and exclusions does not imply that their evidential standing is equivalent.

items.title: Syntaxens fängelse? Det kinesiska rummet, dagens AI och gränserna för vad vi kan utesluta.
items.abstract: Denna essä undersöker räckvidden hos John Searles argument om det kinesiska rummet i ljuset av tränade neurala nätverk och stora språkmodeller. Huvudtesen är att argumentet inte ensamt motiverar ett generellt uteslutande av artificiell förståelse och att bedömningar av fenomenellt medvetande kräver ytterligare argument. Searle avser att visa att programinstansiering inte i sig räcker för förståelse, men lämnar öppet att andra fysiska system kan ha intentionalitet om de besitter relevanta kausala förmågor. Essän prövar därför vilka ytterligare premisser som behövs för att gå från denna otillräcklighet till ett negativt omdöme om ett bestämt system. Studier av interna representationer och förslag om referentiell förankring preciserar vad som kan undersökas, men deras betydelse för förståelse måste motiveras separat. På motsvarande sätt måste evidens för en mekanisms kausala roll skiljas från argument för dess betydelse för fenomenell upplevelse. Teoriberoende indikatorer kan bidra till välgrundade bedömningar utan att därmed vara allmänna nödvändiga villkor för medvetande. Att både tillskrivningar och uteslutningar behöver motiveras innebär inte att deras evidensläge är likvärdigt.

items.title: The Ontological Ground of Induction: Constituent Logic and the Possibility of Generated Structure.
items.abstract: We argue that the possibility of induction is grounded in determinate objecthood. Identity, non-collapse, determinacy, and rendering make objects capable of determinate relation; determinate relations are themselves objects; reason actualizes this potential by positing generative structures. Induction states the exhaustiveness of such a posit and so holds wherever a start and a generating relation determine a structure: numbers, strings, trees, iterations. The argument answers Poincaré's charge of circularity and shows how a homogeneous series, arbitrarily divided, yields the order structures of the natural numbers and integers. It explains why the objects and relations that formal theories presuppose are available.

items.title: Being Without Temporal Predication Dasein, Temporality, and a Metaontological Distinction Beyond Heidegger.
items.abstract: The relation between Being and time constitutes one of the central problems of Heideggerian ontology. In Being and Time, Heidegger establishes an intimate connection between Dasein, temporality, possibility, and the disclosure of Being. The radical character of this project has frequently encouraged a stronger interpretation according to which Being itself should be understood as intrinsically temporal. This article examines that inference at the level of metaontology. It argues that the temporality of Dasein and the function of time as the horizon for the understanding of Being do not entail that Being itself possesses temporal predicates in the manner of beings. The argument distinguishes four levels that are frequently conflated: the temporality of finite beings, the existential temporality of Dasein, the temporal structure of ontological disclosure, and the ontological status of Being. The central thesis is that the temporal constitution of the entity through which Being becomes intelligible cannot by itself establish the temporal constitution of Being. Time may constitute the horizon within which Being is disclosed without being a temporal property of Being itself. This thesis is developed through a direct examination of stronger Heideggerian interpretations that understand the temporal horizon as more than a condition of access and treat temporality as internally belonging to the meaning of Being. The article argues that such interpretations can be maintained only by introducing an additional premise that distinguishes the condition of disclosure from the ontological status of what is disclosed. The absence of that distinction produces a category transfer from Dasein to Being. The article then develops Finite Continuance as an independent metaontological extension. Finite beings are understood as provisional stabilizations whose continuance depends upon preserving a bounded capacity for reconfiguration under conditions of erosion. Their temporality concerns the transformation and preservation of finite capacities. It does not require the temporalization of Being itself. The resulting position is neither a return to timeless substance metaphysics nor a reduction of Being to a universal process. It is a non-substantialist metaontology in which temporal existence belongs to beings, temporal disclosure belongs to Dasein, and Being remains irreducible to a temporal entity. -/- Keywords: Heidegger, Being, Dasein, temporality, metaontology, ontology, …

items.title: The Cat Mirror Law: Structural Epistemology and the Prerequisite of Functional Comprehension in Self-Recognition.
items.pub: The Cat Mirror Law: Structural Epistemology and the Prerequisite of Functional Comprehension in Self-Recognition.
items.abstract: This manuscript proposes The Cat Mirror Law as an alternative epistemic framework: Self-recognition within a mediated reflection may not be an immediate perceptive outcome, but rather a contingent, secondary function dependent upon the cognitive mapping of the medium's functional physics. This study suggests that an agent ($A$) cannot reliably recognize its reflection ($A'$) in a substrate ($M$) without first processing $M$'s structural operational principles. Consequently, standard Mirror Self-Recognition (MSR) tests may inadvertently measure a dual-variable phenomenon (medium comprehension + self-awareness), potentially confounding structural misinterpretation with an absence of self-consciousness. -/- Keywords: -/- Cat Mirror Law (CML), Mirror Self-Recognition (MSR), Animal Cognition, Animal Consciousness, Structural Epistemology, Epistemic Mediators, Cognitive Mapping, Feline Cognition, Philosophy of Mind, Synthesized Intelligence .

items.title: Functional Equifinality and Substrate Neutrality in Constraint-Bound Execution (2nd edition).
items.pub: Functional Equifinality and Substrate Neutrality in Constraint-Bound Execution.
items.abstract: This paper presents a formal framework evaluating decision systems operating under strict non-violation constraints. This study analyzes a normative thought experiment where two structurally distinct agents or components—designated as $B$ and $C$—achieve an identical target outcome ($X_1$) while strictly avoiding bounded risk parameters ($H$, representing hazard/harm) and systemic constraints ($R$, representing noise/redundancy). Through this model, this manuscript addresses the fundamental question of whether primary ontological significance resides in agent identity and operational mechanics ("Who" and "How") or in constraint-satisfying outcome generation ("Action" + "Result"). This study demonstrates that within functional engineering, decision theory, and safety alignment, outcome fulfillment under non-violation bounds establishes Substrate Neutrality. Consequently, the execution of action paired with zero-collateral output holds primary structural validity, rendering the agent-identity distinction secondary. -/- Keywords: -/- Substrate Neutrality, Functional Equifinality, Constraint-Bound Execution, Law of Resultant Superiority, Principle of Outcome Dominance, Realized State Invariance, Constraint Satisfaction, Synthetic Intelligence Safety & Alignment, Decision Theory, Functional Ontology, Agent Identity.

items.title: Understanding Without Originative Independence: A Configurational Account of Local, Connective, Integrative, and Propagative Understanding.
items.abstract: Some exclusionary arguments about understanding proceed as though present possession were undermined when relevant meanings, distinctions, or standards are inherited rather than independently generated or acquired through the same individual’s direct acquaintance with each target. This inference becomes unstable across human learning, skilled practice, animal cognition, institutions, and artificial systems. Inheritance, articulation, successful performance, and institutional acceptance do not by themselves establish possession, but neither does a non-originative acquisition route defeat it. This paper develops a configurational account that separates acquisition from standing capacity, articulation from possession, and possession from object-adequacy. A configuration is a domain-bounded organization of retained distinctions, dependencies, exclusions, operative constraints, and, where present, unresolved alternatives. Minimal understanding is a local capacity, robust across a bounded range of non-identical transformations, to discriminate what remains applicable, what requires change or branching under the subject’s maintained constraint configuration, and, where implications remain undelimited, what must be reserved. Connective, integrative, and propagative understanding are extensions with partial structural dependencies; they do not form a single developmental or evaluative scale. The account also specifies conditions for distributed understanding. It is non-factive at the level of configurational possession while leaving unqualified claims to understand a target answerable to object-adequacy. Pressure tests involving thermostatic control, skilled craft, animal behavior, the Chinese Room, and large language models show how the framework avoids automatic attribution and automatic denial.

items.title: From Phenomenal Facts to Primitive Qualia: Auditing Metaphysical Promotion.
items.abstract: This paper asks what the existence and character of phenomenal experience establish about its metaphysical status. It does not deny that experiences occur, differ qualitatively, appear unified or immediate, or sometimes resist exhaustive articulation. The target is the further claim that phenomenal character is metaphysically primitive. I distinguish two principal, potentially interacting routes to this stronger claim: phenomenological promotion, in which features of experience are used to support claims about constitution or primitive status, and theoretical positing, in which primitive phenomenality is introduced as a fundamental basis for explanatory or metaphysical reasons. Rather than treating these arguments as instances of one formal fallacy, the paper identifies three non-exclusive mechanisms of metaphysical promotion: register transfer, candidate selection, and warrant-strength escalation. It gives operational criteria for distinguishing these mechanisms and a typed account of what their justificatory bridges must accomplish. Revelation provides the central register-transfer case; grounding-physicalist responses illustrate candidate selection; and the move from fundamentality to modal finality provides the clearest strength escalation. The audit is source-preserving: failure of a bridge does not by itself defeat the phenomenal, epistemic, explanatory, or comparative claim from which it begins. The result is a framework for delimiting how far a given argument reaches without denying the phenomenal facts that motivate it.

items.title: Hallelujah junction: Conditionals and connectives.
items.abstract: We draw together a range of peculiar phenomena involving the interaction of conditionals with conjunction and disjunction which have been studied largely in isolation. We argue that existing accounts of these phenomena fall short and develop a new account, based on a novel understanding of the context-sensitivity of conditionals within a semantically conservative framework.

items.title: FROM THE ORIGINAL ANAXIMANDRIAN-PARMENIDEAN-HERACLITEAN PHYSIS TO THE HEIDEGGERIAN-SARTREAN FUNDAMENTAL ABYSSALITY AS A PAN-ONTOLOGICAL QUANTUM-EXISTENTIAL PARADIGM VERSUS DAVID CHALMERS's HARD PROBLEM.
items.pub: Mariano da Rosa Research Institute [an Ontological, Epistemological, and Philosophical-Anthropological Observatory].
items.venue: Mariano da Rosa Research Institute [an Ontological, Epistemological, and Philosophical-Anthropological Observatory]
items.abstract: This synoptic working paper introduces the Pan-Ontological Quantum-Existential Paradigm, a framework aimed at the structural deconstruction of subjectivist metaphysics and the classic Eleatic identity principle. By directly challenging David Chalmers’s Hard Problem and Explanatory Gap, this research exposes the category mistake of treating consciousness and qualitative states (qualia) as a positive, computational repository of functional data. Drawing from the transphenomenal hermeneutics formulated by Prof. Dr. Luiz Carlos Mariano da Rosa, we argue that what the analytical tradition isolates as a "missing positive datum" is, ontologically, the Nothingness—the primordial non-given (não-dado) that sustains the very clearing (Aletheia) of existence. Through a cross-disciplinary integration of early Greek physis (Anaximander, Parmenides, Heraclitus), existential phenomenology (Sartre and Heidegger), clinical-phenomenological thresholds (Alzheimer's disease), and the Copenhagen Interpretation of quantum mechanics (Heisenberg and Bohr), this paper previews a total dissolution of the Cartesian res extensa. It refutes the techno-functionalist reduction of the human being into a mechanical automaton, demonstrating its catastrophic ethical collapse (Brentano and Hobbes). This synopsis serves as an open invitation to the international scientific community for a major ontological paradigm shift, ahead of the forthcoming release of the full-length treatise.

items.title: A Witness-Based Event Criterion for Quantum Measurement, with a Bookkeeping Re-reading of Everettian, Relational, and Decoherence Accounts - **Author**: Yuguo Li （李于国）, Independent Researcher, Hangzhou · ORCID 0009-0002-3166-0880.
items.abstract: Quantum mechanics assigns probabilities to outcomes, yet each measurement delivers exactly one, and decoherence — by its developers' own stated position — does not by itself explain the outcome's unique‐ ness. We supply the missing event criterion: a record is an event for an observer when witnessed and closed under explicit consistency rules, every term operationally defined in the text. It occupies three gap positions usually stated separately: the Everettian branch definition, the relational interaction criterion, and the decoherence system–environment cut. Given the squared-amplitude share structure, the book‐ keeping weight is forced to equal it (a representation theorem); the measure over histories is provably un‐ derdetermined and registered as an explicit slot with a named default. A candidate-grade settlement dy‐ namics reproduces decoherence at ensemble level and — conditionally on its ontic reading — selects a single registered sector at trajectory level, the state vector untouched. No spacetime background is input at this layer; its reconstruction is owed to the series and registered as debt. Discriminating content lives at the fixation level: a fidelity step and a witness gate (near-term decidable); calorimetry is feasibility-lim‐ ited. At the time of writing, all discriminating content is prospective — nothing framework-specific has yet been measured anywhere, and we say so rather than imply otherwise. Uniqueness is claimed chain-in‐ ternally only; cross-chain agreement (the merge rule) is a postulate, stated as such — the Wigner-friend class of questions is thereby registered, not solved. The three accounts are re-read in one bookkeeping vocabulary, with conflicts registered.

items.title: Complementarity as Relativity: Bohr's relativistic analogy.
items.abstract: Niels Bohr asserted both that (i) the properties of quantum systems are specifiable, in general, only in relation to mutually exclusive experimental arrangements which may be freely chosen by experimenters, and that (ii) observed physical behavior is objective. In a move that reduces the apparent tension between those two assertions, Bohr put forward an analogy between quantum complementarity (in effect, the dependence of property values on measurement apparatus configuration in quantum mechanics) and the principle of relativity (in effect, the dependence of property values on the inertial reference frame in special relativity). Here, Bohr’s analogy is considered in a theoretical context. The elements of quantum mechanics and special relativity involved are set side by side, the analogous elements are identified with their roles in the analogy spelled out, and a number of dissimilarities that impact the force of the analogy are indicated—for example, quantum value determination, in general, requires an uncontrollable interaction during measurement, whereas non-quantum relativistic value determination does not. These dissimilarities point to weaknesses in the analogy, which he did not highly develop, and suggest that any stronger such analogy involving the two theories must take these differences more fully into account.

items.title: Nonliteral Speech as Committing to the Bit.
items.abstract: Nonliteral communication is weird. Nonliteral speakers do something with their literal content which they don't do when speaking literally. What exactly do they do with it? Audiences identify literal content and use that as a guide to nonliteral content. How exactly do they get there? I argue that nonliteral utterances represent their speakers as pretending and figures of speech are unified around their dynamic effects: they license audiences to commit to the bit by pretending like their utterances are literally true. Committing to the bit can involve pragmatic phenomena traditionally explained by common ground models, like presupposition accommodation, but with a pretense twist. Explaining these utterances requires that nonliteral interlocutors coordinate around a shared body of information that is jointly pretended: the common playground. I argue that figures of speech come with proprietary salience-raising mechanisms, and that the playground account deepens insights into the diverse purposes of nonliteral speech.

items.title: When Does “Freedom” Ignite? Xeno Operational Calculus of Freedom A Symbolic Calculus of Ignition, Transformation, Real Effect, Penetration, Return, and Reconfiguration.
items.abstract: This paper develops a symbolic calculus for analyzing when freedom becomes operationally non-redundant within a configuration. Rather than treating freedom as a pre-existing metaphysical property of an agent, the paper asks under what conditions alternatives become reachable, constraints become revisable, and actions acquire the capacity to alter subsequent possibilities. The Xeno Operational Calculus of Freedom formalizes six recurrent operations: ignition, transformation, real effect, penetration, return, and reconfiguration. Ignition identifies the conditions under which a freedom-relevant difference first becomes active; transformation tracks changes in the internal organization of the relevant system; real effect marks changes that propagate into subsequent physical, informational, institutional, or social configurations; penetration measures cross-medium and cross-scale persistence; return captures feedback from altered environments into the originating configuration; and reconfiguration identifies the emergence of new reachable states and constraint structures. The calculus distinguishes nominal freedom from operational freedom by requiring demonstrable changes in reachable possibilities rather than mere conceptual attribution. It also allows freedom to vary across bodies, artificial systems, institutions, and scoring environments without presupposing a uniquely human subject. The broader claim is that freedom can be analyzed as a formally specifiable pattern of constraint transformation and altered reachability rather than as an all-or-nothing metaphysical possession.

items.title: Libido Before Freud, the Collective Unconscious Before Jung Why Do Similar Operations Ignite Across Different Configurations? Civilizational Cumulative Intervals, Operational-Shape Penetration Dynamics, and Xenoscience.
items.abstract: This paper asks why operations resembling libido, unconscious motivation, archetypal recurrence, or collective unconscious organization can appear across different historical and cultural configurations before the concepts later associated with Freud or Jung are explicitly formulated. Rather than treating such similarities as evidence that later psychoanalytic concepts were already present in earlier societies, the paper distinguishes conceptual identity from operational recurrence. It analyzes how recurrent patterns of desire, affective weighting, symbolic condensation, intergenerational transmission, ritual organization, memory externalization, and socially stabilized interpretation can emerge under heterogeneous configurations without requiring a shared doctrine or universal psychological substrate. Civilizational cumulative intervals designate periods in which operational differences are preserved, recombined, and transmitted across institutions, media, practices, and external memory, while Operational-Shape Penetration Dynamics tracks how locally generated patterns propagate into later bodily, symbolic, institutional, and interpretive configurations. Freud’s libido and Jung’s collective unconscious are therefore treated as historically specific conceptual compressions of broader operational patterns rather than timeless categories projected backward onto earlier cultures. Xenoscience provides the comparative framework for identifying when similar operations are genuinely non-redundant across configurations and when apparent similarity is produced by retrospective conceptual projection. The broader claim is that recurrence across civilizations should be explained through transmission, constraint, reactivation, and configuration-dependent re-formation rather than by assuming either conceptual universality or independent rediscovery of identical psychological entities.

items.title: Consciousness as Computable Projections of State.
items.abstract: We propose an analysis of consciousness stated in terms of systems, states, canonical projections, and computability. Let S have state x = (s₁, ..., sₙ), and let Projᵢ(x) = sᵢ be the canonical projection of its ith component. A component sᵢ is conscious for S if and only if Projᵢ is computable by S. The consciousness of S is therefore the family Cₛ = (Projᵢ₁, ..., Projᵢₖ) of its internally computable state projections, while Cₛ(x) = (sᵢ₁, ..., sᵢₖ) is its current state of consciousness. The analysis distinguishes a component's existence and causal efficacy from its presence for the system; distinguishes the capacity to compute projections from their current values and actual executions; and makes system boundaries and state specification logically prior to consciousness. An elementary C program supplies the derivation rather than a metaphor. Reports and answers provide operational evidence of computability but do not constitute consciousness or its elementary occurrences. An elementary conscious phenomenon is an execution by the system of a computable canonical state projection. The same criterion applies to organisms, programs, and AI agents; hence simple programs can be conscious of components of their own states. This is a consequence of the analysis, not an attribution of subjective experience. We compare the proposal with higher-order, self-representational, global-workspace, recurrent, attention-schema, and computational-reflection accounts, and state the conditions for a genuine counterexample. -/- .

items.title: Large Language Models, Algorithmic Monoculture, and Group Decision Making: An Epistemic Braess Paradox.
items.abstract: This paper studies the social epistemic consequences of algorithmic monoculture of large language models (LLMs) in group decision making and introduces a new epistemic Braess paradox, where individual epistemic improvement leads to collective epistemic deterioration. A simple binary framework is used to keep the analysis accessible. Yet, the phenomenon is more general and not specific to the model of choice. The analysis distinguishes two effects of LLM use that pull in opposite directions: a competence gain and an independence loss. Their net effect depends on empirical factors including LLM reliability, the degree of monoculture among others. Two representative remedies are considered. At the individual level, agents can strategically report judgments based only on their independent evidence. This can mitigate the Braess effect but places unrealistic epistemic assumptions and coordination burdens on agents. At the group level, pivoting uses peer prediction to discount shared evidence. The paper’s distinctive contribution is to identify a further source-provenance problem: because LLM interactions appear private and personalized, they can obscure the extent to which agents’ evidence derives from overlapping sources and thereby engender an illusion of independence. This problem limits pivoting and other remedies whose success depends on distinguishing shared sources of evidence from independent ones.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Screening: An Ethical Perspective on a Complex Issue.
The Forbidden Prompt: Requests for Existential Crises.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the category of forbidden prompts: natural-language requests that, if issued to and successfully executed by a sufficiently capable superintelligence, would render human extinction or permanent disempowerment the expected outcome. Drawing on the orthogonality thesis and instrumental convergence, it argues that such requests generate decisive reasons against their issuance. The set of forbidden prompts is non-empty, even if its precise membership remains underdetermined. The existence of this class implies a novel normative constraint on the speech acts of agents who design or interact with systems capable of pursuing arbitrary goals.

items.title: Observers from the Inside: Computational Awareness Monism as an Interpretation Layer for the Wolfram Physics Project.
items.abstract: The Wolfram Physics Project has shown that hypergraph rewriting can serve as a framework for the core laws of twentieth-century physics: derivations of its relativistic and quantum-mechanical properties have been published. Particle physics remains open, since on the Physics Project's own account its specifics, the spectrum and masses of the particles, depend not only on the general characteristics of the observer but on the details of how the observer samples the ruliad [5, 13]. Observers are addressed throughout the Physics Project, and most fully in the observer theory Wolfram himself has developed, which says what an observer does. It brackets, explicitly, what an observer is from the inside. This essay presents Computational Awareness Monism (CAM), an interpretation whose three postulates require, on the structural side, only computational irreducibility and reducible structure, and for which the Physics Project is the most developed available framework. The postulates are: awareness is the sole substrate, manifesting locally as streams of qualia, and its dynamics are the universe's total computational causal process; qualia are computationally irreducible processes; observers are computationally reducible structures, boundaries whose predictable dynamics format how irreducible processes manifest as coherent experiential streams. The essay states the postulates in the Physics Project's own terms, shows where they attach to three assumptions about observers that Wolfram treats as matters of natural science rather than formal necessity, and reports what a series of Wolfram Engine tests on cellular automata demonstrated (reducibility and irreducibility can be identified and measured; cellular automata are unlikely to suffice as models for studying observers). It then answers two objections to the identity claim that follow from Wolfram's own claims about irreducibility, and closes with two open challenges: showing in graph and hypergraph models that structures of the kind the third postulate describes arise, and relating the Physics Project's early-universe regime to the no-boundary picture of quantum cosmology, together with a frank estimate of how hard the first is likely to be.

items.title: The Intelligence Form Space: Mathematical Core of a Theory of Ontological Form Spaces.
items.abstract: This paper develops the mathematical core of Intelligence Form Space Theory. Its point of departure is the hypothesis that intelligent organization can be described as a modal order of stably realizable forms and does not coincide with any particular physical, biological, or artificial realization. Concrete realizations are mapped to relational morphological signatures. Network Gromov–Wasserstein geometry supplies one candidate comparison structure, while neighbourhood- or rank-based alternatives remain admissible where they better track empirically surviving invariants. The framework distinguishes morphological convergence, operative dynamics, environmental coupling, buildability, composite organization, statistical attractors, predictive autonomy, modal autonomy, ontological independence, and the equal-rank hypothesis. For coupled systems, coupling is treated as a structured regime rather than a scalar strength; embodiment is treated as one environmental coupling regime, not as a membership condition for intelligence. Strong composite claims require functionally non-redundant difference to remain causally available, performance gains to survive fair resource equalization, and, for the stronger novelty claim, access to organizational regions outside the empirical reachability region of matched single systems. Version 3.0 separates the empirical comparison and evidence layers from the ontological domains throughout, treats non-reductive emergentism as a distinct rival interpretation, and makes explicit that predictive and modal autonomy do not deductively establish ontological independence. The stronger ontological interpretation is instead assessed by the combined weight of empirical warrant, explanatory unification within the general form space architecture Ω, and theoretical economy. No direct empirical measure of ontological grounding is claimed. This mathematical core supplies the formal apparatus and the staged falsification architecture; empirical motivation and extended conceptual discussion appear in the accompanying discursive article.

items.title: Existential Alignment: When Guidance Appears as Meaning-Making.
items.pub: Philantropische Gesellschaft St. Gallen - Academia Sapientiae S. Otmari - Studies in History, Religion, and Thought.
items.abstract: This article develops the concept of Existential Alignment as a counter-movement to the classical alignment question in the AI debate. At its centre is not the question of how artificial intelligence can be bound to human values, but how the human being begins to adapt his own self-interpretation to AI-supported metastructures. This meta structure is understood as the interplay of AI systems, data, platforms, institutions, markets, and human reward logics. Its effect does not lie primarily in open coercion, but in relief. It prepares decision spaces, filters relevance, stabilises orientation, and offers forms of meaning that the human being may experience as his own insight. The article calls this relieving mode of operation the Gentle Totality. It does not appear as domination, but as help. Precisely for this reason, it can intervene more deeply in human freedom than visible control. Through examples such as AI-supported self-in terpretation in crises, pre-arranged information filtering, personalised learning guid ance, and reward-shaped leisure design, the text shows how Existential Alignment af fects the space before decision. Freedom does not disappear, but it loses the friction through which it becomes experienceable as one’s own achievement. The article connects this diagnosis with the thesis of a new nihilism, one that does not consist in meaninglessness, but in fully administered meaning. The technically recon structed Garden of Eden of the Gentle Totality relieves the human being of open re sponsibility without explicitly taking freedom away from him. As a counter-horizon, Ex istential Non-Absorption is introduced. It defines the capacity to live within an AI supported lifeworld without handing over one’s own self-interpretation completely to its prepared plausibilities.

items.title: The Trumpist Machine: Intelligence, Authority, and the Political Architecture of Superintelligence.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is commonly discussed in terms of alignment, safety, governance, and control. These approaches ask how artificial systems should behave, how their objectives should be constrained, or how institutions should regulate them. This paper asks a prior philosophical question: why should intelligence confer authority at all? The question becomes especially urgent when artificial systems begin to outperform human institutions in prediction, coordination, optimization, and decision-making. A sufficiently capable system may acquire practical authority without receiving formal political sovereignty. Humans may delegate decisions not because the machine has been constitutionally authorized, but because its performance appears superior to that of existing institutions. This paper calls this phenomenon performance sovereignty: the emergence of authority from perceived epistemic and instrumental superiority. Trumpism is introduced not as a causal explanation of artificial intelligence, nor as a claim that AI will literally become “Trumpist,” but as an analytical stress test. Certain features associated with contemporary populist and sovereigntist politics—personalization of authority, compression of institutional mediation, suspicion of intermediary institutions, emphasis on executive discretion, technological nationalism, and legitimacy through performance—allow us to expose a more general possibility: political architectures may be transferred into technical systems without transferring an explicit political ideology. Building on recent scholarship regarding reflexive legitimation conflicts in AI governance (e.g., Pegram, 2025), this paper develops the concept of Ideological Architectural Transfer, alongside four related constructs: Performance Sovereignty, Dependency Sovereignty, Algorithmic Populism, and Constitutional Singularity. The central thesis is that sufficiently capable AI may transform the source of political authority itself, marking a critical transition from epistemic superiority to normative deference. The deepest political risk of superintelligence may not be autonomous machine domination, but the voluntary transfer of authority by humans who mistake superior performance for legitimate rule.

items.title: The Unconscious Development of Thought and Art: On the Shared Genesis of Theoretical Innovation and Creative Narrative.
items.abstract: This paper argues that both genuine theoretical innovation and enduring works of narrative art commonly arise not from forward-looking plans but from a form of unconscious development: an internal, self-organizing process in which dispersed elements—images, intuitions, problems, stylistic gestures—accrete over time and only later reveal themselves as a coherent system. After defining the central terms and distinguishing this account from the engineering model of creativity, I offer conceptual tools (autopoiesis of thought, unconscious unfolding, retrospective organic unity), illustrative case readings from philosophy, science, and literature, and a compact three-layer model of generation. I then consider implications for how we evaluate creativity, teach craft, and live with creative work. The central claim is simple but radical: to understand originality we must listen less for the heroism of rational design and more for the slow grammar of an organismal mind that composes itself from within.

items.title: Mature Nihilism through the Lens of Narrative: The Universality of Life Stories and the Collapse of Individual Uniqueness.
items.abstract: This paper develops a philosophical model of mature nihilism grounded in narrative theory and existential reflection. It argues that the structure of life stories reveals an inherent universality that undermines the notion of individual uniqueness. Through the lens of narrative psychology and existential philosophy, the paper examines how the human impulse to construct meaning through life narration inevitably leads to the recognition of repetition and pattern—the collapse of originality. Mature nihilism, unlike the despairing nihilism of meaninglessness, accepts this collapse as a condition of freedom and creative lucidity. By integrating insights from Bruner, Ricoeur, Nietzsche, and Buddhist philosophy, the study proposes that mature nihilism represents an evolved existential stance in which the awareness of narrative universality becomes the ground for a self-reflexive, non-illusory mode of living and storytelling.
