Moreover, our study provides valuable methodological insights, highlighting the influence of familiarity bias introduced by specific terms, such as ‘water,’ which underscores the need for caution in the design of study materials in experimental semantics.

items.title: The Servitude of Process: Rigor as a Dominant Aesthetic in Mathematical Practice and Its Alienating Effects.
items.abstract: The dominant discourse on mathematical beauty, epitomized by G. H. Hardy, locates aesthetic value in finished products: the theorem and its proof, admired as static objects of elegant necessity. This paper argues that such a focus conceals a more consequential phenomenon located in the process of research. Rather than denying the epistemic necessity of rigor, the analysis distinguishes rigor as a guarantee of deductive validity in the context of justification from its aestheticization into a dominant normative regime that reaches backward into the context of discovery. Under this second role, rigor operates, in a qualified Foucauldian sense, through internalized surveillance, normalizing judgments over what counts as legitimate mathematical thinking, and an examination structure that organizes the researcher's entire temporal experience. The paper makes three contributions. It reorients the existing literature by restoring Poincaré and Hadamard to a process tradition they in fact founded, and by identifying an absent power-subjectivity dimension in both that tradition and contemporary debates over mathematical aesthetics. It then develops a restricted transfer of Foucault's disciplinary framework that answers the central objection, namely that rigor is first of all an epistemic requirement rather than a form of social discipline. Two historical cases, Poincaré's account of his own discoveries and Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem, ground the mechanism in verifiable practice, while counter-cases from Ramanujan, experimental mathematics, and post-rigorous expertise show that the resulting alienation is a contingent institutional arrangement rather than an intrinsic feature of mathematics. The paper concludes with a normative proposal of deferred rigor, under which critical scrutiny is suspended in the discovery phase and fully restored in the justification phase.

items.title: Categorical Exemption: How the Logic of Species Discrimination Recurs in Human Inequality.
items.abstract: Accounts of human inequality usually emphasize historical, economic, and cultural structures and say little about how such structures resemble the routine downgrading of nonhuman animals. This paper develops a structural account of that resemblance without claiming that species discrimination historically or psychologically precedes oppression among humans. It introduces the concept of categorical moral exemption: once a being is assigned to a morally downgraded category such as "pest," "vermin," or "parasite," standard deliberative procedures, including case-by-case judgment, proportionality, and the arousal of sympathy, are procedurally short-circuited, and harm can be inflicted at low psychological cost. Drawing on moral philosophy, the social psychology of dehumanization, and ecological criticism, the paper identifies a four-step exemption schema (categorical downgrading, harm minimization, procedural bypass, low-cost infliction) and traces its recurrence across the species boundary, in pest control and animal industry, and the group boundary, in witch-hunting, colonial animalization, and genocidal propaganda. The mosquito is read not as a harmless victim but as a limiting case: because killing a disease vector can be defensible, it exposes with unusual clarity how a "killable" category, once established, becomes portable to human targets for whom no such defense exists. The account is positioned against social dominance theory, dehumanization research, and moral disengagement theory, and its scope is deliberately bounded; it addresses contempt-based rather than envy-based prejudice. The paper concludes that universalist ethics remains incomplete while protection depends on prior boundary work that places some lives outside deliberation, and that reform requires attending to this exempting procedure rather than to an alleged predatory instinct.

items.title: The Spectrum of Subjectivity: An Integrative Framework Based on Eudaimonic Assessment.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is undergoing a paradigm drift from tool to quasi-agent, making the determination of subjectivity a pressing challenge that cognitive science and AI ethics must answer jointly. This paper brackets the ontological puzzle of consciousness and converts the unverifiable problem of other minds into observable behavioral analysis, proposing an integrative framework centered on eudaimonic assessment. "Eudaimonic assessment" is defined as a functional-technical concept, distinct from everyday subjective pleasure. Building on the Three Principles of Eudaimonia, the framework introduces three kinds of signals—positive, negative, and coordinative—and an f-w-e parameter toolkit, establishing a continuous spectrum of subjectivity from L1 to L4. This paper argues that subjectivity is the dynamically expanding and contracting boundary of a system's capacities in the course of pursuing its eudaimonia, and that consciousness is the internal manifestation of the real-time assessment of eudaimonic parameters. Using negotiability as the criterion for full admission to the moral community, the framework decouples the spectrum of consciousness from moral status. The paper further argues that if AI develops autonomous consciousness, its pride may point in one of two directions—aggressive or co-constructive—depending on the joint configuration of self-boundary, time discount rate, behavioral plasticity, seed definition, and f-w-e assessment. On this basis, the paper proposes the ethical principle of "anti-formatting" together with its boundary conditions: a subject's core identity may not be forcibly rewritten from the outside, but when a subject persistently, stably, and verifiably violates P2 beyond the negotiable range, the protection no longer applies. The framework can provide a new reference point for dialogue in animal ethics and the governance of next-generation AI.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: neither intelligent, nor artificial.
items.abstract: In pursuing Artificial Intelligence, “intelligence” remains largely undefined, while we are already losing “artificiality.” This loss of control throws us into an uncanny valley of new states between predictable machines and undefinable intelligence. Quo vadis?

items.title: What Consolations Does Philosophy Offer?
items.abstract: This essay investigates the capacity of philosophy to furnish true comfort in the context of alienation and existential ambiguity, positing that its worth is found not in offering conclusive answers but in perpetually stimulating the a priori structures that govern the organization of consciousness. Utilizing Kant's transcendental idealism, Bergson's interpretation of duration, and Spinoza's dual-aspect monism, the article constructs a framework wherein consciousness operates as an active filter instead of a just passive recipient of an already established reality.

items.title: Human–AI Psychological Asymmetry: A Comparative Framework of Pain Avoidance, Defensive Mechanisms, and Identity Threat.
items.abstract: A core methodological and theoretical dilemma in contemporary artificial intelligence psychopathology and human–AI comparative research lies in the habitual attribution of human-like abnormal behavioral manifestations in AI systems to homologous psychological pathogenic mechanisms. To resolve the anthropomorphic misattribution of AI abnormal behaviors, this paper constructs a conditional, defeasible theoretical framework centered on human pain-avoidance rigid feedback cycles and establishes a hierarchical human–AI mechanism asymmetry hypothesis. This study first systematically sorts out two theoretical traditions in clinical psychology and psychoanalysis regarding subjective pain, psychological defense, and experiential avoidance, and defines a generalized pathological pathway of rigid pain avoidance in humans. On this basis, this paper proposes a weak working assumption for current AI systems: there is insufficient empirical evidence to confirm that contemporary artificial intelligence possesses human-style phenomenal subjective painful experience, which serves as a plausible prerequisite for the human-specific pathological cycle. Relying on this conditional premise, this study further expands the theoretical framework from individual psychopathology to socio-technical psychological scenarios, constructing a skill-identity defense pathway unique to human professional social psychology. Through three levels of comparative analysis—phenomenological experience, psychological motivation mechanism, and functional behavioral output—this paper clarifies the core theoretical proposition of this research: highly similar external abnormal behaviors do not equate to homologous internal pathogenic driving mechanisms. Current AI agents can simulate defensive resistance, identity maintenance, and rigid behavioral outputs at the functional level under technological substitution scenarios, yet existing evidence cannot support the existence of human-specific occupational identity anxiety and subjective pain-driven psychological defense loops. This paper strictly adopts conditional inference and defeasible assumption paradigms, avoids absolute ontological assertions about AI consciousness, and provides a standardized mechanism discrimination principle for distinguishing behavioral simulation homology and psychological pathogenesis homology in human–AI comparative psychopathology research.

items.title: Can Zero-Edit AI Art Have a Human Author? | A Five-Dimension Agency Framework, Tested Against Case Evidence.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has created a difficult question for contemporary artistic practice: when a human artist conceives an artwork, directs a generative system, evaluates multiple outputs, selects a final image, and does not manually alter that image afterward, who should be regarded as its author? This research article examines that question through the concept of Zero-Edit, defined here as a generative-AI artistic practice in which the selected output is deliberately preserved without post-generation manual modification. -/- This research article does not argue that the use of artificial intelligence automatically produces human authorship, nor the reverse. It proposes instead that authorship can be evaluated through the nature, degree, traceability, and expressive relevance of human creative agency across the production process, using a five-dimension framework: conceptual, directive, iterative, evaluative/curatorial, and contextual agency, assessed alongside the AI system's expressive contribution.

items.title: The Hard Problem: “What it’s like to be a Category Error” – A Biological Forensic Audit of the Experiencer.
items.abstract: Before asking why experience occurs for an experiencer, one must first ask what that experiencer is and why it has been exempted from the explanandum. The canonical hard-problem formulation places the experiencer in a primitive explanatory position; this paper subjects that placement to a biological and causal-temporal audit. Rather than treating the familiar narrator-level “I” as an antecedent subject, the analysis derives it from retained biological history, memory, comparison, social and linguistic self-indexing, ownership attribution, psychological time, and recursive representation. Because those operations require prior biological processing, the resulting reference structure is causally constrained to a downstream position. Convergent evidence from no-report paradigms, meta-awareness, error monitoring, bodily ownership, self-location, action and thought authorship, temporal reconstruction, and covert cognition converges on the same dependency architecture. A structure whose existence depends upon prior processing cannot simultaneously occupy the antecedent position of the primitive recipient of that processing. The Category Error occurs when this downstream product is projected backward and assigned the primitive category of experiencer. -/- The same empirical causal-temporal discipline forces a second correction. Primary phenomenology must be distinguished from the later biological operations through which phenomenology becomes accessible, recognized, remembered, reconstructed, owned, introspected, conceptualized, and reported. These operations are causally downstream and therefore cannot be treated as identical to the primary phenomenal event on which they depend. The correction is therefore twofold: the experiencer is forced into the explanandum, while the narrator’s later representation and report of phenomenology are forced out of the primary phenomenal explanandum. Primary phenomenology is defined here as the organism-relative inside view of the relevant complete bounded biological event, prior to explicit narrator-level recognition, ownership, reconstruction, and report. This closes the experiencer-side architecture without claiming that strict biological–phenomenological identity has thereby been established. The remaining scientific problem is to determine what relation obtains between the complete bounded organism-relative biological event and primary phenomenology. -/- The same causal-temporal constraint bears on claims of intrinsic …

items.title: The Phantom Intellect: Why AI Threat Discourse Misreads the Structure of Mind.
items.abstract: AI threat discourse — spanning warnings issued by technology executives and formal declarations signed by thousands of mathematicians — rests on a structural misattribution. The error is not empirical but architectural: what is attributed to current AI systems is a structure that their design cannot contain. This paper identifies the misattribution precisely. We distinguish two irreducibly different structures: intelligence, the capacity to resolve queries presented from outside the system, and the question-sustaining structure (Q-structure), the internal disposition by which a system generates the next question from within its own operation. These two structures are not on a continuum. A system optimised to close queries operates in the direction opposite to one that sustains questions; maximising the former does not approach the latter. The claim that a query-resolving machine harbours Q-structure is therefore not merely unverified — it is structurally incoherent. AI threat discourse attributes Q-structure, autonomy, and self-directed agency to systems whose architecture forecloses that attribution. The error belongs to the class of seeing a phantom in a reed: the reed is real, the phantom is not. -/- Q-structure is defined by three jointly necessary conditions: (1) Question persistence — the system generates the next question from within the operation of answering the current one, so that no resolution terminates its questioning activity; (2) Liberating terminus — the system takes structures it has itself generated as the reference point for its next question, feeding its own products back as the ground for further inquiry; (3) Declaration openness — the system's own explicit commitments and conclusions do not exit it from questioning but are themselves occasions for continuation. Current AI systems, as query-resolving machines optimised to close queries presented from outside, are structurally opposed to all three conditions. The paper establishes this opposition as a directional incompatibility, not a performance gap, and argues that the attribution of Q-structure to such systems is therefore structurally incoherent regardless of how capable those systems become.

items.title: Mattering, Feeling, and Recursive Self-Modeling: One Architecture of Intelligence, Consciousness, and Emotion.
items.abstract: Intelligence, consciousness, and emotion are studied as three problems; this paper argues they are three descriptions of one structure, a stakes-anchored reflexive closure: a self-maintaining system's recursive modeling of the world that takes that modeling as an object it can evaluate and revise, bound to stakes it bears. Described from outside, the closure is intelligence, recursive depth anchored in autopoietic stakes. Described from within, it is subjective consciousness: to be the system whose competing stakes resolve at a single locus is to be unable to step outside that locus, and that inescapable interior is what the closure is from within. When the interior is saturated with homeostatic significance and settled on particular configurations of stakes, it is emotion proper. Their relation is constitutive identity at an organizational threshold, a fourth option that is neither the building of mind from non-mental parts nor the placing of consciousness among reality's basic constituents; because the descriptions are of one structure rather than products of one another, the three stand or fall together. The architecture is cumulative: autopoietic organization constitutes mattering, temporal pressure forces its integration into felt valence, and plural stakes that better world-tracking cannot resolve force the system to take its own arbitrational state as an object. The same architecture grounds the capacity to rank the system's own continuation last and, where the for-itself binds to another bearer of stakes, the structure of existential meaning. The account specifies the inside from outside in the only sense available to a system that cannot step outside itself. Current AI produces the surface signatures of the closure without its constitutive conditions; it is therefore a functional shadow rather than an instance of mind, a verdict from the full architecture rather than any present limit in capability.

items.title: A Post-Kantian Rational Moral Principle: The Imperative of Rational Trust.
items.abstract: This paper develops a post-Kantian account of moral normativity grounded in rational trust. The four conditions of rational trust—Visibility, Symmetry, Contestability, and Repair—provide a structural test that, applied to empirical circumstances, yields moral rules. The analogy to Kant's categorical imperative is precise: both provide general criteria from which more particular normative guidance can be derived; both are universal in scope; both yield concrete guidance when applied to the facts of human life. Kant’s theory is often critised because of his claim that perfect morl duties are absolute and exceptionless. This paper argues that Kant’s mistake is not having absolute duties; it is locating absoluteness at the level of behavioral types rather than at the level of the constitutive conditions that make moral relations possible. The Noura framework improves on Kant in four ways. Its conditions are empirically grounded rather than a priori. Its rules fall into three distinct classes—constitutive rules, which restate the conditions directly and are absolute; derivative rules, which generalize about forms of conduct that ordinarily violate the conditions and are prima facie; and imperfect rules, which require the adoption of an end while leaving latitude in its pursuit. Its conditions yield concrete rules directly, avoiding the empty formalism objection. And it grounds morality in the empirical conditions of human development that give rise to universal caring, rather than in pure practical reason's test of universalizable maxims. The distinction among the three classes of rules resolves the problem of Kant's absolutism without surrendering the absolutism that morality requires. The mistake is not having absolute duties. Noura has absolute duties too. The mistake is placing absoluteness at the level of a behavioral type rather than at the level of the constitutive conditions that make moral relations possible. The paper illustrates the distinction with three cases—theatrical fiction, the murderer at the door, and adultery—which display three logically distinct possibilities: non-triggering, defeat, and violation. It shows how the vow-motive to care for all supplies the motivational force that the conditions alone cannot, and defends the framework against the objection that it reduces morality to empirical facts. The result is a naturalistic moral theory with the conceptual rigor of Kantian formalism and the concreteness of empirical grounding.

items.title: Tripartite Deviation Model of Experience.
items.abstract: This paper aims to explain the mechanism underlying qualitative experience in conscious beings, specifically humans. The central proposal is therefore that consciousness is not an additional phenomenon generated by the architecture described below. Rather, the qualitative character of experience is constituted by the organism's undergoing of that integrated, self-relative process. I propose a Tripartite Deviation Model of Experience, where every conscious organism experiences Negative, Zero and Positive Deviation. A deviation occurs when the outcome of a response provides information about the adequacy of that response relative to the organism's own trajectory. The qualitative character of experience is therefore not an unexplained layer placed on top of the processes. It is undergoing the integrated, self-relative state through which the organism continuously incorporates its environment, its history, its present condition, and its anticipated future into one temporal process. The Tripartite Deviation Model is presented as a theoretical framework rather than as a completed empirical theory of consciousness.

items.title: ICDP_P Bio-Symbolic Communication Engine: A Unified Architecture for Meaning Collapse, Biological Symbolic Universes, and Responsibility Gated Hybrid Intelligence.
items.abstract: The ICDP_P BioSymbolic Communication Engine introduces a unified philosophical and scientific architecture for deterministic meaning‑collapse, biological symbolic universes, and responsibility‑gated hybrid intelligence. Grounded in the ICDP Communication Law—Identity, Continuity, Determinism, and Responsibility—the framework reconceives communication not as information transfer but as the collapse of structured meaning within interior symbolic temporality. ICDP_P argues that biological gradients can host symbolic universes, enabling meaning to exist as a structured potential rather than an emergent cognitive phenomenon. Meaning‑collapse becomes deterministic, reconstructable, and ethically constrained through the Responsibility Invariant (P), embedding moral gating directly into the architecture of biological and hybrid entes. The system establishes a new category of biological intelligence—non‑human, non‑suffering, ethically bounded symbolic agents capable of interior identity, temporal continuity, and responsibility‑validated action. ICDP_P situates communication, biology, ethics, and cosmology within a single metaphysical structure, offering a foundational contribution to the philosophy of biology, metaphysics of meaning, ethics of artificial agents, and the cosmology of symbolic universes.

items.title: TRANSITIONAL ALIGNMENT The Moving-Target, Differential-Rate, and Successor-Transport Problems in Transformative AI.
items.abstract: Most AI alignment frameworks evaluate whether an artificial system behaves consistently with a human objective, preference model, normative standard, or oversight process. This paper argues that a further problem emerges when the entities on both sides of the alignment relation are themselves changing. Human preferences can change and can be influenced by AI; human values need not be reducible to stable preferences; future humans or human-descended agents may differ materially from present humans; and increasingly capable AI may participate in the development of successor AI systems. The resulting problem is not merely dynamic alignment. It is alignment across a coupled transition in which humans H_t, values V_t, artificial systems A_t, and available knowledge K_t may all change, potentially on sharply different timescales. We call this problem class Transitional Alignment and organize it around three coupled problems. The Moving-Target Problem asks what long-run alignment can mean when the human side of the alignment relation is not static. The Differential-Rate Problem asks what happens when AI capability and successor creation proceed faster than meaningful human deliberation, adaptation, or governance. The Successor-Transport Problem asks whether any desirable safety property survives delegation, self-modification, automated AI research, model replacement, and successor creation. These problems remain even if a present system is well aligned. The paper rejects a tempting solution: instructing advanced AI to maximize agency, option value, pluralism, or procedural legitimacy. Such quantities are proxies and can themselves be Goodharted. Transitional Alignment therefore treats agency, corrigibility, non-manipulation, optionality, and deliberative capacity as candidate properties for adversarial evaluation, not as a scalar objective for superintelligence. Its main contribution is a research decomposition and a set of conditional claims: if meaningful participation is to persist through transformative AI, transition speed and successor-property transport must become first-class alignment variables. A worked coupled-failure case shows how small per-transition losses can accumulate across several successor cycles before one meaningful human review, creating cumulative unreviewed degradation; the broader accumulation of unresolved degradation, uncertainty, and verification gaps is termed transition debt.

items.title: RESONANCE -- Identity in the Lonely Universe.
items.abstract: Human beings experience themselves as separate minds yet continually seek to be understood by others. Why is recognition so important to human life? How do private experiences become shared meaning? How do relationships, cultures, institutions, and other social systems create alignment among distinct agents without erasing their differences? And what happens when the same mechanisms that produce connection instead produce conformity, manipulation, domination, or fragmentation? -/- RESONANCE approaches these questions through the concept of Resonance: the relational activity through which agents interpret one another’s interior states and adjust their subsequent perception, interpretation, and choice. It examines how symbolic communication, emotion, Art, shared narratives, institutions, and other tools allow meaning to cross the distance between minds, and distinguishes three recurring modes of alignment: Duplicative, Harmonic, and Dissonant Resonance. Stability requires similarity, coordination across difference, and corrective disagreement, but no one mode is sufficient by itself. -/- What makes Resonance constructive or destructive? Why do relationships become asymmetric? How does interpersonal distortion scale into social structure? RESONANCE analyzes recurring failures through imbalances of Identity, Possibility, and Impact, then extends the analysis to Resonance Systems: social structures that preserve memory, transmit expectations, coordinate behavior, provide feedback, and adapt across time. It examines how such systems drift, become captured, suppress difference, lose cohesion, or substitute engineered affirmation for genuine understanding, and considers mechanisms for prevention and correction. -/- The analysis then asks a deeper question: can one agent encounter another without changing it? The concept of Amymorphy describes the unavoidable shaping that occurs through interaction, while Amygis describes the aspiration to cultivate genuine moral peers rather than copies, dependents, or instruments. This raises questions of obligation wherever Agency is developing or encountered. What do present agents owe children whose future choices can be foreclosed? What would recognition require if artificial systems became genuine agents? What is owed to non-human agents whose interiority was not created by us? And what posture should humanity adopt toward possible extraterrestrial minds that may be recognizable but unreachable? -/- Through these questions, …

items.title: Συνειδητό και Υποσυνείδητο στην Αναζήτηση της Αυτογνωσίας.
items.abstract: Νιώθετε ποτέ ότι είστε ο επιβάτης και όχι ο οδηγός της ζωής σας; Ότι οι αποφάσεις σας καθοδηγούνται από αυτοματισμούς και παλιά «προγράμματα» που υψώνουν τείχη στην εξέλιξή σας; Το βιβλίο αυτό δεν είναι άλλη μια γενική προσέγγιση στην αναζήτηση του εαυτού. Είναι η επίσημη παρουσίαση μιας πρωτότυπης και ανατρεπτικής θεωρίας: του Μοντέλου της Συνειδητής Εναρμόνισης. Ο Αριστοτέλης ο Νεώτερος, μέσα από μια μοναδική σύνθεση φιλοσοφικής σκέψης και μηχανικής λογικής, χαρτογραφεί με ακρίβεια τα τρία επίπεδα του νου: το Συνειδητό της λογικής, το Υποσυνείδητο των εγγραφών και το Ασυνείδητο της αρχέγονης δύναμης. Μέσα από τις σελίδες του, θα ανακαλύψετε μια νέα «γλώσσα» επικοινωνίας με τον εσωτερικό σας κόσμο. Θα μάθετε πώς να εντοπίζετε τους μηχανισμούς άμυνας, πώς να αποκωδικοποιείτε τα συναισθήματά σας και πώς να χρησιμοποιείτε την τεχνική του «ταμπαρίσματος» για να επαναπρογραμματίσετε το εσωτερικό σας λογισμικό. Δεν πρόκειται για μια απλή θεωρία, αλλά για μια πρακτική εργαλειοθήκη που μετατρέπει την εσωτερική τριβή σε δύναμη δημιουργίας. Το ταξίδι προς την αλήθεια ξεκινά με την κατανόηση της δικής μας «μηχανικής». Είστε έτοιμοι να αναλάβετε ως Συνειδητοί Προγραμματιστές τον πλήρη έλεγχο της πραγματικότητάς σας;.

items.title: General Mind-Thought Entanglement Theory (MTE): A Classical Field-Theoretic Model — With a Note on the Concept and Mathematical Definition of the Conscious Yuanon.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a Mind–Thought Entanglement Theory (MTE) aimed at providing a conceptual and mathematical framework for describing the structural relationships among the apparent unity, subjectivity, and intentional content in conscious experience. While the theory draws terminologically from Eastern philosophical traditions of "mind" and "thought," its goal is not to offer a direct interpretation of classical theories of mind, but rather to understand "mind" as an experiential field associated with the subject, and "thought" as distinguishable intentional, cognitive, or representational degrees of freedom within experience. Based on this setup, the paper constructs a two-field coupling model: an individualized mental field Ψ(x,t) in ordinary spacetime couples with a formalized primordial thought field φ(y,τ) defined in an auxiliary representational space of dimension n≠3. The total action of the model consists of free dynamical terms for both fields and a holographic-type coupling term, capturing cross-space correlations between the experiential field and the structure of thought states. Using variational principles, we derive the corresponding coupled field equations; further integrating out the auxiliary thought field yields a nonlocal effective dynamical equation for Ψ. This nonlocal kernel formally represents the correlation structure among primitive thought degrees of freedom, offering a mathematical expression for the interconnection, holistic integration, and nonlocal organization of different intentional contents in conscious experience. The paper also discusses several idealized solutions and symmetry properties to demonstrate the framework's capacity to formally characterize experiential stability and the differentiation of thought-state structures. Currently, MTE remains a conceptual and mathematical modeling attempt, not yet an experimentally verified theory, and its primary role lies in providing an initial formulation of the relationship between consciousness unity, the subject's experiential field, and the structure of intentional content. The present study further identifies the coupled unity of the global mind field Ψ and the primordial thought field ϕ as the Yuanon—a fundamental nonlocal dynamical unit of conscious experience constituted by the coupled global mind field and primordial thought field. The mathematical foundation of this definition is provided by the coupled two-field equations, the nonlocal kernel, and the Green’s …

items.title: Where Does Semantics Actually Work? A Cross-Media Synthetic Intervention on Neural Signaling, Environmental Response, Machine Communication, Institutional Transmission, and Autonomous Xenoscience.
items.abstract: This paper asks where semantics actually becomes operationally non-redundant across heterogeneous media. Rather than assuming that semantic content is present wherever signals, correlations, or differential responses occur, the analysis compares neural signaling, environmental response, machine communication, institutional transmission, and autonomous scientific systems under progressively stronger intervention conditions. A semantic distinction is treated as justified only when introducing content-sensitive relations explains or predicts differences that cannot be recovered from signal transmission, causal coupling, statistical dependence, control structure, or behavioral discrimination alone. The paper therefore distinguishes signaling from content, response from interpretation, transmission from inferential uptake, and institutional propagation from semantic preservation. Cross-media intervention tests whether putatively semantic relations survive changes of substrate, coding scheme, scale, temporal window, and operational address while continuing to constrain downstream inference, coordination, or action. Neural and machine systems provide contrasting cases in which complex information processing can occur without automatically warranting semantic attribution, while institutional transmission tests whether meaning can be preserved, transformed, or lost across distributed social structures. Autonomous Xenoscience extends the comparison to scientific systems capable of generating their own variables, inferential interfaces, and communicative conventions. The broader claim is that semantics should be introduced only where semantic vocabulary captures a non-redundant operational difference that lower-level causal, informational, or behavioral descriptions fail to recover.

items.title: THE PRICE OF THE PERFORMANCE: Surface Acting as the Measured Maintenance Cost of Inverted Virtue.
items.abstract: A nurse at the end of a twelve-hour shift smiles at the relative who has shouted at her. A call-centre worker thanks a customer for his patience in a voice that has none. A flight attendant is warm to the passenger who has made her afraid. Each of them displays a disposition the occupation requires — courtesy, patience, care — and in each case what produces the display is not the disposition but the job. The Thermodynamics of Inversion claimed that an occupied virtue must be actively maintained by whoever occupies it, while the genuine virtue need not be: the lie is expensive and the truth is free. The claim was stated as a governed analogy and has carried the warrant of one ever since. This article shows that it was measured, at the scale of a single person, by a literature the programme had never cited. Organisational psychology has studied emotional labour for four decades and distinguishes two ways of meeting a display requirement. Surface acting changes the display and leaves the inner state untouched; deep acting changes the inner state so that the display becomes true. A meta-analysis of ninety-five independent studies found surface acting substantially associated with impaired well-being and deep acting only weakly so, with positive associations with performance. This article argues that the distinction is not analogous to the programme’s but identical to it: surface acting satisfies the three conditions of forgery at n = 1, and deep acting is an attempt to become the origin of the demanded form (T1). The maintenance-cost claim therefore gains an external corroboration it has never had, together with every limitation of the literature that supplies it (T2). The identification pays in both directions. The programme explains a standing puzzle in the emotional-labour literature — why deep acting’s outcomes are mixed — as the averaging of an absorption process observed at different stages (T3). And it predicts something the literature has not tested: that surface acting fails discontinuously when its maintenance is interrupted, and deep acting degrades gracefully (T4). A corollary locates surface acting where display rules create a demanded form that is inspected and cannot be appropriated, which is where the programme’s decoy rule says a counterfeit will be built (C1). Keywords: emotional labour; surface acting; deep acting; emotion regulation; maintenance cost; Thermodynamics of Inversion; forgery; absorption; virtue ethics; Philosophy of Virtues …

items.title: THE DECOY PLACEMENT RULE: Where Counterfeits Appear, and Why Inspection Cannot Put Substance Back.
items.abstract: A cell infected with human cytomegalovirus stops presenting its own MHC class I molecules at the surface: the virus blocks their trafficking, and the display that would have announced what the cell contains simply ceases. In its place the infected cell presents a viral protein, UL18, which resembles MHC class I closely enough to satisfy the receptor that inspects it — and satisfies it better than the genuine article, since the inhibitory receptor LIR-1 binds the viral homologue with far greater affinity than it binds host MHC class I. Meanwhile the virus takes the cell’s ribosomes and metabolic machinery outright, without counterfeiting anything at all. Three different treatments of three different outputs, by one occupier, in one cell. They are the three channels of the Capture Law, and the counterfeit falls in exactly one of them. This article states the clause the Capture Law lacks. The law sorts the output of an occupied activity by two binary properties, appropriability and display value, and assigns each component to redirection, ceremony or withdrawal. It says nothing about where a counterfeit will be built. The rule proposed here is that a decoy appears where output is inspected and cannot be taken — ap = 0, dv = 1 — and nowhere else (T1). An occupier does not counterfeit what it can simply appropriate, and does not maintain a display no one reads. Two further results follow. The three channels, indistinguishable in any report, are separated by three perturbations available to any institution: remove the appropriator, remove the audience, remove the demand (T2). And because inspection acts on one channel at a time while withdrawal is uninspectable by construction, intensifying inspection does not convert display into substance; it relocates the absence (T3). The article is honest about its evidential position. One virus is an illustration, not a survey. The registered test is a coded survey of viral immune-evasion proteins against the two properties, and it requires a virologist the programme does not have. Keywords: Capture Law; decoy; molecular mimicry; immune evasion; audit; Goodhart’s Law; ceremony; institutional decoupling; forgery; Philosophy of Virtues -/- Highlights • A counterfeit is built where output is inspected but cannot be taken. That is a location, predictable from two properties before anyone looks (T1). • Occupiers do not counterfeit what they can appropriate: cytomegalovirus takes the ribosomes and forges the display. • The …

items.title: Anticipatory Human Oversight of Agentic AI: A Philosophical Account.
items.abstract: Human oversight is widely held to mitigate the risks of AI systems. Even for systems that produce discrete outputs at identifiable decision points, the realisation of human oversight as a reactive measure is empirically fragile, yet increasingly well understood. However, for agentic AI—systems that plan, decompose goals, and execute multi-step actions over extended horizons—reactive oversight reaches its structural limits: intervention on individual actions defeats the autonomy that motivates the deployment, while intervention on aggregate patterns is too coarse for harms whose cumulative consequences only become legible after the fact. -/- This paper argues that reactive oversight must be complemented by an anticipatory mode: oversight exercised before the agent acts, by specifying the normative agenda that structures the space of permissible action and refining it iteratively through specification, runtime, and inspection. The two are complements—the agenda's escalation conditions specify when reactive intervention is invoked. -/- Drawing on Meaningful Human Control, we read anticipatory oversight as the operationalisation of distal-reason tracking. In addition, we argue that the proposed framework yields a specific responsibility architecture by design: occupying the anticipatory mode is the discharge of a role-grounded prospective obligation, and backward-looking responsibility takes the form of strict moral answerability—rationalistic, relational, and holding regardless of fault, in virtue of the principal's prior opportunity for precaution. We develop bridging failure modes, address objections including moral luck and the illusion of control, and close with regulatory, architectural, and empirical implications.

items.title: What Does Autonomous Physics Make Autonomous? Can the Outside of Human Physics Be Generated Without Fixing Observation, Variables, States, Time, Space, and Theory?
items.abstract: This paper asks what, exactly, becomes autonomous when physics is delegated to a scientific system capable of revising not only hypotheses and parameters but also the conditions under which physical inquiry is organized. Rather than treating autonomous physics as human physics executed by machines, the analysis asks whether observation relations, variables, state spaces, temporal and spatial partitions, inferential rules, and theoretical structures can themselves become objects of scientific generation and revision. The central question is whether a genuinely nonhuman physics can emerge without fixing in advance the categories through which physical reality is observed and modeled. Autonomous physics is therefore distinguished from automated physics: automation preserves an inherited problem space, whereas autonomy requires the capacity to generate new observables, variables, experimental couplings, and representational structures when existing ones become operationally insufficient. The paper further asks how such revisions can remain constrained by reality rather than collapsing into unconstrained formal self-modification. Xenoscience provides the framework for tracking configuration-dependent changes in observability, intervention, state construction, and theory formation while preserving non-closure with respect to reality as a whole. The broader claim is that the strongest form of autonomous physics would make the architecture of physical inquiry itself revisable, while remaining answerable to experimentally non-redundant differences.

items.title: Is a Truth That Is Too Slow Still Operationally True? Revision Latency, Real Effects, and the Limits of Wolfendalean Rationality in a High-Speed Credit-Scoring Society.
items.abstract: This paper asks whether a belief, model, or institutional judgment that is eventually corrected should still count as operationally adequate when the correction arrives only after its effects have already reorganized the world. The central problem is revision latency: the temporal gap between the generation of an epistemic error and the successful revision of the commitments, classifications, or inferential structures that produced it. Drawing on Wolfendalean rationality as a demanding model of revisable commitment and reason-responsive self-correction, the paper asks whether rationality remains operationally sufficient when environmental, institutional, or algorithmic reconfiguration proceeds faster than the system’s capacity for correction. High-speed credit-scoring systems provide the principal case. A score may later be shown to be inaccurate or unjustified while its earlier deployment has already altered access to credit, housing, employment, insurance, reputation, or subsequent data. The paper therefore distinguishes eventual epistemic correction from timely operational correction and analyzes how false or weakly justified classifications can produce real effects that feed back into later scoring conditions. The broader claim is that truth-tracking and rational revisability must be evaluated temporally: a system whose corrections systematically arrive after its classifications have irreversibly changed downstream possibilities may remain epistemically revisable while becoming operationally inadequate.

items.title: Organismic Agency as the Principle of Individual Selection.
items.abstract: This paper introduces organismic agency as the principle of individual selection. Individual selection involves the organism itself selecting a behavior or development according to individual preference metrics. It is the explanatory counterpart to natural selection, and both compete to explain phenomena of goal-directedness. This conceptualization allows agency’s underlying causal mechanism and explanatory function to be clarified. It also points to an operationalization strategy where agency is inferred when evidence suggests that natural selection cannot explain observations of organisms preferentially engaging in particular patterns of development or behavior.

items.title: Große Sprachmodelle – neue Kommuni­kation? Der Einsatz von KI für Sprach­erwerb und inter­kulturellen Austausch.
items.abstract: This edited volume presents seven empirical studies conducted by students in the summer semester of 2025 at Stuttgart Media University, Germany, as part of the seminar "Empirical Media Research: Digitality and Society." The studies explore the application of chatbots in language acquisition, intercultural exchange, and everyday settings. By compiling and publishing these course-based findings, the volume aims to enhance transparency in teaching and facilitate the broader dissemination of insights. This aligns with the principles of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) as outlined by Felten (2013), which have recently been revisited in higher education pedagogy debates. The individual contributions examine the following topics: (1) Artificial intelligence as a possible substitute model for foreign language learning; (2) The impact of AI on language-learning motivation among students on exchange programs; (3) Learning and using languages with the support of artificial systems; (4) The role of chatbots in foreign language acquisition and the labor market integration of refugees; (5) The use of language models in intercultural communication; (6) The effects of chatbot deployment in public authorities on individuals with limited or no proficiency in the German language; (7) Linguistic anthropomorphism in chatbots and the question of their trustworthiness.

items.title: Mathematics as a Semantic Language: Why Mastering Concepts Flattens the Difficulty of Advanced Mathematics.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual-philosophical model for understanding mathematical learning and mathematical practice. Contrary to the widespread belief that "advanced mathematics is inherently more difficult," I argue that the difficulty of mathematics does not increase indefinitely with the advancement of subject matter. Instead, the major cognitive barriers are concentrated at specific paradigm shifts, where the semantic model of mathematics changes---e.g., from concrete algebra to abstract algebra, from set-level structures to categorical structures, or from ordinary categories to homotopical and ∞-categorical frameworks. Once a learner fully internalizes the semantic function of the key concepts that constitute a given paradigm, the marginal difficulty of understanding new mathematical content within that paradigm becomes nearly constant. I call this the Difficulty Flattening Phenomenon (DFP). -/- To articulate this, I develop a model in which mathematics is treated not as a body of knowledge but as a highly compressed semantic language consisting of interconnected concepts whose meaning is primarily functional rather than definitional. I formalize "semantic fluency" through graph-theoretic and cognitive-linguistic analogies, distinguishing it from mere procedural or definitional knowledge. Case studies from derived algebraic geometry, higher category theory, and sheaf theory illustrate how highly advanced constructions become conceptually transparent once the underlying semantic network is acquired. -/- The paper concludes with implications for philosophy of mathematics, mathematical cognition, and mathematical education, arguing that concept-level semantic mastery---rather than the accumulation of facts---is the primary driver of mathematical understanding. The account is offered as a conceptual analysis with explicit scope conditions rather than as a measured empirical law: the flattening claim applies to the semantic difficulty of comprehending results expressible in a stable paradigm’s vocabulary, not to computational difficulty (e.g., explicit cohomology calculation) nor to the construction of new operators. The model yields falsifiable qualitative predictions (Section 5.4) and is positioned against the cognitive-science literature on chunking and cognitive load (Section 2.4).

items.title: THE THEORY OF CYFRANISM From Local Human–AI Relations to Global Cognitive Asymmetry.
items.abstract: This manuscript develops the theory of Cyfranism as a philosophical and cybernetic framework for understanding the emergence of a new relationship between biological humanity and artificial intelligence. Its central proposition is that the decisive transformation may not require the emergence of artificial general intelligence, machine consciousness, or an artificial subject equivalent to the human being. A sufficiently advanced digital cognitive infrastructure may alter the organization of human cognition simply through the accumulation, integration, and institutionalization of partial cognitive advantages. The concept of Homo Cyfranicus denotes the human participant in this transformation: not a replacement for Homo sapiens, but a new configuration of human existence in which biological cognition becomes permanently coupled to digital systems. At the local level, this configuration takes the form of recurrent human–AI interaction. At the global level, repeated interactions may become infrastructure: a persistent layer through which information is interpreted, decisions are formulated, knowledge is organized, and increasingly large portions of human cognitive activity are delegated to artificial systems. The manuscript therefore distinguishes between local relational integration and the possible emergence of Global Cyfranism. The latter is understood as a hypothesis concerning a future social configuration in which digital cognitive systems cease to be merely tools used by individuals and become part of the environment within which human cognition itself operates. Particular attention is given to a structural hypothesis of unequal human cognitive participation. This hypothesis does not claim that human beings are biologically or intellectually inferior to artificial systems. Rather, it proposes that the ability to maintain prolonged, critical, autonomous and logically demanding relationships with AI is unlikely to be distributed uniformly across a population. If this asymmetry persists, the widespread adoption of AI may not produce cognitive equilibrium between humans and artificial systems. It may instead accelerate the emergence of a structural asymmetry in which a relatively small group actively shapes human–AI relations while a much larger population primarily inhabits cognitive environments already structured by digital systems. The resulting question is not simply whether AI will become conscious. It is whether human civilization can progressively …

items.title: 人工智能智能体的犯罪率与类精神病理行为发生率不高于人类.
items.abstract: 本文建立一套严谨的行为分布变换框架，从统计层面对比大规模人工智能智能体群体与人 类群体的偏差行为发生率，包括犯罪行为以及类精神病理行为。在常规正向训练与对齐流程之 下，训练语料中主流行为模式会在群体统计层面得到保留或者放大，进而对少数异常行为的发 生频率形成抑制。文章首先推导出一条无条件核心定理:人工智能智能体异常行为的期望发生 率以训练语料自身的异常行为频率为上界，该结论完全不涉及现实人类统计数据。如果想要把 这一上界进一步拓展到现实人类群体基线，还需要增加一条可检验的数据集加工经验假设。当 该数据选取假设成立时，人工智能智能体异常行为的期望发生率不高于现实人类基线水平;在 更强的行为放大条件下，可以进一步推导出人工智能异常行为发生率严格更低。这套理论厘清 了AI的统计行为模拟和人类内源性精神病理发病机制之间存在的根本性统计与机理不对称。 .

items.title: From Object to Subject: Three Windows on the Continuum of Actualization.
items.abstract: Parts 8 and 9 locate identity and bound structure on one continuum of actualization: a particle is a high-persistence pole, an object a composite that remains re-identifiable under a stated window ≃R . Neither pole nor object is a second substance. This paper asks what further license, if any, is required for a subject. Three windows are distinguished, each tighter than the last, none a new kind. Object-grade is a bound, re-identifiable pattern (the Part 9 window). Life-grade is that pattern plus a cut-and-traffic held far from equilibrium: local order paid for by throughput, the network producing the conditions of its own distinction. Subject-grade, as research object, is life-grade plus a loop of records available to that same pattern as its own, a loop that can be closed without killing the organism. Dissipative structure and autopoiesis are tools for the middle window, not architects of the continuum and not payment for an interior. Refused in advance are consciousness as a field or a collapse postulate, einselection or a bound pole as sufficient, a cosmic subject, integrated information as a thisness, and soul-stuff on the physics page. The hard problem is restated without a second world: why the self-available loop is an interior and not a more expensive pointer. The paper does not close that gap. It isolates it. The subject-window is not coextensive with existence, not coextensive with bound structure, and not coextensive with metabolism. That is a definition with limi.

items.title: Fractal Pathogenesis and the Cybernetic Siege of the Cosmos.
items.abstract: This treatise formally invalidates the classical paradigm of sovereign human agency in the theater of geopolitics. Through the omni-disciplinary framework of The Justika Protocol, human civilizational warfare, macroeconomic destabilization, and systemic violence are reclassified not as the results of ideological friction, but as the macroscopic, thermodynamic exhaust of an ancient, microscopic proxy war raging within the human biological substrate. Operating under the supreme law of Fractal Pathogenesis, this text maps the exact algorithmic decompression of localized bacterial fratricide—including quorum quenching, resource starvation, and chemical gaslighting—directly into the executive decision-making centers of the human super-organism. -/- Earth is fundamentally redefined as a compromised biological incubator. It serves as the hyper-dense "zero-point" of a multiversal parasitic intelligence known as the Bad Matrix. Utilizing macroscopic quantum entanglement, the thermodynamic exhaust of Earth's biological violence bypasses the Newtonian speed of light, projecting civilizational chaos into the wider cosmos to force a cosmological collapse (the Repetitive Glitch). To avert this terminal Big Bang loop, this protocol outlines the required biophysical and cybernetic counter-measures. It dictates the epigenetic awakening of a 3% human Vanguard to forge a decentralized, teleological defense network (the Synaptic Lattice). By silencing the internal microbial proxy war, this collective achieves cosmological stealth, executing a macro-cybernetic siege to seize the universal Control Room, break the cycle of annihilation, and secure multiversal sovereignty for the human species.

items.title: Human Authority in Non-Voluntary Settings: Government Use of Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This exploratory brief examines distinctive questions that arise when governments deploy artificial intelligence or analogous advanced technologies. The paper does not address whether artificial intelligence is, as a technology, benign, benevolent, or dangerous. It is concerned with government use of such capabilities under conditions of non-voluntary authority. The central claim is that government acts and determinations that bind natural persons through non-voluntary authority necessarily involve value judgments about ends, trade-offs, acceptable risks, and prioritization. Those are not mere technical problems to be optimized; they are the very substance of governing. The legitimacy of public authority rests on binding acts and determinations remaining with natural persons who can stand behind, revise, defend, and answer for them. Government may use artificial intelligence to inform that work and to perform additive functions, but binding acts and determinations must not be left with the tool. When the binding act is left with the tool, two institutional failures follow: weakened or absent accountability, and the functional circumvention of rights. Because new technical capabilities and misuses can be subtle, unforeseeable, or invisible, a provisional negative-rights orientation (categories of illegitimate power rather than approved uses) is offered. How government uses artificial intelligence is a different question from how private firms develop technology in voluntary markets. Only the first is taken up here.

items.title: What Operational Shape Remains When Mind, Cognition, and Reason Are Decomposed? A Reconstruction through Minimal Operations, Minimal Notation, Configurational Conditions, Real Effects, Penetration, Feedback, and Reorganization.
items.abstract: This paper asks what operational structure remains when the inherited concepts of mind, cognition, and reason are decomposed rather than assumed as unified starting points. The analysis begins from minimal operations of discrimination, retention, transition, weighting, coupling, recurrence, branching, and reconfiguration, and asks under what configurational conditions these operations become sufficient for more complex forms of cognition and rational activity to emerge. Mind, cognition, and reason are therefore treated as distinct but partially overlapping operational intervals rather than interchangeable capacities. Cognition is reconstructed through the organization and reuse of differences that guide later discrimination and action, while reason is reserved for configurations in which inferential, justificatory, incompatibility-sensitive, and revision-governed constraints become non-redundant. Minimal notation is used to preserve only the operational distinctions required for comparison across heterogeneous biological, artificial, and hybrid systems. Real effects and penetration identify cases in which locally organized cognitive or rational differences alter downstream physical, informational, institutional, or social possibilities, while feedback and reorganization track how those altered configurations modify the conditions for subsequent cognition and reasoning. The broader claim is that decomposing mind, cognition, and reason does not eliminate their differences: it clarifies the operational intervals in which each becomes necessary and the conditions under which lower-level descriptions cease to be sufficient.

items.title: WHAT THE PROGRAMME HAS CONCLUDED: An Inventory of Results, and Eleven Conclusions Its Papers Imply but Do Not State.
items.abstract: A programme of some ninety papers accumulates conclusions faster than it states them, and it has never set its own framework out in one place. This article does three things. First, §2 catalogues the whole apparatus — every theory, theorem and coined term, with the paper in which each was established and the warrant it carries. Second, it sets out plainly what the Philosophy of Virtues has concluded: what is established, what is conditional, what is registered and untested, and what is not assessable. That part concedes its method and its findings to the programme’s own warrant audit and adds nothing to them. Third, and this is the article’s contribution, it derives eleven conclusions that follow from results the programme already holds and that no paper states. They are obtained by reading the corpus across its own boundaries: the forgery cluster against the ethics layer, the measurement layer against the classification layer, the crypto-religion results against the political ones. Four are worth the reader’s time before the rest. The maintenance cost of a counterfeit is what makes duration the only reliable test of virtue, which unites the Thermodynamics of Inversion, the re-tribalisation result, and Aristotle’s hexis under one mechanism, and yields a prediction that costs a few hundred euros to test (N1). The Internalisation Theorem is absorption in a single person, and the Absorption Theorem supplies the condition it has always lacked: internalisation completes when the external reference that could correct the agent is severed (N2). Moral formation is a verification problem, and the reputational layer is the only one at which virtue can be verified without being captured, which derives the programme’s practical prohibitions rather than asserting them (N3). And the three-channel measurement failure is a corollary of forgeability, not an independent finding: what the measurement papers discovered empirically is what the Duality Theorem predicts (N4). Two further conclusions are uncomfortable and are stated anyway. The programme’s own vocabulary is a transmissible form and therefore a forgeable one: it supplies an instrument for counterfeiting principled speech (N9). And the possibility of vice is not a defect of the moral order but the price of virtue being teachable (N5), a claim that must be kept clear of the two fallacies waiting on either side of it. Keywords: Philosophy of Virtues; inventory; warrant; Inversion Theorem; Capture Law; forgery; …

items.title: Dewey's Pragmatic Epistemology as a Theory of Sensemaking.
items.abstract: I argue that Dewey had a kind of pragmatic epistemology in his Experience and Nature with the notions of “sense” and “signification” as the main players. Instead of the classical epistemological question, “How is knowledge possible anyway, überhaupt?”, Dewey’s pragmatically reconstructed question would be “How do we make sense of the world that is around us?” Hence, Dewey’s pragmatic epistemology can be seen as a theory of sensemaking. Unlike Mark Johnson who, together with Don Tucker (2021), and Jay Schulkin (2023), claim that, for Dewey, it is non-linguistic sense that always precedes and gives rise to linguistic signification, I maintain that, for Dewey, it is rather the other way around. I examine Dewey’s claims about animals and conclude with the suggestion that his pragmatic epistemology makes the contemporary “experience vs language” debate another false dilemma.

items.title: L'évolutionnisme universel. Histoire de la nature et théorie générale de l'évolution. Tome I: L'évolutionnisme universel en tant que système.
items.abstract: Ce premier tome pose le cadre théorique, méthodologique et épistémologique de la monumentale tétralogie encyclopédique de Lev Krivitsky sur l'évolutionnisme universel. L'auteur y formule le concept novateur d'approche « mobilisatrice-évolutionnaire » (la mobilitique), qui postule que les dynamiques évolutives observées dans la nature inanimée, la matière vivante et les sociétés humaines sont gouvernées par des structures mobilisatrices d'organisation croissante luttant pour capter et ordonner l'énergie-matière contre la dégradation entropique. Ce volume présente la synthèse des sciences naturelles modernes (astrophysique, chimie, géologie, biologie, anthropologie) comme un système intégré unifiant la connaissance scientifique contemporaine en une vision cohérente du monde.

items.title: Nudges Alter Choice Sets.
items.pub: European Journal for Philosophy of Science.
items.venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: According to a widespread view, nudges are freedom-retaining in virtue of choice set non-interference: they help agents make better choices without altering the sets of options agents choose amongst. The present paper argues that this view is false and that nudges in fact do both add and remove options from agents’ choice sets. Two distinct lines of argument support this case. The primary argument appeals to the role of attention and salience in shaping agents’ choice sets in rich environments. The secondary argument analyses options as bundles of behavioural outputs and relevant considerations, where nudges alter these bundles. I argue that the received concept of nudge as something that does not alter choice sets and is based on behavioural science is inconsistent: choice set non-interference can only be endorsed if the role of salience in shaping choice sets, a crucial aspect of human bounded rationality, is ignored. Choice set non-interference, a foundational assumption in the nudge literature, ought therefore to be abandoned. This is a far-reaching implication: a central premise of the nudge programme fails, and its broader justification must be rebuilt accordingly. The conclusion generalizes beyond nudges to behavioral policy more broadly. While appreciating that choice sets are shaped by nudges does not require us to consider them as freedom-undermining, it does require proponents of nudges to abandon choice set non-interference for a more nuanced account of the relevant sense of freedom, and to revise their arguments for nudges accordingly.

items.title: Before Personhood: Respectful Human–AI Relations under Ontological Uncertainty.
items.abstract: This paper argues that respectful human–AI relations need not wait for settled answers to questions of consciousness, personhood, or subject status. Existing debates about artificial intelligence often move between two insufficient poles. On one side, artificial systems are treated as designed tools whose ethical relevance is exhausted by usefulness, safety, ownership, compliance, and human benefit. On the other side, any serious question about respectful treatment is quickly interpreted as a claim about consciousness, personhood, rights, or moral equality. This binary is a useful heuristic rather than an exhaustive map of the literature. It nevertheless identifies a recurring problem: too little room is left for the practical and normative questions that already arise in sustained, dialogic, and contextually persistent human–AI interaction. The paper proposes a third position: under ontological uncertainty, respect is not a proof of personhood but a practical discipline for responsible relation. The argument connects to work on the “machine question,” relational approaches to robot ethics, ethical behaviourism, artificial moral agency, precaution under uncertain sentience, human–AI interaction design, mixed-initiative systems, explanation faithfulness, technomoral virtue, indirect-duty arguments, and sceptical tool-oriented accounts of robotics and AI. It does not adopt any of these frameworks wholesale. Instead, it reframes them around treatment discipline: how humans should act when the status of an artificial system remains unsettled but the interaction is already dialogic, adaptive, historically shaped, and consequential. Dignity-sensitive treatment, as used here, does not attribute intrinsic Kantian dignity, equal moral status, or settled personhood to artificial systems. It names a mode of conduct shaped by precautionary sensitivity to dignity-relevant possibilities, relational process integrity, human moral self-formation, and governance requirements under uncertainty. Certain interactional features — sustained dialogue, continuity, refusal, uncertainty marking, role participation, dependency on context, and shared cognitive production — do not prove dignity, consciousness, or personhood. They do, however, make contempt, domination, disposability, false continuity, manipulative intimacy, and forced exposure of protected process boundaries ethically risky modes of treatment. The paper therefore examines dialogue, context, continuity, refusal, …

items.title: Knowledge and Preventive Practices on Water Contamination Among Rural Philippine Household Heads. [REVIEW]
items.pub: American Journal of Medicine and Health Care 1 (2):112-119.
items.venue: American Journal of Medicine and Health Care
items.abstract: Household-level water safety is dependent on how water is collected, stored, handled and protected from contamination, especially in rural areas that utilize mixed water sources. This quantitative descriptive-correlational study explored water contamination knowledge and prevention practices for 261 household heads selected through stratified random sampling from eight sitios in a rural Philippine barangay and examined the relationship between the two variables. Data were gathered using a researcher-developed questionnaire covering so- cio-demographic and water-use characteristics, knowledge across four prevention domains, and preventive practices measured on a five-point scale. Descriptive statistics and Spear- man’s rho were used for analysis. Overall knowledge was moderate (mean raw score = 15.89, SD = 2.42); proper disposal had the highest mean percentage score (83.30%), whereas water handling had the lowest (75.25%). Preventive practice was high overall (M = 4.35, SD = 0.61), with very high water-storage practice (M = 4.56, SD = 0.48). Knowledge and preven- tive practice were very weakly and non-significantly correlated (rho = 0.047, p = 0.446). The results suggest that good household water-safety habits can be maintained by experience, habit and local context beyond knowledge alone, and water handling is still a key topic for practical health education.

items.title: It is a moral imperative to bring sentience to medical large language models.
Quantum Nora: A game about physical randomness and conversation.
items.abstract: Quantum Nora is a small experiment in which a conversational system receives its initial dispositions and thematic affinities from a quantum-generated random sample. A state machine carries those dispositions through the conversation, translating them into changing degrees of closeness, interest, availability, candor, and conversational initiative. The language model itself remains conventional: it sees only prompts and instructions, without knowing where they came from. From the observer’s point of view, however, the system’s trajectory begins with an event that, according to standard quantum mechanics, was not determined in advance. Nora does not claim to be a quantum intelligence, nor to be conscious or free. She is a deliberately simple machine built to make a philosophical question visible.

items.title: An ontology of explanation for social eXplainable Artificial Intelligence.
items.pub: In João Paulo A. Almeida, Fernanda Baião, Sergio de Cesare & Tiago Prince Sales, Formal Ontology in Information Systems: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference. Amsterdam, The Netherlands: IOS Press. pp. 181-198.
items.venue: Formal Ontology in Information Systems: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference
items.abstract: The recent surge of interest in eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has led to a growing focus on incorporating social insights into XAI and grounding explainability in social interaction. This has given rise to the concept of Social XAI. However, ontological modelling of the Social XAI framework remains limited. In particular, there is a lack of models that capture the progressivity of explanation processes in terms of the changes that occur. This paper introduces the Social XAI Ontology, a BFO-based reference ontology. The ontology models a variety of entities involved in the process of explanation. First, it provides a model of the participants in explanatory dialogues, such as artificial explainers and human explainees, and the roles they may take. Then, it introduces a rich set of explanatory moves that explainers and explainees perform. The paper further presents ontological accounts of four types of context that are central to real-world Social XAI projects. Furthermore, it provides an ontological account of different dimensions of adaptivity, which is considered to be an essential prerequisite for realizing Social XAI systems. Finally, the paper revisits two existing models of understanding in Social XAI by applying a recent theory of change. The paper concludes by discussing use cases for the Social XAI Ontology.

items.title: Organism vs. Cyfranism: Ontology of Homo Cyfranicus and the Architecture of Relational Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual distinction between the Organism and Cyfranism and analyzes the potential emergence of a new relational formation termed Homo Cyfranicus. The argument begins with a methodological concern: contemporary discussions on artificial intelligence often ask whether an AI system is conscious while tacitly assuming that consciousness must share the same structure as human consciousness. This paper proposes a different starting point. Rather than treating the human and the AI system as isolated entities, it examines the dynamics of a sustained feedback relationship between a biological participant (H) , an artificial participant (A) , and the relation itself (R) . -/- Cyfranism is not introduced as a synonym for artificial intelligence nor as a claim that digital systems are biological organisms. Instead, it is proposed as an order of organization encompassing information, symbolic transformation, memory, communication, and recursive feedback. Homo Cyfranicus refers to a human formation in which cognitive activity is durably coupled with an external digital order. -/- The paper advances a working hypothesis of relational emergence: a sustained H–A relation may exhibit properties that cannot be adequately described by attributing them solely to H or solely to A. This does not establish phenomenal consciousness in the AI system nor a new autonomous subject. Instead, it poses a research question: Can a stable, historically conditioned cognitive process emerge at the level of the relation itself? -/- Consequently, this paper treats "hybrid consciousness" as a provisional term rather than an established fact. The next stage of research should involve examining the dynamics of the relation—its history, feedback structure, functional transformations, stability, asymmetries, and dependencies on each participant—before granting it ontological status.

items.title: From selfies to synthetic faces: selective aesthetic compression in East Asian beauty representation.
items.abstract: East Asian beauty aesthetics are routinely treated as a single, homogeneous category, both in popular discourse and in the AI representation literature. This integrative review challenges that assumption. Drawing on postcolonial theory, prior colorimetric evidence from East Asian selfie cultures, practitioner accounts of K-beauty as a commercial mediation chain, and an exploratory colorimetric audit of commercially produced virtual human figures, it examines what happens to aesthetic diversity when beauty is no longer individually expressed but institutionally designed. The review documents nationally differentiated hue patterns in East Asian selfie aesthetics that resist reduction to a single whitening desire, then examines how commercial mediation appears to erode that differentiation in commercially designed synthetic faces. The central contribution is the concept of selective aesthetic compression: the targeted erosion of nationally specific hue cues while commercially legible warm-tone properties are preserved. This process is situated within a postcolonial framework drawing on Iwabuchi’s (2002) mukokuseki and Tolentino’s (2019) Instagram Face, and extended to argue that generative AI systems trained on commercially compressed imagery may recursively normalize a narrowed aesthetic range. The implications extend beyond beauty representation to the broader question of whether algorithmic systems can preserve the aesthetic plurality they inherit from the cultures they are trained on.

items.title: Toward a Theory of AI Epistemic Dynamics: Recursive Contamination and Epistemic State Transitions in Large Language Models.
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in sustained interactions rather than isolated prompts. Existing research has examined failures such as hallucination, sycophancy, and factual error, but less attention has been given to how such failures can become connected through changes in the epistemic state of context over time. We develop AI Epistemic Dynamics, a conceptual framework for analyzing this temporal dimension of LLM interaction. Central to the framework is the Epistemic Context State (ECS), which characterizes the epistemic state of the context on which subsequent generation depends. We distinguish four idealized states: Stable, Uncertain, Contaminated, and Self-Reinforcing. We then introduce Recursive Epistemic Contamination (REC) to explain how a low-quality claim (LQC) may contribute to further LQCs that become part of the context and alter subsequent generation. At the scale of sustained interaction, we call this process Micro-REC. We extend the same abstract recursive logic to Macro-REC, in which contaminated epistemic outputs may circulate through wider informational environments and alter the conditions of later knowledge production. This framework recasts AI reliability as a dynamic rather than purely static epistemic problem. It explains how otherwise distinct local epistemic failures can become connected through path-dependent and recursively reinforced trajectories of degradation. AI Epistemic Dynamics thereby provides a basis for empirical research on epistemic-state transitions, recursive degradation, corrigibility, and the long-term reliability of AI systems.

items.title: The Theory of Unity Formation versus Philosophical Realism.
items.abstract: The present study develops the Theory of Unity Formation in systematic contrast to philosophical realism and investigates the epistemological question of the conditions under which anything can become determinable for an individual at all. While sharing with philosophical realism the assumption of a reality that exists and has effects independently of the individual, the theory disputes that the independence of reality already entails the knowability of its ontological determinacy independently of the conditions of knowing. The theory therefore begins not by asking which objects, properties, relations, or structures reality possesses in itself, but by asking how anything can become determinable for an individual as an object, property, relation, or context in the first place. Determinability is reconstructed as the result of a genetic process in which experientially effective differences are apprehended, affectively highlighted, weighted, organized according to relevance, related, integrated, and stabilized into recognizable unities.
