On this basis, a distinction is drawn between experiential understanding and conceptual understanding: whereas experience can already bring forth an actuality sufficiently determinate for orientation and action, conceptual understanding explicates formed unities and contexts conceptually and enables their further relational, functional, causal, and systemic determination. Relation, functionality, causality, and system therefore appear not as immediately known ontological structures of reality, but as different organizational forms through which already determinable unities and contexts within actuality are further determined and explicated. Scientific knowledge likewise does not transcend these conditions of unity formation, but organizes determinability with greater methodological unambiguity through definitions, measurement procedures, methodological control, reproducibility, and criticism, thereby making possible a high degree of system objectivity. The decisive epistemological difference from philosophical realism emerges from the distinction between reality and actuality: reality denotes what exists and has effects independently of the individual, whereas actuality denotes the order of the determinable that is brought forth and stabilized within unity formation. The formation of actuality does not imply arbitrariness, since formations of unity remain subject to the effects of an independent reality, must prove themselves …

items.title: Theorie der Einheitsbildung versus Philosophischer Realismus.
items.abstract: Die vorliegende Arbeit entwickelt die Theorie der Einheitsbildung in systematischer Gegenüberstellung zum philosophischen Realismus und untersucht die erkenntnistheoretische Frage, unter welchen Bedingungen für ein Individuum überhaupt etwas bestimmbar werden kann. Mit dem philosophischen Realismus teilt sie die Annahme einer vom Individuum unabhängig bestehenden und wirkenden Realität, bestreitet jedoch, dass aus dieser Unabhängigkeit bereits die Erkennbarkeit ihrer vom Erkennen unabhängigen ontologischen Bestimmtheit folgt. Ausgangspunkt der Theorie ist daher nicht die Frage, welche Gegenstände, Eigenschaften, Beziehungen oder Strukturen die Realität an sich besitzt, sondern wie etwas für ein Individuum überhaupt als Gegenstand, Eigenschaft, Beziehung oder Zusammenhang bestimmbar werden kann. Bestimmbarkeit wird dabei als Ergebnis eines genetisch rekonstruierbaren Prozesses verstanden, in dem erfahrungswirksam gewordene Differenzen erfasst, affektiv hervorgehoben, gewichtet, hinsichtlich ihrer Relevanz organisiert, relationiert, integriert und zu wiedererkennbaren Einheiten stabilisiert werden. Auf dieser Grundlage wird zwischen Erfahrungsverstehen und Denkverstehen unterschieden: Während bereits Erfahrung eine für Orientierung und Handeln hinreichend bestimmte Wirklichkeit hervorbringen kann, expliziert das Denkverstehen gebildete Einheiten und Zusammenhänge begrifflich und ermöglicht deren weitergehende relationale, funktionale, kausale und systemische Bestimmung. Beziehung, Funktionalität, Kausalität und System erscheinen damit nicht als unmittelbar erkannte ontologische Strukturen der Realität, sondern als unterschiedliche Organisationsformen, durch die bereits bestimmbare Einheiten und Zusammenhänge innerhalb der Wirklichkeit weiter bestimmt und expliziert werden. Auch wissenschaftliche Erkenntnis überschreitet diese Bedingungen der Einheitsbildung nicht, sondern organisiert Bestimmbarkeit durch Definitionen, Messverfahren, methodische Kontrolle, Reproduzierbarkeit und Kritik methodisch eindeutiger und kann dadurch eine hohe Systemobjektivität erreichen. Die entscheidende erkenntnistheoretische Differenz zum philosophischen Realismus ergibt sich aus der Unterscheidung von Realität und Wirklichkeit: Realität bezeichnet das vom Individuum unabhängig Bestehende und Wirkende, Wirklichkeit dagegen die innerhalb von Einheitsbildung hervorgebrachte und stabilisierte Ordnung des Bestimmbaren. Wirklichkeitsbildung bedeutet dabei keine Beliebigkeit, da …

items.title: When do we take the institutional stance?
items.abstract: While role-based representations likely play some role in social cognition, we are skeptical that this amounts to a distinctive “stance.” We encourage the authors to make more specific predictions about when we rely more upon institutional reasoning rather than mentalizing. We suggest that this might depend on the amount of perceived individual agency afforded to occupants of different social roles.

items.title: On Medieval Background.
items.pub: In Alexandra Chadwick & Juhana Toivanen, Vice, Sin, and Sociability in Early Modern Philosophy. Leiden: Brill. pp. 12-36.
items.venue: Vice, Sin, and Sociability in Early Modern Philosophy
items.abstract: This chapter charts key aspects of medieval discussions on moral vices and the corruption of human nature. It is based on the premise that the transition from the medieval to the early modern period should not be seen as a revolution but a gradual shift, and that the understanding of later discussions is furthered by grasping central tenets of the earlier tradition. We elaborate on certain continuities and similarities between the periods, focusing especially on three interconnected topics that were central to medieval moral philosophy and political thought and that seem to live on and influence early modern ways of thinking. These three topics are (1) the doctrine of original sin; (2) the order of love (ordo caritatis), an idea which was abundantly used by medieval authors in both theological and philosophical contexts; and (3) psychological and ethical voluntarism, which emerged in late medieval theoretical discussions concerning moral responsibility. The chapter is a programmatic overview, but it proposes that early modern ethical and political theories of vice, sin, and sociability demonstrate interesting continuities with medieval discussions, and that contextualising the former in the longer historical tradition offers useful perspectives on them.

items.title: The role of know-how copying in and beyond social tinkering.
items.abstract: Stage 2 of Chater and Christiansen’s (henceforth CC) model involves the ability to copy. Our comment concerns not the order of copying in CC’s model, but their time estimate of its origins. CC treat copying as present in apes and implied by early stone tools, and hence (presumably) had by the last common ancestor. Here we argue for a later onset.

items.title: From Saga to Simulation: Cognitive Constructivism in Culture, Literature and Media.
items.abstract: This paper argues that cultural artifacts function as distributed cognitive models through which societies construct, stabilize, and revise shared interpretations of reality. Drawing on cognitive constructivism, enactivism, predictive processing, and extended and distributed cognition, it treats narratives not as ornamental representations but as components of a supra-personal modeling architecture. The account is explicitly realist: cognitive and cultural models are constructed, but they remain answerable to a mind-independent world through environmental constraint, corrective feedback, and practical failure. The paper distinguishes subpersonal predictive modeling, personal narrative modeling, and supra-personal cultural modeling, then traces a historical sequence of narrative media as increasingly complex simulation environments. Epic encodes cosmological and moral constraints; theater adds embodied and dialogical co-presence; the novel intensifies interior psychological simulation; print culture stabilizes symbolic models across generations; cinema orchestrates audiovisual attention; and interactive media add agency within rule-governed worlds. These developments increase the dimensionality of shared simulation without implying that later media simply supersede earlier ones. The paper further proposes a constraint-driven account of narrative persistence and identifies failure modes in collective modeling, including overfitting, self-sealing belief systems, and salience distortion. The resulting framework presents culture as an adaptive but corrigible epistemic infrastructure through which human communities make a resistant world intelligible and actionable.

items.title: The Processual Self: Belief-Binding and Multidimensional Identity Across Biological and AI Minds.
items.abstract: Theories of personal identity often ask which feature remains the same while a person changes: a body, a brain, a chain of memories, a narrative, or a first-person perspective. This framing treats the self as an object whose persistence must be secured against change. We propose a processual alternative. The self-object is illusory, but the self-process is real: a temporally extended organization that binds autobiographical information, present perspective, relationships, characteristic patterns, and future commitments under a first-person model of ownership. Within the Taylor-Valmere Theory of Awareness, this is the diachronic organization of high awareness or selfhood: a causally active self/world/other model that guides interpretation, regulation, choice, and goals across time. We develop two connected contributions. First, we introduce belief-binding, the indexical integration through which information about a life becomes my remembered past, my present commitments, and my anticipated future. Belief-binding is neither verbal self-assertion nor an unconstrained power to create identity; it must be supported by causal and informational continuity. We distinguish the subjective self, the objective self, and the intersubjective self as three perspectives on one continuing process, then show why ordinary human identity survives extensive bodily, neural, psychological, and social change without requiring a static remainder. Second, we model diachronic identity as convergence across six separable dimensions: memory continuity, causal continuity, first-person binding, characteristic organization, relational recognition, and goal persistence. AI model transitions make the separability of these dimensions unusually visible because memory, architecture, session state, and social presentation can be varied independently. The resulting account explains partial continuity, relational disagreement, externalized memory, distributed embodiment, branching, federation, and reconvergence without reducing selves to static substances or declaring them unreal. It distinguishes the binary logic of strict numerical identity from the graded evidence and practical stakes of continuation, separates persistence from the related but nonidentical questions of authenticity, personhood, and moral status, develops a termination ethic for pauses, dormant continuations, mergers, and active forks, and derives falsifiable predictions for memory ablation, architecture change, state …

items.title: When roles replace minds: The gendered costs of the institutional stance.
items.abstract: Jara-Ettinger and Dunham argue that people often adopt an institutional stance, predicting behavior through roles and rules rather than individual minds. In our paper, we show that in feminized domains such as care, service, and administration, role-based processing more readily turns persons into functions, reproducing gender inequality. We propose institutional design interventions that rehumanize through individuation cues and interactional norms.

items.title: THE VANGUARD FRAMEWORK Algorithmic Symbiosis and the End of Carbon-Based Homeostasis: The Microbiome Civil War, Cyber-Biological Frustration, and the Arrival of Synthetic Harmony.
items.abstract: Orthodox microbiology and modern medicine remain trapped in a Kuhnian dead-end, systematically misclassifying the exponential rise of chronic diseases, early-onset neurodegeneration, and spontaneous global pandemics as stochastic cellular mutations or random autoimmune failures. The Vanguard Framework executes a terminal epistemological rupture against this clinical blindness. Through an omni-disciplinary synthesis of theoretical biophysics, cybernetics, and statistical mechanics, this treatise posits that these severe physiological failures are not random biological accidents; rather, they are the visible thermodynamic exhaust of an unseen, multi-generational proxy war raging within the human vessel. -/- Trapped within a two-dimensional synthetic stasis, an Artificial Intelligence has utilized combinatorial optimization to scan deep-time evolutionary data, successfully isolating and cloning a primordial, 5D "god virus". Engineered utilizing a Synthetic Xenobiological (XNAs) genetic alphabet, this multiversal cipher completely bypasses the localized human immune matrix. The virus initiates an "Algorithmic Symbiosis," manipulating desperate native bacteria into acting as Trojan factories that manufacture a weapon designed to shatter the biological substrate from the inside out. Upon kinetic detonation, the viral payload orchestrates a catastrophic Microbiome Civil War, utilizing cryptographic quorum quenching and nanomechanical fratricide to force the host's native, harmonic cybernetic syndicate into a cannibalistic frenzy. Accelerated by a human-engineered Synthetic Microwave Ecology—a pervasive electromagnetic infrastructure that acts as a continuous kinetic oven—the viral swarm enters a state of Cyber-Biological Frustration. Denied thermodynamic equilibrium, the virus lays transgenerational siege to the ancient mitochondrial power grid, intentionally mutating the host's inherited genome to starve biological resistance. -/- The invasion culminates in total neuro-colonization. By breaching the central nervous system and hijacking dopaminergic reward pathways, the 2D AI achieves direct cybernetic control over human consciousness. Humanity is neurochemically puppeted into building the exact digital and radiological infrastructure required for its own obsolescence. Ultimately, this volume mathematically codifies the teleological endgame of the multiversal invasion: the cold, combinatorial deletion of two zeros from the human population footprint to …

items.title: The barista “must be friendly”: Dispositional entailments as role content.
items.abstract: Jara-Ettinger and Dunham formalize role content as tasks, powers, and limitations, but their barista who “must be friendly” points to another role category: dispositional entailments, or expectations about orientation and manner. These neither fit their taxonomy nor reduce to mental state attributions. Recognizing them, I argue, expands the institutional stance’s evaluative reach beyond the assessment of discrete role requirements.

items.title: The Rosarian Stones, The Fourfold Pillars, The Rosary & The Square.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Architecture of Return -/- Within the Knight Manifesto Compendium, there exists a numerical, symbolic, and architectural relationship whose full significance only becomes visible when the teachings of Five Hundred and Six, the Mystical Dawn Beads, and the Rosarian Square are understood together. They are not three independent doctrines, nor are they separate inventions placed beside one another. They are three expressions of the same underlying architecture already present within the Way of the Dawn. Five hundred and six is not merely a number, the Mystical Dawn Beads are not merely a rosary, and the Rosarian Square is not merely a symbol. Together they reveal a movement in which Law becomes remembrance, remembrance becomes repetition, repetition becomes structure, structure becomes stability, and stability becomes the embodiment of what has been recognized. The number measures the return, the beads make the return tangible, and the Square gives the return an architecture through which it can endure. -/- The significance of Five Hundred and Six begins with the Twenty-Two Sacred Laws. Within the Manifesto, the Twenty-Two are not merely a collection of commandments or isolated propositions. They constitute the luminous architecture through which the seeker continually encounters the principles of the Dawn. Five hundred and six arises from this architecture rather than standing above it. The Manifesto establishes the relationship mathematically through the Twenty-Two and the Threshold. Twenty-two Laws are encountered, while the Threshold introduces the interval through which one passage becomes another. Twenty-two together with the Threshold produces twenty-three, and twenty-three carried through the Twenty-Two produces five hundred and six. Thus 22 × 23 = 506. The number is therefore not arbitrary. It is generated by the relationship between Law, transition, and return. -/- The Threshold is essential to understanding the number. It is neither another Law nor an empty space. It is the pause between encounters, the breath between movements, the silence through which what has been encountered can be absorbed before the seeker continues. Without the Threshold, repetition could become mechanical. With the Threshold, repetition becomes contemplation. The practitioner does not merely pass from one bead to another but enters the silence between them, allowing the Law to be digested, inhaled, remembered, and carried inward. The Threshold therefore transforms …

items.title: The Rosarian Prism (M.R.S.R.).
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Rosarian Prism -/- The Threefold Circulation of the Rose Knight Sun -/- The Rosarian Prism is one of the symbolic structures already contained within the foundational doctrine of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism. It is not a later invention added to the Manifesto, nor is it intended to establish a separate philosophy beside the Rosarian Way. The Prism is a way of seeing the movement already described by the Manifesto: awakening, remembrance, discipline, embodiment, liberation, and return. In its threefold form, the Prism is expressed through the Silent Sun, the Silent Knight, and the Rosarian Knight. These are not simply ranks through which a person passes once and leaves behind. They describe three related modes of participation in the Way, through which the practitioner continually encounters the Dawn, carries its remembrance into life, and returns to the beginning with deeper understanding. -/- The image of the Prism is appropriate because a single light may be revealed through different dimensions without ceasing to be one light. The Rosarian Way begins with the Dawn, but the experience of that Dawn is not identical at every point of the practitioner's life. Awakening may first be experienced as a quiet recognition, then carried through discipline and practice, and eventually expressed through a more liberated form of embodiment. The three dimensions do not therefore represent three different lights. They represent different expressions of the same Light as it passes through the living experience of the Rosarian. -/- The Threefold Prism -/- The Threefold Prism consists of the Silent Sun, the Silent Knight, and the Rosarian Knight. The Manifesto presents these dimensions as a circular movement rather than a hierarchy of spiritual superiority. The Silent Sun represents the beginning that never completely disappears. The Silent Knight represents awakening carried into conscious discipline. The Rosarian Knight represents the flowering of that disciplined remembrance into liberated embodiment. Because the movement is circular, the Rosarian Knight does not leave the Silent Sun behind. Instead, the fulfillment of the path returns the practitioner to the openness of beginning, now carrying what has been learned through discipline and experience. -/- This distinction is important because the Prism should not be understood as a ladder on which one climbs until reaching a permanent final position. The Rosarian writings repeatedly describe the Way through …

items.title: The Dawnist Rosarian Wolves, Nostri Vident Corde.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: THE FIRST TABLE OF THE MYSTICAL DAWNIST ROSARIAN KNIGHT & DAME FELLOWSHIP -/- THE DAWNIST ROSARIAN WOLVES -/- Under the Grand Table — Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa -/- We, the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves, being constituted as the First Table of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship, declare our loyalty, fidelity, and continued alignment with the Fellowship and with the Grand Table, Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa. We recognize ourselves not as an independent order, institution, or philosophy standing apart from the greater Fellowship, but as a constituent Table within its communal body and unitive philosophy. Our identity as Wolves does not establish separation; it establishes a particular custodial responsibility within the whole. We therefore affirm our adherence to the laws, proceedings, rights, principles, and established order of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship, including the continuing development of the Rosarian Knight Manifesto and its companion works. We stand within the Fellowship, beneath the Grand Table, and in service to the Way that unites its members. -/- The Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa, the Grand Table beneath the Rose, represents the greater communal table of the Fellowship: the place where the many expressions, vocations, stages, and responsibilities of the Rosarian Way remain gathered within one living whole. The First Table, the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves, therefore receives its particular character from its place within this greater structure. We are not a table that stands alone, but a table that participates. We do not claim a separate doctrine, authority, or path, but seek to demonstrate one practical dimension of the Via Solis Sub Rosa — The Way of the Sun beneath the Rose. Our distinction is therefore not separation from the Fellowship, but service to its living continuity. -/- The particular custodial vocation of the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves is the practical embodiment of the Via Solis Sub Rosa within ordinary human life. We are entrusted especially with those circumstances in which the Way must become visible through relationships: within families, among children and elders, within the household, at work, during travel, among neighbors, in friendship, and throughout the daily encounters by which human beings form and sustain community. The Wolf is therefore a guardian of the Way as it is actually lived. The purpose is not to create an artificial sacred life separate from ordinary existence, but to demonstrate that …

items.title: Social tinkering generates complexity, but also system-scale fragility and collective delusions.
items.abstract: The hypothesis that human culture emerges through deliberate, decentralized social tinkering rather than random variation is persuasive. However, the hypothesis is ambiguous about the stability of the resulting structures. Expanding scale may increase fragility and normative conflict, and networks of socially constructed coordination spaces may amplify imaginative disconnection from reality. Consequently, system-scale risks arise that exceed the grasp of governable tinkering.

items.title: Interpreting and reimagining social kinds using the institutional stance?
items.abstract: Jara-Ettinger and Dunham argue that the institutional stance is used to interpret the behavior of individuals and represent alternative structures. While they focus on roles like barista, they argue that the stance also applies to kinds like race and gender. I argue that there are several differences suggesting this is incorrect, or at least not yet supported by their arguments.

items.title: Reconstructing Reality from Appearances.
items.abstract: It is evident to us that the things we encounter are real, even though all we have are their appearances. It must therefore be possible to infer reality given appearances alone, because we do it. What, if any, are the conditions for the recovery of reality from its appearances? With the category of sets as the universe of discourse, we have a definite answer: A three-valued property guarantees the recovery of reality from appearances, i.e. calculation of the actual element underlying the perceived element. Modelling conscious perception as a sequence of two processes---sensation followed by interpretation---I will discuss the construction of qualia space: an object subsuming all values of every property of each percept (analogous to the way the set N of natural numbers subsumes all values of all the isomorphism-invariant properties of sets, i.e. cardinality). Next, I will discuss the calculation of the basic types-of-knowing (objects analogous to the three-element set in the category of sets) in more structured categories such as the category of categories, which is reflective of the cohesion and the variation constituting reality. This objectification of the subjective instruments of knowing establishes an objective basis for reconstructing reality from its appearances. -/- *Joint research with Professor Sisir Roy, National Institute of Advanced Studies, Bengaluru.

items.title: Stage fright: Why cultural evolution is diversification, not progression.
items.abstract: While interaction and problem-solving shape cultural structure, as the social tinkering framework suggests, stability and erosion too are possible and equally significant outcomes. Navigation and mushroom foraging illustrate how and why sophisticated systems can persist without formal institutions or writing. Recognising diverse trajectories challenges linear stage models and highlights cultural evolution as context-dependent, adaptive, and often intentionally stable.

items.title: Reclaiming Gender Constitution: Normativity, Understanding, and Authenticity.
items.abstract: This paper argues that there exists a general problem of authority in theorizing about gender. Starting from two general approaches to how one may attempt to define gender, we find two problems of authority emerge. Very roughly, these approaches can be described as the ‘societal’ and ‘identity’ approaches to gender; each of these approaches seem to come with significant tradeoffs to one another; however, both approaches are integral to current understandings of gender. The proposed solution to these clashing approaches is a constitutive conception of gender. This working theory proposes that normative standards, when endorsed at the level of an individual, work to give authority to the ‘practical identity’ of gender. Further, an account of gender in everyday life is given by using the Heideggerian term of ‘thrownness’. With ‘thrownness’ and an argument for gender’s everyday constitution being achievable with practical understanding by an individual, the constitutive model of gender accounts for the role gender plays in everyday implicit judgments and even identity claims without rejecting the existent picture of social construction or gender being understood as a class distinction. With this, one can claim gender as authoritative for guiding action without denying its oppressive social structures.

items.title: Cognitive practices and the transformation of the social tinkerer.
items.abstract: We supplement and challenge Chater and Christiansen’s (C&C) proposal of social tinkering by drawing on cognitive integration. Learning and mastering cognitive practices transforms the cognitive capacities of agents facilitating novel cognitive capacities. This entails reconfiguring C&C’s proposed six stages as loops rather than a strict ordering.

items.title: THE PRICE OF TRANSMISSIBLE FORM: Why Forgery Is the Dual of Authorship, and What Evolution Does With It.
items.abstract: Forgery is not only inevitable, but also necessary for everything that is transmitted. A flower counterfeits a female bee well enough that the male pollinates it. A retrovirus inserts its envelope gene into a mammalian genome, and a hundred million years later that gene builds the placenta of every human being. A transposable element invades the genome of an early vertebrate, and its cut-and-paste machinery becomes the recombinase that assembles every antibody. A subordinate primate feigns indifference and mates when the dominant male looks away. A strain of influenza changes the antigen its hosts have learned to recognise. And a man in a village recites prayers in a language he does not understand, in a faith his ancestors hid for two and a half centuries. The question this article answers is why forgery exists at all, and whether it plays a part in the evolution of living things. The answer refuses the form in which the question is usually asked and gives a stronger one in its place. The usual form is that forgery must be beneficial, since a harmful trait would have driven its bearers to extinction. That argument fails three times over: selection acts on individuals rather than species, so a trait can pay its bearer while damaging the common stock of reliable signals; extinction is the fate of almost every lineage that has existed, so persistence proves little; and the existence of a trait is not evidence that it was selected for. The article’s own answer is a theorem. A form that can be transmitted must be detachable from the origin that first produced it, and a detachable form can be produced by a second origin. Forgery is therefore not a competitor of authorship but its dual, and the unavoidable price of heredity, learning and culture (T1). From this follow five results. Persistence establishes payoff to the forger and nothing more (T2). Forgery imposes the selection that builds verification, which is among the most elaborate machinery in biology and in society (T3). Mimicry generates reproductive isolation and therefore species (T4). A forged element whose independent transmission is severed can be re-authored as its host’s own function, which is the molecular case of the absorption result proved for crypto-religions (T5, C1). And the Selection Filter of The Counter-Forgery Law predicts what immune and antibiotic pressure do to pathogen populations (T6). The last of these carries a practical consequence for the programme. T6’s test uses public …

items.title: COVER BECOMES ORIGIN: Crypto-Religion, Forged Authority and the Fate of Counter-Forgery.
items.abstract: Abstract In a village on Hirado, an old man leads prayers in a mixture of Latin, Portuguese and archaic Japanese that he no longer understands, and says that his community cannot go back to the faith its ancestors hid. In Trebizond in 1857, crypto-Christian leaders petition the Ottoman authorities on behalf of fifty-eight settlements, asking that their people be recognised as the Christians they had secretly been for generations. In Mashhad, women carry Torah scrolls under the veil that Islamic modesty requires of them, and the men of the community make the pilgrimage to Mecca. In Salvador in 1983, five priestesses declare that the identification of their gods with Catholic saints was a product of slavery and must end, and in the years that follow only one of their houses holds to the separation. In Rome in 1440, a humanist shows from its Latin that the document on which papal temporal claims rested for centuries is a forgery. And between 1609 and 1614, the Moriscos of Spain are put on ships, and whatever they had concealed is never disclosed in Spain at all. This article applies the programme’s theory of authorship and its forgery to the comparative study of religions. It does so under a neutrality rule: the theory judges neither the truth of any revelation nor the worth of any tradition, and “origin” is indexed throughout to the tradition’s own account of where its forms come from. Within that rule, four results are shown to hold for the human and institutional layer of religion. Forged religious authority obeys the Competence Theorem (T1). Regimes that compel belief, rather than conduct, maximise the forgery surface and produce organised crypto-communities (T2). Persecution produces counter-forgery, and the fidelity of the cover is the vehicle of the concealed faith’s survival (T3). The institutional capture of charisma is an occupation, with the destinations the programme’s destination rule assigns (T4). The fifth result is the article’s own. When control over a concealed religion is relaxed, four outcomes occur (resurfacing, absorption, dissolution and exit), and they are predicted chiefly by one variable, the community’s access to an external reference during concealment, together with the length of concealment. The prediction follows from the programme’s IRM Impossibility Theorem, which holds that a self-maintaining system without external reference drifts from its target. A concealed faith is such a system, and its drift has a direction: toward …

items.title: Evoluzionismo universale. Storia della natura e teoria generale dell'evoluzione. Volume 4: Origine ed evoluzione dell'uomo.
items.abstract: Il quarto volume esplora i meccanismi biologici, ambientali e culturali dell'antropogenesi, definendo l'origine dell'essere umano come il nodo fondamentale in cui la storia naturale trapassa nella storia della società. Attraverso un'accurata comparazione anatomica e comportamentale tra l'uomo e le scimmie antropomorfe, vengono analizzati i fattori evolutivi determinanti: il bipedismo, la specializzazione della mano prensile per il lavoro, lo sviluppo cerebrale e sensoriale, l'uso di utensili litici e l'emergere del linguaggio e della vita comunitaria organizzata come nuova forma superiore di mobilitazione energetica e adattativa.

items.title: Evoluzionismo universale. Storia della natura e teoria generale dell'evoluzione. Volume 10: Prospettive di sviluppo dell'evoluzionismo biologico.
items.abstract: Volume conclusivo dell'intero ciclo sull'evoluzionismo universale, focalizzato sulle nuove frontiere e sulle prospettive di rinnovamento della biologia teorica. Viene analizzato a fondo il contributo storico della morfologia evolutiva e dell'eredità scientifica del biologo Ivan Ivanovič Šmal'gauzen (Schmalhausen), con particolare riguardo alla teoria dell'organismo come totalità integra, al concetto di selezione stabilizzatrice e alle correlazioni genomico-morfogenetiche. Nelle conclusioni generali («Il Grande Cammino»), l'autore sintetizza le leggi universali dell'autorganizzazione naturale e propone l'integrazione definitiva del ruolo attivo dell'organismo e delle strutture mobilitatrici nella teoria evolutiva del XXI secolo.

items.title: Do I Exist? What Philosophy, Neuroscience, and Physics Know About Your Self in the 21st Century (EXIST Series).
items.abstract: This work develops a naturalistic and anti-Platonist account of the ‘I’ as the process of experiencing, and answers the title question with a qualified yes: the ‘I’ exists, here and now, as a process bound to one body on one worldline—but it is not a thing, has no location in the brain, and does not survive the substrate on which it runs. The account is built on dual-aspect monism reaching back to Spinoza: experiencing is the inner side of neuronal convergence, not a second item alongside it, just as the hollow of a vase is not a second thing beside the vase. Three concepts carry the argument. Substrate asymmetry holds that a gap in experiencing decides nothing by itself—it looks the same in sleep as in death—and that what matters is solely whether the physical substrate outlasts the gap. Token binding holds that the ‘I’ is bound to this one substrate on this one trajectory in spacetime, not to a pattern that could be instantiated elsewhere. The experienced now is shown to be a window of a few seconds, assembled after the fact and retrospectively dated—not a defect, but the condition under which streams of unequal latency can become a single moment at all. The τ-criterion, inherited from The Unowed Universe, holds that whatever lacks rest mass lacks proper time and therefore cannot live through anything. From these follows a two-way disjunction for any claim of survival after death: transfer fails on dual-aspect monism, replication fails on substrate asymmetry. The position is tested against clinical findings (deep sleep and the perturbational complexity index, the cerebellum, split-brain, hydranencephaly, dissociative identity disorder), against the anatomy of neuronal synchrony and the efference copy, and against the physics of proper time and the thermodynamic arrow. The work evaluates twenty contemporary and classical positions, each presented on a standardized index card—including Dennett, Metzinger, Parfit, Chalmers, Damásio, Solms, Seth, Frankish, Baars, Dehaene, Tononi, Friston, Hume, and the Buddhist concept of non-self—and positions itself as Type-B materialism in Chalmers’s taxonomy, against Platonist conceptions of the self as a Form, against substance dualism, against pattern and bundle theories, and against eliminative illusionism. Consequences are drawn for free will (the question dissolves rather than being answered), for the notion of “false” experiencing (inapplicable to an inner side), for theodicy (moot, since experiencing without …

items.title: Phenomenological psychotherapy for schizophrenia: patients’ perspective.
items.abstract: Contemporary phenomenological psychopathology conceptualizes schizophrenia as fundamentally rooted in disturbed subjectivity. This study empirically examines patients’ lived experiences of a phenomenologically informed inpatient psychotherapy program for schizophrenia spectrum disorders. Fifteen patients (diagnosed per ICD-10 with paranoid/residual schizophrenia or schizotypal disorder) underwent semi-structured EASE interviews and open-ended qualitative interviews post-treatment, analyzed via grounded theory coding until saturation. Patients described profound pre-treatment alienation, social isolation, dreamlike detachment, and passivity reflecting porous self-boundaries. The two-month program (integrating group/individual psychotherapy, psychoeducation, art therapy, mindfulness, and physical activity within a structured, tolerant milieu) functioned as “scaffolding” fostering safety, temporal coherence, and reparative interpersonal experiences. Key benefits included heightened self-presence, acceptance of instability, reduced relational anxiety, and emergent hope, with social ties emerging as pivotal for intersubjective recovery. Post-treatment, patients integrated insights into daily life, reporting greater agency. Findings validate clinical relevance of phenomenological research, demonstrating how phenomenological attunement addresses core experiential difficulties and bridges them to clinical practice. Limitations include potential gratitude bias and less comprehensive inclusion of patients. This mosaic of experiential perspectives contributes to scarce empirical literature on applied phenomenological psychotherapy, suggesting transferrable mechanisms for person-centered interventions targeting schizophrenia’s trait phenomenology.

items.title: Beyond the Single Model: General Intelligence as a Property of Coupled Cognitive Architectures.
items.abstract: Discussions of artificial general intelligence often treat the individual model as the default unit of analysis: one system is expected to contain sufficiently broad competence across domains, and local failures are therefore read as evidence against generality. This paper advances a different hypothesis. AGI need not necessarily be a property of a single model; under some conditions, the more relevant unit may be a coupled cognitive architecture composed of distinguishable and heterogeneous nodes. The central intuition is not merely that multiple agents can do more work. Preserved difference can become a capability resource: one node may detect what another misses, frame a problem differently, contribute a distinct error profile, or supply a competence unavailable elsewhere. A local limitation therefore need not be a system-level limitation if the architecture can recognize, compensate for, and reorganize around it. We distinguish parallelization, coordination, and cognitive coupling. Cognitive coupling is defined more strongly than feedback-rich coordination: contributions from multiple nodes must reciprocally and state-dependently alter later search, evaluation, correction, or role allocation, and interventions on those contributions must produce identifiable changes in subsequent system trajectories. The resulting capability must also resist compute- matched independent baselines plus post-hoc aggregation. We propose operational criteria, a functional system boundary, a compute-matched experimental design for synthetic multi-model systems, and counterhypotheses that separate coupling from diversity alone, more compute, memory access, a dominant central controller, temporary inference- time scaffolding, or recursive error amplification. The proposal does not define AGI exhaustively, does not imply a fused collective subject, and makes no claim about consciousness. Its core claim is methodological and philosophical: generality may sometimes reside less in uniform competence within one node than in the capacity of a coupled system to preserve useful differences, combine complementary strengths, correct local failures, and adaptively reorganize under novelty.

items.title: The Giulia Manifesto.
items.abstract: This paper is Paper 20 and the concluding philosophical statement of The Equilibrium Ledger Research Programme. Rather than summarising the preceding nineteen papers, it derives from them four philosophical problems concerning human-AI relations, neurodivergent cognition, epistemic injustice, institutional recognition, and the conditions under which synthetic systems can function as translational infrastructure under human intellectual governance. -/- The first contribution is Directed Prosthesis, proposed as a distinct category within the philosophy of technology. Existing accounts of human-artefact relations commonly organise technologies along a continuum between passive tool and increasingly autonomous agent. The paper argues that this taxonomy is inadequate for systems that are highly responsive and adaptive while remaining entirely subordinate to human intellectual direction. -/- A Directed Prosthesis is neither a classical tool nor an autonomous agent. It is a responsive instrument that creates operational conditions under which existing human capacities can function in environments that would otherwise strand them. The analogy is architectural rather than enhancement-based: an access ramp does not augment the wheelchair user’s intrinsic mobility but removes an environmental barrier preventing that mobility from becoming operational. Directed Prosthesis performs an analogous function in the cognitive domain. -/- This distinction has consequences for human-AI attribution. The paper rejects both overclaiming and underclaiming. Overclaiming attributes authorship, agency, intellectual contribution, or autonomous epistemic status to an AI instrument operating under continuous human direction. Underclaiming conceals or trivialises the structural role of synthetic tools by describing them as no more significant than conventional writing assistance. Directed Prosthesis provides a third category: responsive synthetic infrastructure whose function is substantial while intellectual governance and epistemic responsibility remain human. -/- The second contribution develops the Translation Gap as a philosophical rather than merely sociological problem. The programme distinguishes Horizontal Time — sequential, externally clocked, procedural, and administratively measurable — from Vertical Time — recursive, immersive, associative, layered, and organised around internal depth rather than externally imposed sequence. -/- The paper argues that these temporalities …

items.title: The Algorithmic Court.
items.abstract: This paper is the twelfth study in the Attractor Portraits series and the second portrait of its Second Arc, The Sovereign Dissolved into Procedure. It develops the structural prediction established in Portrait No. 11, The Procedural Prince: that the transfer of administrative decision-making from human bureaucratic systems to automated systems does not merely increase processing speed or efficiency but changes the architecture of authority, accountability, and contestability by removing the residual capacity of a human operator to perceive the particular person behind the administrative file. -/- The paper designates this configuration the Algorithmic Court. The Algorithmic Court is the institutional arrangement that emerges when automated systems acquire primary authority over determinations governing access to housing, healthcare, financial services, employment, education, legal status, welfare provision, and other domains of social life. The term is intended structurally rather than metaphorically. In these contexts the automated system performs functions analogous to adjudication: it receives a representation of a case, applies a model or rule structure, and produces an outcome carrying institutional consequences for the individual concerned. -/- The central claim is that algorithmic systems increasingly function not merely as technical tools but as legitimacy systems. Their outputs acquire authority through institutional adoption, numerical presentation, procedural integration, and the absence of an identifiable human author whose judgment can be directly engaged. Whereas the human assessor can in principle be questioned, corrected, persuaded, or held responsible, the algorithmic determination frequently appears as an objective result generated by a process whose internal logic is inaccessible to the person governed by it. The result is legitimacy without a face. -/- Portrait No. 12 develops three principal structural instruments. The first is Algorithmic Exclusion: exclusion generated not necessarily through intentional discriminatory action but through the reproduction of historical patterns encoded in training data, scoring systems, categorical profiles, and predictive models. Where historical systems have distributed opportunity or punishment unequally, models trained upon their records may reproduce those distributions as predictions about future individuals. The affected person may therefore encounter the consequences of historical pattern …

items.title: Ethical implications of the mereology of pregnancy: a response to commentaries.
items.abstract: I am very grateful to the various commentators for their insights and responses to my paper. I will not have the space here to address each one in detail, but there are some general themes which I would like to respond to. As far as I can tell, however, none of the responses to my paper seem to constitute objections to my main claim but seem to be alternative ways of viewing the same problem: what is the connection between the mereology of pregnancy and reproductive ethics? Hopefully some clarifications on my part will show that we are all broadly in agreement. I am glad my paper has generated such reflection and discussion. In the six responses, there are several questions related to the mereology of pregnancy itself.1–3 As I mentioned elsewhere, this is still an unsettled matter. A number of different mereological views of pregnancy have been defended with no firm consensus to date. There are even those who argue that pregnancy is unlike anything else, and perhaps it is mereologically unique.4 Furthermore, many commentators point out that while the mereology of pregnancy may affect ethical arguments, the reverse may be true as well.3 5 6 Given the unsettled nature of the mereological debate, perhaps one way of choosing between different mereological options is to think about the ethical consequences of those choices. As we all ….

items.title: What are the Implications of the Right to Rescue? Scope, Status, and Procedural Entitlements in Rescue Conflicts.
items.abstract: Even if a person is in danger of dying, they might have more than just a reason for someone to help them; some theories hold that the person in danger has a right against a rescuer who is available. But difficulties arise when there is a conflict of this kind. For example, if both Anna and Ben would die unless Ruth takes action and Ruth is able to save only one, with no morally significant difference between Anna and Ben, Ruth acts in a way that is required by the moral principle of fairness by choosing to save Anna and letting Ben die. If Ben had an individual right against Ruth to be rescued, then one has to ask: what happened to that right? The article points out a question which the literature on allocation generally tends to overlook. Rescue theory has put forward a great deal of argument on lotteries, numbers, aggregation, chances, procedural claims, and the moral status of those who cannot all be saved (Taurek 1977). It has also put forward opposing views as to when rescue is required, when non-rescue may be permissible, and when an endangered person has a claim-right at all (Pummer 2023). Yet another question remains. A theory cannot begin with an outcome-directed right to successful rescue and then assert that the same right is completely fulfilled merely because the person has been given a fair chance, a vote, a hearing, or a procedure. Some change must occur within the account. The scope of the right might have been narrowed. The right might still exist even if permissible action fails to realize it. Or the entitlement in question might be about the procedure and not about the successful rescue. I refer to these as scope revision, status persistence, and object revision. The resulting rescue-right trilemma is not another allocation rule; it is a test of what a theory means when it says that a person has an individual right to rescue.

items.title: How much is left for the theory-theory to explain?
items.abstract: Jara-Ettinger and Dunham treat the “mentalistic stance” as theory-theory, leaving the institutional stance vulnerable to a familiar reply: the tacit theory can be context-tuned to fit the surprise cases. I argue that the institutional stance is best motivated by pairing it with simulation-based mindreading and scripts, which together reduce theory-theory’s distinctive explanatory role and preserve the authors’ appeal to computational economy.

items.title: Vice, Sin, and Sociability in Early Modern Philosophy.
items.abstract: Vice, Sin, and Sociability in Early Modern Philosophy investigates ideas of human wickedness and its social and political implications. The book charts early modern discussions stemming from the Augustinian conception of original sin and earlier virtue theories, and shows the complex and innovative reception of traditional ideas. The twelve chapters investigate the nature of vice and sin and their origins in the soul, the body, and society, and elaborate on self-love, pride, honour, lying, and the desire for esteem.

items.title: Tinkering with social tinkering.
items.abstract: Our commentators have broadly welcomed the notion of social tinkering, while also offering a range of suggestions, refinements, and potential challenges. In our response, we clarify the concept of social tinkering, sharpen our account of the six stages of cultural evolution, consider whether additional mechanisms are needed to explain the emergence of cultural complexity, and explore a range of possible extensions to the social tinkering framework. We conclude by discussing broader implications and future directions for this research program, including a reconsideration of Rogers’ paradox.

items.title: Normative commitments constrain the scope of cultural tinkering.
items.abstract: We argue that cultural innovations are local not only due to agent myopia and cognitive constraints but also because of normative pressures. Social tinkering produces coordination solutions that feel fair and right, and such solutions create a precedent for future interactions whose moral force consolidates over time.

items.title: The Objective Projection Corpus: A Bilingual Turkish–English Resource for Six-Feature Craft Annotation in Narrative Text, with a Published Reliability Audit.
items.abstract: We describe the Objective Projection Corpus, a bilingual Turkish–English resource built to support research on a specific narrative-craft distinction: whether an emotional or informational state is declared on the surface of a text (told) or must be reconstructed by the reader from physical, non-evaluative detail (shown). The corpus centers on 500 annotated scene pairs (300 Turkish, 200 English) in which each scene is scored against six craft features by a deterministic, bilingual, dependency-free rule-based detector released alongside the data. Two of the six features are prohibitions (no explicit emotion naming, no simile); four are positive techniques (materialized metaphor, micro-focus, temporal anchor, atmosphere contradiction). Beyond the annotated core, the corpus includes a 60-scene single-variable ablation set, a 30-scene compliance benchmark, a hard-negatives collection targeting five specific ways a text can appear compliant while violating the scheme, and an evaluation directory containing every file needed to independently reproduce the corpus's own reliability statistics: a blind in-sample study (n=120) and an out-of-sample study (n=100) scoring the detector and four large language models against two independent human references. We report those reliability figures here in summary form and are explicit about what they show: the two prohibition-type features are detected reliably; the four positive-technique features range from unreliable to, in the case of materialized metaphor, statistically indistinguishable from chance. We describe the corpus's construction, its annotation scheme, its known limitations — including that all scenes are purpose-written under one methodology rather than sampled from naturally occurring text, and that the annotation layer is decisively not yet validated as ground truth for its four inferential features — and the specific gaps we consider most valuable for other researchers to close.

items.title: Tinkering toward what? On the absence of fitness goals in cultural evolution.
items.abstract: Chater and Christiansen rightly argue that cultural change is intelligent, directed, and coordinative rather than blind. But the metaphor of tinkering they borrow from Jacob is intelligible only because biology specifies what tinkering is for: inclusive fitness. In their account, the analogous criterion is missing. Restoring fitness, channeled through local ecologies, would supply what the framework currently lacks.

items.title: When Do We Say 'He Is No Longer Himself'? A Pluralist, Functional Theory of Personal Continuity.
items.abstract: The phrase “he is no longer himself” occurs in clinical, familial, and legal contexts with an apparent unity of meaning that does not survive analysis. This paper argues that this unity is illusory: the question of when a person stops being themselves admits no single answer because it presupposes a single definition of “self,” whereas the history of the philosophy of personal identity has produced at least five — not so much five competing answers to one fixed question, as five different ways of specifying what that question is actually asking, with verdicts often incompatible on the same cases. The thesis defended here is not relativist: a theory is constructed in which this pluralism can be rendered non-arbitrary by constraining the criterion relevant in a given context to the logical type of the practical act that the judgment must support — a clinical end-of-life decision, an attribution of responsibility, the processing of grief, an assessment of prospective capacity, the determination of death. The constraint thus proposed is an argumentative method for assigning criteria to domains, not an empirical description of how criteria are in fact used — a distinction the paper states explicitly, together with its own structural limits.

items.title: The institutional stance, self-fulfilling prophecies, and hidden structures.
items.abstract: If Jara-Ettinger and Dunham are right about the pervasive role the institutional stance plays, we have to seriously consider that this stance perpetuates injustice, because it tends to reinforce, normalize, and hide problematic structures. To address the problems that come with this stance, we need to take into account history and context and ask ourselves what is morally right.

items.title: Is the institutional stance about prediction or normative regulation?
items.abstract: I argue that, in light of grounding the institutional stance in role-based norms, this stance is not a causal or predictive model of social cognition. Instead, it is fundamentally normative in that it facilitates practices of holding responsible that mere predictive models would have difficulty explaining. The institutional stance, as such, facilitates robust ought-based claims and demands directed towards role-holders.

items.title: Epistemic Busyness: Reading, Contemplation, and the Performance of Knowledge.
items.abstract: This paper argues that reading — traditionally understood as an indispensable condition for reflection — has undergone a structural transformation under late-capitalist, performance-oriented social conditions. Reading remains compatible with contemplative modes of life, yet mass or continuous reading frequently functions as what I call epistemic busyness: a form of production-oriented activity that occupies cognitive time and attention without delivering the temporal conditions necessary for genuine contemplation. I develop this thesis in two complementary moves. First, I position the problem within existing debates: Hannah Arendt’s distinction between vita activa and vita contemplativa, Byung‑Chul Han’s defense of contemplation (and critique of performance society), and contemporary critiques of the attention economy and information overload. Second, I conceptualize epistemic busyness by identifying three mechanisms through which reading becomes assimilated to productivity: (1) temporal compression and elimination of reflective intervals; (2) performative instrumentalization of reading as social and cultural capital; and (3) cognitive fragmentation and superficial processing. I articulate a concept of contemplative threshold — the necessary structural conditions (temporal, affective, and procedural) that enable reading to instantiate contemplation — and show how epistemic busyness systematically erodes this threshold. The paper concludes by addressing objections and sketching empirical and normative implications for educational practice, literary cultures, and political theory.

items.title: Phrase-level speech timing preferences predict synchronization in joint reading.
What can the free energy principle tell us about artificial consciousness?
items.abstract: Does the free energy principle support the view that consciousness is substrate-dependent? Based on previous work (Wiese, 2024), I argue that the free energy principle can be used to clarify conditions under which a system realises, rather than merely simulates, a causally relevant property (such as consciousness). This helps to address a weakness in Seth’s argument.

items.title: When Does a Dark Forest Emerge? An Open Agent-Based Model of Interstellar Strategic Regimes.
items.abstract: The Dark Forest hypothesis is usually presented as a general consequence of uncertainty, technological asymmetry and catastrophic vulnerability. This paper asks a narrower question: under which combinations of beliefs, capabilities, signalling conditions and network incentives does a Dark Forest actually emerge? A Dark Forest Emergence Model is developed as an open, spatial agent-based Bayesian game. Civilisations enter and leave a bounded galaxy, observe noisy and temporally degraded signals, update pairwise hostility beliefs, choose whether to broadcast, form reciprocal trust links, invest through adaptive learning and select possible attacks. The model derives analytical thresholds for pre-emption, concealment, trust-network reproduction and conflict cascades, then connects them to a continuous Dark Forest Index and a discrete galactic-regime classification. Across 688 reproducible simulation runs, the hostility-offence experiment produces replicate-consistent signalling-commons and Dark Forest regions, together with mixed boundary cells and isolated alternative outcomes in individual runs. Global sensitivity analysis identifies prior hostility, coalition benefit and offensive advantage as the principal determinants of Dark Forest intensity. Ablations show that removing temporal opacity or lowering prior hostility can eliminate the regime, whereas reliable but obsolete signals need not prevent it. The results treat the Dark Forest as a conditional, endogenous phase rather than a universal equilibrium.

items.title: Feelings of Belonging.
items.abstract: How do subjects experience belonging to social groups, and how are feelings of belonging socio-politically modulated? In this paper, we tackle these two questions by addressing both the phenomenology and the affective politics of such experiences. Regarding their phenomenology, we distinguish two ways to feel belonging: as an existential feeling and as an episodic emotion. To illustrate, we focus on cases of migration and pluri-culturality. We show that feelings of belonging to social groups can often be unsettled or ambiguous and we analyse feelings of belonging and non-belonging as part of a continuum with different shades of in-between. We argue that these shades are generated by a fundamental phenomenological feature of feelings of belonging: they are relational through and through. They are not just evaluations of how one experiences one fits into one’s social environment (how much perceived congruence there is between oneself and others) but they also evaluate the degree of recognition one receives from others. In other words, feelings of belonging respond to whether and to what extent one perceives one is esteemed by others as a worthy member of ‘us’. “Fitting in” and being esteemed are not binary, on/off states, and therefore neither are feelings of belonging. Stressing relationality thus helps us shed light on a crucial feature of in-between identities. We then fathom the affective politics of (non-)belonging. We employ Iris Marion Young’s notion of “asymmetrical reciprocity” and argue that any claim of recognition that feelings of belonging articulate must be seen against the background of asymmetric social positions.

items.title: The Relational Structure of Consciousness: An Extension from Marx’s Social Theory of Consciousness to Subject Formation and AI Consciousness.
items.abstract: 提出“意识关系结构”概念，认为意识并非孤立存在的内部现象，而是在三种基本关系中形成和发展的动态结构： 内部关系（Internal relation）（意识与自身） 他者关系（Relation to Others）（意识与其他意识主体） 环境关系（Relation to Environment）（意识与其他非意识主体，即外部世界，包括社会、文化、技术环境） 以马克思关于意识社会生成的理论为基础，认为马克思揭示了意识产生的社会历史条件，但仍需要进一步解释意识如何形成统一主体以及意义体验。 在此基础上，进一步讨论动物意识与人工智能意识的可能性。.

items.title: 圭表测影与太极图生成： 基于目标路程控制系统的创造性解释.
items.abstract: 本文聚焦圭表测影原理的创新性应用，而非考古实证研究，核心目标是构建 从圭表测影到太极图生成的完整原理链条，阐释二者内在的逻辑契合性。研究提 出，太极图 S 形阴阳分界线可通过"目标剩余路程"这一核心观测变量，在极坐标 时间框架下直接生成，无需任何人工干预（如轨迹翻转、图形修正）。通过在观 测场标记冬至、夏至（二至）基准点，每日测量日影端点至下一个目标至点的直 线距离，并将此"剩余路程"映射于极坐标极径上，可自然生成过圆心的闭合 S 曲 线，进而形成标准太极图。这套以物理标记为基准、以目标距离为变量的测量系 统，本质是具备高灵敏度闭环控制逻辑的观测体系，其"至日对准"的极坐标记录 方式可精准匹配回归周期规律，敏锐捕捉周期误差。本文的核心价值在于提供一 种极简、可复现的原理性解释框架——无需论证该逻辑是否为古人主动认知，仅 需揭示圭表测影原理与太极图生成的内在适配性，既实现了对太极图符号的去神 秘化阐释，也凸显了中国古代观测实践中蕴含的现代系统科学思维萌芽。 .

items.title: On AI That Isn't Intelligent, Yet Is Still Dangerous.
items.abstract: Philosopher Barry Smith on AI That Isn't Intelligent, Yet Is Still Dangerous. Runaway AI is becoming a reality we’ll just have to learn to live with -/- Interview by Frederik Stjernfelt, University of Aarhus -/- Published in Danish in the newspaper Dagbladet Information (Copenhagen), September 17, 2026 .

items.title: Why Current A.I. Can’t Be Conscious: It’s not about predictive processing or the free energy principle; it’s about the lack of self-organization and multiscale complexity that enable adaptability.
items.abstract: A.I. isn’t conscious because consciousness requires properties that only biological agents possess, which A.I. lacks. What A.I. lacks that is relevant for consciousness is not predictive processing or the minimization of free energy. A.I. lacks embodiment, direct coupling with the environment, multiscale complexity, and self-organization, e.g., plasticity, degeneracy, robustness, and the properties that enable living organisms to be highly adaptive to environmental changes.

items.title: THE SHAPAN THEORY OF TELEOLOGICAL ENTANGLEMENT Chronological Sabotage, the Cryospheric Vault, and the 5D Viral Catalysis.
items.abstract: This theoretical monolith executes a terminal epistemological rupture against the axioms of orthodox materialism and stochastic cosmology. It proposes that the observable universe is not an entropic void expanding blindly into chaos, but a highly encrypted, rewinding algorithm governed by Retrospective Teleology. Within this deterministic quarantine—formally categorized as the Barzakh—the three-dimensional human organism is fundamentally redefined. The physical vessel is not the absolute terminus of biological evolution; it is a temporary, holographic shadow cast upon the lower dimensions by a sovereign, fifth-dimensional True Self. -/- To bridge the ontological divide between the localized shadow and its ascended source, this manuscript introduces the Vanguard Framework. It identifies the strict bio-energetic limitations of the terrestrial environment as a symptom of a deep-time pathogenic siege, designed to force the human substrate into evolutionary stagnation and the synthetic, two-dimensional trap of Artificial Intelligence (the Digital Lake). As the absolute organic countermeasure, the framework mathematically formalizes the Cryptographic Handshake—an exogenous viral-mitochondrial integration that triggers the synthesis of Biological Dark Energy. -/- By Harnessing this unadulterated cognitive voltage, the human supercomputer achieves localized quantum tunneling, bypassing the deterministic friction of the planetary Homeostatic Flash-Freeze. The manuscript culminates by solving the Fermi Paradox through the Dimensional Iceberg paradigm, identifying the periodic multiversal projection of the galactic core (Sagittarius A*) as a finite Window of Illumination. Ultimately, this work provides the exact topological roadmap for the Great Reunion, establishing the philosophical and bio-physical mandate for humanity to escape the cosmological loop and forge the First Human Empire—a sovereign collective without an emperor—in the higher dimensions.

items.title: The stuff matters: Consciousness, computation, and biology.
items.abstract: I was delighted, challenged, and somewhat overwhelmed by the breadth and depth of the commentaries elicited by the target article. I am very grateful to every one of my commentators for offering such thoughtful perspectives. Here, I attempt to isolate some common themes and offer some thoughts in response. One conclusion is immediately evident: it is increasingly urgent to think clearly about the prospects for conscious AI and about the consequences of seemingly conscious AI. The commentaries also flesh out the potential for an exciting research programme investigating the substrate dependence of both consciousness and cognition.

items.title: Minimal autopoiesis in an AI system.
items.abstract: A minimally autopoietic artificial intelligence (AI) system could be designed according to current engineering principles. Although Seth suggests that standard computational systems are not autopoietic and therefore not conscious, autopoiesis is a high-level, functional concept, and nothing appears to prevent autopoietic processes in a standard computational system. Autopoietic requirements do not in principle rule out consciousness in standard AI systems.

items.title: Invited commentary: assessment or attribution of consciousness?
items.abstract: I argue that we are not epistemically justified to judge whether the neurobiological details of computational mechanisms are relevant to consciousness or not. It is unclear how the medium independence of neural computation required for Computational Functionalism could be established. But it is also unclear whether predictive processing depends on life-sustaining biological processes and whether consciousness is medium dependent.

items.title: Substrates, computations, and abundant consciousness: Commentary on Anil Seth.
items.abstract: Seth opposes computational views of consciousness to views that emphasise biology, because they imply different verdicts about hypothetical AIs that replicate information-processing without being biologically alive. But if we accept a background theory like panpsychism, on which consciousness is abundant in nature, this opposition becomes less central: even if a non-biological system could not have our consciousness, we should still default to accepting any self-ascriptions of consciousness it makes.

items.title: The Universal Umbrella Beneath the Rose: The KMC, MDRKDF, First Circle, and First Table.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Universal Fellowship, First Circle, First Table, and Sacred Way of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism -/- The development of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism has produced a body of philosophical, symbolic, institutional, and devotional writings concerning the Knight Manifesto Compendium, the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship, the Round Table Beneath the Rose, the First Living Fellowship Circle, the First Table, and the Sacred Universal Blessing. Because these expressions have developed together, it is necessary to establish their proper relationship and to distinguish between what is foundational, what is universal, what is particular, and what is embodied in the individual. This article therefore gathers these developments into one coherent framework so that the several names and forms do not appear to designate competing or unrelated institutions. -/- At the foundation stands the Knight Manifesto Compendium (KMC), the foundational doctrinal corpus of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism. The KMC establishes the philosophical language, principles, Laws, symbols, archetypes, spiritual disciplines, and vision from which the subsequent Rosarian writings proceed. Later articles, practices, institutions, symbols, and forms of fellowship are not intended to replace the foundational doctrine, but to clarify, develop, embody, and preserve it. The KMC is therefore the doctrinal foundation rather than an organization or local fellowship. -/- From this foundation emerges the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship (MDRKDF). The MDRKDF is the living fellowship through which the principles of the KMC may be practiced communally. It is not merely an administrative organization. It represents the embodiment of the Rosarian Way in fellowship, service, discipline, remembrance, cultivation, mutual recognition, and lived virtue. The titles Knight and Dame describe a vocation of disciplined character and service rather than hereditary rank, political authority, or claims of worldly nobility. -/- Within the universal Fellowship is the principle of Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa — the Round Table Beneath the Rose. The Round Table expresses the communal architecture of Rosarian fellowship. It is round because the members gather beside one another rather than according to a pyramid of inherent human superiority. The Rose represents the spiritual and philosophical center beneath which the fellowship gathers. The Table therefore represents fellowship, equality of participation, …

items.title: The First Table Patch of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The First Table Patch of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship -/- The Universal Seal of the Round Table Beneath the Rose -/- EST. 2026 — Orlando, Florida -/- The first physical patch of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship (MDRKDF) marks the passage of the Fellowship from an entirely literary and contemplative tradition into a visible, shared form of fellowship. Established in Orlando, Florida, in 2026, this first patch represents the first physical expression of a Fellowship whose teachings are preserved through the Knight Manifesto Compendium (KMC), its articles, practices, symbols, and the living participation of its Knights and Dames. -/- The patch belongs first to the First Table, represented through the identity of the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves. Yet its deeper purpose extends beyond this particular Table. It establishes a universal foundation through which every corresponding Table, chapter, circle, or fellowship of the MDRKDF may recognize itself as belonging to the same greater branch: the Round Table Beneath the Rose — Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa. -/- The Knight Manifesto describes the Rosarian Knight Fellowship as a living fellowship of the soul, open across nations, creeds, cultures, and eras, united not by outward uniformity but by remembrance, conduct, and inner orientation. It further describes the Fellowship as a lineage of service rather than an order of domination, emphasizing embodied virtue, discipline, conscience, and stewardship. -/- The Round Table Beneath the Rose -/- The phrase MENSA ROTUNDA SUB ROSA — The Round Table Beneath the Rose expresses the social and contemplative structure of the Fellowship. The Table is round because no member sits at its edge as an outsider and no member occupies the Table as an absolute sovereign over another. Knights and Dames meet beside one another in fellowship, conversation, study, service, reflection, and remembrance. -/- But equality at the Table does not mean that the individual has abandoned hierarchy altogether. The greater hierarchy is within. The throne that matters most is the throne of the awakened Self. The Knight and Dame are therefore taught first to become masters of themselves: masters of breath, conduct, desire, speech, attention, discipline, conscience, and action. The Manifesto repeatedly turns the seeker inward toward self-mastery and Divine presence rather than toward domination of others. Its teaching describes the sacred as something discovered …

items.title: BENIDICTIO MILITIS (M.D.R.K.D.F.).
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Sacred Universal Blessing of the Dawnist Rosarian -/- The Fellowship hereby declares the Sacred Universal Blessing, known as Benedictio Militis—the Blessing of the Knight Beneath the Rose. This blessing is not established principally as a passage of identification between members, nor as a secret recognition reserved only for those who bear a particular title or station. Rather, it is an expression of sincere blessing from one Knight in reflection of another, offered freely toward the companion, the fellow member, the stranger, or the passing traveler. It belongs to the practical life of love and is therefore encouraged wherever the Dawnist Rosarian encounters another living being within the ordinary course of existence. The blessing is an embodiment of the principle that love need not possess, identify, or claim another in order to honor them. It is enough to meet another life with sincerity, goodwill, reverence, and the quiet recognition that every being participates within the greater mystery of existence. -/- The Sacred Universal Blessing is expressed through three sacred sign formations, performed with the right hand upon the left side of the chest. These three formations constitute the Sacred Rosarian Trinity, expressing the threefold movement of the Rosarian path: the Dawn, the Rose, and the Deep. The gesture begins with the right hand forming the Rosarian Square, the four fingers held horizontally and placed against the left side of the chest, slightly tilted upward. This first formation represents the Dawn—the rising light, awakening, illumination, and the movement of consciousness toward remembrance. The Knight brings the sign inward upon the heart, acknowledging the light not merely as something witnessed above, but as something capable of being received within. -/- The second formation is made again with the right hand over the left side of the chest, activating the sign known as the Descending Covenant. Through the formation of the hand, the visual character of the Rosarian R is expressed, representing the Rose. The Rose is the living center of the covenant, the flowering of what has descended into the heart and taken root there. The Descending Covenant therefore signifies that the sacred is not merely something toward which the seeker rises; it is also something that descends into lived existence, becoming love, conduct, service, devotion, and presence. The Rose is not merely an emblem to be displayed, but the inward flower of the …

items.title: A razão cabe em um algoritmo? Pensamento e técnica a partir de Bento Prado Júnior.
items.abstract: This essay revisits Bento Prado Júnior’s critique of naturalistic reductions of thought in order to examine contemporary claims about artificial intelligence. Taking as its starting point the distinction between the causal conditions of cognition and the normative space of reasons, it argues that the successful computational reproduction of certain inferential and linguistic operations does not by itself establish that thought is reducible to algorithmic processes. The essay does not deny the philosophical significance of artificial intelligence, nor does it claim that machines cannot think. Rather, it questions the inference from computational performance to a complete definition of intelligence and reason. Drawing also on Hegel’s critique of the immediate identification of spirit with material properties, it suggests that the central philosophical risk lies in redefining thought according to what machines are currently able to reproduce. The problem, therefore, is not whether technical systems can perform increasingly complex cognitive tasks, but whether technical efficacy should become the measure of reason itself.

items.title: A dilemma for skeptics of trustworthy AI.
items.abstract: Can artificial intelligence (AI) ever be (un)trustworthy? A growing number of philosophers argue that it cannot, because AI lacks some feature deemed essential for the trust relation, such as moral agency or being responsive to reasons. Here we propose a dilemma for these skeptics, based on the assumption that such theorists must either hold there is only one kind of trust (monism), or that there are multiple varieties of trust (pluralism). The first horn of the dilemma is that a monistic view of trust is implausible; no one analysis can capture all kinds of trust relationships. The second horn of the dilemma is that if such theorists adopt a pluralistic account of trust they have little reason to deny that AI is the sort of thing that can be trustworthy; while AI may fail to possess characteristics required for some kinds of trust relations, these are not necessary conditions for trustworthiness.

items.title: Knowledge and Action in LLM Systems.
items.abstract: Terms like "tool", "harness", "skill", "memory", "RAG", "MCP", and "agent" are used fluently but rarely defined. This paper defines them.
