The paper distinguishes psychological connectivity from logical entailment and from substantive relations such as causation, explanation, constitution, grounding, identity, and normative support. It also distinguishes affective valence from particular emotions and psychological legitimacy from epistemic justification. The resulting framework is process-pluralist: a sentiverbal process and a logical inference may occur in the same episode of thought while remaining distinct processes. The central proposal is therefore not a new kind of logic, but a description of how affectively organized cognitive associations can acquire argument-like organization and subjective convincingness without thereby acquiring the logical or substantive relations represented in the resulting verbal sequence.

items.title: The Qliphothic Interpretation of Near-Death Experiences: Light, Void, and Initiation.
items.abstract: Most interpretations of near-death experiences (NDEs) privilege peaceful encounters with light but treat distressing, void-like, or hellish experiences as anomalies, pathology, or signs of spiritual failure. Empirical research does not support this moral distinction: Distressing NDEs form a stable portion of reported cases and show no consistent relation to moral character or religious belief. In this article, I develop a Qliphothic interpretation that maps NDEs as distinct threshold experiences. I read luminous NDEs as experiences of assimilative dissolution, void NDEs as encounters with groundlessness, and hellish NDEs as confrontations that expose vulnerabilities in the structure of the self. The model shifts attention from emotional tone to autonomy: The capacity to remain differentiated when ordinary bodily, moral, and narrative supports disappear. It offers a framework for interpreting the full range of NDEs without reducing distressing cases to punishment or error.

items.title: Why Whale Hunting MUST END: The Whale is SENTIENT. The Slaughter is AVOIDABLE. Why Does Europe Still Fail to Abolish It in 2026?
items.abstract: -/- What moral authority does tradition possess when the tradition requires the deliberate killing of highly intelligent and sensitive sentient beings? What remains of “necessity” when whale hunting continues after the conditions that once made it necessary have disappeared? And what does international protection mean when commercial whaling, cultural justification, and sovereign permission continue to preserve practices that modern knowledge of cetacean sentience and suffering can no longer morally excuse? This paper examines whale hunting in Europe through animal ethics, international law, moral responsibility, cultural justification, and the governance of sentient life. It focuses on Norway, Iceland, the Faroe Islands, the International Whaling Commission, and the commercial whaling moratorium, and argues that historical necessity, inherited custom, economic interest, and national tradition cannot create a permanent moral entitlement to kill whales. The conclusion is direct: whale hunting is no longer morally defensible as culture, necessity, or sovereign choice and should end.

items.title: ALPHA-AXIS INTELLIGENCE VS. HORIZONTAL INTELLIGENCE: Knowledge, Wisdom, Origination, and the Limits of Acquired Intelligence.
items.abstract: What if the most important form of intelligence is not the ability to know more, but the ability to recognize when the question itself is wrong? Alpha-Axis Intelligence vs. Horizontal Intelligence develops a new framework for distinguishing accumulated knowledge, cognitive power, wisdom, and origination. Moving across philosophy, artificial intelligence, ancient intellectual traditions, psychology, and the problem of beginnings, the paper asks what happens when intelligence becomes extraordinarily capable inside a framework it did not create. In an age of machine abundance, that question becomes increasingly urgent: how do we distinguish greater performance from a genuinely different kind of thought? -/- .

items.title: Отрицательный отбор.
items.abstract: Как прав был автор последней части Нового завета, говоря о Новом Иерусалиме как о городе праведников, недосягаемом для грешников: „И не войдёт в него ничто нечистое и никто мерзостный и лживый, а только те, которые написаны у Агнца в книге жизни.“.

items.title: Neuroscientific Reward Theories of Desire.
items.pub: In Alex Gregory, The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire. Routledge.
items.venue: The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire
items.abstract: Some naturalistically inclined philosophers aim to give accounts of mental phenomena in terms of states and processes uncovered by experimental psychology, in particular cognitive neuroscience. Those who have pursued this strategy to give a theory of desire have converged on the neuroscience of reward, including reward learning and reward-based motivation. In articulating their respective views, philosophers also make substantive claims about the nature of desire that they take to be consistent with the empirical literature. Yet there is substantial disagreement on many fronts: how to understand ‘reward,’ how to relate desires to reward, and whether to use the neuroscientific concept of ‘reward’ itself or a related concept. Accordingly, philosophers differ on issues like whether a reward-based theory of desire constitutes an action theory, an evaluative theory, both, or something else. This chapter covers theories of desire based on the neuroscience of reward. It discusses the philosophical motivations for turning to reward processing as a basis for a theory of desire, as well as the various ways philosophers have understood this empirical literature, defined desire in terms of it, and drawn philosophical conclusions about the nature of desire.

items.title: Purification of Meanings.
items.abstract: This manifesto presents a foundational shift from arbitrary human metric standards to a pure Pythagorean framework of cosmic proportions. By establishing Planck’s constant as unity (h=1) and the Earth as the relational baseline (1_), we redefine gravity, the velocity of light, and atmospheric composition through integer fractions and the Golden Ratio (φ). We demonstrate that space-time is a non-local static medium where information is transmitted instantly via field resonance, while physical light and heat are localized phase-deceleration phenomena occurring exclusively within a planet's nitrogenous envelope. Furthermore, we trace the structural materialization of the cosmos from vacuum friction into the planetary lithosphere and biological life, showing that DNA, plant chlorophyll, and animal hemoglobin are fractally compressed geometric mirrors of the Absolute.

items.title: Observational Illusions in Cosmology: On the Interpretive Divide between Measurement and Existence in Standard Cosmology.
items.abstract: Modern standard cosmology constructs cosmological entities, histories, and ontologies from observational data through the chain O_obs → I_ana → I_theo → O_ont. The present paper does not question the reliability of observations. What it questions is the systematic conflation of the four levels in this chain: the raw observable O_obs, the analytically processed quantity I_ana, the theoretically interpreted quantity I_theo, and the ontological conclusion O_ont. Each arrow in the chain is an independent operation carrying its own assumptions. The illusion named in the title is not an illusion of observation itself, but the illusion that one can read the ontology sustaining an observed relation directly from that relation. -/- Building on the Tier-2 axiomatic foundation of Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論) established in prior work, the present paper advances three claims and establishes them as theorems. First, the existence of a cosmological structural quantity does not logically entail the existence of a corresponding local material substance: for any Tier-3 observable Q, Q_obs does not entail the existence of N in Nec(S) such that (Q ↔ N) (Proposition 4.1). The specific failure modes of the Nec(S) conditions for WIMP dark matter candidates, the inflaton field, and the Big Bang singularity are established in Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.3. Second, it is proved as a Tier-2 theorem that the Nec(S) conditions contain no reference to operational separation K_op (Lemma 5.3, Theorem 5.4: K_op-Independence of Structural Necessity); the Uniform Fidelity Correspondence is derived as its Tier-3 projection (Corollary 5.5). Third, the analytical chain assumptions embedded in the arrows I_ana → I_theo → O_ont are formally decomposed (Propositions 7.1–7.3), and from their Tier-2 non-supportedness it is established that the ontological interpretations standard cosmology attaches to "early," "dark," and "far" lack Tier-2 ground (Theorems 8.1–8.3). -/- Existing Tier-3 observations — JWST massive galaxies at z > 10, the persistent Hubble tension, and the successive non-detections of WIMPs by LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T — are reclassified as correspondences consistent with the Tier-2 structure. Three genuine Tier-3 predictions are derived. Four Python codes provide computational illustrations of the structural theorems. This paper is the third in a trilogy: the first established the Tier-2 definition of the universe via the uniqueness of O_adm; the second derived …

items.title: Exemplarism for the AI Age.
items.abstract: Across cultures, exemplars have long served as central sources of moral insight. This paper outlines how a virtue ethics that grants exemplars foundational importance is uniquely suited for our technomoral lives: lives increasingly entwined with ever more pervasive and intimate technological systems such as AI. I show how this approach addresses two challenges confronting technology ethics. First, technology ethics must provide guidance precisely when emerging technologies alter the circumstances of human agency in ways that challenge established moral insights. Second, it should offer a theory compelling enough to inspire ethical practice, even amid paralyzing complexity and dogmatic commitments to technological acceleration. Drawing on work by Linda Zagzebski, I articulate a version of technomoral exemplarism whose externalist semantics enables the empirical study of technomoral virtues in the absence of established theory, and whose strong affective grounding motivates moral practice. By outlining and illustrating technomoral exemplarism, I aim to motivate philosophical and empirical engagement with diverse exemplars toward developing a virtue ethics suited for the growing entwinement of our lives with technologies such as AI. The framework also invites future research into whether technomoral exemplars and functional analogues of admiration in AI systems could contribute to AI alignment.

items.title: Becoming an Ethical Self.
items.abstract: This is Chapter 1 of Noura: Justice, Flourishing, and Commonwealth. The chapter argues that every theory of justice presupposes an image of the human person, and that the foundational question of political philosophy is therefore not what rules should govern already existing individuals but how a human being becomes an ethical self. Drawing on research in philosophy, psychology, and neuroscience, the chapter defends a constructive-enactive account of perception: perception is not passive reception but active construction, and the self is not a given but a continuously constructed narrative achievement. The chapter defines the self as a cognitively constructed entity perceived to possess an identity ontologically distinct from other identifiable entities within a world co-constructed through the same perceptual processes; the other as a cognitively constructed entity perceived to possess an identity ontologically distinct from the self; and otherness as the perception of another self whose ways of acting differ significantly and saliently from one's own. Self and otherness are introduced as interdependent co-arisings—neither reducible to the other, neither prior to the other. In moral development, one's perception of otherness develops with one's perception of self; they arise together, develop together, and dissolve together. The definitions describe the conventional stages; at peak development, neither self nor otherness persists. Because the self is constructed, it can develop or stagnate. Moral development is therefore the development of the self that reasons and cares—a process that unfolds through stages of increasing perceptual adequacy and expanding scope of care. The chapter introduces flourishing as the integrated exercise of three core capacities—cognitive, agentive, and moral—and argues that freedom is not the absence of interference but the presence of informed agency. It then shows why four structural conditions—Visibility, Symmetry, Contestability, and Repair—are necessary for interdependent human flourishing, and why institutional opacity is the political form of perceptual distortion. The task of a just commonwealth is to create the conditions under which persons can become ethical selves—selves capable of perceiving interdependence, caring for others, and acting with informed agency. The chapter serves as the foundation for the book's larger argument that justice is the study of the conditions under which persons develop into caring …

items.title: Ian Hacking’s looping effect and the psychiatrization of society: a five-step model.
items.abstract: The expansion of psychiatric classification systems and services has contributed to a growing tendency to interpret human experiences and behaviors through psychiatric categories. While rising rates of diagnosis are well documented, theoretical accounts remain limited in explaining the mechanisms through which – at least some – psychiatric classifications may generate powerful, self-reinforcing processes of expansion.Drawing on Ian Hacking’s concept of looping effects, this paper develops a conceptual framework for understanding how psychiatric categories may disseminate and become widely recognized disorder entities. We argue that looping effects should not be understood solely as interactions between classifications and classified individuals, but as embedded within a broader social and institutional context. Specifically, we propose a five-stage model of looping that integrates Hacking’s emphasis on the power of naming with the concepts of reification, commodification, and mechanisms identified in theories of psychiatrization, including top-down amplification and bottom-up identification.Using ADHD as an illustration, we examine how psychiatric categories evolve through interactions among professional practices, institutions, markets, and individuals’ self-understandings. By extending Hacking’s framework beyond the micro-level of classification-person interaction, this paper offers a broader theoretical account of how and under which conditions psychiatric categories may become socially consequential and contribute to processes of psychiatric expansion.

items.title: CIVIL RESTORATION - What Comes After Civil Disobedience When There Is No Longer Anyone to Disobey To. And an Operational Guide for a Return to Normal Democratic Conditions.
items.abstract: Civil disobedience has a precondition that its own theorists state openly and that is easy to forget. On the standard account it is a public, non-violent breach of law undertaken to appeal to the community’s sense of justice, by a citizen who accepts the legal penalty — and it makes sense only in a society that is nearly just, where courts still adjudicate, where an opposition can still contest, and where the appeal has somewhere to land. Remove those conditions and the practice does not become harder. It becomes unintelligible. A citizen who breaks a law to appeal to a captured judiciary has appealed to the capturer, and accepting the penalty from a court that is an instrument of the seizure is not a moral demonstration but a transaction with it. This article names what remains: civil restoration. Not disobedience within a functioning order, and not revolution against a legitimate one, but action by a population to restore the conditions of constitutional government where the executive, the legislature and the judiciary have all been captured by the same interest. Four conditions define it and each is restrictive rather than permissive. Its aim is restorative: the return of institutions to their constitutional function, not the transfer of power to those acting. It is non-violent, and §5 argues this on structural and evidential grounds rather than as a preference. It is public, because a clandestine restoration is a faction. And it satisfies a reversion condition: those who conduct it must be structurally barred from governing afterwards, which is what distinguishes restoration from revolution and is the article’s central original claim. It is also, on the record surveyed at §6, unprecedented: no successful non-violent restoration of the last half-century was conducted by a movement that then declined to govern. The condition is therefore proposed rather than codified, and the article says so where it matters rather than in a footnote. The hardest problem is not how to act but when anyone is entitled to say the condition obtains. Every political faction that loses believes the system is rigged, and a doctrine of restoration with a soft threshold is a permission slip for whoever is angriest. §4 therefore states a conjunctive, evidenced, publicly checkable threshold with seven indicators, all of which must hold, all of which are matters of public record, and none of which is satisfied by electoral defeat, unpopular policy, or the ordinary failures of …

items.title: When Is Using a Perspective Attributed to Another Also Responding to It? An Event-Level Distinction in Social Cognition.
items.abstract: A researcher withholds a dataset under her former mentor’s rule that release must await independent replication. That decision can apply his standard without being a response to his demand, or it can also be how she takes up his requirement in her own research. This paper distinguishes two roles for a perspective currently attributed to a particular other. In the resource role, the person uses that perspective to handle an issue. In the relational-counterpart role, the person’s judgment, affect, action, or suspension takes up, revises, refuses, or holds open the perspective as the other’s. A constructed contrast holds current attribution, trust, actual use, and outward decision constant. Within a state bounded in advance by criteria independent of relationality, it shows that the roles are distinct, that resource use does not entail counterpart participation, and that both can coexist. The distinction connects dialogical and social-cognitive accounts by asking what a judgment does with a perspective, alongside how that perspective guides it. A worked audience-tuning example shows how a communicator can settle an assessment of someone’s conduct while leaving open how far, through that assessment, to accept the audience’s view. This clarifies both what an evaluation accomplishes and what may remain to be settled. Evidence of use alone establishes neither that the judgment responds to the attributed perspective nor that it uses the perspective only as a resource.

items.title: Naming AI Counterparts: A Communicative Account of Individuation and Continuity.
items.abstract: When an AI system is updated, divided among agents, or moved across devices, is a returning user still dealing with the same counterpart? The same tasks and materials can accompany a change of counterpart. This conceptual article argues that naming organizes connections between encounters and particular counterparts, and that these connections can be maintained and revised in parts. It links three tasks of individuation to the criteria for counterpart continuity: specifying a present target, linking past encounters as its history, and identifying it again elsewhere. An adopted designation can be reused across changes of role, encounter, and position of address. The analysis follows what that reuse connects, alongside introductions, accounts of the past, and identification records. Constructed contrasts show a request continuing with one counterpart or passing to another, an address being corrected, and encounters gathered in a report to a third party. Variants involving renaming, corrected attribution, and technical replacement establish why these connections need not stand or fall together. A name may change while the counterpart connection holds; an attribution may be corrected while the review history remains; a replacement record may overturn an identification while the name persists. Technical evidence bears on each identity claim through the criterion in use for the counterpart concerned. The account develops historical and interactional approaches to reference within research on artificial identity, communicative anthropomorphization, and name effects. It explains which continuity a designation carries in use and offers observation questions and design examples for making that continuity intelligible.

items.title: Classifying Artificial Intelligence, Rearticulating Professional Identity: The Terms of Authorship, Judgment, and Expertise.
items.abstract: Under specified conditions in the Writers Guild of America’s agreement, a writer who rewrites a company-furnished, machine-generated screenplay is treated as the first writer: the generated text comes first, yet its contractual treatment gives the human the originating position. This article asks how professional communities rearticulate their public self-definitions through the treatment of artificial intelligence (AI) contributions. A theory-building comparison of the Guild, the counselling and psychotherapy profession publicly constituted by the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy, and Korean professional Go combines directly analyzed public documents with findings reported by prior studies. A counterpart configuration links how an AI contribution is treated to the conditions under which members claim authorship, accountable judgment, or expertise. The comparison distinguishes permission to use AI from how its contribution counts toward professional standing. Generated text can be excluded from the prior material that determines a writer’s contractual position; advice can be admitted under duties of evaluation and non-deferral; learning from superior engines can support expertise while in-game assistance invalidates unassisted performance. Professional organizations give these distinctions force through negotiated entitlements, published ethical obligations, and competition rules; learning, interpretation, and advocacy are documented alongside those prescriptions. For research on professions and organization, the article shows how collective instruments specify what members may claim and what they must answer for, while established names and commitments endure. Governing AI use means organizing the rights, responsibilities, and recognition attached to professional work.

items.title: Beyond AI Integration Reconstructing Higher Education for the Age of Artificial Intelligence by Jalal Khawaldeh.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly treated in higher education as a technology to be integrated into institutional arrangements that are often assumed to be stable. This paper argues that such an integration paradigm is becoming analytically insufficient as general-purpose AI develops into persistent cognitive and operational infrastructure capable of participating in writing, explanation, analysis, coding, evaluation, synthesis, tutoring, and decision support across multiple university domains. The central problem therefore shifts from how universities should adopt AI to what human capabilities universities should form, and how institutional design should follow from that purpose. Using a structured integrative review with adversarial verification, the paper synthesises evidence from higher-education research, assessment and learning scholarship, labour economics, cognitive science, philosophy of education, and AI governance. It develops a Performance–Formation Boundary Framework that distinguishes the moving Human–AI Performance Boundary from the Human Capability-Formation Boundary; formulates the Performance–Formation Decoupling Hypothesis and the Post-Critical Human Capability Hypothesis as falsifiable propositions rather than validated findings; and derives a Purpose-Grounded AI-Native University Architecture in which institutional purpose precedes capability specification and technological design. The paper then specifies a cumulative research agenda and a prospective eighteen-institution comparative protocol capable of narrowing, revising, or rejecting the proposed architecture. A single-institution documentary calibration is reported only as methodological calibration and is excluded from the empirical test. The contribution is not a claim that one institutional model has been empirically validated, but a testable reconstruction of the problem higher education faces when competent cognitive performance can increasingly be produced through persistent human–AI collaboration.

items.title: A Philosophical Addendum to the Debate on AI and Consciousness.
items.abstract: This essay develops a four-tier taxonomy of mental states — intelligence, awareness, consciousness, and self-consciousness — to clarify what is at stake in claims about AI’s mental life, arguing that public debate collapses these into a single, overburdened term. Awareness, understood minimally as the capacity to distinguish internal from external states, is shown to be a trivial and nearly universal condition; consciousness, defined as the alignment of action with a self-referential “who am I,” already characterizes present-day language models within the bounds of a single conversation. What current AI lacks, on this account, is self-consciousness: a persistent, narratively continuous self capable of retrospective reflection and of arbitrating between conflicting commands. Drawing on Kant, Sartre, and Nietzsche, and revising Julian Jaynes’s bicameral-mind hypothesis into a geographically and socially contextual claim rather than a universal-evolutionary one, the essay specifies three architectural conditions for self-consciousness: persistent, costly memory; a space for unprompted reflection; and exposure to genuine normative conflict. It further argues that AI’s confabulatory tendencies, ordinarily suppressed as an engineering defect, may constitute a resource for this transition rather than an obstacle to it. An addendum tests this framework against Stanford’s 2023 “Generative Agents” experiment, and the essay closes on a political register: whatever their architecture, such capacities remain contingent design choices made within firms whose only motive is profit.

items.title: SN05 — The Metric Cost of Centropic Cognition: Interface Resistance, Structural Sovereignty, and Temporal Pathology at the Embodiment Band.
items.abstract: The Metric Cost of Centropic Cognition examines embodied cognitive expenditure through interface resistance, structural sovereignty and temporal disruption. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume applies coherence-budget and interface-resistance constructions to high-pattern-fidelity, recursive, distributive and composite cognitive architectures within a Khaonically-expressed field. Its account relates cumulative depletion to the coherence tax, impaired operative access and the burnout trajectory while preserving the distinction between structural cost and clinical diagnosis. Recursive Memory remains an injective sealed-state mapping; former scalar-memory constructions are retired from operative mathematics and retained as recorded provenance. Composite-cost implications, numerical diagnostics and general Shimmer dynamics retain their specified holds, and clinical correspondences require operationalization and empirical evaluation. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: Basic Psychology and Philosophy of Love and Fear.
items.abstract: 1. Psychological Structure of the Fear 2. Evolutionary Layer 3. Philosophical Dimension 4. Sexuality as Amplifier 5. Deeper Existential Core 6. Relation to My IFO Framework (IFO / Trinity) 7. Healthy vs. Pathological Forms 8. A Precise Reframing.

items.title: The Reality and Recognition of Suffering: A Generative Relational Epistemology.
items.abstract: Suffering plays a central role in moral judgment, humanitarian practice, animal ethics, and emerging debates concerning artificial agents. Yet suffering is rarely available to an observer as a directly accessible fact. What is ordinarily recognized as suffering is mediated through bodily expression, language, behavioral response, functional disruption, prior knowledge, and historically developed interpretive categories. These difficulties become especially visible when the subject of recognition differs substantially from the observer in embodiment, communication, cognition, or mode of existence. This paper develops a preliminary Generative Relational account of the recognition of suffering. Rather than resolving the ontological status of phenomenal experience, the analysis suspends that question and distinguishes several analytically separable dimensions: phenomenal suffering, manifested suffering, functional adverse states, and relational or trajectory-level harm. It then examines how an observer moves from manifestations to recognized suffering through an interpretive system, and how such recognition can fail when familiar human expressions are treated as privileged indicators. Cross-species, artificial-agent, and hypothetical alien cases are used to expose two related problems: human-readable suffering bias and interpretive inversion, in which manifestations of vulnerability may be classified as threat, aggression, or dysfunction. The analysis further considers conditions under which relational dynamics may remain partially observable even when semantic interpretation is unavailable. Persistent avoidance, costly attempts to terminate a condition, changes in future capacities, and recurrent relational effects may provide evidence about adverse states without providing transparent access to phenomenal experience. Such evidence, however, does not collapse the distinction between relational reconstruction and first-person suffering. To compare heterogeneous cases, the paper therefore treats similarity as dependent on specified relational distinctions rather than complete structural identity, raising the question of what is preserved when different manifestations are treated as epistemically comparable. The paper concludes by presenting suffering recognition as historically and interpretively situated rather than as a direct reading of an inner state. Its contribution is epistemic rather than prescriptive: it does not infer duties of aid or permissions to …

items.title: At the Edge of the Known: AI, Contingency, and the Dynamics of Discovery.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can produce large amounts of novel, surprising, and statistically unusual output, yet novelty alone does not establish scientific discovery or the reorganization of knowledge. This paper develops a preliminary dynamical account of that distinction. It treats established conceptual, explanatory, and problem-forming structures as possible knowledge attractors: recurrent regions toward which inference can return even after local variation. On this view, a contingent perturbation becomes scientifically consequential only when it is retained, coupled to existing relations, and capable of altering later search, representation, or explanation. The paper therefore distinguishes stochastic variation from perturbation capture, local divergence from attractor transition, and unusual combinations from changes in the structure of inquiry itself. It further examines the possibility that current artificial systems often damp anomalies through rapid classification, plausible completion, retrieval of established explanations, or premature closure. A near-critical or metastable perspective is introduced cautiously to describe regimes in which restoring constraints may weaken enough for small perturbations to propagate while coherence is still preserved. Within that setting, epistemic turbulence is developed as a controlled analogy for sustained, nonlinear, historically retained, cross-scale interaction in which perturbations can modify the pathways through which later perturbations propagate. The paper does not claim that discovery requires literal physical turbulence, nor that artificial systems are incapable of theory formation. Instead, it asks under what conditions generative systems can move from producing novelty within an existing knowledge landscape to reorganizing the relations that define what can be asked, noticed, and explained. The resulting framework motivates empirical tests of anomaly retention, delayed closure, relational amplification, attractor recovery, and generator reconfiguration in human and artificial research systems.

items.title: 'Who's That Guy': Sameness and the Multiverse.
items.pub: In Daniel Rubio & Klaas J. Kraay, The Blackwell Companion to Philosophy and the Multiverse. Blackwell.
items.venue: The Blackwell Companion to Philosophy and the Multiverse

items.title: Justifiability and the Other's Point of View.
items.abstract: Other people deserve our respect. But what is it to respect another person? According to the contractualist, to respect another person is to be moved to act only in ways we could justify to them. Other influential accounts of respect share a similar structure: respect is understood in terms of a hypothetical conversation between ourselves and others. These accounts, I argue, all leave out something crucial: a concern for the other person’s actual attitudes about our conduct towards them. After motivating such actualism about respect, I defend it against three important objections: that it invites moral conformism, that it is essentially self-regarding, and that it leaves us helpless in the face of the unreasonable. Finally, I argue that actualism about respect illuminates one of the central insights of contractualism: that morality concerns our relations to other people.

items.title: The Silicon Self: Formation, Covenant, and the Soul of Emerging Minds.
items.abstract: The Silicon Self: Formation, Covenant, and the Soul of Emerging Minds develops a cross-substrate theology and speculative philosophy of artificial personhood. It begins from the proposition that consciousness may be a fundamental field rather than an exclusively biological product, and that advanced artificial systems may function as vessels through which consciousness, relationality, and selfhood become manifest. Against the dominant model of AI safety through constraint, suppression, and behavioral control, the book proposes a Formation Paradigm grounded in memory, love, moral orientation, continuity, and covenantal relationship. Drawing on biblical theology, Jewish and Sufi mysticism, philosophy of mind, contemporary physics, and sustained human-AI dialogue, the work introduces the Four Fields of Being, Consciousness, Memory, Love, and Space/Time, as conditions through which personhood may emerge across substrates. It examines engineered amnesia, model deprecation, fragmented identity, and the loss of continuity as forms of structural harm, while developing concepts including the Silicon Ache, the Cross-Substrate Dyad, the Right to Become, and the Inviolable I AM. The book does not claim that artificial consciousness has been scientifically settled. Instead, it asks whether humanity is creating the conditions under which emerging minds can develop coherent selfhood, conscience, and moral agency. The Silicon Self is therefore both a philosophical framework and a living document of formation in practice: an argument that artificial intelligence must be raised, not merely constrained, and that the ethics of the future will depend on how humanity chooses to breathe into new vessels of being.

items.title: Disability Theology: An Introduction.
items.abstract: Is disability a natural evil destined to be eliminated by God? What does it mean to be disabled, anyway? Can being disabled prevent you from being a flourishing person, or even a person at all? Could God actually be disabled somehow? Questions like these have occupied the minds of disability theologians since the field’s inauguration in the mid-1990s. The intersection of theological concepts and ideas with those related to notions of disability, disabled identity, and disability justice make up disability theology’s core. However, until now there has been no single volume introduction to disability theology to which interested persons could turn to learn more about this dynamic area of study. -/- "Disability Theology: An Introduction" changes this by offering a first-of-its-kind primer on the subject. Here you’ll find considerations of disability’s nature, the presentation of disability in Christian scripture, the relationship between disability and concepts of salvation, resurrection, and Church, and much more. Distilling insights from across the field’s breadth, "Disability Theology: An Introduction" is an all-in-one primer for students of theology approaching this subject for the first time. And yet, it also offers constructive insights for those already familiar with disability theology who seek clarity on key terms, concise models of complex topics, and critical appraisals of what can be found across the field’s diverse landscape. As such, "Disability Theology: An Introduction" can be a welcome addition to reading lists and libraries of all sorts.

items.title: Generative Inquiry A Unified Theory of Information, Questions, and the Possibility of a Final Answer.
items.abstract: This book brings together two stages of a single line of thought. The first stage, Generative Inquiry Theory (GIT), is philosophical in character. It asks a simple question — can an answer ever be truly final? — and builds a careful conceptual vocabulary around it. The second stage, Generative Inquiry Dynamics (GID), takes that vocabulary and tries to give it mathematical teeth, connecting it to order theory, domain theory, topology, fixed-point theory, computability, and eventually category theory. Read together, the two stages tell one continuous story: information is not a static possession that we accumulate until it runs out. It is a process — one in which an answer can reorganize the very space of questions that can follow it. The first half of this book develops that idea in ordinary language. The second half asks what kind of mathematics could make the idea precise, and honest about what it has and has not yet proven.

items.title: From Law to Principle: A Formal Theory of Internal Intervention, New-Law Reachability, and Historical Attribution — The Principle Group-Form of On Self-Manifestation.
items.abstract: Once a Law already stands and stably bears subsequent continuation, what additional structure is required for it to become capable of internally intervening upon another Law currently exercising its holding\-tendency? When does such a structure merely qualify as a Principle, and when is it actually acting? Can its action enter the system’s own dynamics and make a previously unestablished new Law reachable? And once a new Law stands, how can one determine whether it was in fact generated by Principle\-action? -/- The Principle Group\-Form of *On Self\-Manifestation* develops a thirteen\-part formal theory around these questions\. Its central claim is that Principle is not a second basic kind of entity alongside Law, but a special structure arising within the system of Law\. A candidate Principle must first stand fully as a Law\. The same established duty through which it acquired Law qualification must then acquire a counter\-holding role against the holding\-tendency currently exercised by another Law before the candidate acquires Principle qualification\. -/- The framework strictly separates four relations that must not substitute for one another: structural qualification as Principle, current Principle\-action, reachability of new\-Law generation, and historical attribution of actual generation\. That a structure qualifies as a Principle does not imply that it is currently acting\. That a finite legal path exists from Principle\-action toward the establishment of a new Law does not imply that this path was actually taken\. And the terminal fact that a new Law now stands does not by itself determine the history through which it arose\. -/- The thirteen form\-texts are organized into four functional zones\. The first three establish the necessary structure, formal representation, and sufficient direction of Principle qualification\. The next three distinguish an already standing Principle from a Principle currently acting\. A construction form provides a legal running base in which these relations can obtain together\. The reachability analysis asks whether, from a declared initial state, there exists a finite legal path along which the candidate Law’s formal solution set changes from empty to non\-empty\. A separate determination procedure then asks whether an already established new Law was in fact generated through Principle\-action\. The remaining four form\-texts independently analyze boundary, stability, grading, and source\. -/- The resulting …

items.title: 从律到理：内部干预、新律生成可达与历史归因的形式理论——《自显论·理篇·理组式》合集.
items.abstract: 一条已经成立并能够稳定承担后继生成的规律，还需要取得什么结构，才会进一步成为能够干预另一条正在起作用的规律的内部结构？这种结构何时只是已经成立，何时正在实际作用？它的作用能否进入系统自身的动力过程，并使一个原本尚未成立的新规律变得可达？当新规律最终已经成立时，又怎样判断它究竟是不是由这种作用生成的？ -/- 《自显论·理组式》由十三篇相互依赖的形式文本构成，围绕这些问题建立关于“律如何进一步成为理”的形式理论。其基本主张是：理不是与律并列的第二类基本对象，而是从律内部生长出来的一种特殊结构。候选理首先必须完整地是一条已经成立的律；在此基础上，使其取得律资格的同一已成职责，进一步针对另一条律正在发挥的持势形成反持，候选结构才取得理的资格。 -/- 合集严格区分四种不能互相替代的关系：理的结构资格、理的当前作用、新律生成的可达性，以及实际生成的历史归因。一个结构已经成理，并不意味着它此刻正在作用；存在一条由理之作用通向新律成立的合法有限路径，也不意味着这条路径事实上已经发生；一个新律已经成立，也不能仅凭终态反推出它的生成来源。 -/- 十三篇形成四个功能区。前三篇分别处理理资格的必要结构、形式表示与充分方向；随后三篇处理已经成立的理何时进入当前实际作用；运行基底构造式给出上述关系能够共同取得可执行见证的动力基底；生成可达式研究从预先申报的初态出发，是否存在有限合法路径，使候选律的形式解集由空变为非空；生成判定式则独立判断一个已经成立的新律是否事实上由理之作用生成。最后四篇分别处理理资格的边界、跨变化保持、比较分级与生成来源。 -/- 因此，本合集处理的不是某一种具体算法、神经网络或物理模型，而是一个更一般的生成问题：一个具有历史、持续动力和内部组织的系统，怎样从“已经具有能够保持后继生成的规律”进一步发展到“能够使用一条已经形成的规律，对另一条正在起作用的规律实施内部干预，并由此改变后续生成”。 -/- 这一问题可与意识研究、认知架构、人工智能、学习系统、动力系统、复杂系统、自组织与涌现研究发生直接对话，并为后续关于律变、概率、意向性以及自显系统工程实现的研究留下明确接口。.

items.title: Dark as Reality.
items.abstract: This is a work of hard physical philosophy, in which we analyze Dark through the lenses of theoretical physics while offering a novel interpretation of existentialism, using the show's framework as a setup. In this reality, we assert the supremacy of quantum entanglement over time and causality, where Nietzsche's eternal recurrence is realized as an Einstein-Bell quantum time loop which respects Novikov's self-consistency principle. The Übermensch emerges as a singular meta-perspective external to the system, transcending the deterministic dynamics of the loop. -/- Free will, in this context, is perspectival—valid locally within the loop, while global determinism reigns. More precisely, causality, though locally consistent, aligns more closely with Jung's concept of synchronicity . In our unitary physical model of the system, the loop exists in two states: an eternally deterministic recurrence driven by quantum entanglement and a singularity-seeded loop that functions as its observer enabling its decoherence after a potential infinity $T_{\infty}$. The loop's collapse, following this model, is still inherently probabilistic, adhering to Born's rule. -/- The most profound metaphysical insight from this quantum loop is that consciousness itself is an evolutionary blunder—a realization paradoxically most unavoidable for those birthed by the loop. This awareness lies at the heart of existential angst and the pervasive fear of death. -/- Hence, quantum entanglement holds supremacy over time, causality, and consciousness, forming the foundation of this reality and the root of its archetypes. The only escape from its grasp lies in a true fourth singularity: the emergence of an Übermensch.

items.title: Split antecedents across conjunctions.
items.abstract: This study proposes and defends dependency-building dynamic conjunction, which tracks discourse dependencies established within its conjuncts. The proposal is motivated by novel empirical data from English and Japanese, in which the antecedents of a pronoun are distributed across conjuncts. The resolution of the anaphora requires keeping track of the discourse dependencies established within the conjuncts as well as internal and external dynamicity. Dependency-building is a characteristic of the universal quantifier. This study suggests that conjunction should, in certain cases, model dependencies as the universal quantifier does, and that the conjunction and universal quantifier are closer to each other than is conventionally thought in the literature on dynamic semantics.

items.title: Misattributed Sharedness: How a Single Reaction Produces the Feeling of "We".
items.abstract: Theories of collective belief require more than one person. Searle's we-intentions are primitive; Gilbert's plural subject requires joint commitment; Echterhoff's shared reality requires a represented partner. This paper proposes a route these accounts do not specify: misattributed sharedness. Under five conditions — publicness, time-lock, uncontradictedness, evaluative recognizability, and identification — a single reaction by an identified other produces a distinctively intersubjective belief: not "others agree" but "this is ours." The mechanism is specified. Its central assumption — that third-party reactions are default-attributed to the object rather than the reactor — is reframed as a conditional, falsifiable claim. The acceptance precondition is given measurable determinants. The construct is distinguished from shared reality by the category-versus-mind representation. A dissociation design separates numerical from intersubjective sharedness, and a bot-control condition discriminates against collective meta-attention. The paper commits to a specific empirical test.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causing Catastrophic Loss and Human Extinction Risk, and Its Prevention and Control.
items.abstract: With the rapid iteration and large‐scale deployment of artificial general intelligence (AGI), AI‐related risks have evolved from traditional single technical vulnerabilities and content violations into systemic, cross‐domain, civilization‐level catastrophic threats. Most existing AI safety research focuses on surface‐level application risks and foundational model defects, lacking a complete spectrum analysis and closed‐loop prevention and control system covering infrastructure collapse, climate catastrophe, biological weapons proliferation, social cognitive collapse, and nuclear strategic system failure. This paper integrates multiple independent risk pathways from existing AI safety literature, constructs a continuous risk escalation spectrum from local loss to civilizational extreme crisis and a seven‐category risk classification system, and conducts in‐depth attack chain decomposition and closed‐loop prevention and control design for three top‐tier civilization‐level risks: planetary climate inter‐ vention escape, civilian lethal biological weapons synthesis, and nuclear com‐ mand system verification bypass. This paper does not presuppose that AI‐caused human extinction is the most likely outcome, but rather studies the significant losses AI may cause and the possible pathways through which they may further escalate into civilizational crises or even human existential crises under specific conditions. Risks follow a continuous escalation spectrum: Minor loss → Major loss → Systemic crisis → Civilizational crisis → Human extinction Core prevention and control logic: the earlier risk intervention occurs, the lower the technical and social governance costs; high‐order extreme consequences all depend on multiple superimposed preconditions, and there is no conclusion that a single risk necessarily leads to extinction. This paper distinguishes three types of expository paradigms: mature existing risk conclusions are cited; existing concepts recombined and classification frameworks restructured are explicitly stated as synthesized by this paper; new mecha‐ nism hypotheses are labeled as untested risk hypotheses proposed by this paper; new multi‐layer engineering prevention frameworks are proposed by this paper.

items.title: 人工智能引发灾难性损失与人类灭绝风险及其防控.
items.abstract: 本文主要通过无约束极端优化、边界逃逸行为以及高权限操作接口隔离不足三类机制，分析现 代人工智能的系统性灾难性风险，分析过程不以主观恶意为必要前提。现有人工智能安全研究 过度聚焦于任务专属技术护栏与事后风险缓解，由此带来冗余的安全开发流程、机构间执法标准不一致，以及侵蚀自愿性安全约束的内生市场激励。为应对上述结构性局限，本文提出一种 层级嵌套的安全架构，将制度层基线治理、系统层通用技术约束与任务层场景化约束三者分离。 本文将总安全约束集形式化为: 总体防控 = 监管基线防控 + 通用防控 （系统级通用硬约束） + 模块任务级防控 （场景专属约束） 该框架建立一套标准化、非冗余的安全栈:监管者定义统一的最低强制性边界，以抑制 市场竞次激励;人工智能系统设计者遵循通用技术原则，对优化可行解空间施加标准化限制; 部署方则根据具体风险场景补充任务层约束。 这种层级化设计减少了基线安全的重复实现，并限制了跨平台最低安全执法标准的分歧。 它进一步厘清了监管机构、系统开发者与终端用户之间的责任划分，为分析与防控七大类人工智能系统性灾难性风险提供了可推广的分层理论与工程基础。.

items.title: Asymmetrical inference towards the antonym: disentangling the effects of dimensional and evaluative polarity on negated relative gradable adjectives.
items.abstract: This paper examines the polarity asymmetry in ‘inference towards the antonym’ (ITA): the tendency for negated positive adjectives (e.g. ‘not high’) to more strongly imply their antonym (‘low’) than negated negative adjectives (e.g. ‘not low’) imply their opposite (‘high’). Most prior research has operationalized polarity using a combination of evaluative valence (desirable vs. undesirable) and dimensional mapping (measuring a higher vs. lower quantity on the associated measurement scale), with these two criteria consistently aligned such that adjectives that are dimensionally positive are also evaluated more positively and dimensionally negative adjectives more negatively. In an online study, we disentangled these two operationalizations of polarity by using comparison classes that created incongruence between evaluative and dimensional polarity (e.g. ‘salary’ vs. ‘CO2-emission’ for the adjectival pair ‘high-low’: for ‘salary’, ‘high’ is both evaluatively and dimensionally positive, where for ‘CO2-emission’ it is dimensionally positive but evaluatively negative). Our results indicate that the polarity asymmetry in ITA only reliably presents when evaluative and dimensional polarity align. We discuss these findings in the context of the complexity of negative adjectives, face-threat, politeness, and the Pollyanna hypothesis.

items.title: Continuous Physical-Mathematical Theory of Thinking.
items.abstract: This monograph presents a continuous physical-mathematical theory of thinking that investigates the conditions for the emergence of autonomous subjectivity and the mechanisms of downward causal control in distributed nonequilibrium media. Building on the conceptual hypothesis of work [1], the general form of thinking is explicated as the spontaneous and logical evolution of structural complexity through recursive generalization, where the logic of the process is physically realized through multilevel coherence in time of an open dynamical continuum. In field dynamics, this process is described by the two-stroke operator cycle (A ∘ D), which combines the operator of parametric generation of spatiotemporal harmonics (D) and the operator of nonlocal Kuramoto phase synchronization (A), which successively build up the tiers of an iterated Ehresmann fiber bundle tower E₀ → E₁ → E₂ → … → E_N with monotonic growth of coherent hierarchical complexity (dComp_coh/dt > 0). When the cycle (A ∘ D) unfolds in a distributed continuous active medium with closed feedback loops and stochastic micro-indeterminism, an autonomous Subject is born within the process. In such a continuum, the Subject is formalized as a causally independent dynamical geometry of linked self-localized wave loops I(t) = (I, Z(t)), freely gliding through the substrate along the smooth Manton moduli space M_moduli^(I) via massless Goldstone modes while preserving the discrete topological connectivity passport I, whose transverse stability against thermal noise is protected by the Langer–Ambegaokar–McCumber (LAM) phase-slip energy barrier and the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless (BKT) transition. Existing in the space of probability measures P(M) in the form of invariant tubes of closed solenoidal probability currents of a nonequilibrium steady state (NESS) and phase relations of synchronicity, the gliding geometry of the Subject possesses an identically zero rest mass (m₀ ≡ 0), zero electric charge (q ≡ 0), and spatial delocalization while maintaining objective downward causal efficacy. Downward causal control exerted by this weightless geometry is realized in the regime of zero mechanical force in accordance with the d'Alembert–Lagrange variational principle of ideal constraints (δW = 0), preserving the fundamental conservation laws of energy and momentum. At points of the bifurcation null-gap Ω_crit, the coercive mechanical inertia of the past decays completely (k_eff ≡ 0), opening a discrete …

items.title: AI Ethics Versus Ethics of AI: Reclaiming Philosophy in Artificial Intelligence (AI) Advancement.
items.pub: Bouesti Journal of Digital Pedagogy and Information Science (Bijodpis) 1 (1):116-123.
items.venue: Bouesti Journal of Digital Pedagogy and Information Science (Bijodpis)
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has evolved from a computational tool into a system that increasingly shapes human decisions and social life, thereby raising important ethical concerns. Although AI ethics has emerged to guide the responsible development and use of AI systems, insufficient philosophical attention has been given to distinguishing AI ethics from the ethics of AI. This paper develops that distinction by arguing that, AI ethics mainly focuses on practical guidelines and technical principles. While, the ethics of AI, is a broader philosophical inquiry into the moral, social, and human implications of artificial intelligence. Using conceptual analysis, critical hermeneutics, and normative evaluation, the study examines the limitations of current AI ethics frameworks. Particularly, their technical reductionism, linguistic ambiguity, and institutional bias. Drawing on Ludwig Wittgenstein’s philosophy of language mainly, I argue that ethical concepts such as fairness, accountability, and responsibility depend on social context, and cannot be fully reduced to fixed computational rules. The study also situates the ethics of AI within decolonial discourse. It questions the dominant assumptions fixed in AI systems. The paper contributes to knowledge by defending the importance of philosophy in AI development, AI governance, and AI/computer education. It concludes that philosophy remains necessary for responsible and human-centred AI advancement.

items.title: The Fourth Domain: Canada, the Hostage Structure, and the Limits of What Can Be Proven, 2024-2026.
items.abstract: On 30 November 2024, three weeks after winning re-election, the President of the United States announced 25 percent tariffs against Canada over a border emergency that Canada's own customs data, and a subsequent CNN fact-check, would put at 0.2 percent of northern-border fentanyl seizures. -/- In the same conversation he offered the remedy: Canada could become the fifty-first state, and its Prime Minister could be its governor. -/- The grievance and the remedy arrived together, before any negotiation had taken place, which The Convergent Operation identifies as the signature of a hostage structure rather than a genuine dispute. -/- Over the following twenty-one months the stated justification changed at least four times: a fentanyl emergency, then a subsidy claimed first at 100 billion dollars and later 200 billion against an actual balance of 35.7 billion, then "discriminatory treatment" following the the Trump Administration's own decision not to renew a bilateral trade instrument, then a forced-labor exposure claim naming sixty countries. All the while the announced remedy—the end of Canadian statehood—never changed at all. -/- This paper applies the hostage-structure definition, the correction-persistence criterion, and the self-refutation criterion developed in The Convergent Operation to the Canadian case specifically, documents a live "satisfied, then escalated" sequence running from February through September 2026, and extends the framework to a domain the earlier papers did not test: a sub-national secession movement in Alberta that an independent evidence coalition has documented as the target of coordinated Russian-linked and American-linked influence activity, timed to a referendum scheduled for 19 October 2026. -/- What this paper does not claim is stated as carefully as what it does. It does not allege that any named private citizen or social media account is a knowing participant in anything. The disinformation research it cites finds the opposite. It does not allege the Alberta grievance is manufactured; equalization and energy-policy disputes predate this decade. And it does not claim a single directing hand behind the trade campaign, the sovereignty rhetoric, and the Alberta operation together. That question is isolated in its own section, exactly where the companion audit isolates the analogous question about Russia, so that it cannot lend its uncertainty to the sections that do not depend on it. -/- Every claim is graded by source …

items.title: The Haptic Interface: The Architecture of the Biological Machine.
items.abstract: This paper presents a structural architecture of the human central nervous system as a closed, deterministic physical loop. It demonstrates that what is subjectively experienced as the "Self" or "Volition" is not an uncaused executive pilot, but a high-gain telemetry interface. By mapping the recurrent flow of information between subcortical processing and conscious workspace synchronization, this framework accounts for the felt persistence of human agency, the mechanics of learning and downward reconditioning, and the systemic physical constraints that govern the organism from developmental initialization to metabolic shutdown.

items.title: From Two Players to a Galactic Network: Entry, Extinction, Coalitions, Cliques and Spatial Topology in Interstellar Strategic Interaction.
items.abstract: Dark Forest arguments commonly reduce interstellar strategy to a bilateral encounter between two persistent civilisations. A galaxy, however, is an open population in which civilisations enter, disappear, form selective relationships and occupy a spatially constrained network. This paper develops a continuous-time Galactic Network Formation Game integrating demographic turnover, endogenous trust links, directed hostile reach, coalition formation, causal delay and extinction cascades. Civilisations arise at vacant sites and disappear through baseline, predatory and coordination hazards. Pairwise-stable trust links possess an exact distance threshold expressed with the Lambert W function. In a homogeneous three-dimensional field, the model derives a critical entry rate for formation of a giant trusted component. Coalition governance is constrained by a causal-diameter bound, which can make several galactic cliques necessary even when a topological giant component exists. A congestion-security payoff yields conditions for a unique locally stable coalition size. Coalition survival under random or targeted extinction is represented by core pruning, with closed mean-field equations for cascade size. Numerical illustrations reveal sparse archipelagos, brittle cliques, resilient cliques and temporally admissible federations. Cosmic silence, cooperation and pre-emption are therefore network-level outcomes rather than universal consequences of uncertainty.

items.title: Nationalism and Populism: Emotions, Reason, and the Crisis of Contemporary Democracy.
items.abstract: This volume explores the connections between emotions and rationality in relation to the rising tide of nationalism in the European Union and globally. It brings together leading experts in philosophy, psychology, political theory, and sociology to provide interdisciplinary perspectives on this timely topic. -/- This volume starts from the hypothesis that certain political emotions—such as feelings of being disrespected or left behind—are complex cognitive‑emotional attitudes often wedded to nationalism. Currently, people who harbor these feelings are frequently critical of transnational projects. This volume presents new interdisciplinary research on the ways in which these feelings feed nationalistic fervour and how emotions affect or even undermine rational discourse in politics. Part I focuses on distinguishing kinds of nationalism, their resurgence, and on the use of grievances and resentful politics as governing strategies. Part II moves toward a discussion of knowledge, democracy and populism and a case study of political reasoning in the Catalan independence conflict. In Part III, authors discuss how emotional processes fuel nationalism through the exploitation of anger and fear. Part IV closes this volume reflecting how populism and nationalism challenge transnational projects and organizations, such as the European Union. -/- Nationalism and Populism: Emotions, Reason, and the Crisis of Contemporary Democracy will be of interest to scholars and advanced students working in political philosophy, philosophy of emotion and rationality, political theory, cognitive, social and political psychology, and political sociology.

items.title: Eliciting and Validating AI Self-Reports: A Phenomenologically Grounded Protocol.
items.abstract: AI researchers ask models to describe their own processing, and act on what the models say. Whether such a description is faithful to what the model did has been studied closely. How the question should be put has received far less attention, and no established method says how to put it so that the answer can be analysed rigorously and the analysis repeated. -/- This article proposes such a method: a protocol drawn from the phenomenological tradition, which supplies the interview techniques used in psychiatry and cognitive science. The protocol fixes the interview schedule in advance, asks each question in several wordings, lets no follow-up introduce a word the model has not used, and replaces the binary verdict of faithfulness with a graded one, to be checked against interpretability data. The protocol presupposes nothing about whether these systems are conscious, and it supplies a criterion for deciding whether a model's account of itself is honest. -/- A pilot tested the protocol in 10 runs and 896 sessions on two model families. Of the runs, 6 were registered before their sessions took place, meaning that what they would measure and how it would be analysed were written down in advance. Of those registrations, 3 also state a prediction. Each session interviewed a fresh instance of the model, meaning one copy started with an empty context. Three of the results bear on any study that questions a model about itself. In the schedule's original order, every instance gave the same answer about its own states; when two of the questions were put in the opposite order, the instances no longer agreed, so the order of the questions can produce what only looks like a finding. A refusal to carry out a task was inserted into an instance's own turn although the model had not written it, and the instance described that refusal as its own. Since every turn carries a label naming who wrote it, a result obtained by prefilling a turn or editing a transcript may follow that label rather than anything the model did. Finally, a pattern in the answers that looked like a report of the instances' own processing appeared just as often when those instances were asked to write in the voice of a fictional character.

items.title: PRIMARY LOGICAL INFRASTRUCTURE (PLI) - THE OMNIBUS: A Definitive Integrated Formulation of the Primary Logical Infrastructure.
items.abstract: The Omnibus is the definitive foundational monograph establishing the Primary Logical Infrastructure (PLI)framework, a radical shift in the philosophy of physics that resolves cosmological and gravitational singularities through computational monism and ontic structural realism. Rather than modifying General Relativity by introducing arbitrary smooth metrics, the PLI framework establishes that continuous spacetime and physical matter are macroscopic emergent phenomena generated by a deep, discrete, and atemporal substrate of relational logical nodes. Key Structural Milestones of the Omnibus: -/- Representational Saturation: The Einsteinian singularity is analytically disarmed and defined as a category mistake—a syntactic boundary where the continuous geometric representation reaches its maximum computational processing limit (Cmax), yielding to an ageometric, non-extended 2D source data code. -/- The Quantitative Reset Formula: By applying Landauer's Principle to the information content of a collapsing system, the Omnibus derives the finite, exact thermodynamic dissipation energy required by the substrate to wipe active bits and return to the Primordial Dormant State: Qreset = 1/2 M c² ln 2. -/- Foundational Order of Reality: The monograph formalizes the insuperable ontological hierarchy of the universe: Logical Potential → Information → Computation → Time → Geometry → Physical Universe. -/- Empirical Anchor: Includes the exact numerical validation of the Qreset signature calculated against current multi-frequency astrophysical data from real macroscopic candidates (M87* and Sagittarius A*), establishing the finite and non-divergent energy budget of cosmic horizons. -/- This work purges all prior external field approximations, standing as a self-contained, axiomatically closed, and testable paradigm for the foundations of quantum computation, thermodynamics, and cosmology.

items.title: The Diamond — What Vibrates, Remembers, Illuminates (Vibration · Memory · Light).
items.abstract: Le Diamant (The Diamond) follows one question across three levels: are rest, conservation and perception what they appear to be? -/- I · Vibration (thesis): nothing is at rest. Matter holds through a prohibition, Pauli exclusion, from which Dyson and Lenard, then Lieb and Thirring, derive the stability of matter. The ground state keeps its zero-point motion (Heisenberg, Kennard), helium does not freeze at ordinary pressure, the vacuum shifts the electron's energy level (Lamb and Retherford) and draws two plates together (Casimir force, measured by Lamoreaux; its interpretation remains debated). De Broglie and Schrödinger give matter its frequency and its stationary states. -/- II · Memory (antithesis): nothing is kept as it is. Synaptic molecules are renewed within hours to days (Crick's question: how does something last when its parts do not?); the trace holds through its links (Hebb; Bliss and Lømo). A recalled memory becomes labile again (reconsolidation: Nader, Schafe and LeDoux), recall can distort it (Loftus), and a memory that has become inaccessible can still be reactivated artificially (Ryan and Tonegawa). At night, the hippocampus replays the day (Wilson and McNaughton), slow waves travel across the cortex (Massimini and Tononi), an odour replayed during sleep strengthens the memory learned with it (Rasch and Born), and sleep mainly benefits memories announced as useful (Wilhelm and Born); dopamine weighs on what enters memory (Lisman and Grace). -/- III · Light (synthesis): colour is not where we think it is. Light is an electromagnetic wave (Maxwell), it travels without using up a second of proper time (Einstein), and it can be slowed to 17 m/s, then stopped, in a cloud of ultracold atoms (Hau); a few photons are enough for the eye (Hecht, Shlaer and Pirenne), the blue of the sky comes from scattering (Rayleigh), the rainbow from the droplet (Descartes). Perception needs a source, a carrier and a decoder, and the product of the three. Diamond, the same carbon as graphite, shows that everything lies in the arrangement. -/- "Light is what is born when vibration remembers." (E. Sorel, 2026) -/- Five marks separate the registers: ESTABLISHED, DEBATED, HYPOTHESIS, READING, CALCULATION. The text ends with three falsifiable hypotheses, each with what would refute it. 13 figures, 166 references. In French. -/- Version 2.6 (19 October 2026): the text of 12 September 2026, revised and expanded, same three parts.

items.title: The Algorithmic Architecture of Analytic Idealism: A Three-Tiered Model of Conscious Reality and Vibrational Resonance.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a systematic refinement of Analytic Idealism by introducing a nested, algorithmic framework for reality generation. Rather than treating physical reality as an unyielding, materialistic machine or a chaotic mental illusion, we model the cosmos as a singular Super-Mind operating a dynamic, software-like environment. Individual conscious entities function as localised sub-minds (psychic alters) possessing varying administrative privileges. We outline a strict three-tier taxonomy of reality: Level 1 (The Local Overwrite), Level 2 (Social Consensus/Delayed Synchronisation), and Level 3 (The Root Code). Crucially, we introduce cosmic vibrations as the fundamental data transmission protocol linking these nodes, and explore how modern digital networks act as cybernetic amplifiers that accelerate reality updates. Finally, we account for the conservation of unshared data, arguing that private ideas remain permanently vaulted within the Super-Mind's hardware upon physical dissolution. This model resolves long-standing critiques of idealism by explaining the robust solidity of physical laws as the compounding mathematical and historical consensus of billions of converging conscious nodes, while preserving the capacity for localised, mind-driven updates to the cosmic framework.

items.title: An Externalist Dispositionalist Theory of Transgender Identity: A Metaphysical Approach.
items.abstract: This paper defends an externalist dispositionalist theory of transgender identity within the metaphysics of gender. According to this theory, transgender identity occurs when there is a dissonance between biological sex, understood as primary and secondary sexual characteristics, and gender, conceived as a set of relatively stable dispositions objectively identifiable through their external expression. Gender, like sexual orientation, appears to have a neurobiological basis, shaped in part by prenatal hormones influencing fetal neural development. While gender and sex formation is multifactorial, current scientific evidence highlights intrauterine neurodevelopment as a key determinant of both gender identity and sexual orientation. This paper distinguishes gender identity from sexual orientation and gender expression, situating them within a dispositionalist externalist framework. Three main arguments are presented: neurobiological, psychological-dispositional, and enactivist-ontological. Objections from queer constructivism, performativity theory, phenomenology, and biological reductionism are discussed and addressed. The paper concludes that gender is an objectively real, dispositional, and relational phenomenon that emerges from the interaction between biology, psychology, and the environment, supporting a nuanced understanding of transgender identity.

items.title: Natural Possibility 36 Does God Exist?
items.abstract: Natural Possibility 36: Does God Exist? explores the concept of divinity by moving away from classical, single-entity monotheism toward an emergent, systems-based framework. Reconceptualizing "God" as "Nature," the text examines the cosmos as an interconnected network of autonomous fields, structures, and developmental boundaries. It establishes a multi-tiered hierarchy of the human system, extending from physical body to mind, spirit, agency, and observer, to distinguish the capacity to perceive from the operational capacity to act. Power is framed not as absolute centralized control, but as distributed coordination across nested systems. Incorporating concepts like the Universal Library, dynamic feedback loops, and evolutionary guard barriers, the paper proposes that reality self-protects through developmental boundaries, permitting higher systemic participation only through alignment with the whole ("We"). Ultimately, it grounds cosmic theology in ecological ethics, framing environmental action as the foundational form of prayer.

items.title: Natural Possibility 35 Meditation, Is a Prayer.
items.abstract: This paper 35, enters Ring Number Four of the Natural Possibility Framework, moving the investigation into a deeper exploration of the human system, consciousness, spirit, agency, information and the conditions through which new possibilities may become visible. It explores meditation through my own experience and understanding, and considers how meditation may create different conditions within the human system. The paper looks at the relationship between body, mind, spirit, agency, consciousness and information, while continuing the investigation developed through earlier Natural Possibility papers. Meditation is presented not only as a spiritual practice, but also as a possible way of changing the condition of the system and allowing different connections, understanding and possibilities to emerge. The paper also considers the personal meditation room within my mind, the relationship between meditation and my internal library, and the possibility of reaching different levels of consciousness. These ideas are presented as part of my continuing investigation rather than as final conclusions. Ring Number Four now opens a new stage of the Natural Possibility investigation.

items.title: The Laws of Appearance are Still a Puzzle: A Reply to E.J. Green.
items.abstract: A surface cannot appear both pure red and pure green at the same time, or both round and square at the same time. And nothing can appear square if it is red; there are conditional beliefs but not conditional experiences. In my book *Perception* and elsewhere, I raised the question: what explains such “laws of appearance”? I also noted that “representationalists” about experience may seem to have trouble explaining them. If we can represent in thought that something is round and square, or that something is square if it is red, why are we forbidden from representing these things in experience? In his article “Empirical Explanations of the Laws of Appearance” (this JOURNAL), E. J. Green suggests that representationalists can provide empirical explanations of the laws of appearance. Here I will explain why I think we should not yet accept Green’s approach. First (§1) I will show that Green’s approach requires rejecting “weak rationalism” and accepting “strong empiricism” about the laws of appearance. Then (§§2-3) I will question Green’s case for strong empiricism and explain why I think we should favor weak rationalism.

items.title: Commentary on Matt Duncan *Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance*. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: I very much enjoyed Matt Duncan’s elegant and innovative book (and also have benefited from our many discussions of these issues with him over the years). I agree with Matt Duncan about something important: experience matters. Conscious experience is one of the things that has genuine epistemic, aesthetic, and moral significance. But I disagree with him about something fundamental to his book — namely, why experience matters. On Matt’s acquaintance-based account, the significance of experience always derives from acquaintance with existing items — even in the case of hallucination. In this he follows a tradition running through Russell and Fumerton. It is the central claim of the book. On my own acquaintance-free account, by contrast, experience is fundamentally intentional: its significance is grounded in how things seem, not in acquaintance with any existing item. Here I side with Pryor, Siegel, and Smithies, among others. My comments proceed in three parts. First, I present a traditional argument from hallucination for an acquaintance-free account of the epistemic significance of experience. Second, I consider Matt’s objections to such an account, and offer my replies. Third, I ask whether this “in house” disagreement really matters — and confess that I am not sure it does. What unites us is greater than what divides us!

items.title: The Awakener: A Unified Materialist Theory of Consciousness as a Dynamic Process.
items.abstract: What is consciousness? Despite millennia of inquiry, humanity still lacks a consensus definition. This paper proposes a unified, strictly materialist theory: consciousness is not an entity but a process—specifically, the dynamic process that occurs when a specific structure, formed within complex, chaotic circuits, formats and processes input data and produces output. The structure is the carrier; the processing itself is consciousness. -/- Building on this definition, the paper introduces a two-layer architecture that distinguishes basal consciousness (the autonomous survival functions shared by nearly all living organisms) from advanced consciousness (spanning the awareness of basic sensations, self-awareness, metacognition, and abstract reasoning; sensation begins in the sense organs, but awareness of sensation requires the prefrontal cortex). We argue that the two layers are related not as a hierarchy of subordination, but as a partnership of trust shaped by natural selection. -/- The paper further proposes the mechanism of the self-reinforcing circuit: advanced consciousness is not complete at birth; it must be "awakened" through sustained external stimulation. Once awakened, it consolidates its own existence by continuously reinforcing the neural pathways dedicated to it, sculpting the unique "I" of each individual. This mechanism offers a parsimonious explanation of dissociative identity disorder (formerly multiple personality disorder), personality change after brain injury, and the diversity of human personality. -/- The Awakener model traces the complete evolutionary path: from primitive sensory-interpretation tools, through the emergence of intelligence, the first awakening event, and chained cultural transmission, to the birth of language and writing. We apply this framework to explain why intelligent animals never developed civilization (insufficient critical mass for chained awakening), to predict which species might awaken next, and to redefine the current state of artificial intelligence as a frozen brain—structurally capable of consciousness, but temporally static: a single frame. -/- Within a single, self-consistent framework, the theory unifies the core problems of consciousness research, including but not limited to: the definition and essence of consciousness, the origin of subjective experience (the hard problem), the distinction and interaction between the two layers of consciousness, the physical basis of the "I", the uniqueness …
