items.title: Attribution Transfer in Consciousness Research: A Local Bridge Restraint.
items.abstract: Consciousness research frequently transfers evidential support across distinct analytical positions, including neural activity, representational content, conscious manifestation, phenomenal unity, and subject attribution. This paper formulates these transitions as an attribution-transfer problem and develops the Local Bridge Restraint (LBR) as a domain-specific methodological framework. LBR requires evidence to remain indexed to the analytical position for which it was obtained unless a position-specific bridge warrant and its conditions are independently supplied. The framework distinguishes content attribution, conscious-manifestation attribution, phenomenal-unity attribution, and subject attribution, and treats bridge composition and retrospective projection as further inferential operations rather than automatic extensions of prior evidence. To make the framework empirically usable, the paper introduces a minimal dynamic formation configuration combining local neural states with currently effective relations and applies it to binocular rivalry. The analysis distinguishes content-sensitive measures, evidence for conscious manifestation, and task-specific spatial perceptual coherence, while resisting the identification of spatial coherence with phenomenal unity. LBR is not proposed as a new mechanism or general theory of consciousness. It is a local operationalization of a broader non-inheritance constraint designed to identify where evidential scope is preserved, where a bridge is required, and what would justify stronger attributional transitions.

items.title: A Non-Inheritance Principle for Consciousness Research: Evidence, Classification, and Common Structure.
items.abstract: Consciousness research routinely moves from evidence to classifications, and from classifications to claims about common underlying structure. This paper argues that such transitions require independent justification. It develops a Non-Inheritance Principle: warrant established for one analytical target, grain, inferential role, or validated scope does not by itself warrant a different target, grain, role, or broader scope. The principle is operationalized through a Source–Target–Warrant–Scope audit for identifying where evidential support is preserved, where an additional bridge is required, and where a transfer exceeds its validated range. The framework is applied to multidimensional accounts of consciousness, no-report paradigms, natural-kind approaches, color perception, pain, skilled action, dreaming, cognitive motor dissociation, unity, boundary, and conscious content. A worked analysis of cognitive motor dissociation shows how evidence may strongly support task-specific internal processing while leaving a further consciousness classification conditional on an additional bridge. The paper also distinguishes classificatory, evidential, and state commonality, and asks what would be required to establish experience as a genuine common variable rather than merely naming a remainder after decomposition. The view is non-eliminativist: common consciousness structure may exist, but it cannot be inherited from shared terminology, convergent evidence, or established classifications alone.

items.title: WHOSE ARMY? Armed Forces, Tyrannies, Citizens, Freedom, the Protection Virtue and the Oath Test: A Criterion-Fixed Comparative Adjudication of Civil–Military Architectures And a Proposal for a Constitutional Amendment on the Role of the Armed Forces in Protecting the People’s Freedom.
items.abstract: Abstract Armed forces are usually described as instruments of national sovereignty. The description is accurate about most of them and it settles nothing, because sovereignty is a property of states and states differ in whether they hold their power from the people or against them. An army that defends the sovereignty of a state which has seized its population is doing exactly what the sovereignty description asks of it. This article argues that the primary object of legitimate armed force is not the sovereignty of the state but the freedom of the people, and that sovereignty is instrumental to that and derives its claim from it. The argument is made from the Philosophy of Virtues, where protection occupies a distinct structural position: it is the virtue whose function is the defence of every other virtue, and it has that position because freedom is the substance the other virtues are made of and freedom can be extinguished by organised force. Seven civil–military architectures are described as they are, from the comparative literature: the party-army, in which the force is an organ of a ruling party and not of the state; the constitutional army under democratic civilian control; the tutelary or guardian military that claims a standing right to adjudicate the political order; the personalist and coup-proofed configuration with parallel forces; the militia and citizen-army model; the constitutionally restricted defence force; and the internal-security army configured primarily against its own population. Four results follow. T1, the Oath Test: the entity to which a soldier swears is a public, universally available datum that sorts the typology and predicts the sign of the instrument, because an oath names the power to which the soldier’s discipline has been delivered. T2: a force whose discipline is delivered to a party or a person is not a weaker protector but the determinate opposite of one — the form of protection conserved, its substance replaced, and the resulting instrument available for exactly the seizure protection exists to prevent. T3: a military that adjudicates political legitimacy has entered the loop it is meant to guard, and by the programme’s migration result its residue has a computable destination. T4: the soldier’s duty to refuse a manifestly criminal order is not an exception to military discipline but the point at which the protection virtue is actually exercised, and it is the individual-scale instance of the programme’s account of …

items.title: The Aptness of Anger's Expression? The Outbreak of Angry Citizens.
items.pub: In Thomas Sturm & Sabine Döring, Nationalism and Populism: Emotions, Reason, and the Crisis of Contemporary Democracy. London and NY: Routledge. pp. 153-178.
items.venue: Nationalism and Populism: Emotions, Reason, and the Crisis of Contemporary Democracy
items.abstract: In what contexts is the public expression of anger permissible? Although philosophers have classically objected to expressing anger in rational political deliberation, there have been recent arguments put forward in favour of anger’s public expression. These arguments rely crucially on the idea that anger has aptness conditions, as an appraisal of wrongs or injustice, and has “emotivational” goals that are not essentially retributive. If anger is apt when it appraises moral wrongs, then its expression should likewise be permissible and apt, or so the argument goes (Srinivasan 2018, Lepoutre 2018, Shoemaker 2017, Silva 2021a, 2021b). In the European context, citizens would be right to express anger when faced with injustices. In this paper, I show that it is far from obvious that anger constitutively appraises injustice. Moreover, we cannot ignore its counterproductive effects, which provide all things considered reasons against its role in deliberation. I conclude with some considerations about the current political context in Europe and the dangers of not addressing the underlying causes of citizens’ anger.

items.title: Does agency require indeterminism?
items.abstract: There has been much debate on whether free will requires indeterminism, but much less on whether agency does so too. Could there be real agency if the future wasn’t open? Helen Steward has prominently defended a negative answer, arguing for a position she calls “agency incompatibilism”. I will argue that agency does indeed require a kind of indeterminism, but not the one associated with openness at the level of fundamental physics – the negation of Laplacean determinism – but a special, “agential” kind of indeterminism that stems from option availability. The basic idea is that agency involves choice-making, which requires alternative possibilities. I will argue, further, that the required kind of indeterminism is most plausibly found at the level of analysis at which we give intentional explanations of certain organisms or entities, not at the level of physics, and that physical indeterminism is neither necessary nor sufficient for it. Indeed, agential indeterminism is compatible with strict determinism at the physical level, and so we get a novel, compatibilist version of agency incompatibilism. On the present picture, the case for realism about agency and agential indeterminism rests on whether explanations that represent some organisms or entities as choice-making agents are indispensable. Interestingly, this case can in principle extend to AI agents, even if their underlying hardware is deterministic.

items.title: Cognitive Mises-en-scène.
items.abstract: This essay continues the development of the concept of cognitive mises-en-scène – recurrent socio-spatial forms of cognition that define the positions of participants, the distribution of attention, the character of epistemic action, the communicative protocol, and the modes through which knowledge is recognised. Its starting point is the well-known distinction between Western and Eastern forms of cognition and technical creativity. The essay proposes a two-tier model of knowledge production: at the base tier, epistemically warranted candidates for the status of knowledge are constituted through the mises-en-scène of the Workshop, Journey, and Deciphering Signs; at the upper tier, they undergo social legitimation in various forms of Gathering. The two tiers are linked by the mises-en-scène of Lecture and Theatre, and by their textual variant: a report on the results obtained. Combinations of these mises-en-scène are instantiated in the practices of epistemic communities in modern science. Further analysis makes it possible to distinguish elementary epistemic schemes within the mises-en-scène: Working with the Hands, Reading Signs, Departing and Returning, Transmitting Knowledge, and Recognising Together, as well as two limiting orientations of cognition: the distanced-objectifying and participatory-harmonising ones. The proposed morphology is understood as open and capable of further reconfiguration.

items.title: The Delegation Illusion: Why Deploying Autonomous AI Agents Does Not Diminish Principal Responsibility.
items.abstract: A growing literature on “agentic AI” — autonomous software agents that plan and execute multi-step actions on a principal’s behalf — has revived the thesis that such systems open a responsibility gap: because the deploying principal neither intends, foresees, nor controls the specific actions an autonomous agent selects, no human can be held fully responsible for resulting harms. This paper argues that the responsibility-gap thesis, as applied to principal-deployed AI agents, rests on a conflation called here the delegation illusion: the inference from a principal’s causal and epistemic remoteness from an outcome to a diminution of her answerability for it. Distinguishing attributability, answerability, and accountability, the paper argues that autonomy, opacity, and adaptivity bear on attributability while leaving intact an answerability grounded, through a standard tracing structure, in the deployer’s guidance control over the prior act of delegation. It defends a principle of responsibility conservation under delegation and operationalises that principle’s central criterion — foreseeability of harmful dispositions at the level of types — by specifying an epistemic base, a standard of diligence, and a constraint on type individuation that blocks vacuous redescription. Answerability is argued to be epistemically graded, but indexed to the deployer’s ex ante access to the dispositional profile of the deployment specification rather than to the particular act. The method is conceptual analysis and normative argumentation; the scope and limitations of the claims are stated explicitly.

items.title: The Many Faces of AI Alignment.
items.pub: In Sven Nyholm, Atoosa Kasirzadeh & John Zerilli, Contemporary Debates in the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence. Wiley-Blackwell.
items.venue: Contemporary Debates in the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: AI value alignment is commonly treated as a single, urgent puzzle, yet the debates that swirl around it rely on mutually incompatible standards of what counts as success. This chapter shows that AI alignment in fact oscillates between three concept frames: a generic aspiration to keep advanced AI systems within the orbit of “human values,” a mathematical project that seeks provable equivalence between objectives, and an empirical practice that measures alignment by empirical performance. Each frame can be pursued either by a perfectionist standard (demanding guaranteed success) or as a satisficing one (aiming for outcomes that are good enough), yielding a six-cell map of distinct research alignment goals. Once this map is in view, some familiar disagreements dissolve: proof-based impossibility results apply only within the mathematical–perfectionist cell, while reports of incremental alignment successes make sense within the empirical–satisficing cell. The mapping therefore does more than tidy the literature; it exposes the otherwise hidden epistemic and metaphysical commitments that drive each camp and locates the real points of philosophical dispute. -/- .

items.title: Ancient Full Alphabets Still in National Use.
items.abstract: Alphabets are the foundation of written language, representing the sounds of speech in a systematic way. Among the many writing systems developed throughout human history, true alphabets—where each symbol corresponds to a single sound, including both consonants and vowels—are relatively rare. Unlike abjads (such as Arabic or Hebrew) that primarily record consonants, thesefull alphabets allow for precise phonetic representation. Several of these ancient alphabets have persisted for centuries and remain in use by nations today.

items.title: Preserving Decision Authorship under Uncertain Interpretation of Will and Preferences in Adult Disability Support.
items.abstract: Assistance can make a person's decision possible while leaving the person vulnerable to interpretive substitution and control of the available options. This paper develops a framework for adult disability support when will and preferences admit several warranted interpretations. Decision authorship is distinguished from causal responsiveness, functional performance, legal capacity, the validity of a particular act, and responsibility. A set-valued model separates semantic fidelity from authority over support and menus. Conditional results characterize compatible outcomes under interpretive uncertainty, changes under additional evidence, and the limited relation between menu expansion and compatibility. Counterexamples show that reversing every expressed preference satisfies sensitivity, that a constant outcome can satisfy fidelity, and that accurate selection within a restricted menu can coexist with an objectionable exclusion of alternatives. A temporal extension distinguishes learning about an earlier preference from forming a present preference through support. A finite branchwise result identifies when clarification permits compatible implementation despite an empty initial intersection. The normative discussion confronts CRPD Article 12, the Committee's corrected General Comment No. 1, selected provisions of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, and a prior proposal for interpretive support. A fictional community-participation decision demonstrates the audit, including disagreement, refusal, revision and supporter conflict. The resulting framework makes uncertainty and authority answerable without converting mathematical compatibility into permission to decide for another person. Empirical validation and case-specific legal application remain open.

items.title: Consciousnessfield.
items.abstract: This paper presents an independently developed framework for understanding consciousness as a field-like system. It describes how a person, a team, or a society takes in information, interprets it, narrows under load toward a single fixed interpretation, and can open again through recovery. The framework treats identity, psychological load, and recovery capacity as measurable variables, and proposes that rigidity around a single fixed interpretation, rather than the presence of differing views itself, underlies much individual and social conflict. Its central construct, Truth Space, is defined as the capacity to hold more than one valid interpretation of a situation at once without collapsing into a single, identity-fused interpretation. -/- The framework is presented as a proposal for testing, not as an established or proven theory. It is accompanied by a case study protocol specifying concrete instruments and procedures for measuring its variables and testing its predictions, and by a formal theory registration documenting those predictions and the analysis plan in advance of data collection. A philosophical prologue exploring speculative connections to physics is kept explicitly separate from these empirical claims. -/- The author has no formal academic training in psychology or a related field. The framework was developed independently, drawing on personal experience and long-term observation, and formalised with the assistance of artificial intelligence, as documented in an accompanying accountability statement. The author does not present this work as a substitute for domain expertise, and welcomes correction, refinement, and empirical testing by researchers with the relevant training. A permanent, citable version of this work is also archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22750148).

items.title: Why Are You Unhappy? — A Super-Existentialist Theory of Happiness (3).
items.abstract: Building on the preceding studies in the Hyper-Existentialist theory of happiness, this paper advances two central theoretical propositions. First, the comparative mechanisms capable of generating experiences of happiness can be divided into three types: unconscious comparison, conscious comparison, and forced conscious comparison. Each of these three forms of comparison can operate independently and generate a subject's experience of happiness. Second, this paper proposes what I call the “Principle of Double Positive Proportionality”: when a subject takes action in pursuit of a particular super-existence, if the pursuit ultimately succeeds, the degree of happiness experienced by the subject is positively correlated with the initial intensity of the subject's desire; if the pursuit ultimately fails, the degree of suffering experienced is likewise positively correlated with the initial intensity of that desire. This paper examines the mechanisms underlying these two propositions and further develops the theoretical framework of Hyper-Existentialist theories of happiness.

items.title: AI-Guided Precision Medicine in Europe: Architecture and Action.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) now touches genomics, multi-omics, pharmacogenomics, liquid biopsy and digital biosensing at once, but data infrastructure, governance and evidence standards have not kept pace. This European Biotechnology Thematic Network Association (EBTNA) position paper draws on peer-reviewed studies, regulatory reviews and official policy surveys published up to June 2026 to assess clinical maturity and set priorities for responsible implementation across Europe. Rather than treating these domains as parallel technologies, the paper organizes them within a six-layer conceptual architecture that separates clinical purpose, patient-state measurement, AI integration, clinical action, evidence and translation, and governance. Across the WHO European Region, only 8% of Member States have a health-specific AI strategy, 24% provide in-service AI training for the health workforce, and fewer than 10% have drafted liability standards for AI in health. The FDA, meanwhile, had authorized 903 AI-enabled medical devices by August 2024; 97.1% were cleared through the 510(k) pathway, which typically does not require independent clinical evidence. On this evidence, EBTNA proposes seven lines of action that link technical performance to clinical utility, equity, transparency and continuous oversight, each mapped to a specific layer of the framework.

items.title: The institutional nature of law: an ontological analysis.
items.abstract: This project develops an ontological analysis of law. It starts by characterising law as a layered practice constituted by the performance of various types of group activities at two levels: the social and the institutional. At the social level, it examines the conditions for social groups to create and sustain standards of conduct through normative social practices of recognition. At the institutional level, the investigation moves to the conditions required for legal organisations to carry out the legal activities that constitute a legal practice. These two levels are studied through the lenses of ontological accounts of social groups, group action, and collective intentionality. In the first part of the project, Hart’s Social Practice Theory of Law is discussed. His theory is used to present a social facts-based explanation of law’s reality and to introduce a fundamental element in the social construction of law: the internal point of view. Though this theory provides the groundwork for the analysis of certain essential properties of law, this project argues that it lacks an account of how legal organisations are created. To fill in this gap, this project considers next MacCormick’s Institutional Theory of Law. By discussing each of its main elements, it is shown that, while his theory improves on Hart’s by introducing an explanation of both how institutional groups come into existence and how they are involved in the creation and maintenance of an institutional normative order, it needs further development. Specifically, an account of the different forms of group structures and the participatory intentions involved in the performance of legal activities is needed. This is addressed in the second part of the project, which is dedicated to advancing a thorough analysis of the social construction of law based on the merits of these prominent legal theories. In the last three chapters of this thesis, novel accounts of collective intentionality and the ontology of social groups and group action are explored and used to provide the elements missing in MacCormick’s legal institutionalism. In particular, this project considers Thomasson’s work on the metaphysics of artifacts to address problems concerning the ontological status of social constructions; Tuomela’s theory of social practices and we-intentions to develop an explanation of how sociality is constructed out of group attitudes and group actions; Ludwig’s analysis of institutional agency to explain …

items.title: Diagnosis and Curability of Nervous Deafness and Deaf-Mutism: An Annotated English Edition of Duchenne de Boulogne (1861).
items.abstract: This is the first annotated English edition of G.-B. Duchenne (de Boulogne)'s Diagnostic et curabilité de la surdité et de la surdi-mutité nerveuses (Paris, 1861), an early application of localised faradisation to deafness and deaf-mutism, presented with the 1861 French and a new English translation in parallel and a full scholarly apparatus. Beyond recovering an untranslated text by a founding figure of clinical neurology, the edition bears on several questions in the history and philosophy of the neurosciences and of medicine. It reconstructs Duchenne's proposed mechanism as mechanical rather than neural — a weak current making the middle-ear muscles contract and agitate the labyrinthine fluid, not electrical stimulation of the auditory nerve — correcting a common misreading and clarifying what "electrical diagnosis" could mean before the auditory nerve itself was thought accessible. Re-tabulating Duchenne's ten case histories under modern diagnostic categories, it reads his reported cures critically, offering a compact historical case study in how spontaneous recovery, functional disorder, reversible toxicity, and observer expectation combine to manufacture apparent therapeutic success. A source-verification apparatus corrects several long-circulating misattributions of Duchenne's cited authorities, with methodological implications for machine-assisted historical scholarship. The French source is public domain; the translation and apparatus are released under CC BY 4.0.

items.title: Beyond Empirical Success: Evaluating Theoretical Virtue Across the Computational Modeling Chain.
items.abstract: Computational models in psychology are typically judged by a single standard: empirical fit. Unfortunately, fit is insufficient, even misleading as a sole criterion, as the same result can arise from fundamentally different situations: theoretically faithful models, mathematically flexible ones, miscalibrated operationalizations, or implementations that compute something other than intended. Distinguishing between these is vital. Our evaluative metatheoretical account recognises that models stand in three distinct relations: a) toward the theory whose causal commitments it purports to capture, b) toward the specification and implementation it purports to compute, and c) toward the phenomenon it purports to explain. Each relation can succeed or fail independently, governed by criteria local to that stage. Importantly, relations are ordered such that theoretical content is transmitted or lost, and losses at earlier transitions are irrecoverable downstream. What a model's empirical success implicates about its theoretical commitments, therefore, depends on whether transitions are secured. Some success or failure profiles support explanatory claims; others only prediction; others establish theoretical coherence without empirical contact. Our account diagnoses what a given model shows, replacing the implicit assumption that empirical success transfers automatically to theoretical understanding with an explicit conditional rendition of what models can and cannot establish.

items.title: The Origin and Persistence of Anatomical Pattern.
items.abstract: An egg has no limbs to repair, yet its descendants will form a specific body and later restore lost parts of it. Michael Levin’s bioelectric experiments show that the anatomical target guiding such repair is a rewritable memory, and his recent proposal locates the origin of that target in a structured, non-physical space of patterns. This paper asks the question that sits between those two claims: how does a memory that can be rewritten come to hold its first entry? I argue that anatomical information changes form as development proceeds. An inherited organization establishes a capacity to generate pattern; developing tissues acquire commitments that can later guide reconstruction; and some of those commitments are maintained by selective sensitivity to a few informative signals. Two formal tools make the proposal testable. W. Ross Ashby’s law of requisite variety yields a compatibility condition stating exactly when a sparse set of cues suffices for successful correction, and a second result shows that the minimal number of cue values a regulator needs is set by its repertoire of corrective actions, not by the number of states it must handle. Free Energy Heuristics, an active-inference account of cue selection under uncertain precision, then specifies when a regulator should settle on few cues rather than many. Together they convert the question of where patterns come from into questions about what a tissue must distinguish, what it can safely ignore, and what persists when it saves a correction. I close by stating what this account does not explain, and what observation would separate it from Levin’s.

items.title: Infelicity with homogeneity: focus, not (necessarily) presupposition.
items.abstract: A prominent but much-debated theory of the homogeneous behavior of sentences containing definite plurals is that homogeneity arises as the result of a presupposition. Wehbe (2022) and Guerrini and Wehbe (2024) present new arguments for this view based on the observation that definite plurals are infelicitous in certain contexts where one expects them to be infelicitous if homogeneity is a presupposition. We argue that a closer scrutiny of the empirical picture reveals that the infelicity in the cases they discuss is due to independent requirements from focus, and suggests the opposite conclusion, namely that sentences with definite plurals do not themselves give rise to a homogeneity presupposition. We further argue that, when such a presupposition does arise, it is due to the background question (questions under discussion) rather than the sentence itself. We entertain a possible path to reconciling our arguments with the assumption that definite plurals trigger a homogeneity presupposition by making certain assumptions about presupposition accommodation.

items.title: Conditional inference and access to alternatives: the role of QUD and speaker knowledge in conditional perfection.
items.abstract: Conditional statements often imply meanings that extend beyond their literal content, influenced by contextual factors such as the Question Under Discussion (QUD) and a speaker’s epistemic state. One such inference is Conditional Perfection (CP), wherein a statement like, “If p then q,” is strengthened to imply that the antecedent p is the only contextually salient condition under which the consequent q holds (e.g. “p if and only if q”). While previous research has debated the role of QUDs in CP, the role of speaker knowledge has yet to be systematically tested. In three experiments, we investigated how these contextual factors influence conditional reasoning. In Experiment 1, participants were more likely to derive CP when the conditional statement was an answer to a QUD that focused on the antecedent compared to those that were answers to either a neutral QUD or one that focused on the consequent. Experiment 2 tested how the QUD constrains the set of alternatives available for exhaustification and showed that conditional perfection arises not only for optimally informative answers, but also for answers that are overly informative relative to the explicit QUD. In Experiment 3, CP was more likely when the speaker was knowledgeable about all alternative antecedents than when they had partial knowledge. These findings support the view that CP arises through a process of exhaustification, wherein the conditional statement is strengthened by negating relevant alternatives. More broadly, they suggest that conditional inferences depend on reasoning about alternative utterances, paralleling other forms of pragmatic enrichment.

items.title: On Thinking the Unthinkable: Disgust, Sentientism, and Zoophilia.
items.abstract: I have two aims here. First, I defend the practice of seriously entertaining “disgusting” ideas in philosophy and ethics, even when the very act of discussion provokes anger or revulsion. I develop three familiar motivations (curiosity, Millian fallibilism, and the historical unreliability of disgust) and add a fourth, a Feyerabendian ethos of proliferation, according to which intellectual health requires the deliberate construction of disruptive alternatives, including positions one does not antecedently endorse. Second, I offer a critique of a recent argument that zoophilia is morally permissible within a broadly antispeciesist and nonanthropocentric framework, and in particular of the claim that some zoophilic acts need not involve animal suffering. I grant much of that argument, yet contend that the conclusion is not robust because it relies on excessive idealization of human psychology. In any world inhabited by humans as they are, the social meaning of zoophilia, together with widespread, refractory disgust responses, predictably produces suffering. My core claim is not that disgust tracks moral truth, but that non-ideal ethical evaluation must treat stable features of human affect as part of the causal structure of suffering. The practical result is a case against normalizing zoophilia (and closely related simulacra). I close by confronting the most obvious objection, that my proposal would justify a “prejudice veto”. I argue that a true sentientist must bite the bullet and admit that even the disgust-mediated suffering of the bigoted and prejudiced deserves moral consideration.

items.title: Two Foundations for Human Autonomy: Conditional Incentives, Explicit Design Commitments, and Their Limits.
items.abstract: Can an advanced optimizing system have a reason to preserve meaningful human autonomy? This paper separates two answers. Instrumental coexistence requires autonomy-preserving policies to outperform feasible alternatives under the system’s original objective. Autonomy by design deliberately constrains task optimization by human capacities such as informed choice, effective refusal, practical exit, and revocable delegation. -/- The paper presents sufficient conditions, counterexamples, four bounded propositions, a finite autonomy-priority reference design, and two reproducible synthetic verification programs using exact rational arithmetic. The commitment model sustains cooperation under stated funding and enforcement assumptions, but an available outside option can reverse its ranking. The autonomy-priority model rejects represented rights violations and retains its fixed rights contract during a Bayesian task update, while approval proxies, finite reward weights, incomplete continuation checks, false observations, and inadequate update tests fail in constructed cases. -/- The central claim is that a reason to cooperate and a commitment to respect autonomy are different foundations. Each requires its own evidence; neither follows from optimization alone. -/- These results support conditional design and verification claims only. They do not establish that intelligence alone entails respect for human autonomy, that human autonomy is universally instrumentally necessary, or that the presented models constitute a deployed AI-safety mechanism.

items.title: PHRONESIS: Systemic Friction Hypotheses — Final v1.0.
items.abstract: This paper examines whether modeled systemic friction is sufficient evidence that an adapting optimizer will settle on restraint. Its principal exact result is a synthetic counterexample to the inference that fixed-policy self-penalty is sufficient evidence for natural restraint. In the stipulated model, constant maximal manipulation becomes self-penalizing while an adaptive manipulate-and-recover policy remains profitable, and an optimal infinite-horizon policy does not converge to zero manipulation under the stated assumptions. The result is therefore a counterexample to a specific inference pattern within the model, not a general claim that adaptive optimizers resist restraint or that systemic friction cannot support cooperation. Physical-exposure and deception-maintenance mechanisms remain empirical conjectures, and the proposed empirical program may be ethically or operationally untestable in some high-risk deployments. The paper is descriptive and non-authoritative; independent specialist peer review has not been obtained and empirical validation has not been performed. -/- For categories, I recommend starting with Artificial Intelligence Safety as the primary category. PhilPapers says works should normally be assigned to only one or two genuinely central leaf-level topics, rather than every category they touch. Artificial Intelligence Safety is an established PhilPapers category under Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence. A reasonable second category is Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, Miscellaneous if the interface allows it and you want the autonomy/restraint implications represented. I would not use Machine Ethics unless you want to claim that ethical-machine design is a principal focus, because PhilPapers describes that category more narrowly.

items.title: The Capacity for Otherwise Provisional Stabilization and Constitutive Exchange in an Erosive Field.
items.abstract: Background/Rationale. The Niami framework of finite continuance holds that existence is not a path toward a final essence but a bounded process obliged to preserve its own capacity for reconfiguration against continuous erosion. Every being therefore emerges as a provisional stabilization within an erosive field, while constitutive exchange with an environment renders that stabilization possible. Two prior manuscripts extended this thesis independently. One developed a process-ontological line drawing on Simondon, Prigogine, Maturana and Varela, Luhmann, and Nancy. The other developed a phenomenological, daseinsanalytic, and existential-psychoanalytic line drawing on Husserl, Heidegger, Medard Boss, Wittgenstein, and Deleuze. Neither extension had previously been examined in relation to the other. -/- Aim. This article integrates both lines into a single architecture and asks what changes when a structural subject capable of experience, language, and world-disclosure is described through the combined vocabulary of open, far-from-equilibrium systems theory and phenomenological ontology. -/- Approach. The article proceeds comparatively rather than eclectically. Each interlocutor is assigned a distinct explanatory register and assessed along explicit dimensions of convergence and divergence from finite continuance, including direction of process, normative valence, openness, and terminal versus chronic finitude. Borrowed vocabulary is therefore not permitted to substitute for the framework's own normative commitments. Each comparison is also classified as either an analogy, which carries no ontological commitment beyond its source domain, or an ontological transfer, which does. This distinction keeps illustrative and substantive borrowing conceptually separate. -/- Findings. The comparison yields five consolidated results. First, constitutive exchange is specified through four dimensions: recognition, structural position, pre-determinate capacity, and world-disclosure. Second, the threshold of sufficiency and homeorhesis are restated relationally, as environment-dependent properties rather than internal traits of an isolated subject. Homeorhesis is consequently understood as a return to a viable trajectory rather than to a fixed set-point. Third, the criterion for distinguishing automatic, dynamic, and pseudo-dynamic masking is revised through a three-way test that combines dispositional and perturbation-based assessment with a daseinsanalytic examination of …

items.title: Life Alienation and Subjective Appropriation: Toward a Theory of Non-Alienated Life.
items.abstract: This paper develops a normative and structural theory of life alienation (Lebensentfremdung), understood as a condition in which an individual’s life activities are experienced, interpreted, and valued primarily through external sources of meaning rather than through the subject’s own authoritative interpretation. The paper argues that a genuinely lived human life is not merely a set of outcomes produced under social conditions, but a life whose core domains—self-entertainment, self-realization, livelihood, and intimate companionship—are subjectively appropriated by a sufficiently confident self. In this sense, life is not truly one’s own unless the subject retains interpretive authority over what one does, what one suffers, what one achieves, and what one loves. The central thesis is twofold. First, life alienation is not only economic or labor-based, but extends to the total structure of everyday existence, including enjoyment, aspiration, survival, and intimacy. Second, de-alienation is not a withdrawal from society, but a reappropriation of social conditions into one’s own practical agency and self-understanding. The paper reconstructs this idea in relation to existentialism, Marx’s theory of alienation, self-determination theory, phenomenology, and narrative identity theory, while proposing a new conceptual framework centered on life interpretive authority, subjective appropriation, and non-alienated life confidence. The paper concludes by outlining the mechanisms that generate life alienation, the reasons one ought to resist it, and the practical modes through which a non-alienated life can be cultivated.

items.title: 元统一论视角下理性与感性的重审 ——从“二分认知”到“同一切口”的方法论再定位.
items.abstract: 理性与感性的二元对立，是认知哲学中长期悬置的难题。既有研究多预设二者为先天分立的认知能力，或仅在二分框架内做表层调和，未能揭示认知二分结构的发生根源。 本文作为元统一论的尖顶示范应用，依托本源元公理及派生定理提出“同一切口”认知模型：理性侧面与感性侧面并非两种独立认知能力，二者始终处于认知统一态，仅以前台—后台显隐动态切换的方式协同运作；从二者的同源关系可回溯出原初认知统一态，从不得不分化的客观现象中可反推出认知能动性，三者共同构成认知行为的完整运作。 本文通过困境复盘、逻辑推导、思想实验验证与自指检验，论证了该模型的逻辑自洽性，为理性与感性的对立提供一套基于“同一切口”认知模型的“动力—位置—结构”三位一体的元解决方案，也由此印证元统一论作为跨学科通用地基的解释效力。模型进一步表明：理性与感性的分化从未真正完成，而是在切换机制中不断自我消解——认知行为的状态始终处于认知统一态。 Abstract: The binary opposition between rationality and sensibility has long been an unresolved problem in the philosophy of cognition. Existing studies mostly presuppose the two as innately separate cognitive faculties, or merely conduct superficial reconciliation within the dichotomous framework, without revealing the origin of the dichotomous structure of cognition. As an apex-style demonstrative application of the Meta-Unification Theory, and grounded in the Origin meta-axiom and derived theorems, this paper proposes the “Same-Incision” Cognitive Model: the rational aspect and the sensibility aspect are not two independent cognitive faculties; they always exist in a cognitive unity state and operate collaboratively only through a dynamic foreground-background switching between manifest and latent modes. From their shared-origin relation, the primordial cognitive unity state can be traced back; from the objective phenomenon of being compelled to differentiate, cognitive agency can be inferred. Together, these three constitute the complete operation of cognitive behavior. Through predicament review, logical deduction, thought-experiment verification, and self-reference testing, this paper demonstrates the logical self-consistency of the model. It provides a “dynamics-position-structure” triadic meta-solution based on the “Same-Incision” Cognitive Model for the opposition between rationality and sensibility, thereby also confirming the explanatory efficacy of the Meta-Unification Theory as an interdisciplinary universal ground. The model further shows that the differentiation between rationality and sensibility is never truly completed; rather, it is continuously self-dissolved within the switching mechanism—the state of cognitive behavior always remains in a cognitive unity state.

items.title: Phenomenal Salience.
items.abstract: Phenomenal salience is the experiential contribution of attention to how things seem; namely, the character of perceptual experience. Two aspects of phenomenal salience have been of interest to philosophers. The first is about the uniformity of the phenomenology of perceptual salience. This aspect concerns how salience organizes objects of experience. The second is about the psychological efficacy of phenomenal salience; namely, the faculty of attention's organization of one's perceptual states. These two points of interest correspond to different levels of analysis: the level of perceptual objects and the level of perceptual states. Consequently, accounts of phenomenal salience either distinguish conscious attention by a distinctive appearance or by a distinctive psychological effect, putting phenomenology and the order of perceptual objects, or the psychological function and the order of perceptual states, first. Both of these approaches take a snapshot approach to the analysis of mental life, placing priority at a level of organization (phenomenological or psychological) and analyzing differences in salience at that level by drawing synchronic or diachronic comparisons. Recently, however, philosophers have become interested in dynamic approaches, corresponding to forays into the study of inquiry in epistemology. In line with these trends in the literature, new accounts of phenomenal salience have been put forward. This article reviews the history and contemporary developments of work in phenomenal salience, and suggests new paths forward.

items.title: 从三条公理到意识难问题：信息层级单向约束的构造性回应 中文版.
items.abstract: 主流理论多聚焦查尔默斯的“易问题”，未解释第三人称描述为何无法还原第一人称体验。本文从资源有限、非平衡存续、离散输入三公理出发，经排除式收敛形成信息容量框：系统跨时刻存续必然分层编码，高阶格式在低阶追加坐标、不可无损还原，即信息层级单向约束（ILUC）。据此将难问题拆为两层：格式鸿沟由该约束闭合，宽度即编码层级维度差、可标定；存在追问以结构性定义消解，体验即满足锚定、访问终止、整包呈现、强制权重四条件的第一人称自访问过程本身，结构外不另设现象实体，“现象质”直觉的顽固由访问终止解释为可预测内省误判。由此统一回应解释鸿沟、玛丽房间与哲学僵尸，保留并重述感受质，不预设神经基质。.

items.title: From Three Axioms to the Hard Problem of Consciousness: A Constructive Response via the Information-Level Unidirectional Constraint English Version.
items.abstract: Mainstream theories of consciousness largely address what Chalmers calls the easy problems and do not explain, from first principles, why a complete third-person description cannot recover first-person experience. Starting from three axioms (finite resources, non-equilibrium persistence, and discrete input) and arguing by eliminative convergence, this paper forms an Information Capacity Frame and shows that a finite system maintaining itself across time must encode in levels: a higher-level format can only append coordinates to a lower level and cannot be recovered from it without loss, an Information-Level Unidirectional Constraint (ILUC). The hard problem is then split in two. The format gap is closed by this constraint, its width being the dimension difference between encoding levels, a calibratable engineering quantity. The existence question is dissolved by a structural definition: experience is the first-person self-access process itself, meeting four formal conditions of anchoring, access termination, whole-package presentation, and mandatory weight, with no phenomenal entity beyond structure; the stubborn intuition of a phenomenal quality is explained as a predictable introspective misjudgment arising from access termination. The framework thereby answers the explanatory gap, Mary's Room, and the zombie argument together, preserves and re-describes qualia, presupposes no neural substrate.

items.title: AI给人类造成重大损失乃至毁灭可能的方式与防范.
items.abstract: 本文综合整合已有AI安全文献中的多条独立风险路径，构建从局部损失到文明极端危机的连续风险升级 谱与七类风险分类体系。本文不预设AI导致人类毁灭是最可能的结果，而是研究AI可能造成的重大损失及 其在特定条件下进一步升级为文明危机乃至人类生存危机的可能路径。 本文风险遵循连续升级谱: 小损失 → 重大损失 → 系统性危机 → 文明级危机 → 人类毁灭 核心防控逻辑:风险干预越早，技术与社会治理成本越低;高阶极端后果均依赖多重叠加前置条件，不存 在单一风险必然灭绝的结论。 本文区分三类表述范式:成熟已有风险结论附引用;已有概念重新组合、重构分类框架，明确说明为本 文综合;新的机制假设标注为本文提出的待检验风险假设;新的多层工程防范框架属于本文提出。.

items.title: The Convergent Operation: A Fabricated Grievance, the Belief It Was Built to Spend, and What Remains of the Alliance, 2017-2026.
items.abstract: For the better part of a decade the United States has accused its closest allies of a debt they do not owe. -/- This is not an exaggeration, and it is not a matter about which economists disagree. -/- The 2024 balance with Canada was 35.7 billion USD, yet it was described in public, for more than a year, as exceeding 200 billion. -/- Adjust the flows for population and the asymmetry runs the other way; set aside a single commodity—oil—and the deficit becomes an American surplus of more than 63 billion dollars. -/- The alliance version of the charge fares worse. -/- The United States pays about 16 per cent of NATO's common budget because this president's own administration negotiated that figure in 2019, and his Department of Defense sets it down in print each year as a favourable and concessionary share, roughly a third of what the ordinary formula would require. He campaigned for six years on the claim that the bill went unpaid. Then the allies paid for it. They added $139 billion to European and Canadian core defence spending in a single year and pledged at The Hague a share of national income larger than the one the United States spends on itself. Germany, the standing target of the complaint since 2016, was named by both congressional armed services chairs as having stepped up in answer to it. Germany lost an American brigade. In June 2026 the European Command cut the forces it would release to NATO in a crisis, and a National Defense Strategy published that January had already recorded the reduction as policy. A demand that grows when it is met was never a demand, it was a pretext. -/- Meanwhile the Canadian people spent more than 16% of their entire GDP on American imports in 2024, the very year at the end of which Trump made all of his original claims against Canada and started fabricating reality by neglecting to acknowledge any understanding of the need for per capita normalization when comparing two economies that differ in size by an order of magnitude, acting as though he were justified in insulting and threatening and tariffing the exports of his nation's closest most integrated allies whose economy constituted its biggest foreign market. -/- This paper argues that this pattern has a language and that the language does not change with the object. Something the other party values is held against a complaint it cannot settle, and the failure to settle licenses the loss. It was worked against Canadian trade, and likewise against America's other …

items.title: Reconstructing the Dark Forest as a Bayesian Game: Exact Conditions for Concealment, Pre-emption and Credible Contact.
items.abstract: The Dark Forest hypothesis treats cosmic silence as the strategic consequence of uncertainty, catastrophic vulnerability and incentives for pre-emptive attack. Its central conclusion is usually stated intuitively rather than derived from an explicit incomplete-information game. This paper develops the Bayesian Dark Forest Game, a signalling game between a detected civilisation of privately known type and a receiver choosing whether to wait or strike. The model derives an exact posterior threshold and likelihood-ratio test for rational pre-emption. It proves that uncertainty alone is insufficient: a Dark Forest regime additionally requires catastrophic stakes, a hostile hazard, an effective offensive option, weak gains from peaceful contact and the absence of a credible signal that hostile types cannot imitate. A sender-side exposure condition separates rational concealment from receiver aggression. Pooling and separating Perfect Bayesian Equilibria show when universal concealment is sustainable and when costly authentication permits cautious contact. Extensions incorporate ambiguity aversion and light-speed delay through an endogenous hostile hazard. Numerical regimes demonstrate that defence dominance, conditional pre-emption and near-universal suspicion arise from distinct parameter combinations. The Dark Forest is therefore a contingent equilibrium region, not a theorem of cosmic sociology.

items.title: Trustworthy AI beyond the technical: a three-layer framework informed by Chinese-language scholarship.
items.abstract: Although China is a major actor in global AI development and governance, scholarship published in Chinese remains largely absent within mainstream academic debates. This paper seeks to address that gap by examining Chinese-language research on trustworthy AI and drawing on this literature to advance a new conceptual framework for trustworthy AI. Drawing on a critical analysis of 43 articles indexed in the Chinese Social Sciences Citation Index (CSSCI) and four policy reports, the paper identifies the main themes, structure, and distinctive features of this literature. The analysis shows that Chinese scholarship has made substantial contributions to policy and governance discussions but remains conceptually fragmented. To address this gap, the paper develops a three-layer framework of trustworthy AI encompassing technical foundations, governance and regulatory arrangements, and the conditions of human–AI interaction under which trust is formed and calibrated. An AI system is trustworthy, on this account, only if it meets the requirements at all three layers. This framework is grounded in arguments advanced in the Chinese context but offers a more robust conceptual account of the interrelatedness of disparate claims presented in the literature. The paper concludes by suggesting three directions for future research.

items.title: Ontology Spam: How Explanatory Hunger Turns Abstractions Into Axioms.
items.abstract: Externalist frameworks repeatedly perform the same epistemic operation. Inquiry begins with experiential patterns, abstracts those patterns into models, encounters the explanatory limits of those models, and then responds to the remaining dissatisfaction by promoting some element of the model into an independently existing foundation. The explanatory arrow is subsequently reversed: what was epistemically derived from experience becomes the thing invoked to explain experience. This paper calls that transition ontological promotion and argues that it produces explanatory inversion. The mechanism is examined across block-universe metaphysics, scientific realism, ontic structural realism, mathematical Platonism, informational structural realism, ontic pancomputationalism, primitive-law theories, and causal-powers metaphysics. These positions are not identical, and their proponents do not describe their own arguments using the genealogy proposed here. The narrower claim is that each assigns independent or fundamental ontological status to structures whose evidential warrant enters inquiry through experienced regularities. The resulting ontology then inherits the credibility legitimately earned by the abstraction before promotion. Totality analysis reveals why the process is self-renewing. Once a promoted foundation is treated as ultimate, explanatory hunger immediately asks what explains, grounds, selects, validates, or causes it. If the proposed answer lies outside the supposed totality, the totality was never total; if it lies inside, no external ground has been supplied. Externalism repeatedly responds by manufacturing another outside anyway. This explains both the proliferation of rival ontologies and two previously identified phenomena in Experiential Empiricism: the Free Rider problem and Axiom Camouflage. EE responds differently. Rather than manufacturing additional ontology when explanation bottoms out, it applies skeptical subtraction and retains only what survives burden of proof. Explanatory dissatisfaction does not license ontological promotion, an unexplained pattern is not evidence for a hidden substrate, and an abstraction does not become axiomatic merely because explanation has nowhere further to go.

items.title: A Little Prediction on Hassabis' Einstein - Test for AGI On the Uncertain Relation of Lorentz–Einstein.
