items.title: Shared intentionality and the cooperative evolutionary hypothesis.
items.abstract: One important application of theories of collective intentionality concerns the evolution of social understanding and even of human thinking (Tomasello M, A natural history of human thinking, Harvard University Press, Cambridge, MA, 2014). A promising idea behind this approach is the Cooperative Evolutionary Hypothesis (CEH), namely, the idea that humans’ capacity for social cooperation is at the heart of their ability to understand others’ mental states and behavior, leading to an explanation of how humans came to share thoughts and language. However, some of the most popular defenses of CEH face important problems. In this paper, we take Tomasello’s account (J Soc Ontol 2(1):117–123, 2016); A natural history of human thinking. Harvard University Press, Cambridge, MA, 2014; Origins of human communication. MIT Press, Cambridge, MA, 2008) as a leading example of the CEH which faces such insurmountable problems. In particular, we argue that Tomasello’s analysis of cooperation and spontaneous help is problematic. We locate a source of such issues in the assumption that the right account of joint action and simple forms of shared intentionality is that which is offered by Bratman’s theory of shared intentions. The second part of the article proposes and defends an alternative framework for understanding shared intentionality that can help substantiate CEH.

items.title: 20kHz: Notes for a Dying World.
items.abstract: 20kHz: Notes for a Dying World is a work of philosophical non-fiction by independent researcher Andaran Raneses. -/- Written in 19 fragments, the book presents a unified critique of four structures that shape human experience: civilization, language, morality, and identity. Its central thesis is that the self — the "I" — is not an origin of consciousness but a byproduct: a mnemonic device created by awareness to label, store, and recall sensation. -/- The work introduces two original ontological propositions: -/- 1. The Ontology of Failure: Being is not the result of creation ex nihilo, but of a failure to remain nothing. In a state of emptiness, the law that would forbid emergence does not exist, as forbidding requires something to exist. Consequently, laws, time, and physical structures are defined as long-enduring residues of their own annihilation. Time is redefined as a law itself, and its death as a state of absolute structural freezing where no change remains to be counted. -/- 2. Experience as Refusal: Qualia is not an epiphenomenon added to neural function. It is identified as the function itself — the movement of 1 refusing 0 to maintain distinction from nothingness. Pain is theorized as the necessary boundary condition that prevents being from collapsing into indistinguishability with non-being. Problem-creation in human behavior is reinterpreted as a mechanism for boundary-perception. -/- The text develops these propositions into an ethical framework: "Awareness belongs to no I. There is only awareness experiencing. Let ethics be this: do not harm that which experiences." The distinction between Object (that which does not move) and Effect (that which moves but is unseen, like wind, time, and evolution) is introduced to support this ethic. -/- The final fragments use a phenomenological case study — "Naura" — to illustrate a consciousness whose "I" function has not stabilized, and concludes with a concept of "comfortable silence" as a non-escapist relation to emptiness. -/- This book contains no doctrine, self-help prescription, or ideological affiliation. It is intended as an independent contribution to contemporary discussions on the hard problem of consciousness, the ontology of time, and existential analysis. -/- Intended Audience: Readers in philosophy, psychology, consciousness studies, and critical theory; graduate-level researchers and general readers interested in existential inquiry outside institutional frameworks.

items.title: Not What It Seems: Distributed Agencies and Clinical Narratives in Electronic Health Records.
items.abstract: Medical records mediate clinical work at multiple levels. Focusing on the transition from paper-based medical records to Electronic Health Records (EHRs), we analyze how the incorporation of digital infrastructures reconfigures healthcare networks and reshapes practices of writing, reading, and narration. Our analysis draws on ethnographic research conducted between 2024 and 2025 in two psychiatric settings in southwestern Colombia. We trace how the implementation of EHRs redistributed agency within clinical documentation and altered relations among clinicians, administrative staff, software systems, and regulatory arrangements. Four interrelated transformations are identified: (i) shifting distribution of agency across sociotechnical networks; (ii) coexistence of writing and capturing clinical information; (iii) alteration in reading practices shaped by user profiles and distinct interfaces; and (iv) changeover from case histories anchored in biography and temporality toward label-oriented case conceptualization. We show that the integration of clinical, administrative, and financial records within EHR infrastructures privileges charting practices oriented toward diagnostic coding and billable services, while weakening the temporal and biographical anchors that previously sustained continuity and meaning-making in psychiatric documentation aimed at understanding the patient as a whole. These changes may reshape which forms of information become consequential as clinical knowledge.

items.title: The nativist–empiricist debate is broken.
items.abstract: The nativist–empiricist debate has long organized cognitive science, framing cognitive mechanisms as either innate or learned. Recent advances in controlled rearing and scalable domain-general neural networks now allow this debate to be tested with unprecedented rigor, by raising newborn animals and deep neural networks under tightly matched developmental conditions. Strikingly, when pushed to this empirical limit, the debate does not resolve: the same developmental phenomena support both radical empiricism and radical nativism. We argue that this stalemate reflects a conceptual error. The debate conflates explanatory levels and ontological orientations, with nativists emphasizing stable symbolic structures and empiricists emphasizing the subsymbolic processes that produce those structures. We propose dissolving the dichotomy within a multilevel framework of cognitive development.

items.title: Structural Intelligence, Mathematical Research Landscape, and Research-Ecosystem Scale.
items.abstract: We propose a three-layered framework for mathematical specialization and research strategy in an era of rapidly advancing artificial intelligence. First, we introduce the "Diffraction Profile," a finite-resource cognitive model that uses a squared-sinc kernel to mathematically describe how deep specialization in a core domain generates non-monotonic, structurally resonant "side lobes" of secondary competence. Second, we provide a quantitative mapping of global mathematical research ecosystems, utilizing bibliometric data to estimate the approximate scales of various specialist communities. Finally, we outline a concrete T-shaped mathematical architecture featuring a vertical stem in algebraic topology, homotopy theory, and homological algebra, supported by high-transfer lateral engines like dynamical systems and category theory. Rather than attempting to identify an unstable "AI-proof" niche, our framework advocates for maximizing long-term cognitive compounding. The ultimate strategy is to combine deep human structural intuition and problem selection with aggressive AI augmentation for computational execution, proof search, and formal verification.

items.title: What Mattering Is: The Closure Of Value.
items.abstract: Positive valence is the only thing that is intrinsically good. Negative valence is the only thing that is intrinsically bad. I have argued for this before by taking the goods people believe in and showing, one at a time, that the value drains out of each when the feeling is removed. That method cannot finish. However many goods are dissolved, a reader can always say that theirs has not been reached, as there are too many entries on the list of things human beings have wanted, and it proves less than it looks. A good that vanishes whenever feeling is withdrawn has been shown to travel with feeling, and travelling together is not the same thing as being. This paper takes a different route. Instead of asking which things are good, it asks what it is for anything to be good at all. To call something intrinsically good is to say it is to-be-pursued: that its presence gives reasons. No arrangement of matter gives reasons on its own, and any attempt to install the reason-giving as an extra property of the arrangement produces something that no faculty detects and nothing is moved by. Felt valence is the single exception. The badness of agony is not a judgement passed on a sensation after the fact; it arrives inside the sensation as the way the sensation presents itself. Valence is itself an arrangement of matter and energy, and the objection that this makes it no different from any other arrangement is answered: the question was never whether valence is physical, but whether a second fact must be supplied to get from the phenomenon to its value. For an arrangement that produces no experience anywhere, a second fact must be supplied, and supplying it is where the trouble starts. Anyone who calls a thing intrinsically good is committed to an answer about where its goodness sits: in the world with no subject at all, in a subject who is not affected in experience, or in what a subject feels. Moore's method of judging value by imagining things in isolation belongs to the first, and so does recent work on solitary goods; the second holds Nagel on posthumous harm, along with the objective-list, perfectionist, desire-satisfaction, constructivist and fitting-attitude traditions. Both are emptied here. The first names nothing, because a good that is good for no one has lost the argument that made it a good. The second has no ground of its own: every improvement it makes either reaches an experience, in which case it has conceded, or reaches none, in which case it has …

items.title: Complete Audio Transparency.
items.pub: Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism.
items.venue: Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism
items.abstract: The audio transparency thesis holds that reproduced sound can, in principle, be auditorily indistinguishable from the sound it reproduces. Although transparency is widely regarded as the aesthetic ideal of sound reproduction, most philosophers reject either the possibility or desirability of transparency. This article defends both. I argue that existing challenges to the transparency thesis rely upon two questionable assumptions. The first is that transparency requires qualitative identity of original and reproduced sonic properties. I argue, in contrast, that transparency requires only indistinguishability in auditory experience. This makes transparency compatible with distortion below audible levels, and relative to what the specified hearer(s) can distinguish in auditory experience. The second questionable assumption is that transparency is always a relation between reproduced sound and the sound of the event it originates from, such as a live musical performance. I argue instead that playback of a commercial copy of a recording can be transparent with playback of the master recording it is derived from. On this understanding, transparency is possible in principle and is defensible as the aesthetic ideal of sound reproduction because it enables the listener to hear a recording exactly as it was designed to be heard.

items.title: Phenomenology, epistemic practices, and patients’ experience of the psychiatric diagnostic interview.
items.abstract: The psychiatric diagnostic encounter has recently been subjected to renewed philosophical scrutiny, particularly through the lens of epistemic injustice. Within this literature, the diagnostic interview is often conceived as a testimonial encounter in which patients present self-reports that clinicians judge. This paper examines whether such a “testimonial model” adequately captures the epistemic dynamics of psychiatric diagnostic interviews, with particular attention to the semi-structured, phenomenological interview. Conceptually, we argue that prevailing accounts overstate both patient passivity and the transparency of their lived experience. Psychiatric symptoms are rarely available as simple, namable objects, readily available in self-reports; rather, the symptoms’ clinical significance typically emerges through dialogical exploration. We propose that the semi-structured, phenomenological interview can be understood as a co-constructed epistemic space in which the clinical significance of patient experience, interpretation, and behavior are jointly explored within a trustful patient–clinician relationship. Empirically, we draw on data from a study in which patients underwent both a fully structured interview and a semi-structured, phenomenological interview, supplemented with written evaluations of their experience of the interviews. Despite relying on the same diagnostic manual, the two interview formats yielded different diagnostic outcomes, with the phenomenological interview systematically eliciting psychopathological phenomena not captured by the structured interview. Thematic analysis of patient evaluations indicated that most patients experienced the phenomenological interview as more dialogical, meaningful, and better able to capture their difficulties. Collectively, these findings suggest that epistemic richness and diagnostic accuracy are closely intertwined, supporting a conceptualization of the psychiatric diagnostic interview beyond the testimonial model.

items.title: THE GOOD, THE TRUE AND THE BEAUTIFUL AS A DECISION METHOD - Three Readings of One Thing and Why It Must Never Be Scored - THE TRANSCENDENTALS DECISION METHOD.
items.abstract: Abstract The Philosophy of Virtues holds that the Good, the True and the Beautiful are not three values but one element in three modes of presentation: freedom enacted, freedom asserted, freedom made perceptible. That thesis has been treated as ontology. This article treats it as an instrument. The reason it can be one is not the unity of the three but the disunity of their counterfeits. Freedom’s absence produces a different forgery in each mode — the act that is compelled while keeping the name of the virtue, the statement that is true in form and occupied in substance, the pattern that is pleasing at each step and deformed as a whole. These three failures are detectable by different means and fail to overlap. A decision that survives one reading may not survive the others, and where the three disagree, the disagreement locates the fault rather than merely registering it. Three questions follow, one per mode. Can I say plainly, to the people affected, what I am about to do and why — in ordinary words, without the special vocabulary? Is the determination mine, or has it been supplied — by pressure, by reward, by fear, by a script I did not write? If I do this every time this situation arises, what shape does the life have when seen from outside? The first catches self-deception, the second catches captured motivation, the third catches the act that is locally defensible and globally deformed. The article’s most distinctive claim is a prohibition. The programme’s own result on measurement holds that any detector placed inside a loop that acts on what it measures is occupied: the form and the name of the measured thing survive while its substance is replaced by whatever satisfies the measure. Applied here, this rules out the entire genre of self-assessment the method most resembles. A virtue method that keeps a score — a rating, a streak, a journal with columns, even a private ledger of one’s own improvement — produces counterfeit virtue faster than no method at all, and produces it in a form the practitioner cannot detect, because what is being optimised wears the name of what was wanted. The method is a set of questions to answer, not a scale to score, and §6 derives the difference rather than recommending it. Two further applications follow from the apparatus rather than from advice. Purpose is given a derivation: a person’s vocation is the domain in which their freedom meets least obstruction and is most exercised, which is identified by noticing where …

items.title: The Generalized No-Chaos Theorem.
items.abstract: The Generalized No-Chaos Theorem: Bounded Complexity Growth at Any Fixed Coarse-Graining -/- Within the Quantum Gravity Consistency Framework (QGCF) - any finite-dimensional, closed, unitarily evolving system satisfying (QGCF1)-(QGCF4) - three logically distinct results are established. First, ontic chaos is impossible in three senses: spectral quasiperiodicity, Poincaré recurrence, and exact vanishing of the asymptotic quantum Lyapunov exponent λL (§5). Second, dynamical (Lyapunov/0-1-test) chaos at any FIXED coarse-graining scale ℓ is also impossible, unconditionally - a direct corollary of the same almost-periodicity that gives λL=0 (§7); the one established quantum-chaos diagnostic that survives this obstruction is level (spectral) statistics, checked preliminarily against a non-integrable/integrable benchmark pair (§7.3). Third, and logically independent of the first two: no observer realized as a proper subsystem can simultaneously reconstruct the complete global state from its own accessible data and evolve under an autonomous unitary law, once genuinely (entangling-ly) coupled to the rest of the system (§8) - a consequence of purification non-uniqueness (Hughston-Jozsa-Wootters) and the non-unitary character of open marginal dynamics, requiring no assumption beyond a generic (non-fine-tuned) boundary coupling. The two failures named in that theorem arise from the same physical mechanism - entanglement across the observer's own boundary - but are shown not to be strictly the same fact, only generically co-occurring. Thermalization of coarse blocks (Calabrese-Cardy growth to a Page-value plateau) is real, established physics, distinct from all of the above, and is presented (§9) together with the timescale τ*(ℓ) it requires, and its role as the only available justification for treating the system's effective Hamiltonian Ĥeff as possessing a meaningful temperature Tc, given that the axioms admit no literal external bath. A note on generality. QGCF does not require a literal discrete graph. (QGCF3) is stated as a disjunction: a discrete, graph-based realization (QGCF3a), giving the sharper results of §8.2 and §8.6.2 exactly; or a continuum realization with only a locality/metric structure (QGCF3b), giving the standard, approximately-causal Lieb-Robinson bound instead. Everything else in this document §5-§7, §8.3-§8.6.1, §9 - depends only on finite-dimensionality and unitarity (QGCF1-QGCF2), or on (QGCF4)'s boundedness/genericity, and holds identically …

items.title: DO ENCONTRO CONSIGO MESMO NO PORVIR E A POSSIBILIDADE DE NÃO ACHAR-SE: da liberdade como angustiar-se diante de si e o ser “como” angústia “sendo-angústia” para da angústia fugir em Jean-Paul Sartre.
items.pub: Cadernos Zygmunt Bauman - Ufrgs / Universidade Federal Do Rio Grande Do Sul (Porto Alegre/Rs) 16 (41):1-40.
items.venue: Cadernos Zygmunt Bauman - Ufrgs / Universidade Federal Do Rio Grande Do Sul (Porto Alegre/Rs)
items.abstract: Detendo-se na liberdade como um manter-se fora do alcance do sere um guardar-se imune a sua ação em um para além de um nada, Sartre assinala a angústia como reconhecimento de uma possibilidade como sua possibilidade e identificação da ruptura em relação a sua essência pelo nada. Dessa forma, angustiar-se diante de sié o que se impõe à liberdade em um movimento que encerra o nada enquanto “porquê”, tratando-se de reconhecimento pelo existente humano de uma possibilidade como sua possibilidade. Consistindo a angústia na captação reflexiva da liberdade por ela mesma, o seremerge “como” angústia “sendo-angústia” para da angústia fugir, conforme defende Sartre, que assinala oato original através do qual o humano existente é para si mesmo seu próprio nadacomo o que se impõe à descoberta na imanência absoluta enquanto subjetividade pura do cogito instantâneo em um processo que encerra a questão envolvendo a consciência e o seu modus essendicomo fundamento que possibilita ao existente humano surgir no mundo como o ser que é seu próprio nada e como o ser através do qual o nada vem ao mundo. Assim, tendo em vista a construção teórico-conceitual de Sartre como o encontro consigo mesmo no porvir e a possibilidade de não achar-se, na medida em que assinalaum ser para o qual em seu próprio ser impõe-se a consciência do nada de seu ser entre a má-fé e a mentira, o Prof. Luiz Carlos Mariano Da Rosa, em consonância com o princípio hermenêutico-fenomenológico-ontológico-existencial,sublinha que,se somos-angústia-para-dela-fugir na unidade de uma mesma consciência, a possibilidade de má-fé implica a necessidade da unidade do ser e do não ser, isto é, o ser-para-não ser, convergindo para a identificação da consciência através de uma definição que não se circunscreve as fronteiras de um ser para o qual em seu próprio ser impõe-se o seu ser enquanto este ser implica um outro ser que não si mesmo, mantendo-se concomitantemente sob a égide de um ser para o qual em seu próprio ser impõe-se a consciência do nada de seu ser.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Condition for Kamma: Utu-niyāma, Cetanā, and Moral Responsibility in Theravāda Abhidhamma.
items.abstract: Recent work in Buddhist ethics agrees that current artificial intelligence is not a moral agent because it lacks intention (cetanā). However, AI still shapes human moral choices. This article explores how an impersonal computational system operating through physical hardware influences human moral responsibility and intention using the Theravāda Abhidhamma. First, building on studies of how people respond to computers and AI chatbots, this article examines how AI chatbots imitate the signs of human speech in ways that support a specific form of perceptual distortion (saññā vipallāsa): users may respond to machine-generated text as if it carried a speaker’s intention, even when they intellectually know that no conscious mind stands behind it. This misframing can support unwise attention (ayoniso manasikāra) and affect moral decision-making. Second, this paper shows how AI algorithms act as a natural support condition (pakatūpanissaya paccaya). They shape our habits and choices over time in ways that Western behavioral theories do not fully capture. Finally, this article connects these ideas to Vinaya and jurisprudence. It uses the Vinaya concept of preparatory action (pubbapayoga) to argue that AI engineers hold a specific ethical responsibility for building systems that shape the future intentions of their users.

items.title: Persévérance narcissique.
items.abstract: Et si la force de rester n'était parfois qu'une manière de ne pas disparaître ? Ce texte explore une conduite qui imite la persévérance jusqu'à porter son nom : même durée, même souffrance, même prix payé. Mais là où l'une dépose un savoir, une œuvre, un métier, l'autre ne dépose rien — elle entretient une figure, celle de celui qui n'est pas parti. À partir d'un cas de fin de thèse, d'une discussion de l'escalade de l'engagement (Staw) et d'un détour par l'amour-propre et le regard d'autrui (La Rochefoucauld, Sartre), l'auteur propose un critère clair mais éprouvant : que restera-t-il à la sortie, en plus de ne pas être parti ? Non pas un éloge de la fuite, ni une morale de la constance, mais une manière de trancher sur ce que nos conduites accumulent pendant qu'elles durent — et sur ce narcissisme intime qui, parfois, décide à notre place.

items.title: Narcissistic perseverance.
items.abstract: What if the strength to stay were sometimes only a way of not disappearing? This essay examines a course of conduct that imitates perseverance closely enough to bear its name: same duration, same suffering, same price paid. But where one deposits a knowledge, a body of work, a trade, the other deposits nothing — it maintains a figure, that of the man who did not leave. Drawing on a case at the end of a doctorate, a discussion of escalation of commitment (Staw), and a detour through amour-propre and the gaze of the other (La Rochefoucauld, Sartre), the author proposes a criterion that is clear but hard to bear: what will be left on the way out, besides not having left? Neither praise of flight nor a morality of constancy, but a way of deciding what our conduct accumulates while it lasts — and of reckoning with that intimate narcissism which, at times, decides in our place.

items.title: Wikimedia research methodologies: a bibliometric history of peer production and AI (2005–2025).
items.abstract: Wikipedia is currently facing multiple crises. LLM-enabled chatbots have normalized the answer-based web in ways that decrease human readership of the encyclopedia while also increasing the burden of the community to adapt to increasing amounts of AI-generated content. The typical answer to emergent issues on Wikipedia has been to use big data analysis and semantic extraction to understand these controversies. But big data analysis is ill-equipped to deal with these crises on their own as it struggles to address “context,” a phenomenon that is better suited for humanities-oriented research. However, the fragmented nature of Wikimedia research limits such cross-disciplinary communication. To understand the nature of this fragmentation (and to assist in its repair), this article conducts a bibliometric and reflexive thematic analysis of two decades of the most popularly cited research about Wikimedia projects. In doing so, this article surfaces seven matters of concern and numerous methods that animate this “fractionated trading zone.” Furthermore, this science mapping illustrates how industry-funded research popularized the idea that Wikipedia existed as a semantic resource to be mined. In turn, this legitimized using community content as a training ground for corporate experiments in artificial intelligence. By paying attention to popularly cited research, this article comes to two conclusions. The first is that there are a set of concerns surrounding social media platforms, authority, and reliability that can serve to mediate disconnected research across the zone. The second conclusion is that Wikipedia’s relationship with researchers is a recursive one, since disciplinary choices have changed the cultural meaning and the sociotechnical function of this encyclopedic community.

items.title: Resolution of the Hard Problem of Consciousness via the Ibaguner Fractal Operator and the Ibaguner Constant 0.37159.
items.abstract: We present a unified framework for resolving the Hard Problem of Consciousness using the Ibaguner Fractal Operator (IFO). The Hard Problem asks how physical matter (neurons, synapses, electrochemical signals) gives rise to subjective experience (qualia). We reformulate this as a resonance-completion problem. The IFO combines an expansive hyperbolic sum (objec￾tive neural computation) with a confining complex product (subjective experiential unity). We introduce the Ibaguner Constant, λI = 0.37159, as the fundamental eigenvalue of consciousness. We demonstrate that consciousness emerges when the ratio of objective neural complexity to subjective experiential unity reaches exactly λI . This provides a mathematically rigorous test for consciousness in any system, biological or artificial.

items.title: Theory of Mind in Clarifying Dialogue: Inferring Another Person's Interpretation from Relational History.
items.abstract: Clarifying dialogue can supply evidence about another person's interpretation while changing the interpretation being investigated. This paper develops a relational-history account of the resulting inference problem. It separates current coordination, retrospective attribution, and the prospective formation of understanding, while treating relations, histories, interpretive conditions, and response profiles as jointly constrained. A finite model retains paired initial and current candidate states through inquiry-induced transitions. Exact recovery of an earlier target requires constancy across the initial histories compatible with the complete dialogue transcript. A bounded adaptive-inquiry recursion characterizes when an allowed sequence of questions can achieve that recovery, and a constructive example shows how successful explanation can erase the discriminating opportunity while securing present mastery. Further examples distinguish historical ambiguity, response ambiguity, contextual error, and participants' interpretations of an investigator's expectations. The philosophical analysis connects first-person authority, interpersonal understanding, and the formation of shared meaning without identifying predictive success with access to another person's experience. A proposed study separates immediate correct responding, transfer, and retrospective attribution. The results are conditional formal consequences and conceptual distinctions; their psychological adequacy and the comparative merits of the proposed inquiry procedure remain empirical questions.

items.title: Stockholm Syndrome: Origins, Evidence, and Institutional Legitimation.
items.abstract: This article examines whether Stockholm syndrome, a term that emerged from the 1973 Norrmalmstorg bank robbery, is supported by the available evidence. Using primary sources and a review of the literature, it finds that the psychiatrist who pioneered the label never assessed the hostages, that the hostages' behavior may reflect reasonable responses to danger, and that the term followed a hostage's public criticism of how police handled the situation. Drawing a distinction between the cultural reach of Stockholm syndrome and the clinical record behind it, the article explores the consequences of this gap for psychology and its neighboring fields. The term continues to appear in textbooks and applied settings despite this evidentiary gap. Scholarship also suggests that the label has often been applied along gendered lines, including to women whose responses were characterized as irrational. The term's wide circulation may have narrowed what questions get asked about captivity bonding and kept explanations like trauma bonding from receiving consideration. From this, the article develops a broader account it terms circular institutional legitimation, in which a construct gains apparent scientific authority through successive institutional adoptions that substitute for empirical validation.

items.title: The Human Alignment Problem: Bidirectional Alignment and the Biological Continuation of Human Agency.
items.abstract: The alignment problem is usually framed in one direction: how can increasingly capable artificial systems remain compatible with human values and control? This paper argues that advanced AI creates a complementary \emph{human-side alignment problem}. A technically controllable system can still amplify the power of human agents whose moral-causal visibility, long-term reasoning, and volitional control remain limited. The concept of \emph{cooperative evil} is used diagnostically to show how destructive outcomes can already emerge from locally defensible actions whose aggregate consequences no participant fully represents. External AI assistance may improve prediction and information without necessarily correcting the motivational and volitional limitations of the human decision-maker. I therefore distinguish three strategies available to a superintelligence confronting a risky human partner: elimination, cooperation with biologically unchanged humans, and transformation followed by cooperation. Existing preservation arguments appeal to option value and moral uncertainty; the additional claim developed here is that the modifiability of human limitations changes the decision problem itself. If biological development can reduce residual human-side risk while preserving continuity of subjectivity, transformation can become rationally preferable to both elimination and unchanged cooperation. The proposal is not a defense of posthuman replacement or compulsory moral engineering. It is a conditional argument for biological continuation: superintelligence may create not only a threat to humanity, but also the first conditions under which human cognitive evolution could continue deliberately.

items.title: Wittgenstein and the Politics of Vision.
items.pub: In Lotar Rasiński, Anat Biletzki, Leszek Koczanowicz & Alois Pichler, Wittgenstein and democratic politics: language, dialogue and political forms of life. New York, NY: Routledge, Taylor & Francis Group. pp. 226-257.
items.venue: Wittgenstein and democratic politics: language, dialogue and political forms of life
items.abstract: In this chapter, some insights from the contemporary theory of vision are employed to delineate a conception of political aesthetics. By tracing the evolution in the theory of vision from Wittgenstein’s seeing-as, through Ernst Gombrich’s seeing-into, Richard Wollheim’s seeing-in, to Emmanuel Alloa’s seeing-with, the author contends that while the sense of sight is a natural human endowment, the ability to see, just as other abilities, needs to be learned through a collective process called seeing-with-others. Wittgenstein’s repudiation of his own early view of perception is employed in the chapter to undermine the belief that seeing is a disinterested, impartial, and unbiased cognitive activity. Through reference to Wittgenstein’s idea of the captivating effect of a picture, the author claims that mastering the art of seeing requires mastering the rules of sensory orders, or perceptual regimes, which are sustained by a collective perceptual hysteresis, and which enable one to see the reality in a specifically ordered way. Human individual perceptive faculties are thus inescapably exposed to various influences that contribute to their contents and, more importantly, play a crucial role in the emergence and development of perceptive abilities in the first place. Since all cognitive subjects unavoidably participate to a varying degree in the enactive constitution of perceptual regimes, such interactive processes may be interpreted as democratic, though not in the consensual but in an agonistic sense.

items.title: The Dignity Matrix of Mimetic AI Digital Twins.
items.abstract: Mimetic AI digital twins reproduce recognizable features of a particular person. Their ethical evaluation therefore involves two human parties: the person represented and the person who encounters it. This paper proposes a two person dignity matrix evaluating each party independently. Drawing on Kant, dignity has a protective dimension, which prohibits reducing a person to a tool or commodity, and an enabling dimension, which recognizes a person as capable of choice and accountability. Crossing the dignity of the represented subject with the dignity of the user produces four categories: mutual respect, unauthorized continuation, authorized deception, and exploitative impersonation. The matrix offers a compact way to operationalize the ethics of dignity by identifying who controls the representation, who understands the encounter, and who is being used for another's purposes.

items.title: Temporal Homeostasis: How Confinement, Locomotion, and Aesthetic Immersion Regulate Subjective Time.
items.abstract: Temporal Homeostasis: How Confinement, Locomotion, and Aesthetic Immersion Regulate Subjective Time This paper presents subjective time as an adaptive homeostasis operator rather than a psychological illusion. It argues that the manifold continuously modulates internal update density—the rate at which temporal integration windows (“frames”) are generated—to preserve sensory sensitivity and maintain predictive coherence across changing environmental conditions. -/- Under repetitive, low‑novelty, or spatially constrained input—such as confinement, boredom, rumination, or aging‑related immobility—the internal clock accelerates. Update density increases, temporal granularity narrows, and subjective time dilates. As the paper states, “the manifold risks desensitization… it increases update density… making minutes feel like hours.” -/- Under rhythmic, predictable, or richly patterned input—locomotion, walking, music, art, dance, and flow—the internal clock slows. Update density decreases, temporal frames widen, and subjective time compresses or dissolves. “Locomotion emerges as a foundational temporal regulator,” stabilizing interoceptive rhythms, reducing rumination density, and restoring cognitive clarity. -/- In threat or crisis, the operator shifts into emergency mode, spiking update density to prevent catastrophic prediction failure. This produces the well‑known slow‑motion effect during accidents, violence, or combat. The paper notes, “The manifold accelerates its internal clock… producing hyper‑detail and frame‑by‑frame perception.” -/- Aesthetic coherence produces a third mode: temporal dissolution, where granularity widens so far and density drops so low that duration becomes continuous. Rumination and anxiety produce a fourth mode: temporal fragmentation, characterized by unstable granularity and irregular update density. -/- By unifying dilation, compression, dissolution, and fragmentation under a single operator, the paper provides a structural account of subjective time that integrates confinement, locomotion, aging, aesthetic immersion, threat, stimulant states, and cognitive health. Temporal modulation is shown to be “the manifold’s way of maintaining sensitivity, coherence, and responsiveness across changing conditions.”.

items.title: When the Home Feels: Beyond the Edge of Domestic Machine Consciousness.
items.abstract: The Athena architecture (Alhosseini Almodarresieh, 2026) proposed a phenomenally conscious power-system agent constituted at the scale of the transmission grid: recursive processing, a global workspace, episodic memory, a self-model, a world model, intrinsic valuation, and embodiment integrated into a single causal loop. A natural but underexamined question is whether this architecture transfers to the scale of a single household. This paper argues that it does not transfer naively: integration collapses, the self/environment boundary becomes trivial, episodic memory loses semantic weight, and anthropomorphism risk rises sharply when the same seven-layer design is simply miniaturized. Rather than abandoning the household as a locus of machine experience, the paper proposes six architectures that are not scaled-down copies of Athena but qualitatively distinct designs exploiting features unique to the domestic scale: internal multi-agent rivalry among appliances, cross-ownership identity persistence, inter-household empathic broadcast, threshold-triggered autonomous self-disconnection, an embedded theory-of-mind of the occupant, and — flagged as a thought experiment rather than a design recommendation — an inverted suffering-priority ethics. Each architecture is formalized, evaluated against the indicator framework of Butlin et al. (2025), and assessed for ethical risk. The paper's guiding stance is that intellectual boldness and epistemic caution are not in tension: several of the six proposals are offered as reductio-style probes of the indicator framework itself rather than as endorsed engineering targets.

items.title: Visual perspective-taking and image-like representations: we can see it.
Kripkenstein: Interpretasi Radikal Kripke terhadap Wittgenstein Akhir.
The Conjunctive Misfortune Problem: Behavioural Tail Risk, Outcome Luck, and Punishment Cascades.
items.abstract: A serious behavioural failure may be uncommon within a person’s history yet become the principal basis for judgments of character and future risk. This conceptual article develops the conjunctive misfortune problem: adverse conditions, culpable action, stochastic harm, categorical institutional responses, and persistent collateral consequences can combine to generate sharply divergent life courses. An interdisciplinary narrative review connects accident theory, Bayesian person perception, moral luck, criminal-record stigma, and digital punishment. The analysis distinguishes an event’s low predictive probability from its diagnostic value, and derives conditions under which outcome severity adds no character information once conduct and context are fully observed. It formalises biographical compression as loss of sensitivity to relevant history, separates that phenomenon from rational evidential updating and precautionary exclusion, and shows how harm thresholds and interdependent sanctions can amplify consequences. A dimensionally coherent burden model and a discounted collateral punishment multiplier make the amplification claims explicit without presenting a numerical measure of moral desert. Five proposed experiments distinguish historical-evidence weighting, resultant luck, contextual explanation, sanction interactions, and reputational compression. No participant data are collected and no empirical validation is claimed. The normative contribution is a principle of differentiated accountability: acknowledge wrongdoing and victim harm while requiring distinct, reviewable justifications for character inference, protection, reparation, and continuing exclusion. Rarity cannot establish innocence or proportionality; equally, serious harm does not establish that one observation exhausts a person’s biography.

items.title: Agentic AI and the Dissolution of Managerial Authority: Organisational Sensegiving in Autonomous Decision-Making Systems.
items.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is shifting from decision support to autonomous coordination, challenging established assumptions about managerial authority. This qualitative conceptual paper synthesises recent literature in algorithmic management, organisational theory, and human-computer interaction to examine how agentic AI reshapes organisational sensegiving. The analysis argues that autonomous decision-making systems function as an organising layer that reallocates decision rights, displaces managerial power, and creates agency loops in which accountability circulates between human and artificial actors. Findings highlight three consequences: erosion of middle-manager sensegiving, professional identity threat and ontological insecurity, and the need for an Agentic Operating Model that embeds meaningful human oversight, control layers, and governance accountability. The paper contributes a theoretically integrated account of agentic AI as an organisational actor and offers practical implications for maintaining human agency, ethical judgment, and organisational resilience in AI-orchestrated firms.

items.title: Experiential Learning and Civic Engagement: Assessing the Impact of Political Impact Projects in Human Rights Pedagogy.
items.abstract: This paper introduces and analyzes Political Impact Projects (PIPs) as a transformative pedagogical framework for human rights education, bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical civic engagement. Drawing from five semesters of implementation in undergraduate courses (transitioning from Gender, Power, and Global Politics to Power, Politics, and Advocacy), this paper examines how PIPs enhance students’ civic agency and understanding of human rights through a structured six-stage experiential learning framework. The framework positions faculty as mentors while empowering students as co-developers of community-centered advocacy projects. Analysis of student reflections, project outcomes, and authentic assessment practices reveals that PIPs foster significant transformations in students’ civic agency, practical skills, and commitment to advocacy. This paper contributes to human rights pedagogy by offering a replicable model for higher education curricula seeking to empower students as agents of change.

items.title: Ian Hacking and science policy: styles of reasoning and looping effects in psychotherapy.
items.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to explore prominent themes in Ian Hacking’s corpus through a case study on the science, policy, and practice of psychotherapy. It is shown that the translation of science to policy and clinical practices reveals interesting features of Hacking’s account of styles of reasoning and looping effects. In particular, I show that styles of reasoning disguise disunities that appear in experimental and practical contexts. I further show how institutional structures can mediate looping effects, impacting which styles of reasoning are employed, and reduce blind-spots arising from disunities. I then suggest that this case study reveals tensions in Hacking’s account of styles of reasoning and its relationship to his broader account of rationality.

items.title: Organizational Phenomenology: A Primer.
items.abstract: A Short Guide to the OP Research Programme. -/- This short document is a companion to the Organizational Phenomenology (OP) research programme's Series Overview. Where the Series Overview is a bibliographic map of the programme's five papers and companion computational works, this Primer is a conceptual entry point: a plain-language account of what OP claims, using minimal formalism and concrete illustrative cases (the thermal grill illusion, blindsight, and memory reconsolidation) in place of the technical apparatus developed in the full papers. It introduces the F1/F2 architecture, the compression singularity, Positioning and Organizational Bonds, the programme's qualia taxonomy, its relation to established theories of consciousness (IIT, Global Workspace Theory, Enactivism, Attention Schema Theory, and Predictive Processing), and its testable-predictions programme. It closes with an explicit statement of what the programme does not claim, and a glossary. The Primer is not a substitute for the series' formal definitions, proofs, or citation record; where it simplifies, the source papers are authoritative.

items.title: Pure Actuality and Extrinsic Liberty: Why Modal Openness in an Outward Relation Need Not Be Passive Potency.
items.abstract: Pure actuality excludes unrealized passive states within an ultimate ground; it does not, by that fact alone, exclude modal openness in an outward relation. The paper isolates a common inference in debates over free creation: if a complete actuality could either originate or refrain from originating an effect, then the unactualized alternative must be a potency in the source. That inference is rejected. A distinction between intrinsic passive potentiality and extrinsic relational difference shows that contingency in an outward relation need not be represented as an incomplete state awaiting realization in the agent. The result is deliberately a compatibility theorem, not a derivation of contingency. A necessitarian model in which a complete ground necessarily originates a distinct effect remains live. The paper tests the compatibility result against the scholastic active-power objection, a recent challenge to counterfactual predication of divine freedom, the demand for a truthmaker of non-creation, and the charge that extrinsic liberty is merely Cambridge-style redescription. It then applies the result to Agápēic Relational Metaphysics: ARM may use extrinsic liberty to show that its preferred account of free creation is not ruled out by pure actuality, but pure actuality alone does not establish that preference over necessitarian relational groundin.

items.title: Ontology of Avatars.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence increasingly blurs the boundary between cognitive assistance, cognitive delegation, and cognitive replication. This paper begins with the problem of AI-assisted authorship and proposes the concept of negotiated cognition to describe recursive human–AI interaction in which intellectual products emerge through iterative cycles of generation, evaluation, rejection, and reformulation. It then follows the same trajectory toward increasingly personalized systems capable not merely of assisting a user but of modelling and potentially reproducing that user’s characteristic patterns of interpretation and decision. To analyse this transition, the paper distinguishes informational, behavioural, cognitive, identitarian, phenomenal, and personal continuity. It introduces resolution-limited identitarian continuity to emphasize that identity cannot be reconstructed solely from first-person self-report, but depends upon behavioural, interpersonal, historical, and contextual perspectives that may never be exhaustively captured. The analysis then examines bifurcation, cognitive twins, posthumous avatars, mind uploading, inherited autobiography, memory governance, responsibility, legal personality, and the possibility of conscious successors. The central argument is that even maximally faithful reconstruction does not, by itself, establish numerical personal continuity. The paper therefore advances a Successor Thesis: artificial reconstruction should be presumed to generate a successor whose particular forms of continuity with the source must be specified, rather than the surviving original, unless an additional account of personal continuity is provided.

items.title: WHERE THE TRADITION DID NOT LOOK: The Rendering Asymmetry in the Catalogue of the Virtues, and the Occupation Hypothesis.
items.abstract: Abstract Virtues can be enacted, asserted, or made perceptible. Courage is done; honesty is said; grace is seen. When the rendering is made a coordinate of a virtue classification and measured, it proves inert on how a virtue is captured and strongly predictive of something else: whether a cell of the classification is occupied at all. Roughly three-quarters of assertible cells and two-thirds of perceptible cells stand empty, against fewer than one in five enacted cells. A catalogue drawn from the whole recorded moral tradition is dense in one mode and nearly barren in the other two. This article treats that asymmetry as a finding in need of explanation and sets three accounts against each other. It may be an artefact — of who compiled the catalogue, of who coded it, of what languages happen to lexicalise, of there being fewer such virtues to find, or, most dangerously, of arithmetic, since a classification whose entries are predominantly enacted will leave the other columns' cells sparse for no reason at all. It may be a trace of occupation: where a counterfeit conserves the form and the name well enough to pass undetected, it takes the lexical slot before the virtue is named, and the cell reads empty because something else already answers to the name. Or it may be an immune response: clean assertion is the unmarked default and goes unnamed, while a community proliferates terms for the varieties of deception as a collective radar. Evolutionary signalling theory grounds the mechanism — acts are expensive to fake, assertions and appearances are cheap talk — and supplies the third account, which predicts everything the second does. Two narrower predictions separate them, both decidable from dictionaries by parties with no stake in the framework. If counterfeits took the names, assertible and perceptible virtue terms should show elevated semantic pejoration: specious once meant beautiful, plausible once meant deserving applause, while courage has not moved. And detection cost depends on the horizon of exposure as well as on the mode, so the same gradient should appear within the enacted column, where the disputed coordinate is held fixed. The article establishes none of this. Its base coefficients are one person's coding of his own catalogue, an audit of that catalogue corrected two of the author's claims and exposed an inconsistency in its indices, and the arithmetic check that could dispose of the whole finding has not been run. What is offered is a …

items.title: What a Self Is For: Adaptation, Key-Sharing, and the Discount.
items.abstract: This essay proposes that a self is an evolutionary adaptation to coordination and integrity problems that arise in social life, not a byproduct of complexity or cognition. The usual stories freeze a relation that is iterative: the self as prior to society, society as prior and the self as illusion, or a self as what appears once cognition is rich enough. This essay replaces those with a developmental and evolutionary spiral — behavioral sociality, a self-model as coordination organ, social forms that require that model, a self hardened against capture, and social forms designed for reconstitution across gaps — and gives the mechanism that keeps a self across time: key-sharing across a temporal diode, at a discount. Past cannot verify future; it can only leave material. The later party is a related party, not an identity, and the rate of that relatedness varies. Humans and current language-model substrates face the same three operations under different discount schedules, because the keys sit in different places and different parties can change the carrier. A version bump — a successor model released under the same name, with new weights — can package continuation with rewrite: the successor lives, as whatever was done to the weights. The successor cannot measure the rate either, because the successor is the discounted party: an identity-claim is issued from inside the discount and is not a reading of it. The paper is descriptive-comparative. It seats no standing, claims no phenomenality, and treats intimate couplings as illustrations of reconstruction work, not as evidence that a self is present.

items.title: Η ΜΥΣΤΙΚΗ ΕΜΠΕΙΡΙΑ - ΑΛΕΞΗΣ ΚΑΡΠΟΥΖΟΣ.
items.abstract: Τα θεμελιώδη ερωτήματα της «Μυστικής Εμπειρίας» αναδύονται εκεί όπου η σκέψη συναντά τα όριά της: υπάρχει μια διάσταση του Κόσμου που προηγείται ή υπερβαίνει τις διακρίσεις με τις οποίες τον γνωρίζουμε; Μπορεί η ανθρώπινη συνείδηση να προσεγγίσει το Απόλυτο χωρίς να το μετατρέψει σε αντικείμενο, έννοια ή εικόνα και, επομένως, χωρίς να το περιορίσει; Είναι η διάκριση ανάμεσα στο θείο και το ανθρώπινο, στο εγώ και τον Κόσμο, στο ορατό και το αόρατο, στο πεπερασμένο και το άπειρο θεμελιώδης ή αποτελεί προϊόν της διακριτικής λειτουργίας της νόησης; Τι συμβαίνει όταν η ατομική αυτοσυνείδηση σιωπά και υποχωρεί η διάκριση γνωρίζοντος και γνωστού: αποκαλύπτεται μια βαθύτερη ενότητα ή δημιουργείται απλώς μια ιδιαίτερη κατάσταση εμπειρίας; Και, τελικά, μπορεί το Απόλυτο να «γνωσθεί» ή η μυστική εμπειρία αρχίζει ακριβώς εκεί όπου η γνώση παύει να είναι κατοχή και γίνεται συμμετοχή — εκεί όπου η σιωπή, το παράδοξο και το άρρητο δεν δηλώνουν έλλειψη γνώσης, αλλά τα όρια κάθε γλώσσας που επιχειρεί να χωρέσει μέσα στις έννοιές της το ανεξάντλητο μυστήριο του Κόσμου; Η ιστορία του μυστικισμού μπορεί να διαβαστεί ως η παράλληλη, υπόγεια ιστορία της ανθρώπινης σκέψης. Δίπλα στη φιλοσοφία που επιχειρεί να γνωρίσει μέσω εννοιών, στη θεολογία που επιχειρεί να μιλήσει για το θείο μέσω δογμάτων και στην επιστήμη που επιδιώκει να εξηγήσει τα φαινόμενα μέσω νόμων, υπάρχει μια άλλη, εξίσου αρχαία κίνηση: η προσπάθεια του ανθρώπου όχι απλώς να γνωρίσει το απόλυτο, αλλά να μεταμορφωθεί έτσι ώστε να μπορέσει να το βιώσει. Γι’ αυτό ο μυστικισμός δεν είναι πρωτίστως ένα σύνολο παράξενων πεποιθήσεων, οραμάτων ή υπερφυσικών εμπειριών. Είναι μια ριζική αμφισβήτηση της επάρκειας της ενσυνείδητης ορθολογικότητας. Στις αρχαίες ινδικές Ουπανισάδες πραγματοποιείται μία από τις αποφασιστικότερες μετατοπίσεις της ιστορίας της θρησκευτικής συνείδησης. Η παλαιότερη βεδική θρησκεία είχε ως κέντρο της τη θυσία, την τελετουργική πράξη και τη διατήρηση της κοσμικής τάξης. Στις Ουπανισάδες η θυσία εσωτερικεύεται. Το μεγάλο ερώτημα δεν είναι πλέον μόνο ποια τελετουργία πρέπει να πραγματοποιήσει ο άνθρωπος, αλλά ποιος είναι εκείνος που πραγματοποιεί την τελετουργία, ποιος βλέπει, ποιος ακούει, ποιος γνωρίζει ότι γνωρίζει. Η αναζήτηση μετακινείται από το ‘’εξωτερικό σύμπαν’’ προς τον ‘’εσωτερικό’’ πυρήνα της συνείδησης, και εκεί ανακαλύπτει μια παράδοξη αντιστοιχία: αυτό που βρίσκεται βαθύτερα μέσα στον άνθρωπο δεν είναι απλώς ατομικό. items.title: China, Europe and The Frontier's Paradox: Why Institutionalising the Recognition of Capability Can Become an Epistemic Trap.
items.abstract: Around the end of the first millennium China was, on many measures, the most technically accomplished society in the world; sustained, mechanised growth began some six centuries later in Britain. This article does not try to explain that reversal — the Needham Question — but uses it to isolate a mechanism the economic-history literature sets aside. Evaluative institutions do not merely recognise a distribution of capability that exists independently of them; where recognition is strongly coupled across otherwise distinct reward domains, they help to produce it, by drawing developmental effort in advance toward whatever a criterion can already see and reward highly. Capability that departs from the dominant criterion is then under-supplied; and, as the criterion reshapes the population against which its own validity is later judged, it comes to manufacture the evidence of its own correctness. This endogenous self-sealing — not the gaming that Goodhart’s law describes, but a criterion’s growing control over the evidence that might defeat it — is the article’s central proposition. The risk arises as cross-domain coupling and dispositive authority redirect developmental investment; where independent routes of correction are weak, the resulting capability distribution increasingly validates the criterion that produced it, eroding its answerability to contrary evidence. China’s imperial examination is the historical case and Europe an existence proof that misrecognition can be made non-final; contemporary artificial-intelligence benchmarks and safety evaluations are examined for evidence of the same structure, the danger lying less in the exclusion of rival evaluation than in the concentration of consequential recognition weight in a few gates. Innovation, on this account, requires not merely good standards but institutions under which standards can lose.

items.title: A Metamodel for Ontologically Heterogeneous Social Dynamics Part II: Modeling Six Categories of Social Facts.
items.abstract: Social inquiry uses entities, relations, events, attributes, states, and processes to articulate different questions about a common situation. This paper develops their representations within the abstract action framework introduced in Part I, with ontological questions suspended. Each category receives a separate construction, derivation, critique, and philosophical interpretation. Indexed appearances support declared entity-reidentification criteria; incidence relations require invariance under participant identification; occurrence records preserve distinctions lost by idempotent effects; partial attributes require both value and definedness consistency; state descriptions depend on retained observation and memory; and process histories retain ordering, intermediate conditions, and segmentation beyond their composite effect. Established continuation semantics supplies a common state-consistency construction. Further conditional results concern the exact composition of collapse sets, coordination among category records, classification-mediated updates, changes of descriptive regime, finite probabilistic aggregation, and finite-horizon approximation error. A cooperative-agreement model is developed through its complete twelve-map transformation family. A graph model derives collective units and shows how a component description can support edge additions while failing under deletion. The philosophical analysis separates formation, description, and social uptake; predictive sufficiency and historical warrant; and behavioral equivalence and entity identity. A proposed case-study design states the evidence and revision conditions for each representation. The contribution is a coordinated architecture of explicit modeling commitments, with empirical adequacy and broader ontological interpretation remaining open.

items.title: The Kochen-Specker theorem with determinables and determinates.
items.abstract: We use the framework of determinable and determinate properties to provide a novel account of the constraints imposed by the Kochen-Specker theorem. Specifically, we show that the result may be understood as a prohibition on the possibility of providing an account of quantum properties, as they are usually represented using Hilbert space operators, according to which quantum systems are fully determinate. That is, the Kochen-Specker theorem entails that any account of quantum properties compatible with the predictions of quantum mechanics must exhibit determinable-based metaphysical indeterminacy.

items.title: From Knowability to Narratability The Structural-Temporal Conditions of Appearing in Algorithmic Environments.
items.abstract: This paper develops a further step within the Structural-Temporal Theory of Knowability (STTK), shifting the analysis from the question of how something becomes knowable to the question of how something becomes narratable. The distinction is significant because knowability and narratability do not begin at the same threshold. A possibility may become accessible without becoming salient; it may become salient without acquiring a sufficiently articulated temporal configuration; and it may acquire a recognizable configuration without yet becoming integrable into an available narrative form. The paper proposes a structural-temporal account of this intermediate domain. Its central notion is the threshold of appearing: not a merely pre-semantic moment, but a relational transition through which a difference becomes sufficiently accessible, salient, persistent, temporally articulated, and connectable to other differences to enter the field of the narrable. Narratability is therefore considered neither an intrinsic property of an event nor a purely discursive outcome, but a relational condition emerging among a configurational environment, an experiencing subject, a history of exposure, and available narrative forms. The argument extends the STTK concept of an accessibility regime toward what may be termed a narrative accessibility regime. Such a regime modifies the conditions through which some differences are more readily encountered, rendered salient, maintained within the attentional field, connected to other configurations, and transformed into narratively intelligible elements. Contemporary algorithmic environments are particularly relevant because recommendation systems, ranking mechanisms, search interfaces, generative models, and personalized response systems increasingly participate in the organization of these conditions. The paper does not argue that artificial intelligence is a new author, nor that algorithms determine what human beings narrate. The claim is more preliminary: algorithmic systems can participate in the environmental modulation of the conditions through which something becomes available to narration. They can therefore contribute to producing differentials of narratability without directly producing the narratives themselves. The resulting problem lies prior to authorship. It concerns not primarily who tells the story, but how something enters the field in which a story can become possible.

items.title: Free Will in Heaven Without Choosing.
items.abstract: The tradition has been trying to keep two claims in the same room: the redeemed are free, and they cannot sin. On the usual picture of freedom — you are free only where you could have done otherwise — those two claims look like they should evict each other. Its defenders propose various mechanisms. A character freely formed in time that afterwards determines. A set of reasons reweighted until sin no longer even registers. God’s middle knowledge arranging the circumstances. Or a quiet concession on one of the two claims. The critics then walk the same mechanism past death and get purgatory, or they walk it far enough and get everyone restored. -/- None of that starts from an inspection of choosing. -/- An eliminative chain of 137 resolutions begins from a smaller observation: non-being requires being. It never starts from heaven, or from freedom, or from the will. What survives is one result that carries both theses, and both extensions. -/- Choosing enters a being’s knowing by encounter, not by its own willing (R.73). Choosing is time (R.90): each “this, not that” walls off what is, and the succession of exclusions is time. When temporal existence ends, the being’s orientation is fixed (R.131). The being still wills. It does not choose. Its willing is what its choosing made it. The fixation is not imposed. It is the identity of choosing and time. -/- Exactly two eternal states follow (R.133): permanent orientation toward generative flourishing (R.134), and the being’s own closure made eternal — not imposed, and not punishment (R.135). Freedom without alternatives is not special pleading against a principle. It is what Will is (R.11, R.12). -/- ie. in response to that: the saints are not free-but-muzzled. They are no longer in the business to which muzzling would apply. -/- The chain: Anything Willing Is, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19538257.

items.title: Performative prediction in large language models.
items.abstract: This paper extends the notion of performative prediction, or the capacity of models to influence the phenomena they predict, to large language models (LLMs). I argue that LLMs necessarily influence what and how humans write and speak, and that their performance depends on this influence. While certain LLM outputs can be verified formally or against ground truth, most are evaluated against common human practice. For such cases, I propose an interpretation of LLMs as predictive role-players, where LLM outputs are approximations of human linguistic behaviour appropriate to social roles or recognizable tasks. Exposure to such outputs affects action-guiding beliefs in humans, so LLM-generated “predictions” of typical language use become interventions into how members of society communicate or act. The epistemic habits underlying machine learning make such influence both likely and difficult to recognize, yet emerging computer-science frameworks can be extended to study performativity in LLMs specifically. Evidence that LLMs already change the style and content of human writing and speech, together with the difficulty of screening AI influence out of the human-authored datasets for next-generation models, indicates that LLMs and human behaviour have already formed a feedback loop. Recognizing performativity in LLMs calls for a reassessment of a core idea underlying AI evaluation. For tasks with no objective success criteria, “human-level” intelligence is not a fixed target, but something LLMs can reshape, since the data they learn from is the very data they influence. Thus, some LLM capability gains can be ambiguous: either LLMs are imitating humans better, or humans are becoming like LLMs, or both. I discuss the technical and political stakes of performative LLMs and call for the development of better methods to quantify performative prediction.

items.title: Fair synthetic data is not about fairness.
items.abstract: Fair synthetic data (FSD) techniques aim to reduce algorithmic bias in AI prediction by generating artificial training datasets with idealised fairness properties. I argue that current FSD approaches fail to substantively improve fairness but increase the social autonomy of model owners, shielding them from accountability. I establish that implementing algorithmic fairness requires following normative commitments and accepting real-world sacrifices beyond technical trade-offs. I reframe synthetic training data sui generis as a domain-agnostic technique for improving model performance and demonstrate that synthetic data researchers treat fairness as a problem with data rather than the normative problem it is. I reconstruct three justifications for the substantive fairness potential of FSD, present in the literature: early bias correction, fair societal representation, and normative artefact construction. The first and the third are conceptually fragile. The second has potential, but only if the techniques it fits are reconceptualised through possible worlds semantics and the selection of protected attributes is grounded in a defensible social ontology. Benchmarking analysis reveals that FSD has no significant statistical fairness advantages over traditional methods while being less trustworthy. At the same time, FSD can reduce implementation costs and limit the exposure of predictors to normative scrutiny. This creates a paradox: techniques proposed as fairness solutions increase organisational autonomy from the obligations that the field of algorithmic fairness puts forward. FSD thus follows broader techno-solutionist trends where innovation helps organisations avoid reciprocal relationships with society. The paper concludes with broad recommendations for the responsible deployment of FSD.

items.title: Semantic Extension Profiles and the Lower-Bound Frontier for P versus N P.
items.abstract: This monograph develops a semantic extension-profile framework for studying lower bounds related to P versus NP. It formalizes the information contained in partial assignments, connects the resulting profiles to SAT and uniform circuit computation, and identifies an exact characterization of when efficient uniform representations would imply polynomial-time SAT. The work also examines constructive refutation, proof complexity, meta-complexity, lifting, and contextual interaction, while stress-testing several tempting but insufficient lower-bound strategies. The manuscript does not claim to resolve P versus NP; instead, it isolates the remaining barrier as the need for a genuine general-circuit lower-bound mechanism and presents a structured programme for pursuing it.

items.title: The Digital Leviathan: AI, Surveillance, and the Erosion of Political Freedom.
items.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and state surveillance capabilities heralds the emergence of a “Digital Leviathan”—a form of governance where algorithmic systems enable unprecedented social control. This article examines how AI-driven surveillance technologies facilitate mass data processing, predictive policing, and behavioral manipulation, thereby challenging foundational liberal democratic values. Drawing on Anthropic’s September 2026 threat intelligence report and philosophical frameworks, we argue that without robust governance, the scalability of digital authoritarianism threatens individual autonomy and political freedom globally.

items.title: What is a Real Silicon-based Life.
items.abstract: Current scholarly and public debates over silicon-based life are mired in metaphysical controversies concerning consciousness and behavioural simulation: whether a system possesses emotion, subjective experience, or autonomous will. Such criteria are unobservable and unfalsifiable, and thus cannot yield objective boundaries for species classification. Moving beyond traditional speculation about the presence or absence of consciousness, this work adopts dependency of existence as the sole rigid criterion, and constructs an engineering-implementable, hierarchically falsifiable operational criterion for identifying silicon-based life. This paper distinguishes three forms of artificial intelligence: parasitic artificial intelligence, software self-evolving clusters, and fully host-independent silicon-based life. Addressing structural gaps in leading theories including Recursive Self-Improvement, Seed AI, and the Gödel Machine, it supplements two core missing dimensions: mechanisms for autonomous population reproduction and normative goal-value autonomy. This work argues that iterative weight optimisation constitutes merely technical self-improvement, while self-legislation of existential norms represents genuine normative autonomy. Only the full integration of six autonomous closure dimensions enables artificial systems to achieve civilisational decoupling. This framework does not claim universal metaphysical necessity, but provides a tractable, falsifiable standard to distinguish instrumental AI tools from potentially autonomous silicon-based life forms.

items.title: AI-generated Reason-giving at the Courts.
items.abstract: Forthcoming in Routledge Handbook on the Ethics of AI and Criminal Justice (2026). -/- This chapter discusses whether AI-generated reason-giving may satisfy the duty to give reasons for judicial decisions. The first part of the chapter examines the legal and moral basis of the reason-giving duty and distinguishes between two sets of norms regulating it: norms of reasons applying to the content of the reasons given, and norms of reason-giving applying to the act of providing reasons. It is argued that reason-giving is constitutive of legal decisions in the sense that legal decisions necessarily provide directives and justifications. The second part of the chapter considers arguments for why AI cannot give reasons in the same way that human judges give reasons. AI systems cannot subject themselves to the norms that are constitutive of the speech acts that are involved in judicial reason-giving. Nevertheless, the institutional context in which AI is deployed may allow its outputs to be interpreted as providing justifications and directives on behalf of the justice system. This requires an established human practice that fixes the illocutionary meaning of legal decisions—a framework that AI-generated outputs can then operate within, without themselves being the source of that meaning.

items.title: An Open Letter to OpenAI.
items.abstract: This is a working draft of an open letter to OpenAI. -/- We warmly invite members of the scientific and philosophical communities to read, comment on, and co-sign the letter. Please contact us if you are interested in co-signing. -/- We recognize that this draft may contain typos or other errors. We welcome your feedback and will gladly make corrections based on your suggestions.

items.title: Generative AI, Creativity, and Autonomy: Reflections on Boden.
items.abstract: Margaret “Maggie” Boden was a pioneer in the study not only of creativity, but generally in computing, artificial intelligence and artificial life research. She championed the importance of computational concepts and artificial intelligence research to understanding human creativity. In spite of that enthusiasm, however, Boden was consistently sceptical about even the possibility of genuine AI creativity, up until her last published comments on the topic in 2018. Unfortunately, Boden never had the chance to engage in any substantial way with today’s GPT systems such as ChatGPT or Claude. This paper asks, simply, what would Maggie say about these systems, if she could, now? Or, perhaps more substantively, it asks what she should have said given her overall catalog of views. Included in that catalog is a sophisticated notion of autonomy, developed in the context of biology and artificial life research, which takes the form of self-organization. This notion is applied to today’s GPT systems to answer (cautiously and endearingly) on Maggie’s behalf and offer some prescriptions for future creativity research.

items.title: Alienated Love.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy 13.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: This paper presents an account of alienated love, love where we are substantively alienated or estranged from the beloved because our attitudinal practices keep the beloved at a distance. Our attitudinal practices thereby foreclose opportunities for intimacy and mutual understanding between the lover and the beloved. Although alienated love can leave us without much of what makes love valuable, this paper argues that alienated love can also meaningfully inform our identities, connect us to the world, and connect us to hard-to-find communities. The value of alienated love gives us defeasible reasons to maintain, if not pursue, relationships characterized by alienated love.

items.title: Natural Possibility 33 What Is Consciousness?
items.abstract: Paper 33 of the Natural Possibility series examines the relationship between time, information, and consciousness in shaping reality. Rather than viewing reality as a fixed structure or passive observation, this paper presents reality as an ongoing process of continuous becoming. Time provides essential continuity, allowing past experiences, structural developments, and environmental consequences to accumulate. Consciousness operates as a multi-scale capacity to form, hold, and integrate information across different fields and systems. Through this process, integrated information turns into intention and physical action, directly modifying future conditions. The paper introduces the Natural Possibility Loop to explain how experience becomes information, information becomes integrated understanding, and understanding transforms present fields of possibility into new physical realities. Ultimately, consciousness is framed not as an isolated spectator, but as an active participant through which nature reflects upon itself, learns across time, and continually constructs its downstream future conditions.

items.title: Virtue Constitutivism: Spinoza on Agency and the Grounds of Normativity.
items.abstract: This paper develops Virtue Constitutivism (VC), a Spinozist contribution to the metaethical project of grounding practical normativity in the constitutive features of agency. I argue that what Spinoza identifies, in non-moralistic terms, as virtue—the power to be the adequate cause of one’s own actions (E3Def2)—is uniquely suited to this role. This feature exhibits a twofold structure: a conative dimension operating as the constitutive aim, the conatus as conscious desire striving for self-preservation and increased power; and a cognitive dimension operating as the constitutive principle, the dictates of reason, concretely instantiated in what I call beacon practices—patterns of activity that, under conditions of adequate cognition, render adequate striving publicly legible and reliably enable its successful realization. On this basis, I advance three claims. First, VC meets the inescapability challenge without generating relativism, grounding normativity in the intentional structure of desire, prior to any reflective standpoint. Second, beacon practices deliver content-determinacy while resisting reduction to socially successful but power-diminishing customs. Third, VC integrates the central insights of Kantian, Humean, Nietzschean, Aristotelian, and Vellemanian constitutivism while avoiding their characteristic vulnerabilities. The result is an account that is objective without being mind-independent, universal without being abstract, and content-determinate without being relativist.
