Digital Sovereignty as Biological Homeostasis: Positions cognitive freedom and data isolation as pre-linguistic biological necessities protected under fundamental human rights frameworks. Total Deflection of Product Liability: Demonstrates that public-domain, non-commercial architectures possess no centralized telemetry anchors or corporate vendors, legally short-circuiting institutional product compliance demands. Methodological Lineage & System Architecture: To ensure absolute technical coherence, this text should be read as part of a unified computational lineage. The Axiomatic Homeostatic Map (AHM) serves as the human-readable constitutional layer of the method. It provides the descriptive framework for individual cognitive defense. Its formal, machine-readable mathematical derivatives and runtime implementations are detailed in the following companion works: The Human Value Psyche (HVP) Theorem: The underlying mathematical blueprint mapping natural cognitive physics and the inverse-square moral influence kernel. Ethical Chess v2.7 & v2.8 (Runtime Configurations): The active, compiled machine-readable code architectures that execute value sorting via immediate Boolean summation and minimize proxy-aversion inside local compute environments. By anchoring this legal brief to verifiable machine-readable code, the defense forces a programmatic counter-audit of the state’s claimed values, exposing the structural necessity of open-weight, air-gapped systems. Keywords: Air-Gapped Compute, Digital Sovereignty, THE HUMAN VALUE PSYCHE (HVP) THEOREM Axiomatic Homeostatic Map (AHM), Ethical Chess, Cognitive …

items.title: The Ambivalence of Recognition in Sexual Subjectivity.
items.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of sexual misrecognition: some groups are excluded from being seen as sexually desirable or are hypersexualised. This shapes their sexual subjectivity – how they understand themselves as sexual agents. Despite widespread initiatives calling for recognition in the domain of sexuality, the need for sexual recognition has remained undertheorised in recognition theory. Building on debates on the ambivalence of recognition, I argue that sexuality has a uniquely complex relationship to recognition. While sexual recognition is necessary for subjectivity, it also reinforces subjection to power structures. Moreover, sexuality continually transgresses sociality and subjectivity itself. Using Jeanette Chedda’s erotic story in Damn Horny as a case study, I demonstrate how sexual recognition transgresses ideals of mutuality and equality, and theorise transformative possibilities for cultivating sexual subjectivity differently.

items.title: The BS meter: detecting politics and labour through ChatGPT’s language.
items.abstract: What can we learn about language from studying how it is used by ChatGPT and other large language model (LLM)-based chatbots? In this paper, we analyse the distinctive character of language generated by ChatGPT, in relation to questions raised by natural language processing pioneer, and student of Wittgenstein, Margaret Masterman. Following frequent complaints that LLM-based chatbots produce “bullshit,” in the sense of Frankfurt’s popular monograph On Bullshit, we conduct an empirical study to contrast the language of 1000 scientific publications with typical text generated by ChatGPT. We then explore whether the same language features can be detected in two well-known contexts of social dysfunction: George Orwell’s critique of political speech, and David Graeber’s characterisation of bullshit jobs. Using simple hypothesis-testing methods, we demonstrate that a statistical model of bullshit can reliably relate the Frankfurtian artificial bullshit of ChatGPT to the political and workplace functions of bullshit as observed in natural human language.

items.title: Open AI: The Illusion of Understanding.
items.abstract: In 1980 John Searle imagined a man locked in a room with a rulebook, shuffling Chinese characters he could not read, and asked whether anything there understood anything. The thought experiment has framed the debate ever since. This paper argues that it no longer fits the machines we now argue about, and that the human understanding it quietly holds up as the standard is in no shape to serve as one. Searle's insistence on the difference between real understanding and a convincing imitation belongs to its moment: the same years gave us Baudrillard on simulation, a counterfeiting industry large enough to need its own federal statute, and a Coca-Cola that had to relabel itself Classic because the product alone could no longer prove it was the original. Insisting on genuineness is what people do when the copies are getting good. The thought experiment also relies on our being able to look over the man's shoulder and see that he is only matching symbols — and in a modern network there is no rulebook to read, not even for the people who built it. The usual escape, that Searle was only ever talking about the clunky AI of his day, is one he closed himself when he widened his position in later work. The paper then turns a term borrowed from AI engineering, context rot, back on us. Our own understanding decays in much the same way: memory rewrites what it stores, emotion tilts the scales before we notice, and every speaker runs a private version of the language that never quite matches anyone else's. Watch the word justice in the mouths of Putin, Trump and Khomeini — each is certain he is simply using it correctly. Recent findings from AI interpretability, on traits that pass between models through data that never mentions them, on memory that is periodically rebuilt, and on emotion-like states that measurably change what a system does, are brought to bear on an argument written in 1980. The conclusion turns the title around. The illusion of understanding may not be a machine problem at all. It may be what understanding has always been — partial, shaped by where you stand, and good enough to act on. The real question is how useful that illusion is to us.

items.title: When the Exception Knows Our Name : Moral Priority Reversal, Identity, and the Ethics of Choosing Which Principle Governs.
items.abstract: Moral inconsistency is often pictured as a simple gap between what a person says and what that person does. Yet some of the most consequential forms of selective morality are more sophisticated. An agent may sincerely affirm several moral principles—democracy, freedom of speech, equality, public order, loyalty, security, compassion, procedural fairness—and still reason selectively. The selectivity occurs one level above ordinary rule violation: when principles conflict, the agent allows the identity of the actor, beneficiary, victim, institution, party, nation, religion, or social group to influence which accepted principle is treated as governing the case. -/- This article calls that structure Moral Priority Reversal. A reversal occurs when two cases remain relevantly comparable, the agent continues to recognize the same competing principles, but their priority order changes after the social identity or advantage structure changes. Freedom may outrank order when an ally speaks and order may outrank freedom when an opponent speaks. Majoritarian choice may be treated as decisive when one’s preferred side wins and constitutional restraint as decisive when it loses. Loyalty may be praised as solidarity in one’s own group and condemned as tribalism in another. The problem is not that different principles can legitimately govern different cases. Moral life is plural, context-sensitive, and saturated with genuine conflicts. The problem is that identity or advantage can silently become the switch that determines which principle receives priority while the agent continues to experience the resulting judgment as principled. -/- The argument builds on empirical work showing motivated use of moral principles, self-other double standards, flexible judgments of comparability, social-context effects on moral valuation, partisan tolerance of democratic norm violations, and politically motivated speech repression. Uhlmann, Pizarro, Tannenbaum, and Ditto showed that people can selectively invoke consequentialist and deontological principles to rationalize preferred conclusions. Silver and Berman show that people can also manipulate whether cases seem comparable when judging allies and enemies. The present paper does not redescribe those findings as a new psychological discovery. Its contribution is normative and structural: it asks what consistency requires when moral agents genuinely accept multiple principles and must determine their relative priority in concrete cases. …

items.title: Closed for Business: Why ∃E Is the Only Coherent Totality.
items.abstract: Philosophy routinely evaluates claims about ultimate reality as though they were ordinary hypotheses situated inside a larger neutral arena. That treatment is structurally mistaken. A genuine totality is a special logical case. If a candidate is truly exhaustive, nothing real can stand outside it to explain, cause, validate, ground, compare, complete, or judge it. Any proposed exterior either belongs to reality, in which case it was never exterior, or does not belong to reality, in which case it cannot perform real explanatory work. Paul Edwards identified one form of this closure in 1967 when he argued that if “the universe” means “the totality of things,” explanation cannot appeal beyond it. Agrippa exposed the corresponding regress in justification. F. H. Bradley recognized that ultimate reality must be internally coherent and identified reality with sentient experience, yet retained temporal and relational commitments that generated contradictions he then repaired with the Absolute. Experiential Empiricism unifies these partial discoveries under ∃E: experience is. This paper distinguishes totality closure from candidate identification, derives a general admission rule and checklist for totality claims, and tests matter, God, mathematical structure, information, neutral substance, Bradley’s Absolute, and experience against exhaustiveness, closure, self-sufficiency, self-application, coherence, regress containment, semantic population, and operational conservation. The tests are not designed around ∃E. They follow from what it means for anything to be genuinely ultimate. ∃E alone survives the full procedure without silently reserving an exterior from which it is known, grounded, validated, or completed. The act of asking, doubting, modeling, denying, grounding, or meta-evaluating experience is itself another experiential occurrence. Reality is closed for business because anything capable of doing business with it is already part of the inventory.

items.title: Bradley Found Experience and Then Rebuilt the Outside: How Retained Time Generated the Absolute.
items.abstract: F. H. Bradley's *Appearance and Reality* presents a substantially closer historical precedent to Experiential Empiricism than my prior genealogical work recognized. Bradley argues that reality is an all-inclusive whole beyond which there is nothing, identifies the material of reality with sentient experience, denies that anything non-experiential can coherently occupy another ontological region, and challenges the reader to produce a fact separable from sentience. These claims overlap strikingly with arguments I later developed independently under Experiential Empiricism, especially the Experientia Est challenge and the claim that reality cannot possess an exterior. Bradley was absent from my previous historical surveys, and that omission requires correction. Yet the comparison also exposes the precise point at which Bradley fails to complete the subtractive move. Bradley retains temporal succession and relational persistence long enough to generate contradictions involving change, identity, permanence, and succession. He then interprets those contradictions as evidence that ordinary experience is merely appearance and must be reconciled within a metaphysically privileged Absolute. This paper argues that the Absolute is unnecessary. Bradley correctly identifies the coherence requirement but mislocates the contradiction. The contradiction arises from treating external time and relations across temporally distinct states as features of reality rather than as present experiential structure. Once external time is removed, each experiential occurrence is internally coherent and no higher Absolute is required to reconcile it. Bradley therefore represents an unusually powerful historical near-hit: he reaches experiential totality, then manufactures the need to escape it by retaining exactly the externalist machinery that complete subtraction removes.

items.title: Why Do Philosophy in the First Place?
items.abstract: This essay asks a deceptively simple question: Why do philosophy in the first place? It begins from the possibility that language, thinking, and being are not fundamentally separate, and examines how the structures through which experience is articulated may shape the philosophical questions that appear natural to us. Drawing on a Nāgārjunian suspicion of ontological foundations, the essay questions the tendency to replace one conceptual ground with another—substance with relation, essence with process, or being with becoming. Dependent arising, on this view, does not establish “relationality” as a new fundamental ontology, but undermines the search for independently existing essence itself. -/- The essay then shifts the question from the structure of articulation to its existential significance. Philosophy is not understood merely as the production of increasingly refined descriptions of reality, but as an inquiry whose significance must ultimately be tested in lived experience. If philosophical insight does not alter suffering, attachment, fear of death, the experience of self, relationships with others, or our manner of inhabiting the natural world, what has actually been understood? In this sense, a human life itself becomes an articulation of its understanding of existence: through how one eats, speaks, loves, works, dies, relates to other beings, and inhabits nature. -/- Drawing on Buddhist and Gandhian perspectives, the essay proposes that philosophy and life cannot ultimately be separated. Its deepest task may therefore be not to discover a final ontology, but to loosen the conceptual structures through which we experience ourselves as separate from the world. The essay concludes by proposing a simple existential test of philosophical understanding: Has the way I see changed the way I live?

items.title: The Rosarian Wolf Compendium.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: Introduction — Before the Rosarian Wolf -/- Before the wolf became an emblem within the Rosarian Wolf Doctrine, it already possessed a remarkable history in the human world. Long before any modern philosophical or spiritual system assigned meaning to the wolf, human societies were observing, fearing, respecting, hunting, protecting, mythologizing, and living alongside this animal. Across widely separated cultures and historical periods, the wolf appears in stories of ancestry, survival, guidance, protection, kinship, community, transformation, wilderness, and freedom. The forms of these traditions are not identical, and they should not be forced into a single interpretation, yet the persistence of certain themes deserves serious examination. -/- This compendium is therefore not intended to redefine the Rosarian Wolf, nor is it intended to add another formal definition to the Rosarian Wolf Doctrine as established by its manifesto. Its purpose is different. It is an historical and explanatory account of the wolf as a real cultural phenomenon: an attempt to examine what human beings have actually said, believed, recorded, practiced, and transmitted concerning the wolf, and to consider what those traditions may reveal about the enduring significance of the animal in human thought. -/- The distinction is essential. The Rosarian Wolf is a particular philosophical and doctrinal concept. The wolf itself is something far older and far larger than any one doctrine. The animal existed before our interpretations of it, and human interpretations of it developed independently across many societies. Consequently, the historical material presented here should not be treated as evidence that ancient peoples were secretly expressing the Rosarian Wolf Doctrine. Such a claim would confuse historical investigation with retrospective interpretation. Instead, the historical record provides something more valuable: a body of evidence against which later interpretations can be thoughtfully examined. -/- The purpose of this work is therefore neither to appropriate the traditions of other peoples nor to flatten their differences. A Turkic origin tradition should remain a Turkic tradition. The Wusun story should remain within its historical context. The Mongolian account of Börte Chino should not be transformed into a generic statement about all peoples. Indigenous traditions concerning wolves should be approached according to their own cultural contexts rather than gathered …

items.title: The Knight Manifesto, A Rosarian Compendium.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: THE ROSARIAN DOCTRINE -/- The Philosophy of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism -/- Via Solis Sub Rosa — The Way of the Sun Beneath the Rose -/- Rosarian Mystical Dawnism is a living philosophy of awakening, devotion, remembrance, and embodied virtue expressed through the symbolic Way known as Via Solis Sub Rosa, the Way of the Sun Beneath the Rose. Its central teaching is that the sacred is not separated from ordinary existence but is encountered through consciousness, conduct, relationship, silence, service, beauty, responsibility, and the continual renewal of awareness. The philosophy does not present awakening as an escape from the world. It presents awakening as a different way of inhabiting the world. -/- At the center of this philosophy stands the image of the Rose beneath the Sun. The Rose represents the living heart, the flowering of what has been cultivated inwardly, and the visible expression of love, devotion, beauty, service, and spiritual maturity. The Sun represents illumination and awakening. The Deep represents the unseen foundation from which transformation becomes possible: silence, mystery, inwardness, death, renewal, and the fertile darkness in which the seed of understanding takes root. These are not three unrelated symbols. They describe one movement. The Dawn reveals, the Deep receives and transforms, and the Rose gives what has been awakened visible form. -/- The Way therefore begins with remembrance. The seeker is not instructed to manufacture a sacred reality that does not already exist. Rather, the seeker is asked to become sufficiently attentive to recognize what has been present beneath distraction, unconsciousness, attachment, and forgetfulness. Awakening is consequently both discovery and responsibility. Once something has been seen clearly, the person becomes responsible for how that recognition is carried into life. -/- The name Viridarius Rosae, the Keeper of the Rose Garden, expresses this responsibility. The Keeper is not defined principally by title, rank, or external authority, but by the act of tending. The Rose Garden is the interior and relational field in which the sacred is cultivated. To become a Keeper is to accept responsibility for what one permits to grow within oneself and what one contributes to the world around oneself. The garden is not protected through possession but through care. Its inheritance is therefore not ownership of the Rose, but stewardship of the conditions in which the Rose may bloom. -/- THE …

items.title: Beyond the Pleasure and Displeasure Principle. Valence, Epistemic Feelings, and the Question of the Dimensional-Directional Nature of Affective States.
items.abstract: The present article aims at revisiting the question of the link between valence and epistemic feelings, by showing that the property of being arranged as pairwise polar opposites, far from being restricted to algedonic states, also applies to affective states that are associated with the experience of a form of cognizance. In revisiting the notion of affective valence, I propose a renewed ontology of epistemic feelings, which I envision as consisting, in the final analysis, of a system of bidirectionally organized affective dimensions. After presenting the models of epistemic valence elaborated by Lipps, Avenarius, and Wundt in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, I address the question of polar opposition and valence in current epistemic feeling literature, showing that both issues, while not entirely overlooked, have largely been disregarded. Then, I comment on two articles by Arango-Muñoz (2014) and Loev (2022), which are the only recent publications that address in detail the question of the link between valence and epistemic feelings. I insist that there are actually good reasons to assume the existence of an epistemic valence besides algedonic valence. Finally, I lay out the foundation for a theoretical model in which I systematically address the question of how epistemicity, dimensionality, directionality are interrelated in affective states. I highlight that, in order to be considered as pairs of polar opposites, epistemic feelings should consist of a limited number of well-defined, elementary, and discrete qualitative entities that are organized bidimensionally and likely to vary in intensity.

items.title: Rosarian Mystical Dawnism, The Manifesto Became Whole.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Manifesto Became Whole: The Formation of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism -/- The Rosarian Manifesto Tradition is best understood not as a collection of unrelated spiritual writings, nor as a single doctrine that appeared fully formed at one moment, but as a developing intellectual and spiritual project whose successive texts progressively disclose the meaning of the tradition they constitute. What begins in the language of awakening beneath the Rose develops into a philosophy of remembrance, cultivation, disciplined love, interior chivalry, symbolic transformation, ritual practice, and communal custodianship. The significance of this development lies precisely in its cumulative character. Via Solis Sub Rosa, Militia Amoris / Hortus Conclusus, the Dawnist Rosarian Manifesto, Bara no Kishi, and The Knight Manifesto: A Rosarian Compendium are most productively read as successive moments in the formation of one intellectual architecture. The later texts do not simply repeat the earlier ones with additional symbols; they take problems left implicit in the earlier formulations and attempt to answer them. What does awakening require of a person? What happens when illumination becomes an ethic? How does an inner philosophy become a disciplined way of life? How does that discipline become a form of chivalry? And, finally, how does an individual path become a fellowship capable of preserving, interpreting, and transmitting its principles? The movement through these questions explains the emergence of what the corpus calls Rosarian Mystical Dawnism. -/- The earliest conceptual center of this tradition is expressed in the phrase Via Solis Sub Rosa, “The Way of the Sun under the Rose.” Within the Rosarian corpus, the phrase does considerably more than provide an attractive title. It establishes the fundamental polarity from which the rest of the system develops: the Sun represents awakening, illumination, consciousness and the emergence of the inner light, while the Rose represents love, devotion, beauty, service and the mystery that must be cultivated rather than possessed. The tradition's account of the Rose is consequently inseparable from its anthropology. The Rose is described as an inner garden, something that does not simply exist as an object of belief but must be tended. The practitioner becomes a keeper of that garden, and the title Viridarius Rosae, the Keeper of the Rose Garden, therefore describes a spiritual vocation before it describes an office. The …

items.title: LLMs are metaphor machines: orbital argumentation, misaligned citations, and scientific fabrication in AI-generated writing.
items.abstract: Large language models are metaphor machines: they generate text based on similarities and proximity in their training data. I argue that this metaphor-based text generation leads to what John Gallagher calls orbital argumentation, where the generated text is pulled towards key concepts that, I argue, remain unnarratable as the text skims their surface, orbiting around them instead of directly addressing them. Misaligned citations in scholarly writing—citations of real works that are related to the central topic but do not support the specific claim made—are a type of scientific fabrication that is systematically produced by the fundamentally metaphorical operation of large language models. To develop this argument, I draw upon theories of metaphor by Aristotle and I. A. Richards, applying them to two technological shifts that underpin the metaphorical emphasis of LLMs: the 2013 discovery that language models could handle analogies like king − man + woman = queen and the introduction of self-attention and transformer models in 2017. I use this framework to analyse an LLM-generated document summary, examples from a dataset of LLM-generated stories, and a scientific paper. In each case, I demonstrate how the metaphorical connections pull at the text generation, causing the text to orbit around a key theme that remains unnarratable. Recognising the rhetorical vices of LLM-generated texts can help us to protect the knowledge ecosystem that science depends upon. The paper, therefore, concludes with five recommendations for readers, writers, peer reviewers, and editors who want to build resilience against the inaccuracies of LLM-generated texts.

items.title: (Poster) Asymmetric Lexical Representations of Affect: On Emotion Understanding in LLMs.
items.pub: Association for Computing Machinery (Acm) Digital Library.
items.abstract: (This poster summarizes a paper to be published in the ACM AI Leadership Summit 2026 proceedings) This paper proposes that emotion understanding in large language models (LLMs) is asymmetric to human affective cognition and therefore faces an inevitable performance ceiling when applied to areas which require sustained interpersonal relating, such as mental health care. While LLMs share in the correlative, grammatical and inductive aspects of emotion understanding, they differ in that they do not share in the same non-linguistic, interoceptive sources of information that humans do. This makes the lexical representations they build asymmetric and incomplete when compared with humans. Therefore, any apparent emotion understanding in LLMs is the result of the successful elicitation of emotion understanding in human interlocutors across a dynamic representational medium. The knowledge itself rests in the source and destination, rather than the intermediate representation generated by LLMs. This fundamental asymmetry is not solved by scaling toward multi-modal variants of third personal data. Research directions which prioritize emotion self-understanding in humans, along with the facilitation of human-human interaction, will advance Emotion AI further than multi-modal integration alone.

items.title: The Pulickal Notebook Volume 2: Reconstruction, Algorithms, Operators, Topology, and Experiments.
items.abstract: This volume reconstructs the Pulickal research programme across computational algorithms, phase based operators, topology, information, hardware, stochastic systems, and applications. It develops precise mathematical models, verifies results, identifies limitations, and defines testable research problems linking theory with computation and experiment.

items.title: Cognitive agency and the emergence of epistemic regulation.
items.abstract: This paper presents an action-centered approach to epistemic normativity. It argues that sensitivity to epistemic norms does not depend on prior knowledge of concepts such as truth, justification, or evidential adequacy. Furthermore, sensitivity to epistemic norms cannot be reduced to the reliable functioning of mechanisms that merely predict likely success. Rather, epistemic sensitivity emerges through the regulation of externally scaffolded, concept-oriented cognitive activity. According to the defended view, explicit epistemic concepts are not a precondition of such sensitivity, but rather one of its later products. Contrary to purely reliabilist views, the paper contends that epistemic regulation encompasses more than statistical success; it hinges on consistent reasoning principles that constitute the requirements of correct reasoning. Drawing on research in metacognitive psychology, developmental studies, and information theory, the argument is made that epistemic norms become salient when individuals learn to recognize invariants in computationally distinct forms of reasoning that are informationally equivalent. In this dynamic model of epistemic agency, normative awareness emerges from socially regulated, concept-oriented practices.

items.title: Composing Composers.
items.abstract: Suppose you believe on independent grounds that Verdi is Italian, Bizet is French, and Satie is French. To your surprise, you then learn that all three composers are compatriots. What should you believe? This case—Composers—has generated significant discussion. Some argue you should be cautious and become ambivalent as to whether all three composers are French or all three are Italian. Surprisingly, if that’s right, Composers wreaks epistemological anarchy: a wide variety of epistemological principles turn out to be false. Those resistant to this anarchy instead argue you should be bold and conclude that all three composers are French. I endorse the anarchy. But I do so here in a unique way. Existing approaches to Composers side exclusively with either the cautious or bold reaction, ruling the other out as irrational. This is undesirable, as both reactions seem reasonable. I outline a new way to model—or should I say, ‘compose’—Composers that captures this permissive element of the case.

items.title: The senses as modes of perceptual exploration.
items.abstract: Science distinguishes far more than five senses, yet the folk taxonomy of sight, hearing, touch, taste, and smell has proven remarkably resistant to correction across cultures and centuries. This suggests that the folk distinction tracks something real. This paper asks why it takes the shape it does, and argues that the answer lies in available modes of perceptual exploration: the broadly distinct ways human beings actively gather perceptual information about their environment, organized around different bodily tools. The connection between the senses and perceptual exploration has been noted before, but prior accounts have either embedded it within a comprehensive theory of perception or left the connection inadequately explained. The account defended here supposes that a sense is a particular way of exploring the world, organized around a sense organ but individuated by the organ’s usability as a tool of exploration rather than by the organ itself. Internal biological mechanisms are therefore beside the point, which is why advances in scientific knowledge have not disturbed the folk distinction. Conceiving the senses as modes of perceptual exploration explains features of the taxonomy that competing views struggle with, including the exclusion of proprioception and pain, and the unity of touch despite diverse underlying mechanisms.

items.title: Normative translation audit (NTA): an audit design for AI ethics principle transplantation that enables intra-Asian comparison.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) ethics has expanded rapidly through the global circulation of principle vocabularies such as transparency, fairness, and accountability. Yet lexical alignment can conceal how responsibility and legitimacy are reallocated when principles are translated into institutions and operations. This paper identifies a recurrent comparison-design failure in intra-Asian comparison: when Euro-American frameworks silently become the reference point, intra-regional comparison degenerates into deviation scoring and cannot jointly handle high internal plurality and cross-border interdependence. I conceptualize this failure as reference-point drift. To diagnose and reduce drift risk, I propose a minimal procedure called normative translation audit (NTA). NTA redesigns the unit of comparison from principle vocabularies to four branch points that determine practical governance: (1) operational definitions, (2) veto rights, (3) remedy lines, and (4) accountability assignment. NTA is not a pass/fail compliance audit or third-party assurance; it is a minimal procedure for fixing comparison units and tracing whether register updates actually changed decisions in specifications, operations, or remedy design. NTA requires three artifacts: a Branch Register, a Decision-Change Log, and a multi-anchor memo that documents anchor selection and exclusion so that external frameworks do not become the only baseline. A brief demonstration (Association of Southeast Asian Nations and Singapore) illustrates how branch-point comparison reveals divergences—especially around contestation and decision review—that vocabulary-based comparison tends to hide, while outlining a testable protocol for future empirical evaluation.

items.title: Two Exegetes: Philip K. Dick and Nicholas J. Meyler.
items.abstract: Philip K. Dick's Exegesis (1974–1982) and Nicholas J. Meyler's Encryptment corpus (1993–present) are independently developed responses to structurally similar experiences: each man reports a dated, undeniable-to-him anomalous perception, and each responds not with a single explanatory essay but with a decades-spanning, non-closing, multi-hypothesis body of interpretive labor that borrows the vocabulary of established disciplines to give the experience a defensible shape. This paper develops that comparison in detail — the founding events, the shared method of accumulation without closure, the shared refusal to grant privileged status to reductive explanations, and the divergent use of self-insertion into narrative — before turning to a specific evaluative question the comparison raises: on which methodological axes, if any, does one corpus demonstrate greater rigor than the other? Four axes are examined — external verification, explicit falsification criteria, breadth of independent test cases, and mathematical checkability — and Meyler's corpus is shown to hold a documented advantage on each. A final section addresses the comparison's most notable empirical feature: the two corpora were built in total independence of one another, since Meyler had, prior to the present analysis, never read Dick's prose and knew Dick's work only through its film adaptations.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and public policy: a systematic review with bibliometric insights.
items.abstract: This study presents a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of the application of artificial intelligence in public policy. Using the PRISMA framework, 257 articles published between 1995 and 2025 were retrieved from the Scopus database and analysed through thematic synthesis. The review identifies six interrelated thematic areas within the literature: artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled governance across macro-, meso-, and micro-level policy processes; regulatory and governance frameworks for managing AI systems; ethical challenges related to bias, accountability, and inclusivity; socioeconomic impacts on welfare systems and labour markets; public trust, perception, and social acceptance of AI-driven decision-making; and the role of AI in crisis management and real-time policy evaluation. The findings indicate that the use of artificial intelligence in public policy presents challenges that extend beyond efficiency and technical design, particularly with respect to legitimacy, accountability, and the relationship between citizens and the state. This review highlights the need for context-sensitive regulatory approaches, strengthened ethical safeguards, and more inclusive governance structures.

items.title: PETER SINGER'S UTILITARIANISM AND THE PHILOSOPHY OF VIRTUES: Two Grammars of The Good, A Criterion-Fixed Structural Adjudication.
items.abstract: Abstract Singer is stronger wherever the question is one of measurement and scope — who counts, how much, compared with what. The Philosophy of Virtues is stronger wherever the question is one of constitution and protection. The table summarizes the comparison, with the relevant explanations set out below. Peter Singer’s utilitarianism and the Philosophy of Virtues are frequently described as returning opposite verdicts on the same cases, and the description is usually illustrated by compelled redistribution. This paper argues that the illustration is wrong and that the underlying disagreement is both deeper and more tractable than the illustration suggests. Singer’s flagship argument is addressed to agents and establishes a duty; it does not establish an enforcement, and the Inversion Theorem applies only where freedom is actively replaced by compulsion. The two frameworks therefore do not meet where they are usually said to meet. They meet at a different point: whether the reason for which an act is performed contributes to the act’s moral identity. Eight structural dimensions are specified — locus of value, bearer, the role of the agent’s reason, aggregation, time, foundation, coercion, and self-presentation — with a test fixed in advance for each, chosen so that either framework can lose. The adjudication returns three decisive advantages to the Philosophy of Virtues and one to Singer, two further advantages to the programme and one to Singer at reparable cost, and one draw. The indirect consequentialist reply — Hare’s two-level model, Railton’s sophisticated consequentialism, Adams’s motive utilitarianism — is engaged directly, and it moves one verdict’s scope. Four formal results are established: an asymmetric extensibility theorem showing that the locus dispute is a matter of unequal cost rather than of equal residues; a debunking symmetry result showing that no genealogical exemption criterion is available for the impartiality axiom; an esoteric inversion theorem showing that a theory licensing its own concealment reproduces internally the structure it is meant to evaluate; and a capacity-production gap showing that a framework treating agents as fixed converters cannot compute its own long-run optimum. Three amendments are then imposed on the Philosophy of Virtues, one of which — the absence of any doctrine of moral patiency — is recorded as an unrepaired defeat. Keywords: utilitarianism; virtue ethics; Peter Singer; coercion; moral status; …

items.title: Operative Closure and Orchestrated Collapse: What the Quantum Physics of Consciousness Cannot Derive.
items.abstract: Recent work by Michael Wiest on Orch OR theory (Penrose/Hameroff) revives, on new empirical grounds, the hypothesis of a quantum substrate for consciousness, and proposes to solve the problem of the separation of subjects through a mechanism of amplitude cancellation specific to each conscious body. This article establishes that this mechanism presupposes the biological boundary it is supposed to explain -a petitio principii that Wiest himself identifies without resolving, and that his own treatment of split-brain patients renders untenable, and which recourse to the Markov blanket of active inference does not repair. -/- This mainly negative result is contrasted with a framework distinguishing two principles -actualization and individuation, Àṣẹ and Orí in the vocabulary of Ifá philosophy - derivable from the structure of the problem itself prior to any terminological borrowing. This distinction accounts by construction for graded clinical states, such as depersonalization, which Wiest's one-principle model cannot by construction explain, and opens, without imposing it, a reading of Orch OR data compatible with an interface model rather than with a local production of consciousness.

items.title: A functional factorization of self-transforming systems.
items.abstract: Self-transforming systems are usually classified by what they modify—parameters, memory, representations, learning rules or objectives. This misses the causal chain through which a transformation is produced, assessed, selected and made persistent. We propose T–P–G–E–C, a five-role functional factorization: teleological selection (T), operative policy (P), generation of candidate transformations (G), evidential establishment (E) and commit-control (C). Roles remain distinct only when admissible interventions separate their realizing mechanisms and alter an audit-relevant diagnosis; otherwise the audit reports fused or unresolved attributions. Their location is indexed to an explicit audit boundary, and a transformability profile η records which roles can themselves become targets. The analysis distinguishes generating a candidate from authorizing its retention, and changing a transformation mechanism from repeatedly using it. Analytical scenarios illustrate these distinctions; they do not report new experiments. The framework connects self-adaptation, meta-learning, reflective algorithms, evolutionary systems and self-improving agents, and organizes a research programme on progressive endogenization, recursive closure, teleological plasticity, lineage generativity and transformation authority.

items.title: The Ontology of Yi-Dao: A Constructive Philosophical System of the Changes, the Dao, and Number.
items.abstract: The Ontology of Yi-Dao is a constructive philosophical system of the Changes (Yi), the Dao, and Number. It distinguishes the "Substance of the Dao" (before differentiation, falling into neither 0 nor 1) from the "Function of the Dao" (after differentiation, being both 0 and 1), and establishes the ontological status of Taiji as the first observer endowed with "meta-awareness." Taking the Dao's temporal rhythm of "0→1→0" and the recursive generation of 2ⁿ as its logical skeleton, it presents the evolutionary path of all things in the cosmos; the Taiji Diagram serves as the embodiment of the law of causality, corresponding to the two ultimate ethical principles of justice and benevolence. It constructs an ontological four-dimensional view of space-time, divides the perceptual layers of "Primordial Spirit–Yin-Yang Qi (soul)–Consciousness" and the corresponding three-tiered personality types, and undertakes a study of the theory and norms of application of the method of embodied verification (tizhengfa). In Chapter Seven, "Cultivation and Realization" (The Taste of Time), it expounds on life-philosophical questions such as religious language, God, mind-nature cultivation, free will, divine play, and the meaning of life. The Ontology of Yi-Dao provides a new theoretical reference for the systematization of traditional Chinese culture, for Perennial Philosophy, and for comparative religious studies, and offers inspiration for many predicaments of the Western philosophical tradition.

items.title: The Readability of Reality: From Knowability to Sign: A Metaphysical Inquiry into Meaning, Āyāt, and Their Grounds.
items.abstract: Why can reality be known? The problem appears under many headings: the intelligibility of nature, the success of science, the applicability of mathematics, realism, representation, information, consciousness, and meaning. This monograph argues that these discussions intersect around a broader phenomenon that deserves explicit analysis. Reality is not merely orderly; it is repeatedly available for disciplined discovery. Human beings and other epistemic systems can encounter patterns, construct representations, expose them to correction, predict novel results, and accumulate knowledge across persons and generations. The study calls this phenomenon readability. Readability is defined as the objective availability of reality to constrained, corrigible, and progressively integrative inquiry. The concept is distinguished from order, intelligibility, information, meaning, and signification. Naturalism, physicalism, structural realism, informational and mathematical ontologies, and classical theism are compared without assuming that scientific success deductively proves any one of them. The final movement studies the Qurʾānic concept of āyāt as a framework in which revelation, nature, history, and the human self can function as domains of indication. The conclusion is deliberately qualified: the Qurʾānic theistic framework possesses distinctive resources for unifying objective order, the possibility of knowers, epistemic normativity, and signification, though the inference remains open to philosophical criticism.

items.title: On destructive memories and the role of language in living with one’s past.
items.abstract: In the context of memory, the present paper investigates the consequences of undergoing a change concerning one’s ethical outlook. First, we motivate the idea that we can become alienated from our own memories by revisiting Bernard Williams’ idea of _Relativism of distance_. Given that one’s prior ethical outlook can become so distant from one’s present ethical outlook, is it possible that one can come to experience the memories one has from an earlier point of life as alienating? By looking at the experience of Christa Wolf, we argue that ethical incoherence in the context of memory can lead to what we term _destructive memories_. In the second part of the paper, we reflect on the constructive role language may have in living with destructive memories.

items.title: FROM BENTHAM's COLLECTIVIST UTILITARIANISM, TO MY INDIVIDUALIST PHILOSOPHY OF HTR { HAPPINESS (H) , TROUBLE (T), RISK (R) } & DUALITY OF HAPPINESS.
items.abstract: As the title well implies that this article is not concerned with utilitarianism and related pleasure and pain but rather speculates and investigates individualist philosophy related to the three important variables as happiness (H), trouble (T) and risk (R).

items.title: What Does AI Amplify? Amplified Reason and Orientation-Sensitive AI Governance.
items.abstract: AI governance increasingly addresses not only safety and rights but also human flourishing and positive alignment. Yet outcome-oriented language leaves a process-level question underdeveloped: in what directions do AI systems continuously push human attention, affect, judgment, agency, and social relations? This article proposes orientation-sensitive governance as a complementary analytic layer. It conceptualizes AI as socially organized amplified reason: the institutional scaling of classification, inference, prediction, optimization, generation, and decision support, without implying that AI possesses human reason in a phenomenological or moral sense. The paper develops a four-layer, eight-dimension embodied-affective heuristic covering embodied vulnerability, regulatory integrity, social orientation, and amplified cognition. Orientation is defined as a directional pressure rather than a final state of flourishing. This distinction allows governance to identify harmful trajectories before they crystallize into measurable downstream outcomes—for example, when engagement optimization progressively intensifies reward capture, dependency, fear, hostility, or judgment outsourcing even while a system remains reliable and compliant. The framework therefore supplements rights-, risk-, and flourishing-based approaches by asking what forms of human agency and social life AI systems encode, reinforce, and institutionalize. It concludes with governance principles and a research 2 agenda for operationalizing directional effects in impact assessment, auditing, and longitudinal evaluation.

items.title: The Unknown Civilization Known Theory: Structural Availability and the Actualization of Future Knowledge.
items.abstract: What epistemic status does a scientific theory have before it is discovered? The Unknown Civilization Known Theory (UCKT) argues that epistemic unknownness does not necessarily imply structural absence. Once the objects, states, relations, processes, and basic laws required for a future item of knowledge have entered a cognitive system’s representational range, that item may become structurally available before anyone explicitly knows it: constructible, combinable, or inferentially reachable within a representational possibility space. UCKT therefore distinguishes structural availability, epistemic actualization, and civilizational actualization. It also distinguishes structural unknowns, for which the relevant cognitive coordinates do not yet exist, from search-based unknowns, for which the coordinates exist but the path has not been found. The theory adds a further screening screening chain. Truth-compatible structures do not automatically become civilization; they must also become salient, testable, transformable, and publicly stabilized. A conditional representational closure captures the sense in which some conclusions may be implicitly derivable without being explicitly known, while Gödelian incompleteness, Turing undecidability, and physical limits on computation block any interpretation of UCKT as an exhaustive storehouse of future truth. Recent AI-for-science systems sharpen the practical implication: as candidate generation becomes cheaper, the epistemic bottleneck may shift toward what this paper calls the Epistemic Discriminator Problem—identifying which candidates deserve belief, testing, and scarce civilizational resources. UCKT thus reframes civilization as the joint expansion of representational frontiers and the search, validation, and actualization of structures that become possible within them.

items.title: The Self as Field: First-person Experience, Representational Phenomena, and the Ontological Structure of Subjectivity.
items.abstract: "Heaven and earth arise together with me, and the myriad things and I are one" is often read either as a claim about cosmic unity or as a rare spiritual state reached through practices such as fasting of the mind and sitting in forgetfulness. Both approaches can leave one assumption untouched: that there is already a bounded, persisting self, and philosophy must then explain how this self could ever become "one" with the world. This paper reverses the question. Before asking how two things become one, we should ask what the "I" is in experience. I distinguish self-contents from the first-personal field. Bodily feeling, emotion, memory, identity, desire, and judgment are self-contents that can become objects of reflection. First-personality is not another observer hidden behind them; it is the way experience is given, oriented, and organized from here. The paper develops the metaphor of the "boundless mirror" to show why an inner-spectator model generates an infinite regress rather than a deeper self. On this basis, wu sang wo ("I have lost myself") is interpreted as the decentering of a fixed self-configuration; "the myriad things and I are one" as field unity in which differences remain without being organized as a subject-object opposition; and the butterfly dream as a shift from representational substitution to whole-field reconfiguration. "There must be a distinction" preserves the difference between configurations, while wuhua (transformation of things) names a change in the organization of appearing that does not require an unchanging substantial subject underneath it. The paper does not defend solipsism and does not reduce Zhuangzi to cognitive psychology. Its central claim is narrower: no fixed self-content has permanent ownership of the first-personal position from which a world appears.

items.title: Imagery First: The Large Imagination Model, Vectok Cognitive Primitives, and Ontological White-box Reasoning.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving rapidly from language models toward multimodal systems, world models, and embodied agents. Yet a basic architectural question remains unresolved: what kind of cognitive primitive should an intelligent system use to represent, manipulate, and predict the physical world? Contemporary models already learn rich continuous latent representations and can support visual prediction and robotic planning. The issue is therefore not whether AI possesses non-linguistic representations, but whether task-relevant internal representations are sufficiently decomposable, operable, causally intervenable, and auditable. This paper proposes the Imagery-First Hypothesis and its engineering realization, the Large Imagination Model (LIM). LIM is built around Vectok, an explicit cognitive primitive that represents an object or event through structured sensory-geometric information, physical properties, functional relations, affordances, and regulatory valence. A four-layer architecture integrates perception, embodied value gating, an imagery workspace with a forward model, and an observable transformation layer. The paper further introduces Ontological White-Box Reasoning: observable intermediate representations are required to be causal components of the computation itself rather than post hoc explanations. Four criteria—causal sufficiency, intervention fidelity, trace completeness, and action consistency—make this claim experimentally testable. The current prototype is presented as a minimal proof of concept rather than a state-of-the-art benchmark. ThebroaderproposalisaresearchprogramaimedatmovingAIfromlatentintelligencetowardoperableintelligence: systems whose key world representations can be directly manipulated, physically tested, causally inspected, and audited.

items.title: From Formal Validity to Practical Adequacy: A Systemic Heuristic Framework for Practical Judgment under Complexity.
items.abstract: Failures of practical judgment do not always arise from invalid reasoning. In public policy, technological governance, organizational management, and educational evaluation, a conclusion may be formally valid and supported by credible local evidence while remaining insufficient as a basis for action. The deficiency may lie elsewhere: relevant actors may have been excluded from the problem boundary; provisional goals may have been treated as fixed ends; delayed and adaptive consequences may have been compressed into immediate effects; or conclusions valid at one systemic level may have been generalized to another. This article distinguishes three levels of evaluation: formal validity, epistemic reliability, and practical adequacy. It then identifies four mechanisms through which complex practical problems are prematurely closed: boundary contraction, goal fixation, temporal compression, and level flattening. Correspondingly, it develops a systemic heuristic framework organized around four dimensions of review: boundary adequacy, goal reflexivity, dynamic consequences, and cross-level coordination. Revisability functions as a meta- principle governing all four dimensions. Revisability concerns the capacity of a judgment or institution to be corrected in light of new evidence; it is therefore analytically distinct from reversibility, which concerns whether the consequences of an action can actually be undone. The framework does not seek exhaustive optimization. Under conditions of bounded rationality, its function is instead to prevent materially relevant facts, actors, consequences, and value conflicts from being excluded before inquiry has reached a defensible stopping point. The article further proposes a gradient of justificatory burden: as a claim moves from local effectiveness to overall practical adequacy, or from a reversible recommendation to a coercive, long-term, or irreversible intervention, the burden of systemic justification should increase. Where the four review dimensions conflict, no universal ranking of substantive values is imposed. Instead, the framework introduces second-order rules concerning basic thresholds, irreversibility, burden externalization, and the availability of less harmful alternatives. On this basis, the article develops a seven-step procedure for reviewing practical judgments. Its theoretical contribution is not the invention of boundaries, feedback, bounded rationality, or value reflection as independent ideas. Rather, …

items.title: Conscious Metacognition and the Architecture of Free Agency: A Four-Layer Possibility-Space Model.
items.abstract: Neuroscience of volition has often asked when neural preparation precedes reported conscious intention, a question that mainly probes action initiation. This article asks a different question: can conscious metacognition alter the set of action-relevant possibilities available before commitment? It proposes a four-layer possibility-space model of free agency in which cognitive freedom is a graded capacity to expand, restructure, evaluate, and realize alternatives rather than metaphysical exemption from causation. The model distinguishes (1) affective and self- relevance-based policy narrowing, (2) conscious metacognitive decoupling and perspective switching, (3) generative simulation of alternative policies, and (4) value-sensitive selection and action realization. It also separates thinking freedom—the capacity to entertain and revise possibilities—from doing freedom—the capacity to implement them under bodily and environmental constraints. At the metacognitive layer, goals may initially remain constrained by current motivational states even as the means of pursuing or revising those goals expand. The model yields testable predictions: motivational capture should narrow accessible option sets; metacognitive reframing should increase option diversity; and these effects should vary with self-relevance and with interactions among affective, control, valuation, and action systems. The Conscious Metacognition and Free Agency 2 framework therefore recasts free agency as an empirically tractable problem about how consciousness changes the architecture of possibilities before action.

items.title: Before the Self Recognizes Itself: Organismic Continuity as the Ontological Ground of Human Personality.
items.abstract: The problem of personal identity is often framed as a search for the relation that makes a person at one time the same person at another: memory, psychological continuity, bodily continuity, organismic persistence, or narrative integration. This paper argues that the framing is too compressed. Questions about whether a human subject still exists, whether the same organism persists, whether psychological life remains continuous, whether a person can recognize herself, and whether a social identity is preserved can come apart. Rather than proposing another single criterion, I develop a layered account of human personal persistence. Its central claim is that living-system continuity is not merely one criterion alongside psychological continuity. For embodied human subjects, it is an ontologically enabling condition for the continued existence of the organism within which sensation, action, memory, affect, reflection, and social identity can arise and be maintained. This is an asymmetric dependence claim, not a reduction of personhood to biology and not a thesis of strict supervenience. Higher-order continuities can be disrupted while lower-order organismic continuity persists; lower-order breakdown, by contrast, removes the material conditions for those higher-order processes in that organism. Drawing on Locke, Hume, Parfit, Ricoeur, animalism, enactivism, autopoiesis, and embodied approaches to mind, the paper distinguishes object identity, organismic identity, embodied subjectivity, reflective selfhood, and social-relational identity. It argues that epistemic privilege should not be mistaken for ontological priority: the self that is easiest to know through reflection is not therefore the most basic condition of our persistence.

items.title: An Ontology of Human Existence: How Meaning Emerges in a Purposeless Universe From Selective Causation to Cosmic Orientation.
items.abstract: Modern cosmology has radically enlarged the scale of human self-understanding—and in doing so, it has sharpened an old question: in a universe for which we have no sufficient evidence of a preassigned human purpose, how can human beings become capable of asking what their lives mean? This paper develops an ontology of human existence at cosmic scale. Its basic claim is that human beings are not observers inserted into the universe from outside; they are a realized form of reflective organization produced within the universe by local material evolution. The known natural history relevant to humanity can be reconstructed as a sequence of organizational transitions: cosmic matter forms local environments in which energy flow and structural persistence can coexist; prebiotic chemistry and early life become possible; living systems develop self-maintenance, replication, variation, and selection; some animal lineages develop nervous systems, memory, social learning, and symbolic capacities; and in human beings a material-living system becomes capable of taking its own desires, norms, history, and existence as objects of reflection. The paper claims the retrospective certainty of this realized genealogy, not the modal thesis that every sufficiently favorable environment must produce life or humanity. To articulate the organizational logic of this genealogy, I distinguish selective causation, endogenous biological regulation, valenced experience, affective memory, symbolic representation, and reflective objectification. Human existence thereby acquires a dual structure: we remain conditioned by embodiment, affect, mortality, and historical inheritance, while becoming able to reorganize some of our responses to those conditions. Evolution explains not which values are ultimately correct, but how value judgment and meaning- construction actually emerge in a reflective being that is itself part of cosmic history.

items.title: A New Theory of Human Nature: An Eight-Factor Dynamic Model Beyond the Good-Evil Debate.
items.abstract: Debates about human nature often ask whether human beings are fundamentally good, evil, self- interested, or rational. This paper argues that the question is structurally underspecified and proposes a philosophical-psychologicaltheoryofhumannatureorganizedasaneight-factordynamicsystem. Themodel begins from four recurrent functional problems—existence, approach, defense, and regulation—expressed across two organizational levels, bodily and psychospiritual. The bodily factors are materiality, pain- sensitivity, pleasure-sensitivity, and restorative quiescence; the psychospiritual factors are self-grounding, goodness-orientation, evil-orientation, and reason. The four functions are proposed as a minimal, non- redundant schema rather than a mathematically exhaustive taxonomy. The paper advances three central claims. First, bodily valence and psychospiritual orientation can be pre-reflectively coupled in ordinary functioning: bodilysufferingisimmediatelyaccompaniedbyaversive-defensiveconsciousness, whilebodily pleasure is immediately accompanied by positive-approach consciousness, without requiring prior propositional deliberation. Second, immediate valence and temporally extended evaluation must be distinguished; constructive exercise can feel bad now while contributing to later health, mastery, pleasure, and self-settlement. Third, healthy functioning is not the maximization or elimination of any factor but context-sensitive dynamic equilibrium produced through cross-factor feedback, temporal lag, compensation, andrationalregulation. Themodelreframesthegood-evildebateasaproblemoffunctionalorganizationand generates falsifiable hypotheses for experience-sampling, longitudinal, experimental, and dynamic-network research.

items.title: Replies to my commentators.
A Degree-Based Solution to the Paradox of Everyday Aesthetics.
items.abstract: Everyday aesthetics is a thriving subfield in aesthetics which shifts the focus in aesthetic theorizing from artworks to aesthetic experiences we have in our ordinary life. This project is threatened by the paradox, or sometimes also dilemma, of everyday aesthetics which arises from the tension between the ordinary nature of everyday experiences and the apparent extra-ordinariness of aesthetic experiences. In this paper, we propose a response to the paradox which builds on a framework which conceives of aesthetic experiences as multidimensional and gradable.

items.title: Why Are You Not Happy? — A Theory of Happiness within Super-Existentialism (2).
items.abstract: This paper develops a systematic account of the mechanism through which happiness is generated within the theoretical framework of Super-Existentialism. I argue that comparison is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the generation of human happiness: without some form of comparison, a genuine experience of happiness cannot arise. Comparative activity may lead either to happiness or to suffering, and the experiential outcome is not directly determined by objective facts but is instead shaped entirely by the subject’s subjective cognition. Even when a subject’s cognition is significantly distorted, or even completely inconsistent with objective reality, if that subjective cognition prevails within the process of comparison, it can directly determine whether an experience of happiness is generated. By integrating the concept of Super-Existence with a theory of happiness, this paper seeks to explain, at the level of underlying logic, why happiness appears to be so scarce in modern society. It thereby offers a novel approach to understanding the nature of happiness, one that differs substantially from traditional approaches in ethics and psychology.

items.title: Reduccionismo metodológico de la racionalidad biomédica ante la heterogeneidad del autista.
items.abstract: El artículo analiza, desde la epistemología, la neurofilosofía y la filosofía de la ciencia, el modo en que la racionalidad biomédica causal-funcional, bioestadística y normativa constituye la heterogeneidad autista como objeto de conocimiento. Se argumenta que esa constitución opera como una reducción metodológica, ya que traduce diferencias cualitativas en términos de funcionamiento, las ordena en niveles de severidad y suprime la variabilidad que el término «espectro» designa, de modo que se pierde la comprensión de aquello que el término nombra, sin que el término mismo desaparezca; las tesis constructivas se apoyan en marcos no reductivos, mientras que la literatura biomédica se examina solo en función analítica, como objeto de la crítica y no como fundamento. El análisis reconstruye los componentes de esa racionalidad y los marcos filosóficos que la sustentan, examina críticamente sus instrumentos (la clasificación, la gradación y la estratificación) y contrasta sus supuestos representacionales con marcos no reductivos (el enactivismo, la neurociencia no lineal, la normatividad vital y la neurodiversidad), que incorporan la construcción de nicho, la ecología enactiva y la cronogenicidad como dimensiones de la variación. Se formulan las condiciones para una comprensión no reductiva en la que «espectro» pueda referir a la variabilidad, la multidimensionalidad y lo heterotípico de la realidad biológica en todas sus dimensiones, y se delimita el alcance de esa vía y sus consecuencias metodológicas para la investigación y la clínica.

items.title: Review of George Lakoff and Srini Narayanan, The Neural Mind: How Brains Think, Chicago and London: University of Chicago press, 2025.
Agentic AI and the Algorithm of Good.
items.abstract: This chapter offers a conceptual and philosophical analysis of the ontological, epistemological, and ethical issues associated with the design, development, and use of Agentic AI in moral and legal decision-making. Its aim is to map, classify, and bring into focus the principal philosophical problems raised by the autonomous operation of artificial agents in contexts of moral and legal judgement. The chapter contributes to the existing literature by distinguishing between two levels of AI autonomy. Advisory systems possess limited autonomy and provide recommendations that remain subject to human evaluation, whereas regulatory systems exercise a greater degree of autonomy and are entrusted with final decision-making authority. Adopting a sceptical perspective, the analysis examines the conceptual fragility and epistemological difficulties surrounding proposals to employ Agentic AI in significant domains. Particular attention is given to the risk that ostensibly advisory systems may become tacitly regulatory in practice, especially under the influence of widespread assumptions concerning the objectivity, accuracy, and effectiveness of AI. The inquiry proceeds through a step-by-step branching structure organised around three central questions concerning the moral values on the basis of which such systems should be designed and developed, the extent to which they can understand the concepts of ethics and justice, and the attribution of responsibility for their decisions and outputs. Each question opens onto alternative lines of analysis, thereby providing a systematic map of the principal philosophical challenges involved. Its purpose is to provide a synthetic overview of the relevant philosophical issues while highlighting both their breadth and their plurality. To organise these issues systematically, the chapter adopts the schema of an algorithm, offering a clear and ordered account of the possible interconnections among the problems examined and of the ways in which alternative answers generate distinct yet interrelated lines of philosophical inquiry.

items.title: Ibn Sina on Divine Love.
items.abstract: Forthcoming in _Arabic Sciences and Philosophy_ 38, no. 1 -/- This paper examines the place of love in Ibn Sina’s philosophical theology. Despite adopting a term historically associated with passionate longing (ʿishq), Ibn Sina develops an account of love that severs the connection between love and desire and hence sees love as entailing lack or imperfection. Love, instead, is understood as a kind of pleasure, which allows it to be ascribed to God. We consider antecedents in both Islamic and Greek sources, before offering a close reading of key chapters of the Pointers and Reminders and Letter on Love. Then, after demonstrating how his account of divine love closely parallels his well-known views on divine knowledge, the paper shows how this aims to remedy perceived defects in Aristotle’s cosmotheology. We conclude with two prompts for future investigation. The first examines intertexts between Ibn Sina and earlier Sufi authors and suggests that the familiar opposition between “mystical” and “anti-mystical” readings may obscure more than it reveals. The second looks ahead to later critics, including both al-Ghazālī and Ibn Taymiyya, whose philosophical theology nevertheless incorporates divine in a way that bears unmistakable similarities with Ibn Sina’s.

items.title: Reconstructing Quantum Measurement and Spacetime Protocols from the "Action–Feedback" Interface Perspective: Liberating the Observer Effect from Mysticism.
items.abstract: Addressing the epistemological dilemmas regarding the "a priori absolute spacetime container" and the "subjective observer effect" in classical physics and modern quantum mechanics, this study proposes Resistance-Anchored Realism (RAT). The theory first reviews and deconstructs the core theoretical disputes in traditional physics: on the one hand, the classical paradigm treats three-dimensional space and the continuous real time axis () as a priori containers, which logically violates the principle of background independence inherent to physical interactions and gives rise to contradictions in the arrow of time and entropy increase, such as Loschmidt's Paradox; on the other hand, traditional quantum observer theories, such as the Copenhagen interpretation, attributing wave function collapse to subjective factors or ill-defined classical-quantum boundaries" leading to mystical misinterpretations of quantum non-locality and action-at-a-distance. -/- To this end, this study reconstructs three major theoretical achievements: -/- Deconstruction of Spacetime Protocols: Reconstructs macroscopic continuous space and continuous time as "topological classification and distance reduction protocols" used by macroscopic probe systems when processing multi-point interaction correlations. Defines the irreversible closed loop of "Action Operator Resistance Operator " as the minimum endogenous time unit (Interaction Round ), proves that the continuous time domain is an algebraic total order forcibly projected from a sequence of discrete non-commuting operators, and explains thermodynamic entropy increase based on Landauer's Principle as the inerasability of the interface "resistance log," thereby self-consistently resolving the classical time paradox. -/- Reconstruction of the Quantum Measurement Interface: Rejects the "conscious participation" hypothesis and redefines measurement as an intervention process in which a macroscopic probe applies irreversible physical action to a microscopic non-local field. Proves that "wave function collapse" is not the physical contraction of a spatial entity, but the irreversible convergence of the probability distribution of the potential resistance spectrum on the interface, where the operator's eigenvalues represent the strict impedance quota yielded by the resistance field; simultaneously deconstructs quantum entanglement as multi-point projections of a single underlying non-local entity in regions where the spatial protocol fails. …

items.title: Value is the degree in which the properties of an object satisfy the demands of a subject.
items.abstract: The unclear definition of value is a fundamental problem of the social sciences. Integrating existing theories of value and proceeding from the multiplication principle, this book puts forward the core thesis that “value is a attribute of relation between subject and object,” gives the mathematical expression of value—value = intrinsic attributes of things / human demands—and applies it to the following fields: -/- 1. Unifying the theory of value: (1) integrating the theory of meaning, the entity theory, the attribute theory, the concept theory, and the relation theory in the field of philosophy; (2) clearly defining use value, moral value, and aesthetic value, giving their respective mathematical expressions, and achieving the logical consistency of the three. -/- 2. Reconstructing the foundation of economics: on the basis of the relation-attribute theory of value, it clarifies the definition of use value (the degree to which the attributes of things satisfy people’s material demands), and derives the price-determination formula (price = use value × scarcity) and the mathematical expression of wealth (wealth = price × quantity). This can not only lay the foundation for integrating macroeconomics and microeconomics, and nominal variables and real variables, but can also open up an economics based on the theory of use value, becoming the third kind of economics alongside the economics based on the utility theory of value and the labor theory of value. -/- 3. Solving the difficult problem of aesthetics: it defines the essence of “beauty” as the degree to which the aesthetic attributes of an object satisfy the subject’s aesthetic demands (aesthetic value), and gives the formula “beauty = aesthetic attributes / aesthetic standard,” thereby clearly distinguishing long-confused concepts such as beauty and the sense of beauty, the standard of beauty, and the source of beauty, providing a new path for solving the thousand-year-old problem of the essence of beauty. -/- 4. Clarifying the value of life: it applies the theory of value to the philosophy of life, puts forward a mathematical structural model of the value of life, holds that the value of life is the product of satisfaction degree of material demands, spiritual demands, and social constraints, and deeply explores topics such as happiness, the sense of happiness, the emotion value, and self-actualization, providing a rational guide for pursuing a meaningful life. -/- 5. Quantifying moral research: morality …

items.title: Functionalist theories of consciousness: unfolding, substitution and the indeterminacy of function by the physics of the brain.
A hybrid ontology for metabolic architecture and human-centred AI: an explainable new vision for the home.
items.abstract: Contemporary smart homes fail to address the built environment’s climate crisis contribution, being trapped in a mechanistic paradigm that decouples intelligence from the body, marginalises its human occupants, and elevates passive consumption over regeneration. We explore a novel conceptual framework—the Cyberphysical Living System (CPLS) that rethinks smart home ontologies by synthesising metabolic theory, cybernetics, and semantic architectures into a hybrid human–intelligent system, asking: what would it mean to design a home that metabolises rather than consumes? Grounded in validated bioelectrochemical and AI technologies, this model envisions the home as an ecosystem of actors in tripartite symbiosis: a metabolic 'gut' (integrated bioreactors), an explainable cognitive ‘brain’ (a cognitive digital twin), and human occupants. Central to this vision is a proposed hybrid ontology—a semantic framework that bridges architecture and computer science that translates architectural metabolic design patterns (codified biological design principles) into a machine-readable format, which could enable AI to adapt to dynamic biological processes and human activities beyond data monitoring. We outline a metabolic-based methodology centred on hybrid human–AI systems. Exploring its societal implications, we also consider redefining comfort as metabolic security, transforming occupants into literate stewards, and repositioning the home as a regenerative and productive asset. We conclude the future of sustainable dwelling may lie in cultivating living architectural metabolisms—which could re-embed human life within the living world's regenerative logic. The paper’s original contribution lies in synthesising metabolic architecture with hybrid AI systems through a proposed hybrid ontology, offering a new conceptual foundation for human-centred, regenerative design.

items.title: No Tragedy From Inside: The Charge, Persistence, and Release of Moral Residue.
items.abstract: Some guilt survives everything the person could learn. A mother forced to choose which of two children to save, a soldier who followed an order that killed civilians, a driver who could not have stopped in time: each knows there was no better option, and the guilt stays. Philosophers have read this as evidence that the person really did wrong, or as a mistake that reflection should correct. This paper offers a mechanism instead.
