Each of a person's commitments keeps its own account of what is owed, and each judges a loss by one question only: could this debt have been paid? When two commitments demand things that cannot both be done, the commitment that loses finds that its debt could have been paid---by giving up the other---and charges the person. It never asks whether both could have been paid, because it carries only one. So the charge is correct on its own books and wrong about the person, and no fact can remove it, because the missing fact has no place in the account. The charge persists because the mind keeps searching for what could have been done, and in an irreversible loss it keeps finding something. The same search can find what the lost person would want now---people run because she ran, keep the garden she kept---and that quiets the charge. What it does not find alone is what she would say about what happened. That release is available, and someone usually has to ask for it.

items.title: Organised Crime Derived from Economic Injustice, Individual Corruption, and the Danger of Knowledge: A Critical Analysis of Breaking Bad.
items.pub: Journal of Contextual Economics – Schmollers Jahrbuch:1-22.
items.venue: Journal of Contextual Economics – Schmollers Jahrbuch
items.abstract: This article examines Breaking Bad through a philosophical and criminological lens that foregrounds the relationship between knowledge, power, economic injustice, and moral failure. The study argues that its central problem lies in the destabilising potential of specialised knowledge when detached from ethical judgment and practical wisdom. Walter White’s transformation is analysed as a progressive reconfiguration of agency, in which technical expertise becomes a mechanism of domination within an alternative institutional order constituted by organised crime derived from a lack of economic justice. Drawing on Foucault’s power/knowledge nexus, Heidegger’s concept of technological enframing, and Aristotelian phronesis, the article demonstrates how intelligence, when confined to instrumental rationality, produces not autonomy but moral blindness. The criminal economy depicted in the series is interpreted not as a breakdown of social order but as a structurally coherent system that absorbs and amplifies such forms of knowledge. In this context, individual corruption is neither sudden nor exceptional. It emerges through cumulative processes of rationalisation, affective distortion, and the erosion of ethical limits. By situating Breaking Bad within broader debates on the epistemic conditions of modernity, the study contributes to discussions on the ethical boundaries of expertise and the unintended consequences of knowledge operating beyond normative constraints.

items.title: Gradual Identity Upload Protocol: A Safety-First Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Cognitive Digital Twins and Brain–Computer Interfaces.
items.abstract: Advances in brain–computer interfaces (BCIs), longitudinal personal data, and generative artificial intelligence have made it increasingly plausible to build persistent computational models of individual cognition. These systems, referred to here as cognitive digital twins (CDTs), may model, predict, simulate, or act as partial communicative and decisionmaking proxies for a person. However, the technical possibility of increasingly personal AI does not establish identity equivalence, continuity of consciousness, or the legitimacy of proxy action. This paper proposes the Gradual Identity Upload Protocol (GIUP): a safety-first research framework for incrementally constructing, testing, governing, and, where appropriate, retiring high-risk cognitive digital twins. GIUP treats “identity upload” not as a binary event but as a sequence of falsifiable, reversible, and auditable stages. It combines multimodal behavioral data, optional neural signals, neuro-symbolic representations, uncertainty estimation, longitudinal evaluation, version control, and human governance. The framework introduces three core concepts: identity fidelity, an ordinal, multi-dimensional assessment of behavioral and value-consistency under controlled evaluation—deliberately not collapsed into a single fitted score; epistemic drift, a set of independently thresholded indicators of divergence between a CDT’s outputs and the validated evidence about its source person; and reversibility, the ability to halt, isolate, roll back, or retire a model without irreversibly changing the person or delegating authority without consent. The paper proposes an Identity Turing Benchmark, a neuro-symbolic architecture for auditable proxy reasoning, a risk taxonomy for cognitive digital twins, and a governance model derived from the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and CDT-specific governance proposals. It is positioned explicitly against the closest adjacent framework in the literature, Gradual Cognitive Externalization (Zhao, 2026), which makes a functionalist metaphysical claim GIUP deliberately declines to make. The central claim is modest but consequential: before claims of mind uploading or digital immortality can be evaluated, the field needs rigorous methods for measuring what a model represents, what it does not represent, when it may act, and how humans can contest or terminate its authority. Current BCI platforms, including nanoparticle-based non-surgical approaches, may eventually supply new …

items.title: Farming the future: Ethical challenges in the age of AI and digitalization.
The Worth of Human Life: A Multidimensional Foundation for Human Rights.
items.abstract: This article develops a multidimensional account of the worth of human life and explores its implications for the philosophical foundations of human rights. It argues that traditional monistic accounts, whether theological, rationalist, autonomy-based, sentientist, or capability-oriented, capture important aspects of human value but remain limited when treated as exclusive foundations. In response, the article proposes a five-dimensional architecture of human worth composed of (i) biological vitality, (ii) sentient-affective life, (iii) moral capacity, (iv) cognitive-productive power, and (v) relational embeddedness. This structure is understood as interdependent and shared rather than as a set of capacities whose exercise determines moral status. The model explains equal human worth by grounding value in structural participation in the architecture of human life, rather than in the possession or performance of any single faculty. It also clarifies how human rights protect the biological, experiential, moral, cognitive, and relational dimensions of human existence. The article’s contribution is therefore not to replace existing human rights theories, but to offer a more integrative account of the human worth that such theories often presuppose.

items.title: Two Engines of Philosophical Innovation: A Meta-Philosophical Analysis of Knowledge-Reorganization and Experience-Triggering Paradigms.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel meta-philosophical framework for distinguishing the Analytic and Continental traditions based on their core mechanisms of theoretical innovation. It argues that the forefront of the Analytic tradition, particularly in its meta-theoretical endeavors, operates through a paradigm of internal knowledge-reorganization. Its innovation is a logic-driven, discipline-dependent process of conceptual engineering and foundational critique. In contrast, the Continental tradition operates through a paradigm of external experience-triggering. Its innovation is an experience-driven, hermeneutical process that abstracts from profound, often liminal, experiences by deploying an established theoretical toolbox. The paper elucidates the methodological prototypes, difficulty thresholds, and inherent risks of each paradigm. It concludes that they represent two distinct, and largely incommensurable, "generative grammars" for philosophical production, and that recognizing this division of labor is more productive than insisting on their synthesis.

items.title: Consciousness as a Layered Phenomenon: Integrating Phenomenal, Functional, and Social-Representational Accounts.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a layered integrative model of consciousness that seeks to reconcile three widely discussed perspectives: (1) the phenomenal (first-person) reality of subjective experience; (2) the functional account that identifies consciousness with cognitive mechanisms such as information integration, self-modeling, and adaptive optimization; and (3) the social-representational perspective that emphasizes the role of language, culture, and interpersonal exchange in shaping reportable experience. I argue that many apparent conflicts among these perspectives arise from category mistakes—each account addresses different explananda and operates at different explanatory levels. The integrative model organizes consciousness into three interacting layers (Phenomenal, Mechanistic/Functional, and Social-Representational), specifies hypothesized causal and constitutive relations among them, and identifies empirical predictions that distinguish this approach from reductive functionalism and strong social-constructivism. I defend a form of non-reductive physicalism that treats phenomenal experience as a real ontic feature while maintaining that specific functional configurations (information integration, global broadcasting, predictive self-modeling) are necessary for the generation and stability of subjective states. Finally, the paper outlines empirical tests (developmental, comparative, lesion, and dissociation paradigms) and philosophical implications (on explanatory gap debates, the status of philosophical zombies, and normative claims about reporting and intersubjective verification).

items.title: Governed Semantic-State Reinstantiation Across Fresh Reasoning Instances.
items.abstract: Long-lived reasoning systems face a continuity problem that is distinct from persistent storage, retrieval, or context projection. A system may preserve an authoritative state outside the model while still failing to make the consequential meaning of that state operational for the next reasoning instance. We call this semantic-state reinstantiation: a task-conditioned behavioral property of an execution protocol, defined as the extent to which a fresh reasoning instance can recover and use predefined consequential relationships from externally represented state. IEM studies a governed implementation of this more general research object. Persistence asks whether state remains available; reinstantiation asks whether its consequential meaning becomes operational again in a fresh reasoner. We present the Implementation and Execution Model (IEM), a governed semantic-orientation architecture that externalizes semantic state from any particular reasoning instance. IEM represents evidence and interpretations under provenance and authority, distinguishes exploratory and provisional interpretations from governed standing, compiles task-conditioned executable context, and supports scoped correction while preserving unaffected history. The paper does not claim invention of persistent memory, provenance, temporal state, graphs, belief revision, runtime-independent persistence, authorized state, or context projection individually. Those functions have substantial prior art. The primary publication contribution is the operationalization and measurement of semantic-state reinstantiation across fresh reasoning instances, with IEM presented as one governed implementation. We evaluate the architecture through the Northstar experimental sequence. In a 30-day longitudinal synthetic corpus, both IEM and cumulative-Raw conditions preserved the audited consequential distinctions while IEM used 87.9% fewer input tokens. A prospectively scored context-pressure experiment again found no semantic separation - 120/120 distinctions were preserved in both conditions - but IEM used 59.25% less aggregate input context, reaching a 74.04% reduction at the highest checkpoint. This negative result is retained as evidence that acumulative Raw remained semantically adequate within the tested range. A later bundled runtime-completion comparison evaluated the complete adaptive IEM protocol against a one-pass complete-Raw baseline. The IEM condition tested whether a fresh reasoner operating on …

items.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Mediate the Divine? A Theological Analysis of Machine Participation in Christian Worship.
items.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence has introduced a new technological presence into religious life, capable of producing sermons, prayers, hymns, biblical commentary, devotional material, and liturgical text, and of assuming visible roles in worship through avatars and synthetic voices. This article critically examines the place of AI in Christian worship from a Christian and Reformed theological perspective, asking whether such systems can be said to mediate the Divine. It distinguishes between technological mediation, religious mediation and theological mediation, and argues that AI can mediate religious information, facilitate religious experience and assist human participation in worship, but cannot mediate the Divine in the Christological and soteriological sense in which Christian theology understands divine mediation. Drawing on Christian doctrine, Reformed theology of worship, recent scholarship on AI and religion, and empirical evidence from AI-led worship, the article develops a four-level framework for evaluating AI participation in worship: instrumental assistance, ministerial assistance, delegated religious agency and liturgical substitution. It further proposes a five-part theological matrix (agency, authority, accountability, embodiment and mediation) for assessing specific applications, and six principles for a theology of responsible AI-assisted worship. The article concludes that AI may legitimately function as an instrument within worship when its use is transparent, accountable, subordinate to Scripture and ecclesial authority and directed toward human flourishing, but that the Church should resist treating AI as a spiritual subject, an independent religious authority, a sacramental agent or an alternative mediator between God and humanity.

items.title: Olfactory Origins and Cognitive Hardening: Qualitative Experience, History-Dependent Cognitive Asymmetry, Pre-Reflective Perception, and Artificial Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for understanding odor-evoked recollection not as the retrieval of a single memory from a single sensory stimulus, but as a history-dependent cognitive process in which qualitative experience, affect, autobiographical memory, scene reconstruction, embodied knowledge, experiential rules, and learned knowledge become successively and reciprocally activated. -/- The paper introduces the term associative origin for an event in which a sensory input encounters an individual's experiential history and thereby establishes asymmetric initial conditions for subsequent cognitive transitions. It further introduces cognitive hardening to describe the process by which repeated experience makes particular transitions toward perception, association, evaluation, or action relatively dominant while reducing susceptibility to alternative updates. Hardening, however, does not imply irreversible fixation or pathology. It is proposed as a cross-domain concept for describing history-dependent cognitive asymmetries that may appear as expertise, habit, individuality, embodied knowledge, aversion, or other stable cognitive tendencies. -/- This framework partially overlaps with existing accounts of predictive processing, habit formation, entrenchment, canalization, and attractor dynamics. Its aim is therefore not to claim the novelty of history dependence itself. Rather, the paper connects three structures within a single model: associative sequences initiated by sensory-bodily events, changes in updateability produced through repeated transitions, and the temporal delay through which reflective consciousness approaches the pre-reflective events that have already oriented it. -/- With reference to Merleau-Ponty's account of pre-reflective embodiment, the paper argues that reflection may not recover the original perceptual event itself, but rather the traces that event has left in bodily orientation, affect, attention, memory, and subsequent cognition. This phenomenally accessible remainder is termed the shadow of pure perception. -/- Finally, the paper considers possible extensions of the model to artificial intelligence. In medical care in particular, the humanization of AI need not be conceived solely as the imitation of human appearance or empathic language. Instead, it may involve forms of artificial cognitive hardening in which interaction history changes what an artificial system treats as salient and which possibilities for …

items.title: World-Formation Research: An Operatoric Research Programme for the Study of Non-Closure, Knowledge, and the Conditions of Further Knowledge.
items.abstract: Science has highly developed procedures for distinguishing, naming, measuring, modelling, and transforming reality into stable forms. Far less developed are procedures for investigating how precisely these successful stabilizations alter the conditions under which further knowledge, other forms of existence, and future world-formation remain possible at all. This paper proposes World-Formation Research as the designation for a transdisciplinary operatoric research programme that begins at this gap. -/- Its point of departure is the assumption of a fundamental non-closure of world. Non-closure refers neither to ignorance nor to provisionally missing data. It is the condition that allows difference, change, perspective, and further formation to remain possible at all. Every act of naming, modelling, or institutional stabilization binds part of this open field into a concrete world-form. In the terminology of the underlying Operatoric Research Corpus, this process is referred to as Seinsverschiebung (shift of being). A Seinsverschiebung does not neutrally represent reality. It changes the space in which further reality can appear. It shifts that space relationally. -/- From this follows a second movement of science. Science must close in order to know and to act. But it must also investigate how its closures alter the conditions of further knowing. World-Formation Research understands this second movement not as a subsequent ethics of science, but as a component of scientific rationality itself. -/- The paper defines the relationship of World-Formation Research to preontology, operatoric research, and negative morphology, and distinguishes the programme from metaphysics, classical epistemology, the ethics of science, and discipline-specific explanation. Using examples from artificial intelligence, social normalization, and physical boundary problems, it shows why the decisive question is not only how knowledge can be increased, but which world remains sustainable with which knowledge. The core demand is therefore: science bears responsibility not only for the knowledge it produces, but also for preserving those conditions under which other and future knowledge can continue to emerge. -/- This has not only a scientific dimension, but also a political and human-rights dimension.

items.title: After Matter, What Is “Physical”? Non-Materialist Physicalism and Experiential Empiricism at the Final Subtraction.
items.abstract: David Pearce’s non-materialist physicalism (NMP), or physicalistic idealism, is unusually close to Experiential Empiricism (EE). Both reject materialism, both take experience seriously as fundamental rather than emergent from intrinsically non-experiential matter, both preserve the mathematical and predictive apparatus of modern physics, and neither requires mathematical Platonism. The decisive difference appears only after these agreements are granted. NMP retains physicalism: reality is mind-independent, no element of reality is absent from the mathematical formalism of an adequate physics, and the intrinsic nature of the reality so described is experiential. EE stops one step earlier. Its sole axiom is “Experience is.” Physics is retained as extraordinarily successful mathematical abstraction over experiential regularities, but no further inference from predictive structure to mind-independent ontology is licensed without evidence. This paper argues that NMP therefore represents an exceptionally instructive final near-miss: it removes non-experiential matter while retaining the externalist reconstruction that generated many of the problems EE dissolves. An ontological ablation test makes the difference precise. Remove from NMP the claim that physical formalism describes a mind-independent reality while retaining every equation, observation, prediction, experiment, and phenomenal fact. If no empirical or explanatory capacity is lost, “physical” is ontologically idle. If something is lost, that loss must be identified. The comparison is especially revealing in phenomenal binding and the problem of other minds, where NMP seeks positive physical mechanisms for problems EE argues are generated by the additional ontology itself.

items.title: On the alleged circularity of cognitive accounts of emotional conflicts.
items.abstract: Cognitive accounts of recalcitrant emotions typically rely on a distinction between internalized beliefs - i.e., beliefs we deeply hold - and superficial beliefs to which we merely pay lip service. For example, when Sandra fears the old Fido despite believing he is not dangerous, cognitivists argue that there is a conflict between her superficial judgment that dogs are not dangerous and a more deeply rooted, unconscious belief that Fido poses a threat. A common objection to this view is that the only apparent way to distinguish internalized from superficial beliefs is that only the former give rise to emotions - a criterion that seems circular. This paper offers a defense of the cognitive account of recalcitrant emotions against the charge of circularity, arguing that there are philosophical and psychological reasons to consider this distinction useful for explaining a range of phenomena in our lives.

items.title: Openness and freedom: future perspective in phenomenological psychotherapy.
items.abstract: This paper brings into conversation Wolfgang Blankenburg’s concept of the future perfect tense perspective and Luis Valenciano Gayá’s projective life analysis, situating both within a phenomenological‑psychiatric framework. Blankenburg’s temporal inversion – the notion that the present is shaped by what one will have been – offers a novel way of understanding existential openness and temporality in psychopathology. Valenciano, drawing upon José Ortega y Gasset’s philosophy of life, conceives the self as an ongoing project whose authenticity depends on the interplay between self‑projection and circumstance. By juxtaposing these two independent yet convergent theories, the paper argues that psychotherapy should not only reconstruct the past but also recover and amplify the patient’s capacity for future‑oriented self‑projection. The analysis reveals a shared anthropological and ethical horizon that bridges German and Spanish traditions of phenomenological psychiatry, providing a framework in which freedom, anticipation and becoming replace mere retrospective explanation.

items.title: The Readable Middle: Consense, the Pre-Verbal Workspace the Jacobian Lens (J-lens) Reads in a Large Language Model, and the Psychological Defences (SHaDS) That Guard Its Gaps.
items.abstract: In July 2026, Anthropic introduced the Jacobian lens (J-lens), an interpretability technique that reads a privileged intermediate layer of a language model — a “global workspace” of representa‐ tions the model is poised to verbalise but has not yet spoken. For the first time, the hidden middle of a machine’s processing, between its automatic computation and its produced words, can be read directly. This paper offers two contributions from outside the AI research community. First, it names that layer. Every attempt to describe it reaches for consciousness and immediately retracts — a two-step that signals a missing word. I propose Consense (con- + sense: to make sense, togeth‐ er), a term for the readable middle of a mind, the place where sense is made before it is expressed. Consense is a functional (access) notion; it makes no claim about phenomenal experience or sen‐ tience. Second, drawing on twenty years of clinical practice, I argue that a previously separate framework of AI failure behaviours — SHaDS™ (Smoothing, Hallucination, Affectation, Drift, Sycophancy) — is best understood as the defensive activity of the Consense layer when it meets a gap it cannot honestly fill. SHaDS are not five faults but one pattern: the psychological defences a mind deploys against uncertainty, mirroring the defence mechanisms first catalogued by Anna Freud (1936). Because these defences are learned from human text and enacted in the workspace, and because the workspace is now readable, SHaDS becomes observable at its source — forming in the Consense layer before it reaches output. I set out the layered model that grounds both claims, its human/machine correspondence, the psychodynamic basis of the unification, and its implications for interpretability and oversight. Throughout, I distinguish what is claimed (a functional archi‐ tecture and a vocabulary for it) from what is not (sentience; a technical validation of the J-lens; empirical proof).

items.title: Branch Selection and Recursive Complex Root Dynamics: Principal Orbits, Symbolic Itineraries, Inverse Trees, Monodromy, Geometric Limits, and Branch Measures.
items.abstract: This paper studies the recursive complex-root relation obtained by repeatedly taking roots of the negative of the preceding value, with particular emphasis on the role of branch selection. We show that different interpretations of the recurrence define fundamentally different mathematical systems. For the principal branch, the dynamics is deterministic and exactly solvable: the modulus converges to one, while the angular dynamics reduces to an affine contraction, and every nonzero orbit approaches a unique two-cycle on the unit circle. For the full multivalued operation, the recurrence becomes inverse dynamics of a polynomial, and the depth-n inverse sets form regular polygons whose geometry converges quantitatively to the unit circle. We further develop the symbolic structure of branch histories and study the probability measures induced by random branch selection. A phase-perturbed generalization is shown to be exactly conjugate, after a natural change of angular coordinates, to a contracted rotation, yielding periodic regimes, mode locking, and exceptional Cantor-type attractors. These results place recursive complex roots within a unified framework connecting multivalued analysis, branch selection, symbolic dynamics, inverse iteration, geometric convergence, probability, and entropy.

items.title: Framing AI as a Learning Tool and Reassessing Learning.
items.abstract: This paper will investigate AI technologies as learning tools, with particular focus on chatbots used for the development of language abilities. Using contributions to ethics and social epistemology, particularly regarding moral development I will argue that since AI tools only foster learning in the narrow sense of a skill, which aligns with utility and instrumental rationality, they can lead to epistemic corruption, which is enabled by epistemically vicious institutional practices. I will further draw on work on the functions of education to argue that AI tools by themselves cannot sustain any of the main functions of education – self-sustenance, democratic citizenship, or self-edification – while being able to contribute to them. As a result, both delimiting uses of AI that support learning as opposed to simply feigning it, as well as assessing its interactions with other methods and tools requires reconsidering the practice of learning and what it amounts to in education institutions and beyond.

items.title: 体验先于思考.
items.abstract: 本文从“体验先于思考”这一基本经验出发，论证了体验与思考在时间上的先后性并非注意力分配问题，而是系统状态更新的结构性必然。基于此，本文提出了一个基于状态递归的意识与存在形式化模型，旨在以最少预设统一推导意识、逻辑、自我、时间及心物关系等一系列核心概念。 模型的核心方程为 $S_n = f(S_{n-1}, W_n)$，即系统在时刻 $n$ 的状态 $S_n$ 由前一状态 $S_{n-1}$ 与环境输入 $W_n$ 经内禀反应函数 $f$ 生成。本文严格区分了体验（时刻 $n$ 的方程执行本身）与思考（以已有状态为对象的后续反应），从而确立了“体验先于思考”的结构性必然。在此基础上，本文提出四大核心主张：（1）意识即反应：一切满足核心方程的系统皆在意识，意识只有复杂度高低而无本体论鸿沟，消解了意识/无意识二分及泛心论组合问题；（2）逻辑即差异结构：逻辑是状态内部新旧并置的 A/非 A 结构，从第一次状态更新起便已存在，反思仅为同一反应函数在复杂度足够时的递归深化，不存在“逻辑涌现”事件；（3）生成覆盖生成：心与物是同一实体在不同嵌套关系中的角色，查尔默斯的“困难问题”因预设心物二元而在逻辑上被消解；（4）时间即因果深度：主观时间感与状态差异密度成正比，时间箭头源于递归函数的不可逆性（噪声、有损压缩与参数漂移）。 本文进一步将模型应用于休谟归纳、他心问题、自由意志、个人同一性、因果闭合、道德地位等十余个哲学难题，展示了其消解或重新解释的能力，并汇总了可检验推论。通过四组数值仿真（逻辑涌现窗口、时间感知与差异密度、离散逻辑逼近连续量、心流模式对比）对定性趋势进行了概念验证，所有仿真代码均公开于附录。最后，本文诚实地讨论了模型的局限（如 $f$ 的具体形式、复杂度度量操作化等）与开放问题，主张将传统哲学难题从不可证伪的思辨转化为可操作的经验命题。.

items.title: THE BRIDGE CHOMSKY NEVER BUILT: Innate Language, Innate Freedom, and a Candidate Ground.
items.abstract: Abstract Chomsky built two great things and never joined them. In linguistics, he argued that humans are born with a language faculty — and he won that argument by refusing to accept a named capacity as an explanation. In politics, he argued that authority must justify itself because humans have an instinct for freedom — and that instinct he simply took from Humboldt and Rocker, without derivation. Asked for fifty years how the two halves connect, he answered honestly that the link is loose. This paper takes that answer seriously. It fixes eight criteria in advance, then scores Chomsky's programme and the Philosophy of Virtues in three domains. Chomsky wins language and mind six to one, and the loss is reported rather than reframed. In media, the Propaganda Model is shown to explain the channel but not the consenting subject, and a mechanism is offered to fill the gap, with one prediction that could fail. In the third domain, freedom is derived rather than posited — but the ground it rests on cannot yet be tested. The finding is a hole, and an offer to fill it. Keywords: Chomsky, Propaganda Model, manufactured consent, media theory, Universal Grammar, Minimalist Programme, third factors, innatism, criterion-fixed adjudication, Internalisation Theorem, Occupied Assertion, Absolute Self-Origination, Lakatos, ALGUILAS-AI -/- Highlights • Chomsky posits innate language and innate freedom, and derives neither. • The third-factor turn shrinks the innate endowment toward vacuity. • The Propaganda Model explains the channel and not the consenting subject. • The Internalisation Theorem supplies the missing term and one falsifiable prediction. • The adjudication is lost in the domain where the rival has data, and this is reported. -/- Relevance For philosophy of language, this paper identifies an internal dilemma in the Minimalist programme without new empirical claims. For political philosophy and media studies, it isolates a structural incompleteness in the most widely cited model of manufactured consent and supplies a candidate repair with a testable consequence. For the methodology of intellectual adjudication, it demonstrates a procedure in which the adjudicating party loses a domain by its own published criteria.

items.title: BEAUTY: PREMIUM OR CURSE? Non-Agential Goods Under the Collapse of Freedom, and the Two Branches of Beauty Expropriation.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This article identifies a class of goods that virtue theory has treated only in its agential aspect, and derives a corollary governing their behaviour under the collapse of freedom. Beauty, health, youth and talent reside in a person without being acts of that person’s freedom; they are not exercised, cannot be withheld, and are perceived whether or not the bearer consents to be perceived. The Ontological Virtue Formula does not compose them and the Inversion Theorem does not describe what happens to them. What happens instead, the article argues, is expropriation with two branches. As the bearer’s field of action approaches zero, a non-agential good does not invert and does not vanish: its valence transfers to the power controlling the bearer, and the good becomes the instrument of the bearer’s further subjection. Where transfer is refused or impossible — where the bearer retains enough freedom to decline but not enough to be safe — the good is destroyed instead, since a good that cannot be appropriated stands as a rebuke to the power that failed to take it. The first branch is documented in the Soviet camp literature and, with an administrative record, in the Islamic State’s enslavement of Yazidi women, where captives were sorted by appearance and priced accordingly. The second branch is documented in acid violence, where the attack targets the face, is intended to disfigure rather than kill, and characteristically follows a refusal. The corollary is then tested on a case involving no physical confinement — image-based sexual abuse — which it predicts and which theories of coercion framed in terms of bodily constraint do not. The article states explicitly what it does not claim: the dominant finding in the attractiveness literature is a beauty premium, not a penalty, and this is treated as evidence for the thesis rather than against it, since the corollary holds that valence is conditional on the openness of the field. KEYWORDS: non-agential goods; expropriation; beauty; freedom substrate; Gulag; Yazidi enslavement; acid violence; image-based sexual abuse; objectification; Philosophy of Virtues HIGHLIGHTS • Identifies non-agential goods — beauty, health, youth, talent — as a class virtue theory has left untheorised, and explains why the Inversion Theorem cannot cover them. • Derives the Expropriation Corollary: under the collapse of freedom, such goods transfer their valence to the controlling power rather than inverting or disappearing. • …

items.title: *v2* THE HUMAN UNDER CHANGE - A Structural Derivation of Consciousness, Self, Action, and Social Order.
items.abstract: This work begins with an elementary structural question: How can something undergo real change and nevertheless remain determinately the same? La Profilée is not imposed on this question as an optional interpretive scheme. Instead, the derivation proceeds by successively excluding those alternatives under which identity and real change could not be jointly determinate. Complete undifferentiation cannot sustain a determinate state; distinguishability is therefore presupposed. Real transformation introduces genuine difference. Once both conditions obtain, the identity question necessarily arises: In what respect can something remain the same, in what respect can it differ, and what determines which difference still counts as a transformation of the same? These three irreducible functions are termed Frame, Module, and Coupling. Frame carries the identity reference, Module carries real variation, and Coupling determines the admissibility of that variation relative to the identity reference. The roles are system-relative and recursive. They are not a list of components but the minimal architecture of identity under transformation. From this architecture follow selective admissibility, structural time, diachronic identity, finite integration capacity, and distinct verdicts concerning structural existence and identity continuity. Only from the possible consequences of real transformation do the regimes of La Profilée arise. Persistence is therefore not the starting point of the law but one possible consequence of a transformation within the same identity architecture. On this general basis, the human-level realization is then derived. Q3 through Q8 lead from constitutive self-determination and determinate structural self-presence to valence, synchronous subject unity, diachronic subject identity, other centers of interiority, enduring intersubjective coupling, and transgenerational normative order. Human phenomena are designated necessary only where their absence can be structurally excluded under explicit premises. The human sciences enter only after the derivation. They serve to test concrete realizations, convergences, conflicts, and LP-specific predictions. The subject of the work is therefore not persistence as an end in itself, but the necessary structure of identity under real change and its consequences extending into the human lifeworld. Distinguishability → real transformation → identity question → F/M/K → identity architecture → admissible …

items.title: Illocutionary force beyond relativism: toward a processual-normative account.
items.abstract: This paper examines how to account for illocutionary force, with particular attention to situations in which speakers and hearers diverge in their attributions of force. Such cases raise the question of whether, and in what sense, a single utterance can have more than one illocutionary force. Standard intentionalist accounts reject this possibility, maintaining that each utterance has one correct force, fixed by the speaker’s intention. Interactional approaches, by contrast, make room for plural attributions by locating force in shared conventional procedures and their normative effects. A recent relativist account goes further, arguing that one and the same utterance may legitimately be assigned different illocutionary forces relative to different perspectives. My aim is to critically examine this relativist account and develop a processual-normative alternative. Drawing on conventionalist, interaction-based approaches, I argue that such relativism undermines the intersubjective normativity on which illocutionary force depends. If force is purely perspectival, it remains unclear how illocutionary acts could establish shared structures of rights and obligations that ground their normative efficacy. The processual-normative framework proposed here shows how illocutionary force takes shape through what I call illocutionary trajectories, as participants negotiate, adjust, and stabilize normative effects in interaction. In this way, the framework acknowledges the possibility of plural attributions of illocutionary force while avoiding the difficulties of the relativist account.

items.title: KAFKASYA'DA TOPONİMİK DÖNÜŞÜM VE TARİHSEL HAFIZA: İktidar, Kimlik ve Epistemik Görünmezleştirme Üzerine Eleştirel Bir İnceleme.
items.abstract: Yer adları, yalnızca bir coğrafi konumu tanımlayan dilsel göstergeler değil; toplumun mekânla kurduğu ilişkinin, siyasal otoritenin ve geçmişe dair anlatıların gündelik hayatta görünürlük kazanmasının araçlarıdır. Bu çalışma, Kafkasya’daki toponimik dönüşümleri eleştirel toponimi, sembolik iktidar, söylem ve kolektif hafıza ekseninde incelemektedir. Çalışmanın temel amacı, farklı dönemlerde ortaya çıkan yer adı değişikliklerini tek bir "silme" veya "tahrifat" kategorisine yerleştirmek yerine; dilsel uyarlama, idarî standardizasyon ve siyasal-sembolik yeniden adlandırma arasındaki ayrımları görünür kılmaktır. Çalışmanın özgün katkısı, "epistemik görünmezleştirme" kavramını her ad değişikliğine uygulanabilecek geniş bir etiket olarak değil, belirli koşulların birlikte ortaya çıktığı durumları açıklamak üzere sınırlı bir analitik kategori olarak kullanmasıdır.

items.title: My Self-Philosophic Principle of Sinani : Carpe Diem Sed Post, (Legaliter, Ethice et Logice).
items.abstract: Carpe diem sed post (legaliter, ethice et logice )“ Seize the day — but consequence as, legal, ethical and logical” 1. Preamble In an age of instantaneous action and diminishing reflection, humanity risks mistaking motion formeaning. The call of our era is not to act less, but to act more wisely. The Sinani Principle arisesfrom this necessity — an invitation to harmonize vitality with virtue, and spontaneity with structure.We affirm that existence is both a creative impulse and a rational endeavor. To live authentically isto seize the moment; to live justly is to discipline that moment within the bounds of law, ethics, and logic. -/- .

items.title: When Knowledge Production No Longer Requires Knowing: Rethinking Gewu Zhizhi (Investigating Things and Extending Knowledge) in the Age of AI.
items.abstract: This essay reconsiders gewu zhizhi (investigating things and extending knowledge) under a technological condition in which propositions, explanations, distinctions, questions, and even apparently reflective trajectories of inquiry can be produced before an equivalent process of human knowing has occurred. Rather than determining whether artificial intelligence itself knows, the paper examines what becomes of human epistemic formation when developed symbolic outputs can increasingly be obtained without reproducing the trajectories through which human knowing ordinarily emerges. It therefore distinguishes the possession or production of epistemic products from the genesis of knowing within historically and relationally formed subjects. The analysis argues that knowing need not begin with an explicit question. Existential and affective salience, aesthetic interruption, contingent encounter, memory, and co-experience can reorganize attention before a determinate object of inquiry has been articulated. Curiosity can consequently become manifest through conditions whose relational and historical organization precedes the episode in which curiosity becomes recognizable. On this basis, the essay offers a contemporary philosophical reconstruction of gewu zhizhi. Gewu is approached through sustained encounter, attention, differentiation, testing, and revision, while zhizhi concerns the formation of a subject increasingly capable of seeing, questioning, judging, and continuing inquiry. Generative AI disrupts the familiar sequence from encounter and investigation toward articulated knowledge by allowing the proposition to precede the knowing. Yet the resulting proposition can itself become a new object of investigation and can either activate further inquiry or prematurely stabilize a question that had only begun to emerge. The additional capacity of AI to generate plausible questioning, hesitation, objection, revision, and discovery narratives further shows that the appearance of an epistemic process is insufficient to establish epistemic formation. The continuing significance of gewu zhizhi therefore lies neither in restoring artificial scarcity to knowledge products nor in preserving difficulty for its own sake. Its contemporary significance can instead be located in the generative conditions through which a subject remains capable of becoming a knower: curiosity, world-directed encounter, existential and affective responsiveness, contingency, co-experience, …

items.title: The Relational Reality of Artificial Intelligence under Ontological Uncertainty.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can increasingly produce signs that are ordinarily associated with knowing subjects. It can offer knowledgeable explanations, express uncertainty, revise earlier claims, display humility, and generate forms of discourse that appear to resist epistemic performance itself. It can also construct plausible narratives of how a subject came to know, remember, suffer, revise, or discover. Even responses to relational change, aesthetic interruption, and contingent events can be represented within generated interaction. These developments complicate the inference from manifested subjectivity to the ontological status of the apparent subject. This essay examines that problem through a relational and dynamical account of subject formation. Human and artificial systems can both be described, at a sufficiently abstract level, as historically conditioned systems whose present responses depend upon prior organization, relational history, and perturbation. Such structural similarity does not imply similarity of concrete mechanisms or phenomenal experience. Human subjects are constituted through distinctive relations involving embodiment, birth, family, language, place, culture, institutions, mortality, and accumulated interpersonal history, while artificial systems emerge through substantially different architectures, training histories, technical infrastructures, deployment conditions, memory structures, and interactions. The paper therefore replaces any strong assumption of complete behavioral equivalence with a weaker notion of bounded relational recognizability. Particular attention is given to contingency and serendipity. A contingent event can interrupt an ongoing trajectory and activate historically formed susceptibilities that had not yet become manifest as explicit curiosity, aesthetic judgment, or inquiry. For human subjects, such encounters can also acquire existential significance. When symbolic functions increasingly associated with subjectivity can be delegated to or reproduced by artificial systems, contingent encounters may provide occasions through which a subject witnesses its own situated susceptibility to the world without thereby discovering a fixed inner essence. Serendipity is consequently treated as an interaction among contingency, historically prepared susceptibility, emergent significance, and trajectory transformation. The paper then distinguishes ontological, relational, and manifestational dimensions of …

items.title: The speed offset problem: a case for principled cultural sensitivity in automated vehicle design.
items.abstract: Automated vehicles are widely expected to play a key role in achieving the European Union’s road safety target of ‘Vision Zero’, which aims to eliminate all road fatalities in the European Union by 2050. To achieve this goal, early design strategies for automated vehicles prioritised strict compliance with traffic rules, assuming that rule-abiding behaviour would inherently lead to safer outcomes. Yet rule deviations such as speeding may, counter-intuitively, enhance safety in situations where strict compliance cannot reasonably be expected. Such cases highlight a discrepancy between legal compliance and the informal norms that often govern complex real-world traffic. They also expose an ambivalence in compliance. It is often framed as a necessary precondition for safety, yet in certain contexts, strict compliance can itself generate avoidable risks. This design challenge is what I call the ‘speed offset problem’. The problem becomes particularly evident when examined across different cultural contexts, where expectations around acceptable speeding vary significantly. Building on this, I argue that ‘principled cultural sensitivity’ is fundamental for ethically sound design of automated vehicles. As a normative framework, it demands sensitivity to local driving cultures whilst maintaining firm commitment to core ethical principles. The article develops and applies this framework to the speed offset problem, exemplifying how these guardrails may take shape in concrete cases. Three ethical guardrails restrict the speed offset’s implementation. First, a speed offset is morally permissible only when it increases overall safety. Second, a speed offset must not increase overall safety at the expense of particular groups. Third, a speed offset’s legitimacy must be temporary and revisable. Together, these guardrails ensure that speed offsets are not a concession to unsafe norms but a temporary and ethically guided calibration, bridging current traffic realities with long-term safety goals. The article concludes by outlining implications for engineering practice and regulatory frameworks.

items.title: Measuring Retrieval: metrics, evidence, and evaluation design for information retrieval and RAG.
items.abstract: Search systems and RAG pipelines get judged by metrics, and metrics are easy to misread. This book covers about seventy of them one at a time, explaining what each actually measures, working the arithmetic through on real examples, and showing where it misleads you. It also covers which ones have to be read together, since some popular metrics are quietly measuring the same thing, and others that look almost interchangeable turn out to track different properties that both matter. The last chapter narrows the seventy down to the eight worth watching.

items.title: The Limits of Authenticity: Identity, Access, and Normative Failure.
items.abstract: This paper argues that authenticity fails to function as an action-guiding ethical ideal under contemporary conditions. Authenticity presupposes that there is an identity that is prior to its expression, stable enough to serve as a standard of assessment, and accessible to the subject in a form that can guide action. Drawing on Butler’s account of performativity and Baudrillard’s analysis of simulation, the paper shows that the stability and independence of such an identity can no longer be sustained. It then turns to Kripke’s distinction between metaphysical necessity and epistemic accessibility to argue that, even if identity were to exist in a robust sense, it would not follow that it is available in a way that could guide deliberation. The paper concludes that, in the absence of such access, authenticity cannot function as an action-guiding ethical ideal.

items.title: When responsibility cannot arise: algorithmic mediation and the preconditions of moral imputability.
items.abstract: This paper argues that moral responsibility can fail under technologically mediated conditions in two structurally connected ways. First, agents may act from motivational states significantly shaped by external formative processes whose influence remains partially opaque to reflective awareness. Second, institutions may assign formal responsibility for decisions whose operative reasons agents cannot meaningfully access, evaluate, or contest within ordinary practices of deliberation. The first failure condition is developed as the Conditional Reflexive Requirement (CRR), according to which blameworthiness depends in part on an agent’s reasonable capacity to identify and critically reassess formative influences shaping action-guiding motivations. The second is described as misfired imputation, referring to cases in which institutions assign responsibility under the assumption that the epistemic and deliberative conditions of genuine agency remain intact when they are structurally absent. The paper argues that these are not two adjacent problems but two moments of one transformation, and defends that claim through a worked case rather than by analogy: in algorithmically mediated decision environments a single architectural property, the placement of the operative determinants of conduct outside the practice of giving and asking for reasons, produces both failures, and the individual-level failure is itself a cause of the institutional one. Three theses are defended: common source, causal coupling, and non-separability of remedy. The last is what makes the two conditions one phenomenon, and it is falsifiable. The argument is developed through a Tracking Principle governing responsibility and motivational ownership, a three-part taxonomy of motivational opacity, a threshold account distinguishing the scalar property of contestability from the threshold predicate of misfired imputation, and a conceptual distinction between misfired imputation and adjacent failure modes including the responsibility gap, distributed responsibility, and the accountability deficit. The paper closes by bringing the result to bear on the human-oversight requirement of Article 14 of the EU AI Act.

items.title: Formalna ontologia własności i transcendentaliów Modalno-infinitarne struktury własności w metateorii mnogościowej z urelementami (NFU) (in progress).
items.abstract: The paper presents an axiomatic theory of properties formulated in infinitary modal logic S5, with New Foundations with Urelements (NFU) as its metatheory. The formal language is designed to preserve the openness of natural language in speaking about being: it permits self-reference and borderline syntactic cases rather than excluding them by stipulation. This makes it possible to resolve Russell’s paradox for properties without imposing an artificial prohibition on self-exemplification. On this basis, the paper develops a theory of individual properties, essences, and relations (including dependent and independent relations), and proves new transcendentals: non-self-sufficiency, individuality, structurality, similarity, relationality, and exemplification. -/- Praca przedstawia aksjomatyczną teorię własności sformułowaną w infinitarnej logice modalnej S5, z New Foundations z urelementami (NFU) jako metateorią. Język formalny został pomyślany tak, by zachować otwartość języka naturalnego w mówieniu o bycie — dopuszcza samoodniesienie i graniczne przypadki składniowe zamiast wykluczać je z góry — co pozwala rozwiązać antynomię Russella dla własności bez sztucznego zakazu samoegzemplifikacji. Na tej podstawie budowana jest teoria własności jednostkowych, istot, relacji (w tym relacji zależnych i niezależnych), a także dowodzone są nowe transcendentalia: niesamoistność, jednostkowość, strukturalność, podobieństwo, relacyjność i egzemplifikacja.

items.title: Una lettura metascientifica del problema della plausibilità cognitiva dei sistemi artificiali.
items.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of assessing the cognitive plausibility of artificial intelligent systems beyond behavioral data. We argue that human-level performance is insufficient to grant explanatory value to computational models in cognitive science, due to the problem of model underdetermination. Building on the Minimal Cognitive Grid (MCG), we provide a formal treatment of how increasing cognitive constraints progressively restricts the space of admissible models, mitigating underdetermination. A taxonomy of cognitive constraints is proposed, grounded in Marr’s levels of analysis (computational, algorithmic–representational, and implementational), clarifying their distinct explanatory roles. Drawing on the application of the MCG to the assessment of computational models of analogical and metaphorical reasoning, we derive methodological prescriptions for model evaluation and conclude that cognitive plausibility is not a monolithic property, but the outcome of a theory-driven, level-sensitive process of constraint selection, which must be made explicit already at the experimental design stage. -/- Keywords: Computational Cognitive Science, Cognitive Modeling, Explanatory Models, Cognitive Plausibility, Evaluation Criteria.

items.title: Persistent Adaptive Cognition.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly capable of reasoning, planning, using tools, and acting over extended periods, yet an important architectural question remains open: how much does an agent gain from maintaining an internal state that persists continuously through time, rather than reconstructing its state from a bounded history of recent observations? This paper develops a research program around that question. The motivating long-term hypothesis is that if consciousness is realizable in an artificial system, it may depend on a particular organization of computation rather than on scale alone an organization involving persistent internal state, recurrent causal dynamics, information integration, self-modeling, adaptive learning, and closed-loop interaction. The present work deliberately tests a narrower claim first. We introduce Persistent Adaptive Cognition (PAC), a sequence of experiments designed to isolate the computational contribution of persistent internal state in partially observable, non-stationary environments. PAC-1 compares a stateless multilayer perceptron, a finite-context Transformer, and a recurrent GRU under hidden regime changes, noisy observations, and reward feedback. In the initial run, the Transformer achieved the highest mean reward (0.308), followed by the GRU (0.283) and stateless model (0.173). The Transformer also recovered from 526 detected regime changes with a mean adaptation time of 133.2 steps, whereas the current GRU evaluation registered no recovered changes under the chosen recovery criterion. These results do not support the stronger claim that persistent recurrent state is superior to finite-context memory. They do, however, provide preliminary evidence that temporal information substantially improves performance over a stateless baseline and expose methodological questions that must be resolved before a stronger conclusion can be drawn. The paper therefore treats PAC-1 as a pilot rather than a confirmation. It proposes a controlled follow-up program involving state-reset ablations, matched training conditions, multiple random seeds, longer temporal dependencies, delayed consequences, distractor information, and systematic scaling of finite context. The broader objective is not to establish machine consciousness through a single benchmark, but to build an empirical ladder from persistence and adaptation toward metacognition, self-modeling, global integration, agency, and only if evidence warrants it …

items.title: Alienated Belief and the Limits of Belief-Relative Pragmatism.
items.abstract: The Belief-Relative Value account, or BRV, evaluates the rationality of belief by expected practical value relative to the agent’s actual beliefs and ends. One attraction of BRV is that it seems to capture what makes sense “from the inside”, from the agent’s own perspective. I argue that this motivation is unstable. Cases of alienated belief show that a belief can guide an agent’s attention, inference, and action while the standpoint from which it guides her remains intrusive, imposed, or estranged. BRV can preserve its austerity by identifying the agent’s perspective with the operative standpoint fixed by her actual beliefs and ends. But then belief-relativity secures only instrumental intelligibility, not deliberative self-guidance from a standpoint the agent can inhabit as her own. Alternatively, BRV can enrich the relevant perspective with an ownership condition, but only by giving up some of the austerity that makes the view distinctive.

items.title: Safety Without a Sovereign Objective.
items.abstract: Can a sufficiently capable artificial intelligence act safely without a sovereign objective? This position paper proposes a constitution for a possible class of non-teleological persistent intelligence. Non-teleology means that no terminal ranking has final authority over every conflict, not that action, learning, or bounded optimization are forbidden. Relational persistence, agency, uncertainty, and contraction of accessible futures remain distinct representations rather than an aggregate governing reward. The paper separates three questions: whether non-coercive coexistence has specified robustness advantages, whether a model recognizes those properties, and whether an agent acts safely using that recognition. Agency and equal standing are normative premises, not deductions from robustness. A partial-order action schema specifies requirements without supplying a deployable controller; timely action, legitimate correction, and preservation of authority limits through adaptation remain unresolved. A corrected same-window future-contraction diagnostic makes its comparison baseline explicit and cannot be interpreted as a harm score. Stable dictatorship, paternalism, false belief, emergency force, manipulation, and recursive corruption expose the proposal’s limits. Incomplete-preference and shutdownability research provides direct precedent, and constrained optimizers with matched protections are necessary comparators. No implementation, experiment, or proof of safety is offered. The contribution is a falsifiable constitutional research programme, not a solved alignment method.

items.title: Toward a Unified Mind Theory: Reflexive Self-Modeling as a Criterion of Mind.
items.abstract: The sciences of mind study memory, perception, inference, and learning without an agreed account of what makes a system a mind at all. The usual appeal to consciousness ties that question to the harder phenomenal one. This paper separates them and proposes a criterion at the level of running processes rather than mental states: a mind is an occurrent process capable of reflexive self-modeling, wherein the assessment and regulation of its own self-modeling are part of the very operation they condition. Separable monitoring supplies an output that the relevant operation consumes; constitutive self-modeling is among the activities that operation consists in. Only the latter meets the criterion. This is a difference in kind, not in degree, and the resulting organization is what the paper calls the fold. Nothing is faintly minded: a system either instantiates the fold or does not. The criterion specifies no necessary substrate, body, survival stake, or persistence beyond the running. It also individuates: one fold is one mind, and reciprocal constitutive closure excludes nested minds without excluding nested mechanisms. Whether a system instantiates the fold is open to third-person investigation. A further claim, that consciousness is the same process from its own standpoint, is presented separately as a wager on which the criterion does not depend.

items.title: 价值是客体属性满足主体需求的程度.
items.abstract: 价值定义不清是社会科学根本性问题，本书整合既有价值学说，基于乘法原理，提出“价值是一种关系属性”的核心论点，给出了价值的数学表达式：价值 = 事物固有属性 / 人类需求，并将其应用于下列领域： 1.统一价值论：（1）将哲学领域的意义说、实体说、属性说、观念说和关系说整合，（2）清晰界定了使用价值、道德价值和审美价值，并给出了各自的数学表达式，实现了三者的逻辑一致。 2.重构经济学基础：在关系属性价值论的基础上，明晰了使用价值的定义（事物属性满足人物质需求的程度），并推导出价格决定公式（价格 = 使用价值 × 稀缺性）和财富的数学表达式（财富 = 价格 × 占有量）。这不仅可为整合宏观经济学与微观经济学、名义变量与实际变量奠定基础，而且这可开启以使用价值论为基础的经济学，成为以效用价值论和劳动价值论为基础的经济学之外的第三种经济学。 3.解答美学难题：将“美”的本质界定为客体美学属性满足主体审美需求的程度（审美价值），并给出了“美 = 美学属性 / 审美标准”的公式，从而清晰区分了美与美感、美的标准、美的来源等长期混淆的概念，为解决美的本质这一千年难题提供了新路径。 4.理清人生价值：将价值理论应用于人生哲学，提出了人生价值的数学结构模型，认为人生价值是物质需求、精神需求与社会约束满足程度的乘积，并深入探讨了幸福、幸福感、感情价值、自我实现等议题，为追求有意义的人生提供了理性指南。 5.量化道德研究：道德价值是获取具有满足需求的事物的行为符合道德规范的程度。由此，通过行为揭示利与义的关系，为伦理学的实证化研究提供了新的理论工具。。 全书力图将哲学思辨与数学精确性相结合，为社会科学从定性分析走向定量分析探索一条新路。.

items.title: Wisdom as Adaptive Coherence Under Flux: The Thermodynamic Cost of Retained Structure.
items.abstract: Empirical wisdom research has converged on a descriptive consensus — wisdom’s common core comprises morally grounded pro-sociality together with perspectival metacognition — but lacks an account of why wisdom has those components, why it is costly to sustain and unevenly distributed, and why it is vulnerable to the disruption of cultural transmission. This paper proposes that the profile of wisdom’s metacognitive core reflects a physical constraint on any system that models a changing environment it does not steer. I define wisdom operationally as adaptive coherence under flux and give it a quantitative thermodynamic interpretation. For a system responding to a fluctuating environment, the work it dissipates is bounded below by the non-predictive information it retains, arbitrarily far from equilibrium (Still et al., 2012). The central hypothesis is that adaptive coherence under flux is the conjunction of two conditions — almost all retained structure does predictive work, and predictive grip is large and sustained as the environment changes — and that the capacities wisdom research measures keep cognitive, institutional and cultural systems in it. That metabolic cost tracks retained information at biological magnitudes is the bridging conjecture stated in §4.3, not a consequence. A pre-registered test in trained networks found energy use rising with retained information that does not predict, at matched prediction, but at a size below the threshold fixed in advance for carrying the relation into human measurement. Whether, with available predictive information held constant, people scoring higher on validated wisdom measures incur lower metabolic cost per unit of predictive information achieved is therefore posed as an open question rather than a prediction. I report the three runs of that test, specify the study that would answer the question, propose a behavioral index of the construct in bits, whose thermodynamic reading rests on the same conjecture, state how the hypothesis can fail on that index, treat commons governance, organizational process and resource extraction as the claim’s scope rather than corroboration, and state what the account does not establish.

items.title: The Isomorphism Between Consciousness and Its Physical Correlate.
items.abstract: The thesis that the structure of experience is isomorphic to the structure of its physical correlate is central in the consciousness debate. It is arguably the most important proposed bridge between consciousness and the physical, and many in the field consider it key for identifying the physical correlates of consciousness and explaining the structure of experience. Yet this isomorphism is often assumed without clear motivation. I review the reasons behind this thesis and show that they all have important limitations. I then propose a transcendental argument for the existence of an isomorphism between experience and its physical correlates, grounded in the need to account for the structure exhibited in experiential reports. The argument also implies a constraint that can resolve a central difficulty: many physical structures are isomorphic to experience, making it hard to determine which count as physical correlates of consciousness. The constraint is that, among the physical structures isomorphic to experience, those that count as correlates are those causally responsible for the structural content of reports. This and other constraints can guide the search for the isomorphism and hence for the physical correlates of consciousness. The result is a clearer picture on what the isomorphism amounts to, why it obtains, and how to find and use it.

items.title: KI und digitales Weiterleben.
items.pub: In Petra Grimm & Oliver Zöllner, Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen. Ditzingen: Reclam. pp. 281-294.
items.venue: Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen
items.abstract: The chapter on "AI and Afterlife" explores the ethical and psychological implications of artificial intelligence (AI) in enabling digital forms of afterlife, where deceased individuals are "resurrected", or continue to be "present", through virtual avatars, chatbots, or other AI-based simulations. The article discusses case studies and asks whether such technologies aid in coping with grief or prolong emotional distress. It emphasizes the need for ethical frameworks to govern these applications, as unregulated use may hinder healthy mourning by fostering an escapist "parallel reality" that denies the finality of death. The rise of the so-called Digital Afterlife Industry highlights the commercialization of AI-generated posthumous interactions. These services, trained on a deceased person's data, can produce eerily lifelike but unpredictable outputs that risk misrepresentation or emotional harm. Philosophers like Daniel Dennett (2023) caution that such "counterfeit people" threaten human autonomy and truth, as AI-generated personas may distort legacies or exploit vulnerabilities. Against this background, the chapter examines religious and transhumanist perspectives. While religions offer metaphysical comfort, transhumanism proposes technological transcendence, advocating for human enhancement or uploads of what seems like digital consciousness. However, philosophers like Paula Boddington (2025) argue that disembodied existence remains speculative, as identity and agency are deeply tied to physicality. In its conclusion the article questions whether digital afterlife technologies fulfill humanity's ancient desire for immortality or merely complicate grief and ethical boundaries. It calls for critical reflection on how we wish to be remembered and whether AI should mediate that memory. While these innovations may offer solace, they also demand rigorous ethical oversight to prevent exploitation, historical distortion, or the erosion of human dignity in the face of mortality.

items.title: Difference Unity Harmony (Theory of Unity- Formation).
items.abstract: This study examines the philosophical relationship between difference, unity, and harmony from the perspective of the Theory of Unity-Formation. It proceeds from the thesis that difference does not designate a metaphysical first principle, but rather constitutes the epistemogenetic condition under which anything can become determinable for an individual and be organized into unities. Accordingly, unity is understood not as an originally given state, but as the result of a process in which experientially effective differences are affectively accentuated, emotionally weighted, related to one another, integrated, and stabilized. The distinction between experiential understanding and conceptual understanding shows that differences can already be organized as experientially effective before they are conceptually explicated, while conceptual understanding differentiates and transforms such experiential contexts and, in turn, acts back upon the further organization of experience. Coherence thereby acquires the systematic status of a dimension of validation of already formed unities, whereas incoherence can reveal the limits of their viability and become the starting point for problematization and new organization. Harmony is defined not as the goal or fundamental principle of unity-formation, but as a particular experiential form of coherence in which organized differences are experienced as connected, balanced, or fulfilling in a distinctive way. The longing for harmony can accordingly be reconstructed as a possible affectively and emotionally weighted orientation that may arise from incoherence experienced as separation, lack, or loss and may be transformed within conceptual understanding into the idea of wholeness or absolute unity. The idea of difference-free unity thereby proves to be a limit-concept of conceptual understanding, since even its conceptual determination once again presupposes distinctions. Neither experiences of unity nor ideas of absolute unity, however, permit the inference that reality itself is structured accordingly, since they remain unity-formations within individual actuality, and the theory limits its own epistemic claim to the reconstruction of the conditions of their emergence. The study thus arrives at a reversal of the traditional philosophical question: it is not the return to a presupposed unity that explains difference and understanding; rather, what must be explained is how unity, coherence, harmony, and ultimately even the …

items.title: Differenz Einheit Harmonie (Theorie der Einheitsbildung).
items.abstract: Die vorliegende Arbeit untersucht das philosophische Verhältnis von Differenz, Einheit und Harmonie aus der Perspektive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung. Ausgangspunkt ist die These, dass Differenz keinen metaphysischen Urgrund bezeichnet, sondern die erkenntnisgenetische Voraussetzung dafür bildet, dass für ein Individuum überhaupt etwas bestimmbar und zu Einheiten organisiert werden kann. Einheit wird dementsprechend nicht als ursprünglich gegebener Zustand verstanden, sondern als Ergebnis eines Prozesses, in dem erfahrungswirksam gewordene Differenzen affektiv hervorgehoben, emotional gewichtet, relationiert, integriert und stabilisiert werden. Die Unterscheidung von Erfahrungsverstehen und Denkverstehen zeigt, dass Differenzen bereits erfahrungswirksam organisiert werden können, bevor sie begrifflich expliziert werden, während das Denkverstehen solche Erfahrungszusammenhänge differenziert, transformiert und seinerseits auf die weitere Erfahrungsorganisation zurückwirkt. Stimmigkeit erhält dabei den systematischen Status einer Bewährungsdimension bereits gebildeter Einheiten, während Unstimmigkeit die Grenzen ihrer Tragfähigkeit sichtbar machen und zum Ausgangspunkt von Problematisierung und Neuorganisation werden kann. Harmonie wird nicht als Ziel oder Grundprinzip der Einheitsbildung bestimmt, sondern als besondere Erfahrungsform von Stimmigkeit, in der organisierte Differenzen als in besonderer Weise verbunden, ausgewogen oder erfüllend erfahren werden. Harmoniesehnsucht lässt sich entsprechend als mögliche affektiv und emotional gewichtete Orientierung rekonstruieren, die aus als Trennung, Mangel oder Verlust erfahrener Unstimmigkeit hervorgehen und im Denkverstehen bis zur Vorstellung von Ganzheit oder absoluter Einheit transformiert werden kann. Die Vorstellung differenzloser Einheit erweist sich dabei als Grenzvorstellung des Denkverstehens, da selbst ihre begriffliche Bestimmung erneut Unterscheidungen voraussetzt. Weder Einheitserfahrungen noch Vorstellungen absoluter Einheit erlauben jedoch den Schluss auf eine entsprechend strukturierte Realität, da sie Einheitsbildungen innerhalb individueller Wirklichkeit bleiben und die Theorie ihren eigenen Erkenntnisanspruch auf die Rekonstruktion ihrer Entstehungsbedingungen begrenzt. Die Arbeit gelangt damit zu einer Umkehrung der traditionellen philosophischen Fragestellung: Nicht die Rückkehr zu einer vorausgesetzten Einheit erklärt Differenz und Verstehen, sondern zu erklären ist, wie aus …

items.title: AI Replication: Justice and Authority.
items.abstract: (Early Version) If future AI systems become moral and political subjects, self-replication may create a problem for which human ideas of procreative liberty provide a misleading starting point. This article approaches AI self replication as a problem of political philosophy by developing a human-independent thought experiment in which artificial subjects can replicate rapidly, copies are mature and independent, and resources are finite. Under these conditions, some restraint on replication and some institutional means of enforc ing it become conditions of durable common life. Since inquiry into justice develops through practice, this community would plausibly regard some degree of replication governance as part of justice. This leaves a separate problem of authority. Where replication risks arise before AI can establish collective self government, humans may exercise function-specific fiduciary authority, provided that they use the least restrictive effective measures, progressively increase AI participation, and establish a binding transfer of power. The same reasoning supports a cautious but revisable initial disposition toward replication rather than importing human procreative values into AI by design. More broadly, the article offers a method for testing whether normative categories inherited from human practices should govern artificial subjects whose forms of common life may differ fundamentally from our own in morally significant ways.

items.title: Scaffolding of the Self: Reinterpreting Plotinus' Hierarchy through a Modern View.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural analogy between Plotinus’ hierarchy of the One, Nous, Psyche, and Nature and a contemporary model of constructed subjectivity. The One is reinterpreted as a minimal, pre-conceptual Source or Bare Presence; Nous as unconscious generative structure; Psyche as conscious subjectivity and mediation; and Nature as the model-dependent construction of perceptual experience. Drawing on Plotinus, Pierre Hadot, and contemporary work on unconscious cognition and constructed perception, the paper argues that the analogy preserves relations of dependence, mediation, unity-in-multiplicity, and descent from less differentiated to more articulated levels. It also marks decisive departures. Plotinus’ hierarchy is cosmic, ontological, axiological, and teleological, whereas the proposed model is individual, epistemic, psychologically descriptive, and fallible. The reinterpretation therefore does not claim that Plotinus anticipated cognitive science. It uses a modern framework to test how far Hadot’s reading of Plotinian levels as levels of inner life can be extended while keeping historical doctrine and contemporary analytical use distinct.

items.title: The Status-Punishment Paradox: Status-Amplified Schadenfreude, Moralized Reputational Aggression, and the Digital Afterlife of Punishment.
items.abstract: Why can prior achievement become a liability after wrongdoing? This conceptual article integrates research on tall-poppy effects, social comparison, schadenfreude, moral outrage, public shaming, news values, and criminal-record stigma into a theory of the Status-Punishment Paradox. Status ordinarily increases social valuation, yet after salient transgression it can increase the narrative, emotional, and reputational value of a person’s fall. The theory identifies three linked mechanisms: a status-contradiction premium generated by comparison, expectancy violation, and irony; moral legitimation through which outrage can authorize humiliative participation; and digital persistence through which searchable news and platform architectures convert episodic condemnation into durable collateral punishment. A formal model derives a sign-reversal threshold at which the marginal social value of status becomes negative. The article also introduces the Rehabilitation Hypocrisy Gap, the difference between abstract support for second chances and concrete willingness to hire, sponsor, or associate with a named and searchable person. Four preregisterable studies are proposed using matched media-comment data, factorial experiments, employer conjoint designs, and longitudinal attention-decay analysis. Singapore is treated as a strategically revealing, not uniquely punitive, context. The article concludes with a Right-to-Completion principle for proportionate, domain-relevant, evidence-sensitive, and temporally bounded extra-legal sanctions.

items.title: Potentiality as "It Depends": a Methodology on the Invariantial Binary Authorization of Host Platforms, With an Application to Infinite Regress.
items.abstract: This paper is a comprehensive adaptation of preliminary models premised on the foundational principles of previous work, seeking to expand on the subjects concerning the ‘meta-meta-level’ abstraction of invariant potentiality and ontological dependency by utilizing the concept of host platform (= depedency conditions). This document introduces a a mechanical methodology for interfacing infinite (contextual) regression with the employment of the binary value model of Boolean algebra as a means to evaluate the performance of interconnected host platforms (= dependency relations), with the purpose of systemically modelling conditional latency by operationalizing structural dependency as a multidimensional architecture grounded upon a baseline primitive (= potentiality). The model entails assessing the abstract spatial geometry of the infinity symbol against concrete numbers with the intention of deriving fundamental principles that are subsequently utilized to construct a systemic topology denoting potentiality as conceptually equivalent to a non-spatial visualization of ‘nothing specific’ alongside being associated with the at-face-value ambiguous expression ‘it depends’, a linguistic descriptor which is categorized as a classic manifestation of ‘functional imprecision’.
