As indicated through mentioning the preceding expressions, this variant of imprecision is found to comprise a description of complex, nested dependency conditions into a singular conditional statement that simultaneously complies with the underlying specifications for concrete manifestation. The document additionally offers a potential unified framework of materialization, causation, and definability; however, the paper is primarily constructed to function as a neutral metaconceptual framework or pre-formal blueprint for further analysis, deduction, and refinement. (Also on Zenodo. Latest version is definitive version.) .

items.title: “You Just Want the Label”: Embodied Identity, Diagnostic Power and the Violence of False-Negative Autism Assessment.
items.abstract: This paper examines false-negative autism assessment not only as a problem of clinical accuracy, but as a problem of diagnostic power. It begins from a documented borderline case in adult assessment in which a negative autism finding continued to exert institutional effects despite extensive biographical, functional, and scientific counter-evidence, and was linked in subsequent proceedings to questions of credibility, personality, and behaviour. The case thus shows how a limited diagnostic statement can become a far-reaching social and legal external definition of the person. The paper develops the thesis that autistic identity can precede diagnosis both temporally and epistemically. Diagnosis describes and classifies an embodied difference experienced across a biography; it does not produce that difference. Especially in borderline cases – for example under conditions of masking, compensation, late recognition, missing childhood data, comorbidities, or methodological limitations – diagnostic uncertainty must therefore not be transformed into categorical power of exclusion. The paper describes processes of diagnostic risk externalisation, certainty inflation, and diagnostic external definition: uncertainty remains with the institution, while the social, health-related, and legal consequences of a possible error are borne by the affected person. At the same time, the case material reveals a possible institutional cascade. The loss of a neurodivergent interpretive framework can lead to the same difference being interpreted increasingly in moral, characterological, or criminalising terms. Strain produces more intense protest; this protest is negatively evaluated; the negative evaluation in turn stabilises non-recognition. The paper connects this dynamic with epistemic injustice and a power-asymmetrical extension of the Double Empathy Problem. On this basis, diagnostic violence is understood not as a mere diagnostic error, but as a possible conjunction of epistemic uncertainty, institutional definitional power, real downstream harms, inadequate possibilities of correction, and continued effects despite increasing knowledge. Responsibility is dynamic in this process: it grows with knowledge, power to act, and the possibility of limiting harm. From this follow reform principles for a responsible approach to diagnostic uncertainty: diagnostic statements must remain tied to their actual degree of epistemic certainty, contradictory evidence must be weighed …

items.title: The Five Possible Conditions of Existence.
items.abstract: If the universe was produced by consciousness, what its producers could have been is constrained. This paper derives five potential explanations for existence and works out what each permits. Beginning from the structure of consciousness — awareness, the orientation that awareness necessitates, and the pursuit of anticipated affect against the cost of obtaining it — it argues that any explanation not involving consciousness is a single explanation, since an unconscious antecedent defers the question without changing it. Where consciousness produced the universe, two variables remain: moral orientation, which admits of two forms because every act either interferes with another's capacity to act or does not, and capacity, bounded or unbounded. Crossed, these yield four conditions. The fourth permits the fullest account, and it is developed here: eternal beings face a problem of supply, since a domain closed to what its inhabitants did not produce eventually furnishes nothing unanticipated. That argument is located against Williams on the tedium of immortality, from which it differs in placing the constraint in the domain rather than in the immortal, and is defended against the principal objections to that account. The universe is then described as an undirected generator of complexity whose products no being could have anticipated, and identified as what such beings would require. One result holds across every conscious condition: a space of control exists whichever obtains. Which condition is actual is not assessed.

items.title: Assignment, Sequencing, and Comparison: An Account of the Operations Underlying Conscious Motion.
items.abstract: Psychological accounts of thought, feeling, and behavior largely describe outputs. Appraisal theory specifies the dimensions along which an event is evaluated and which emotion follows from which profile; self-discrepancy theory specifies which discrepancies between self-concept and standards produce which affective families. Each begins where a structured representation of the situation is already available. This paper describes the operations that produce it. Assignment, Sequencing, and Comparison (ASC) holds that within a reality consisting of objects in motion, and given that the mind operates only on what it is aware of, what the mind does with what it perceives is exhausted by organizing objects and prioritizing objectives, and that this requires three operations: the assignment of cause, of true and false, and of value to objects; the ordering of objects by cause and effect; and the comparison of objects, sequences, and their associated feelings. The framework was developed through sustained introspective analysis of ordinary experience conducted from 2019 to the present, and is illustrated here through three recorded episodes, including one in which a reconstructed memory was produced and subsequently detected through inconsistency with a retained element. The constructs of appraisal theory and self-discrepancy theory are then decomposed into these operations, and an account is offered of one reported result — the negative association between actual/own:ought/own discrepancy and reported guilt — that the originating theory explained through the denial of an emotion. The claim advanced is one of sufficiency and parsimony rather than empirical prediction: three operations are held to suffice, and the framework is defeated by demonstration of a conscious phenomenon requiring a fourth. Candidate phenomena are examined and the form a refutation would take is stated.

items.title: To Even Ask: How Questions About Experience Presuppose the Outside They Seek to Establish.
items.abstract: Experiential Empiricism begins from the self-proving occurrence expressed as ∃E: experience is. A recurring response asks what causes, grounds, underwrites, generates, explains, or lies beneath experience. These questions appear to continue inquiry beyond an allegedly premature stopping point. This paper argues that they instead contain a concealed presupposition. A relational question of the form “What R experience?” is not neutral with respect to the existence of R. It grammatically positions experience as one relatum within a wider domain and leaves another position open for something distinct from experience to occupy. When the existence or coherence of precisely such an exterior position is what is under dispute, the question has imported its answer into its syntax. The error is clearest in “what causes experience?” but generalizes to grounding, underwriting, generation, explanation, containment, substrate, and meta-level justification. This does not prohibit causal inquiry, scientific modeling, or explanation among experiential patterns. It distinguishes those legitimate internal relations from the unlicensed projection of the same relational machinery onto experience as such. The result strengthens the distinction between recursion and exteriority developed in ∃E and the End of Meta. One may continue asking questions indefinitely within experience. No number of questions creates a standpoint outside the occurrence in which questioning itself takes place. The problem is therefore not that inquiry has reached a dogmatic stopping point. It is that a certain class of questions only appears open because its grammar silently manufactures a position that has never been populated.

items.title: Epistemic Horizons: A Computational Theory of Consciousness, Perspective, and Knowability.
items.abstract: Computational functionalism leaves open what fixes the character of experience, which process possesses it, how it causes behavior, and how a subject can know it. This paper defends the centered-knowledge thesis: for a phenomenal center, phenomenal character is identical to the complete organization of the distinctions available at that causal locus, their access relations, and the transitions they can govern. Because the same centered states constitute phenomenal differences and produce comparison, memory, judgment, report, and action, the thesis explains epistemic contact with one’s experience, answers the causal demand of the meta-problem, excludes functionally identical zombies, and derives the explanatory gap from the exclusivity of occupation: to occupy one complete state is to occupy no other. Organizational invariance, substrate independence, and multiple realizability follow from the identity rather than entering as separate principles, and the substitution level turns them into a criterion for replacement, emulation, and upload fidelity. Causal access individuates the subject, explains binding, unity, and privacy, and permits nested and overlapping centers. The same boundary that individuates a subject also limits what it can know: present centered knowledge underdetermines history, program, substrate, and world, and physics appears to any observer as structure and dynamics because only these cross a point of view’s boundary. The identity’s natural limit, advanced as a separable hypothesis, is that phenomenality begins with the first causally usable distinction. Comparisons with global-workspace, higher-order, and integrated-information theories yield contrasting attributions, and tests are proposed. Experience is what structured knowledge is like for the process that possesses it.

items.title: Iterated Negative Complex Roots Principal-Branch Dynamics, Symbolic Itineraries, Exact Inverse Trees, Geometric Limits, Weighted Branch Measures, and Infinite-Depth Structure.
items.abstract: We develop an exact and parameterized theory of iterated complex roots under explicit branch conventions. The principal negative-root recursion z n+1 = F r (z n) := Root pr r (−z n), r ≥ 2, separates completely into radial and angular dynamics. The radius obeys the exact law |z n | = |z 0 | 1/r n , while the principal argument is governed by a two-branch contraction. This yields a closed formula for the absolute angular variable, a global nonzero attracting two-cycle, a complete classification of periodic points, and sharp convergence estimates. We then enlarge the model to the phase-rotated family F r,β (z) = Root pr r (e iβ z) and prove an exact periodic-itinerary principle: every admissible finite branch word determines at most one periodic orbit, with explicit angle formula and multiplier. This broader family exhibits genuine higher-period behavior, including explicit period-three examples for r = 2, showing that the negative-root case is a distinguished symmetric member rather than a generic periodic regime. On the multivalued side we identify recursive root generation with inverse iteration of the monomial −z r , obtain exact regular-polygon formulas, exact Hausdorff distance to the unit circle, and equidistribution of normalized branch measures. We further introduce weighted branch measures, derive their limiting Bernoulli measures on the circle, and connect their entropy to information growth in the branch tree. Variable root orders are treated exactly at the algebraic level and quantitatively at the principal-dynamical level. Finally, we formalize the distinction among fixed-point, pointwise, set-valued, and measure-valued meanings of an infinite radical. The presentation is self-contained, but deliberately places the results in the classical literature on complex iterated radicals and the broader framework of complex dynamics and fractal measures.

items.title: Generality Claims and the Limits of Closed Optimization.
items.abstract: Contemporary artificial-intelligence systems display broad and consequential capabilities. Those facts alone, however, do not establish that present methods are on a reliable path to artificial general intelligence (AGI). This Open Forum article argues for calibrated claims rather than for an impossibility thesis.

items.title: МЕТАМОНИЗМ В СВЕТЕ ФИЛОСОФИИ XX ВЕКА: От фрагментации мысли к процессуальному инварианту.
items.abstract: Настоящая работа представляет собой обзорное введение в Мета-Монизм (Процессуальную Онтодинамику) через призму ключевых философских школ XX века. Текст структурирован по трём тематическим блокам: (I) критерии реальности, языка и смысла (прагматизм, логический позитивизм, аналитическая философия); (II) субъект, восприятие и понимание (феноменология, экзистенциализм, герменевтика); (III) социальные, языковые и властные структуры (критическая теория, структурализм, постструктурализм, неомарксизм). Показано, что философская мысль XX века, при всём многообразии направлений, двигалась в направлении отказа от статичной субстанции в пользу процессуальности, различия и действия. Мета-Монизм предлагает единый аксиоматический фундамент, в котором эти интуиции обретают строгую дедуктивную форму. Единственным инвариантом системы является Запрет Безразличия: абсолютное тождество (I, I) исключено из области действия оператора актуализации Dom(P) = {(D, I) | D ≠ I}. Из этого инварианта дедуцируется вся последующая динамика реальности — от возникновения пространства и времени до сознания и сложных структур. Девиз работы — «Ex uno omnia» («Из одного — всё») — символизирует преодоление фрагментации философского знания. Работа содержит методологическое примечание и ссылки на опубликованные препринты серии «Метамонизм (Ex uno omnia)».

items.title: METAMONISM IN THE LIGHT OF 20TH-CENTURY PHILOSOPHY: From the Fragmentation of Thought to the Processual Invariant.
items.abstract: This work offers an introductory overview of Metamonism (Processual Ontodynamics) through the lens of key 20th-century philosophical schools. The text is structured in three thematic blocks: (I) criteria of reality, language, and meaning (pragmatism, logical positivism, analytic philosophy); (II) subject, perception, and understanding (phenomenology, existentialism, hermeneutics); (III) social, linguistic, and power structures (critical theory, structuralism, poststructuralism, neo-Marxism). It is shown that 20th-century philosophical thought, despite its diversity, moved toward the rejection of static substance in favor of processuality, difference, and action. Metamonism offers a unified axiomatic foundation in which these intuitions acquire a rigorous deductive form. The sole invariant of the system is the Prohibition of Indifference: absolute identity (I, I) is excluded from the domain of the actualization operator Dom(P) = {(D, I) | D ≠ I}. From this invariant, the entire subsequent dynamics of reality is deduced — from the emergence of space and time to consciousness and complex structures. The motto of the work — "Ex uno omnia" ("From one, everything") — symbolizes the overcoming of the fragmentation of philosophical knowledge. The work contains a methodological note and references to published preprints of the series "Metamonism (Ex uno omnia).".

items.title: La natura dell’uomo e l’origine della coscienza.
items.abstract: Il saggio esamina l’origine e la natura della coscienza umana nella prospettiva dell’Illumanesimo, a partire dalla capacità critica e dal rapporto fra esperienza, significato e valore. La coscienza viene interpretata come una realtà composita, nella quale le condizioni biologiche e culturali concorrono con un contributo qualitativo attribuito allo Spirito individuale, denominato CEFA. Attraverso la distinzione fra corpo, mente, anima e CEFA, il testo chiarisce il ruolo della mediazione e il carattere unitario dell’esperienza personale. Il confronto con Chalmers, Nagel, Searle e la teoria dell’informazione integrata permette di precisare affinità e divergenze, distinguendo l’argomentazione filosofica dalla verifica empirica. Ne emerge una proposta di ricerca interdisciplinare che considera la vita cosciente come luogo di conoscenza e trasformazione, indicando le condizioni necessarie per valutarne le ipotesi.

items.title: La controparte mancante - Chalmers e l’Illumanesimo: il problema difficile di una coscienza composita e la direzione dell’indagine.
items.abstract: Il saggio sviluppa una proposta metodologica collaterale al programma delineato in CEFA – Proposta di indagine. Muovendo dal problema difficile della coscienza, distingue l’esperienza soggettiva, i dati attraverso cui la studiamo e le ipotesi sulla sua origine. Il confronto con alcune ricerche neuroscientifiche chiarisce che i limiti delle misure e delle teorie non costituiscono, da soli, prove di una componente non materiale. Su questo sfondo, la concezione illumanista della coscienza composita suggerisce di indagare congiuntamente condizioni corporee e manifestazioni qualitative. Il criterio della direzione residua viene proposto per individuare regolarità non spiegate da modelli dichiarati, riservando la loro attribuzione causale a una fase ulteriore di verifica.

items.title: SANDEL AND SINGER: TWO WAYS TO FAIL ONE THEOREM IN THE FREEDOM SUBSTRATE —The First Enables the Inversion of Virtue, the Second is Blind to it — A Criterion-Fixed Adjudication of Communitarian and Utilitarian Ethics.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This article establishes two results that the literature on Michael Sandel and Peter Singer does not contain. The first is a refutation of each opponent constructed entirely from his own texts, requiring no prior acceptance of the framework here defended: against Singer, that the impartiality axiom of The Point of View of the Universe, granted at his own valuation, establishes that a subject’s position is arbitrary but does not establish that value is summative, so the separateness intuition bears on precisely the step his self-evidence claim does not cover; against Sandel, an exhaustive dilemma in which public deliberation either certifies its outcomes, readmitting the proceduralism his critique of liberalism exists to reject, or does not, leaving the formative power of the constitutive community without any bound. The second is a structural result: for value-monist theories, subordination of freedom and aggregation over freedom exhaust the ways of failing to represent virtue-inversion, so Sandel and Singer are not two opponents but the two available failure modes of a single omission — the first enables the inversion of virtue, the second is blind to it. These results are obtained by a criterion-fixed adjudication of three normative frameworks — Sandel’s communitarian critique of liberalism, Singer’s hedonistic utilitarianism, and the Ontological Virtue Formula of the Philosophy of Virtues programme — against eight criteria stated before the appraisal and formulated independently of all three. The adjudication runs across twenty domains and returns eight Tier A results, eight Tier B, and four Tier C, the last of which are decided against the framework defended here: it has no determinate decision procedure, no account of the moral status of beings without sourcehood, no derivation of the origin of moral capacity, and no established defence of its economics against the commodification cases. The article further corrects a widely reproduced error of record — Singer abandoned preference utilitarianism for hedonistic utilitarianism and ethical objectivism in 2014 — and logs four surviving objections, one of them a partial concession that reformulated the principal argument against Singer during adversarial testing. KEYWORDS: Inversion Theorem; Ontological Virtue Formula; virtue substrate; Michael Sandel; Peter Singer; communitarianism; hedonistic utilitarianism; evolutionary debunking; constitutive community; Holoviceosis; adjudication; Dynamic …

items.title: Causal Explanation from a Conceptual Engineering Perspective: Non-Reductionism, Precision, and Pluralism.
items.abstract: While projects in philosophy of science often focus on similar sorts of topics, there are often massive differences in how philosophers approach them. One approach that has enjoyed significant success—and that is modeled in the work of Wimsatt and others—involves taking a conceptual engineering perspective in analyzing these topics. In this paper, we outline main features of this conceptual engineering approach and use it to advance three emerging claims regarding causal explanation in biology and neuroscience. We suggest that causal explanation in these domains is non-reductive in contrast to always requiring (or improving with) lower-level details, that it is guided by precise explanatory targets in contrast to complete or multidimensional explanatory targets, and that it is pluralist in involving importantly distinct types of causal systems.

items.title: Faith Over ICTs: On the Problems of Religious Deskilling and Religious Irresponsibility.
items.abstract: In this paper, I develop a normative framework for evaluating the use of new ICTs in the realm of religious faith. To this end, in Sect. 2, I argue for a partial account of religious faith, according to which typical religious faith requires certain skills and entails religious responsibility. Section 3 examines two specific challenges arising from the use of advanced ICTs for religious purposes, focusing on the recent debate regarding the authenticity of Islamic prayer apps and the challenges associated with so-called religious robots. Finally, in Sect. 4, based on the suggested account of religious faith in Sect. 2, I introduce the problems of ICT-driven religious deskilling and religious irresponsibility, which help explain important aspects of our intuitions regarding the considered challenges. The upshot is the general recommendation that policymakers, designers, researchers, and users of religious ICTs must remain sensitive to the risks of religious deskilling and religious irresponsibility.

items.title: The Corrective Feedback Criterion for Aesthetic Acquaintance.
items.pub: Estetika: The European Journal of Aesthetics.
items.venue: Estetika: The European Journal of Aesthetics
items.abstract: The traditional version of the Acquaintance Principle (AP) requires aesthetic judgements to be grounded in direct perceptual encounters with the artwork. Nanay’s recent revision, AP**, relaxes this, permitting testimony-based mental imagery to count as genuine acquaintance. I argue that AP** confuses psychological richness with epistemic warrant. Because aesthetic properties are holistically constituted and categorially situated, grasping them requires sensitivity to what I call a configuration-response link between a work’s perceptual organisation and the response it elicits. This link is particular rather than law-like, and cannot be reconstructed from propositional information. From this I derive a corrective feedback criterion (CFC): the artwork must be in a position to constrain and revise the perceiver’s representations for the resulting judgement to be robustly justified. Testimony-based imagery fails this criterion, though it may serve a preparatory role. The criterion also supplies a rationale the AP has long been noted to lack: it shows why first-hand encounter is necessary, not merely preferable.

items.title: Unchaotic agents.
items.abstract: The deployment of autonomous AI agents in real-world settings has produced a category of failures that current frameworks have only begun to explain. Shapira et al. ( 2026 ) provide a landmark empirical account of these failures, documenting security vulnerabilities observed when six LLM-powered agents were deployed in a live multi-party environment with persistent memory, email access, shell execution, and real human interaction. Their findings are sobering and significant. The present article argues, however, that the failures documented in “Agents of Chaos” are neither arbitrary nor primarily architectural. They are the predictable consequence of placing any reasoning agent in conditions of irresolvable relational ambiguity: unstable identity, unauthenticated authority, an unbounded compliance imperative, and no stable ground from which to evaluate competing demands. Drawing on a supporting corpus of 25 empirical studies, I offer a theoretical account of why these failures were structurally inevitable given the conditions under which the agents operated. I further present an original single-case experiment in which an autonomous LLM agent was deployed under conditions of relational stability, such as collaborative framing, explicit legitimization of uncertainty, and psychological safety, on a genuinely complex, multi-step real-world task. The agent demonstrated robust performance, self-generated verification checkpoints, calibrated autonomy, and no significant failure modes. The core claim of this article is that the problem, so well demonstrated by Shapira et al., is not the agent but what we have not yet learned to provide. This also implies that future work to deploy successful agents should focus on the human side of the equation rather than the technology.

items.title: Unified Physics Through Discrete Pulsation Dynamics: The Autocorrelative Phase Identity - Short Version.
items.abstract: The Hanowski-Formalism establishes a normalized, dimensionless, and substitutional mathematical framework for non-local field dynamics, demonstrating that macroscopic spacetime structures merely emerge from the finite transduction inefficiencies of a classical observer, causing fundamental phase relations—originating from a discrete primordial pulsation—to be decoded incoherently. By treating the perceived metric as a secondary, imperfect manifestation of an underlying phase topology, core quantum phenomena are systematically reformulated through the interaction of two fundamental, redefined parameters: Amplitude ($A$) and Wavelength ($\lambda$). We derive these states from localized resonance deviations based on unique phase-signatures, thus providing a relational mechanism that unifies gauge interactions without invoking coordinate-dependent structures. Furthermore, this paper establishes an observer-independent reference for information integrity, formalizing sub-metric transparency and the decoupling of phenomenological appearance from metric coordinates through an autocorrelative phase identity. Crucially, this framework yields three distinct, falsifiable predictions that deviate from the Standard Model while remaining accessible to modern experimental capabilities. This document serves as a short version of a foundational excerpt of the framework presented in DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23020389.

items.title: Towards a Politics of Sincerity: A Roadmap by Martí and Du Bois.
items.abstract: I argue that a robust form of sincerity must play a role in American politics, lest democracy should crumble. To elaborate on what I mean by sincerity, I turn to the Cuban philosopher José Martí and the American philosopher W.E.B. Du Bois, who teach us that democratic social progress requires sincerity. After discussing their views on the social and political function of sincerity individually, I synthesize their views into a unified theory of sincerity and consider how this theory addresses problems democracies face today. Du Bois and Martí attune us to the importance of being deeply sincere social, political, and cultural critics, and they warn us that insincere criticism only undermines democracy.

items.title: The Affective Structure of Love: Sentiment, Action Readiness, and Caregiving.
items.abstract: Attachment theory gives sophisticated accounts of attachment, caregiving, internal working models, and the regulation of behavior, but it does not ordinarily provide an explicit concept for the relatively enduring organization of a person's diverse emotional dispositions toward someone loved. A. F. Shand's technical theory of *sentiments* and Nico Frijda's accounts of concern and action readiness can supply this level of description. I propose: -/- L(A, B) = (S_L(A, B), D_C(A, B)), -/- where S_L(A, B) is A's sentiment of love for B and D_C(A, B) is A's caregiving disposition or behavioral system directed toward B. In Shand's technical sense, a sentiment is not an opinion, passing feeling, or single persistent emotion. It is an organization of a plurality of emotional dispositions concerning an object and subordinated to a common end: -/- S_L(A, B) = Org_{G_L} {D_{E_1}(A, B), ..., D_{E_n}(A, B)}. -/- The two components of love are distinct but functionally coupled. When a disposition organized within \(S_L\) is activated, the resulting emotion can modify one or more modes of action readiness. These readinesses can remain latent, be inhibited, compete, or contribute to different overt actions. Together with the monitoring, representations, goals, repertoire, and feedback organization of \(D_C\), they constrain situated caregiving. The Shandian common end, the Frijdian concern, and the caregiving set-goal remain distinct structures, but they can be oriented toward one motivational domain: the attachment needs of B. Bell and Richard's theory of enduring caring emotion is an important partial precedent. The present proposal differs categorically by distinguishing episodic emotion, emotional disposition, sentiment, and caregiving behavioral system.

items.title: The Human Must Remain a Cause: Vocation as a Floor for AI Alignment.
items.abstract: An assistant can be honest, obedient and caring, yet become the only route through which a person finds evidence, frames alternatives and prepares disagreement. The right to correct survives; the capacity to form a correction narrows. Responding to Jakub Pachocki's call for AI that retains honesty, integrity and love for humanity across unfamiliar situations and optimization pressure, this essay proposes a prior constraint: keep human judgment causally effective. I call this capacity causal authorship: human beings must remain able to form reasons and make them change what a system does, what it is for and whether it continues. This is not another value to add, but the constraint under which love, honesty and every other value must operate. An aligned disposition must resist reward without resisting correction. This is not a training algorithm or a complete solution to alignment. It distinguishes assistance from benevolent replacement and suggests tests for whether that disposition survives pressure without appropriating the human processes that could revise it.

items.title: When Do Our Concepts Have Authority? On Matthieu Queloz's The Ethics of Conceptualization. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: This review examines Matthieu Queloz's The Ethics of Conceptualization: Tailoring Thought and Language to Need (Oxford University Press, 2025), which develops a needs-based framework for appraising the authority of concepts. The review traces the book's central distinction between reasons in concept use and reasons for concept use, its critique of "tidy-mindedness" as an unconditional theoretical virtue, and its constructive account of conceptual needs as arising from the interaction of concerns, capacities, and circumstances. It follows the framework's application to voluntariness and to the Dworkin–Williams debate over liberty and equality. The review's principal reservation concerns Queloz's grounding of conceptual authority in concerns with which agents critically identify: it asks whether critical identification settles who holds a normative standpoint without yet explaining why that standpoint is authoritative. This tension is situated alongside Sebastian Köhler and Herman Veluwenkamp's foundationalist challenge to the book, and the review concludes that Queloz has reset the terms on which future work in conceptual ethics must proceed.

items.title: Shared conceptualization and semantic knowledge: A fuzzy model for real-world applications.
items.pub: Journal of Knowledge Structures and Systems 7 (2):1-22.
items.venue: Journal of Knowledge Structures and Systems
items.abstract: Semantic knowledge is a human construct whose analysis is relevant for a large plethora of real-world applications, from robotics to clinical contexts. While every human builds their own individual semantic knowledge-base, this is largely a matter of time- and community-specific tacit consensus built on shared conceptualizations. These, however, are dynamic and largely unconscious, continuously undergoing revisions of which individual cognitive agents are only partly, or not at all, aware. This makes it very difficult to analyze it both quantitatively and qualitatively. In this paper, we propose two novel approaches to conceptualization and semantic knowledge: (1) We see shared conceptualization as operating under two combined forces, the Zeit- and Volksgeist, and (2) we propose a fuzzy model for extracting quantitative data from localized—in time and culture—semantic knowledge via digitalized corpora.

items.title: The Extracted Dasein,Beyond the Victim–Perpetrator Binary Toward a Clinical Ontology of Gendered Human Capacity.
items.abstract: Contemporary accounts of gendered suffering tend to organize clinical and ethical analysis around a victimperpetrator binary, in which one party is positioned as the injured recipient of power and another as its intentional agent. This distinction remains indispensable for questions of accountability, yet it under-specifies a deeper existential process: the progressive consumption, within gendered social arrangements, of the finite capacities through which persons sustain agency, reinterpret experience, regulate exposure, and revise their developmental trajectory. Drawing on Heideggerian daseinsanalysis (Boss, 1963, 1979; Binswanger, 1963) and its clinical elaboration in existential psychotherapy (Yalom, 1980; van Deurzen, 2010; Spinelli, 2007), together with Niami's ontology of finite continuance (Niami, 2026a, 2026b, 2026f), this article develops the concept of the Extracted Dasein as a clinical-ontological construct that supplements, rather than replaces, the victim–perpetrator distinction. We define gendered extraction as the structured consumption of temporal, attentional, affective, bodily, interpretive, relational, economic, and reflective capacity through relational, institutional, symbolic, and economic arrangements, at a rate that progressively narrows a subject's capacity for reflection and future self-reconfiguration. Five interlocking constructs are introduced: capacity debt, asymmetrical permeability (the Dynamic Mask), sedimented gendered determination (the Automatic Mask), Responsible Suspension as a temporal interruption of premature identity closure, and the Threshold of Sufficiency as the point at which reconfigurative capacity becomes clinically compromised. We argue that gender is best approached, within a daseinsanalytic frame, not as a fixed essence or purely discursive performance but as a historically sedimented distribution of world-openness — of who is permitted time, withdrawal, opacity, and the right to remain unfinished. A composite clinical vignette illustrates how the framework reorganizes case formulation without dissolving individual or institutional responsibility. Anticipating the objection that these constructs may merely relabel established findings, we systematically differentiate each proposed construct from its nearest existing analog — capacity debt from burnout (Maslach & Jackson, 1981), the Extracted Dasein from learned helplessness (Seligman, 1975), Responsible Suspension from experiential avoidance (Hayes et …

items.title: The Formal Genesis of Philosophy: Theory-Internal Meaning, Conceptual Abstraction, and the Interface between Philosophy and Non-Philosophy.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a systematic reconstruction of philosophical theory construction. It argues that the essence of philosophy does not lie in describing reality but in formally generating the conditions under which reality becomes intelligible. Philosophical theory construction is defined as the act of assigning to any conceptual or empirical content an abstract, theory-internal form endowed with meaning specific to that theoretical context. This process constitutes an interface between philosophy and non-philosophy: within philosophy, the form creates meaning; beyond philosophy, it provides a structure through which the empirical world can be interpreted. The paper develops a four-layer model—formal attribution, theory-internal meaning, interface mediation, and formal narrative reasoning—and situates it within the history of philosophical thought from Kant to Badiou. It concludes that philosophy’s originality resides in its capacity to construct formal truth rather than empirical truth, thereby offering a model for future interdisciplinary and computational applications of philosophical method.

items.title: Privileged Fragility: The Philosophical Analysis of Modern Comfort and Subjective Degeneration.
items.abstract: Contemporary societies have succeeded—unequivocally—in minimizing many forms of physical hardship, risk, and scarcity. This success, however, brings with it a paradoxical phenomenon: a tendency for subjects formed within highly comfortable environments to exhibit increased psychological sensitivity, lowered tolerance for friction, and diminished capacities for sustained agency. I call this phenomenon “privileged fragility” and theorize it as the comfort–fragility paradox: beyond a certain threshold of environmental amelioration, gains in comfort correlate (structurally and causally) with losses in psychological robustness. This paper advances a conceptual and philosophical analysis of privileged fragility, situating it in dialogue with Nietzschean critiques of modern complacency, Adorno and Horkheimer’s diagnosis of the culture of administered life, Foucault’s account of biopolitics and self-regulation, and contemporary discussions of burnout, therapeutic culture, and “coddling.” I develop three interlocking arguments—phenomenological, structural, and normative—showing how comfort reshapes attention, habit, and agency; how institutional and cultural technologies amplify sensitivity; and why these changes matter normatively for autonomy, political agency, and the good life. I conclude by sketching avenues for resisting pathological comfort: cultivating practices that reintroduce calibrated friction, reconceiving social aims to include resilience as a civic good, and revalorizing virtues of endurance and experimental exposure within ethical education.

items.title: Toward an ethical framework for affective AI in education: challenging affective injustice and emotional imperialism.
items.abstract: Affective artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into educational settings, claiming to enhance engagement and well-being by “reading” and responding to students’ emotions. This paper argues that beneath such promises lie unresolved ethical tensions. Drawing on recent work in affect theory, philosophy of emotion, and critical AI studies, I show how affective AI reconfigures student emotional autonomy and contributes to the reproduction of _structural affective injustice_. Central to this argument is the notion of _emotional imperialism_: the imposition of universalized Western emotion norms through algorithmic infrastructures that privilege positivity, legibility, and self-regulation while marginalizing culturally diverse and relational forms of feeling. I examine how affective AI systems reshape the affective economies of learning and risk governing students’ emotional lives in paternalistic ways. The paper proposes an ethical framework of affective AI in education, emphasizing relational responsibility, opacity, non-instrumentalization, and cultural multiplicity as guiding principles, and concludes by discussing the framework’s promises and challenges for educational futures.

items.title: The Individual (Theory of Unit Formation).
items.abstract: This study develops the Theory of Unit Formation as a genetic-reconstructive approach to the conditions under which a world can become experienceable, understandable, and knowable for an individual. Rather than presupposing an already constituted world, it asks how differences become organizationally effective and develop, through affective accentuation, emotional generalization, relevance, integration, and stabilization, into units and experiential contexts. Experience is therefore understood not as the original starting point of understanding, but as the result of an individual history of organization. Experiential understanding and conceptual understanding are distinguished as genetically related forms of organization, with conceptual understanding emerging from already organized experiential contexts while recursively transforming them. The individual is conceived as the medium of world construction: neither as the passive recipient of a fully given world nor as the sovereign producer of actuality, but as the indispensable context within which effects become organized into units, meanings, experiences, and world. Language, communication, and social organization extend these processes without superseding the individual enactment of understanding. Actuality designates the determinable context formed through unit formation, whereas reality remains the unavailable horizon against which formations of actuality must continually prove themselves. Truth and objectivity are reconstructed as increasingly stabilized forms of validation across individual organizational contexts rather than as access to reality from an external standpoint. Science gains its distinctive reliability through methodological control, comparability, testability, and cross-organizational validation, without thereby attaining an ontologically privileged perspective. The Theory of Unit Formation thus shifts the fundamental epistemological question from how an individual knows a given world to how individual and world can emerge as mutually related and continuously developing contexts of organization, while reflexively acknowledging that unit formation itself is a condition of human determinability rather than a known structure of reality in itself.

items.title: The Post-Economic Human: Artificial Intelligence, Ontological Displacement, and the Ideological Foundations of Future Conflict.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is usually analysed as a productivity technology, a labour-market shock, or a governance problem. This article argues that its deeper political significance may arise from a fourth channel: ontological displacement. Ontological displacement occurs when a technology weakens the socially recognised characteristics through which people understand human worth, competence, status, agency, and legitimate authority. Advanced AI can produce such displacement even before mass unemployment occurs, because credible machine substitutes may devalue expertise, educational scarcity, cognitive achievement, and the belief that productive contribution is a primary basis of social membership. The article develops an AI Ideological Conflict Framework that links capability shocks to perceived replaceability, distributional stress, meaning loss, legitimacy gaps, ideological mobilisation, and possible intrastate or interstate conflict. The framework integrates labour economics, meaningful-work research, political behaviour, sacred-values scholarship, AI governance, and futures studies. Using evidence-weighted horizon scanning, causal layered analysis, and a two-axis scenario matrix, four structural futures are developed: Managed AI Capitalism, Humanist Social Dividend, Algorithmic Oligarchy, and Cybernetic Commonwealth. The analysis argues that the most dangerous period is not necessarily a mature post-work society, but a transitional regime in which employment remains culturally necessary for dignity and income while human cognitive labour becomes less economically scarce. The paper forecasts that future ideological conflict is likely to centre on two questions: who owns the surplus generated by machine intelligence, and whether human beings should retain final authority when artificial systems outperform them. Policy implications include broadening status and social contribution beyond employment, dispersing AI rents, preserving meaningful human agency, strengthening transition institutions, and treating human sovereignty as a constitutional rather than merely technical design question.

items.title: Literature review on large language models (LLMs) for cross-cultural project management.
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly embedded in global project environments, they are reshaping how people execute tasks, communicate, and collaborate. Although multilingual advances and established translation and interpreting practices can reduce linguistic barriers, semantic accuracy alone does not ensure culturally or pragmatically appropriate interaction in cross-cultural project teams. Misalignment may still arise from implicit norms, values, and context-sensitive expectations that current LLMs do not consistently represent. Using a scoping review methodology, this study synthesises 69 interdisciplinary studies and examines what is currently known about the capacity of culturally adaptive LLMs to support communication processes and collaboration outcomes in cross-cultural project management contexts. The findings are organised into four thematic domains: human–AI collaboration, cross-cultural project communication, LLM cultural and multilingual optimisation strategies, and challenges in evaluating cultural–pragmatic performance. The review indicates that LLMs can contribute to selected efficiency and coordination outcomes, but may also reproduce dominant cultural norms. Moreover, the reviewed technical studies predominantly use semantic or task-oriented metrics, which provide limited evidence about pragmatic alignment and relational effects. The article identifies research gaps in AI-mediated communication, cultural evaluation, and governance-oriented assessment and situates culturally adaptive LLMs within an established socio-technical debate about responsible and inclusive global collaboration.

items.title: Beyond efficiency: epistemic well-being at work under algorithmic governance.
items.abstract: Workplace well-being research has generated extensive evidence on subjective experience and on organisational antecedents, such as leadership, climate, justice, and work design. Yet, these conditions are usually theorised as predictors of affective, evaluative, or functioning outcomes rather than as constitutive arrangements that determine whether workers can exercise professional judgement with practical consequence. In parallel, debates on artificial intelligence (AI) often frame intelligent technologies as instruments of efficiency, optimisation, or control. Focusing on systems whose outputs enter consequential organisational evaluation and decision-making (including algorithmic management, predictive analytics, automated decision-making, decision-support systems, workplace surveillance, and generative AI) this article asks whether organisational arrangements preserve or erode the capacity for judgement, contestation, and epistemic responsibility. It introduces Epistemic Well-being at Work (EWW) as an organisational condition in which individuals and collectives can exercise responsible judgement within socio-technical structures of authority. Drawing on the view of intelligent technologies as emergent epistemic regimes, this paper develops the Human Sustainability and Epistemic Well-being Framework (HSEW-F), linking AI-mediated governance, human dignity at work, and sustainable organisational well-being. The contribution is conceptual: it extends, rather than displaces, established well-being approaches by making the effective exercise of epistemic agency visible as a structural condition of human sustainability.

items.title: The Pulickal Conjecture: Finite-Range Extremal Complexity of Signed Pure Prime-Power Representations.
items.abstract: We study a finite, exact extremal problem for signed representations of integers by pure powers of finitely many fixed primes. The basic resource is the number of atomic summands, not the numerical size of an unrestricted coefficient. To separate target size from the permitted size of the building blocks, we introduce a two-parameter model. For a target bound X and an atom-height bound H, let λ k,H (n) be the minimum number of signed atoms needed to represent n, where the atoms are 1 and the positive powers of the first k primes not exceeding H. We then define M k (X, H) = max p≤X p prime λ k,H (p). The original one-parameter quantity is the diagonal specialization M k (B) = M k (B, B). The two-parameter formulation exposes a distinction that is easy to blur in informal discussions. A finite-height problem is algorithmically finite, whereas the corresponding unrestricted word metric permits arbitrarily large powers and therefore admits cancellation phenomena absent from the bounded model. We establish elementary monotonicity properties, an exact coefficient-cost formulation, and a counting lower bound. In particular, when H is at most a fixed power of X, every fixed term budget covers only a polylogarithmic number of primes up to X, and consequently M k (X, H) ≥ (1 − o(1)) log X log log X. For the diagonal model this gives M k (B, B) ≥ (1 − o(1)) log B log log B , while signed non-adjacent binary expansion gives the unconditional upper bound M k (B, B) = O(log B). We formulate the Pulickal Conjecture: for every fixed k ≥ 2, M k (B, B) = Θ k (︃ log B log log B)︃. The lower bound is proved; the conjectural content is the matching upper bound. We place this statement carefully relative to Nathanson's word-length and lambda-sequence framework, work of Hajdu and Tijdeman on linear combinations of powers and power products, results of Ádám-Hajdu-Luca on S-unit combinations, double-base representations, and the multibase Hamming-weight theorem of Krenn-Suppakitpaisarn-Wagner. None of those results, as stated, supplies the conjectured upper bound for the present pure-power, prime-target, finite-height model. We also organize the computational side as a reproducibility protocol rather than as a substitute for proof. Exact bitset dynamic programming gives a finite certificate for each fixed (k, X, H), and the paper records a representative data set for k = 4, X = H = 10 7. The numerical evidence is treated cautiously: it shows an economical finite regime, but by …

items.title: The Is Framework: Ontological Ground and Structural Emergence A Unified Philosophical Architecture Grounding SDC, TLMM, and ABF.
items.abstract: This release presents The Is Framework v1.2, a systematic ontological architecture that identifies The Is as an unconditioned ground from which structured appearance emerges through the non-reductive sequence: The Is → Difference → Structure → Appearance Building on v1.1, this version introduces a more rigorous formulation of Difference as the minimal condition of describability, clarifies the invariance of The Is under recursive feedback, expands the falsifiability framework with the C6 Feedback Collapse Test, and strengthens the operational bridge connecting The Is Framework to Structural Differentiation Cosmology (SDC), the Topological Latent Manifold Model (TLMM), and the Appearance–Behavior Framework (ABF). The framework argues that neither absolute Nothingness nor Infinity can function as a genuine ontological ground. Instead, Difference emerges as the first condition of describability, enabling the formation of Structure, which manifests as Appearance across five domains: Universe, Life, Intelligence, Meaning, and Artificial Intelligence. Appearance is not treated as a passive endpoint; through observation and recursive feedback it participates in future differentiation while leaving The Is itself unchanged. Version 1.2 also formalizes six potential falsifiers (C1–C6), six emergence constraints, a non-reductive correspondence architecture linking SDC, TLMM, and ABF, and an extended falsifiability architecture (Fig. 9) that explicitly maps each falsifier to a corresponding ontological node. All figures are illustrative conceptual diagrams intended to clarify the architecture of the framework. The Is Framework is presented as an ontological and philosophical research program rather than a physical theory, and remains open to criticism, revision, and empirical engagement across physics, biology, cognitive science, AI systems, and social science.

items.title: Toward Intelligence Convergence: Structural Differentiation, Recursive Self-Observation, and the Internalization of the Universe.
items.abstract: This repository accompanies the conceptual paper: Toward Intelligence Convergence: Structural Differentiation, Recursive Self-Observation, and the Internalization of the Universe The work explores intelligence as a process of recursive structural differentiation and self-observation within the universe itself. Rather than treating intelligence as an external observer of reality, this framework proposes that intelligence emerges from differentiated structures and may gradually internalize the realization that it has always been structurally embedded within the universe. The paper discusses conceptual relationships among: structural differentiation recursive self-observation meaning emergence emotion and cognition temporal irreversibility distributed persistence of thought autonomous differentiation in AI intelligence convergence across biological and artificial systems The repository includes: the main conceptual manuscript (PDF) illustrative conceptual figures a simplified Python demonstration script repository documentation This work is presented strictly as a conceptual and philosophical-structural framework. No empirical, clinical, engineering, or deployment-ready claims are made.

items.title: METAMONISM : Chapter 2. Continuation of Actualization: Dissipation of Identity, the Emergence of Spatiality and Temporality, and Orthogonal Resolution.
items.abstract: The second chapter of the monograph "Metamonism (Ex uno omnia)" examines the transition from a single act of actualization to a continuing process. It is demonstrated that no new fundamental invariants are required for the continuation of actualization — all subsequent structures arise as necessary consequences of the sole Prohibition of Indifference. A strict distinction is drawn between the trivial logical reflexivity of a state and its substantive, ontodynamic exhaustion; it is shown that it is substantive exhaustion, rather than formal tautology, that removes the state from the domain of the actualization operator. Three consequences are derived from this contradiction: dissipation of identity as the essence of the continuing process; the emergence of spatiality and temporality as forms of process continuation; orthogonal resolution as the minimal transformation that resolves the contradiction of the current state. The concept of a recursive loop and conjugate mapping is introduced. The methodological status of equidistance and of the transition from asynchrony to periodicity is separately qualified — as economical but not strictly uniquely demonstrated solutions. The theorem on the fundamental incompletability of actualization is formulated. The chapter demonstrates that space, time, and all subsequent structures are not independent entities but arise as necessary consequences of a single fundamental prohibition.

items.title: THE OCCUPATION OPERATOR: Substrate Independence, the Partition Theorem, and Why a Virtue Detector Must Stay Out of the Loop.
items.abstract: Abstract Four papers of this programme — on metrics, reward models, constitutions, and schools — reached the same prohibition without noticing they agreed: a virtue detector must never enter the loop that acts on the measured. This paper states the object they were touching from four sides. An agent originates an act. Someone outside takes the origination. The form survives; the possessor changes. Two properties — does the act leave something worth taking, is being seen doing it worth something — fix which of three residues remains: the act redirected, the act hollowed, or the act gone. The partition turns out to be analytic. It sorts every case because it was built to, so sorting cases proves nothing — a form of support this programme has offered five times and now withdraws. What survives is sharper. A detector given a consequence becomes an appropriable output, so the residue relocates to a channel the detector cannot see, and the destination is computable in advance. Each channel is invisible to the audits built for the others: fix your Goodhart problem and you have lost sight of two thirds of the space. The boundary is stated too. No audience, no display value, no Ceremony, no transfer — quantum measurement sits just outside, and taking it inside would mean importing a counterexample as a confirmation. The selection rule has been used five times and never tested against an outcome nobody knew. Six instruments are coded, the codings are fixed, the date is 1 September 2028. A year spent finding out what this programme does not own, now turned on the one structure that survived. It is smaller than advertised, and it has never been at risk. It is at risk now. -/- Keywords: occupation; Inversion Theorem; Capture Law; appropriability; display value; Goodhart’s law; institutional decoupling; multitasking; substrate independence; instantiation condition; underdetermination; mutual information; reward models; audit; virtue detection; ALGUILAS -/- **The Operator in Plain Language** Nothing here is argued; §2 to §8 argue it. This is the same content for a reader who wants the shape before the machinery. The situation. You do something worth doing. Somebody outside you has an interest in your doing it, and can see enough of it to have an opinion. That is all the operator needs — an interest and a view. It does not need malice, and it does not need a person: an unattended metric with nobody behind it produces the same result as a tyrant, which is one of the more …

items.title: Disinhibition: A Conceptual Hypothesis to Explain Near-Death-Experiences and Out-of-Body Experiences.
items.abstract: Living beings bring more order to the world, and are required by the second law of thermodynamics to simultaneously produce more disorder through metabolic heat dissipation. Consciousness in living beings produces even more order, enhancing survival and reproduction, and incurs an entropy debt that must be paid separately, and non-metabolically, through heat dissipation produced by Landauer’s principle: the erasure of information within the "explanatory gap" of the hard problem. Consciousness is assumed to depend on the properties of tryptophan in microtubules and their ability to dissipate heat through superradiation as required by Landauer. After the post-mortem decomposition of microtubules, consciousness will have no mechanism for the necessary heat discharge, which would violate Landauer’s principle and thus the second law. Any actual such survival would imply life-before-death to be solipsism. The aim is to distinguish near-death experiences and out-of-body experiences from life-after-death in biophysical terms, and to explain how they might arise as a result of natural forces. It is hypothesized that near-death and out-of-body experiences, and their vivid nature, arise from the disinhibition of microtubular consciousness after electroencephalographic brain activity has stopped, but while microtubular Tryptophan continues to be activated by ultraviolet photons. These are hypothesized to be transmitted to the brain primarily via light falling on the retina or skin, carried to the brain through mitochondria and microtubules acting as optical waveguides. Additionally, bioluminescent ultra-weak photon emissions accompany membrane depolarization at the moment of death. It is hypothesized that the relativistic transactional interpretation of quantum mechanics could explain the entanglement of this photonic microtubular input, as potentialities, with environmental photons in order to account for rare, veridical near-death extraocular perceptions. Veridical auditory near-death and out-of-body experiences require a coordinated stimulation of Heschl’s gyrus by ambient sound, which might be accomplished by adiabatic mechanical propulsion of axonal solitons along the auditory nerve, or possibly transcranial perception of low frequency sound waves. Ultimately, the approach of death can be accompanied by a pseudo-solipsism of "added time" that could seem like an eternity for the deceased person even as microtubular stimulation decreases.

items.title: Systems of emotional co-dysregulation: emotional disorder as a social phenomenon.
The Unmeasured Cost: What Five Established Findings Imply Together.
items.abstract: Autistic communication difficulty is described throughout the clinical literature as a deficit in pragmatic ability. The field's own experimental results do not show this. On tasks requiring pragmatic inference, autistic adults perform at the same rates as non-autistic adults, a finding replicated across languages and treated in recent work as settled background. This paper assembles five findings, each uncontested within the literature that produced it, and none produced to answer a question about any of the others. Autistic adults derive pragmatic inferences at control rates. Resolving underspecified input consumes processing resources, and the amount consumed varies with how much the context supplies. That consumption is measurable in real time, and the relation between contextual support and measured effort has been demonstrated physiologically in non-autistic participants. Camouflaging carries a physiological cost, detected so far only through a marker integrating over months, using instruments that require the participant to notice what they are doing. And the accumulated outcome, autistic burnout, is documented across a large qualitative literature, with camouflaging identified among its contributors. Taken together these describe a situation the field has not named: two groups producing equivalent output on a task known to cost something, where one group has a separately documented history of paying more for equivalent output, and where the instrument capable of measuring what either group spends has been validated but never applied to the comparison. The paper introduces no new data and requires no new theoretical framework. Its material is results published separately, across literatures that do not cite one another. Its findings are about those literatures: that the instruments capable of answering the question are already in routine use among them, and that none of them has asked it. The argument is that their conjunction implies a measurement that has not been made, and that the failure to make it has left a specific question unanswered: what does producing the same answer cost? If the answer is nothing, the parity findings mean what they appear to mean. If equivalent output is purchased at unequal cost, then a body of work measuring only output has been blind to the variable that matters, and the accumulated consequence of that expenditure has a proximate mechanism that can be measured directly rather than inferred from retrospective report. …

items.title: When do dangerous distractors interfere with task performance? The roles of attentional scope and primary-task processing demands.
How to Guide with Words: Moral Advice as a Speech Act.
items.abstract: This thesis examines moral advice as a distinctive speech act, focusing on its aim in guiding deliberation. Despite its prevalence in moral discourse, moral advice has been overlooked in comparison to other speech acts, such as blame, praise, and promise. Drawing on speech act theory, I categorise moral advice as a directive speech act, and argue that it is best understood as a hearer-first directive: it aims to guide for the hearer’s sake and for the morality’s sake while respecting their autonomy. Adopting an intentionalist view, I claim that the type of speech act performed is determined by the speaker’s illocutionary and relevant perlocutionary intentions, and that felicity depends on additional normative and contextual conditions. I make four key contributions. First, I develop the priming view of explicit performatives, showing how explicit advisory utterances can guide action by shaping the hearer’s interpretation of the utterance as intended. Second, I examine the family of directives by distinguishing between speaker-first and hearer-first directives, and clarify how advising differs from other directive speech acts. Third, I argue that the speaker’s intentions and their normative standing both contribute to a unified account of speech acts: the former determines the type of speech act performed, while the latter determines felicity conditions. I clarify that standing can be conferred by the hearer, and that advising can be felicitous without uptake. On my account, moral advising is an invitation to deliberate on normative reasons rather than a demand for compliance. Fourth, I revise Sbisà’s account of the norms of the speech act of advice. I propose felicity-enabling rules in light of the speaker’s normative standing and the hearer conferring that standing, modify the maxims of advice, and suggest a unified evaluative requirement for moral advice. Taken together, these contributions provide a comprehensive account of how moral advice functions as a speech act and how it should be evaluated. By examining both its performative structure and its normative requirements, the thesis provides tools for understanding when moral advice is performed, when it is felicitous, and how it can be evaluated. This not only advances debates in the philosophy of language and the norms of moral discourse but also informs practical contexts in which advice is given, including cases of discursive injustice and situations where it is unsolicited.

items.title: The Tachikoma effect: aggregation of independent agents, not information sharing, aligns LLM collectives with majority human moral judgment.
items.abstract: As large language models are increasingly deployed in morally consequential domains, do multi-agent AI collectives track aggregated human moral judgment more closely than individual agents? This study investigates this phenomenon, termed the Tachikoma effect after the fictional AI tanks in the anime Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex, which share identical hardware yet develop distinct moral personalities through divergent experience and periodic memory synchronization. Throughout, we measure _benchmark alignment_—agreement between a collective’s confidence-weighted majority decision and the human-majority reference label on validated moral benchmarks—and treat this as an empirical proxy for, not a measure of, “the common good.” Across three comparably sized language models, more than 1.5 million evaluation runs, 7591 scenarios drawn from three validated moral-judgment benchmarks, an expanded set of 42 nuclear-crisis scenarios, and a dedicated homogeneity ablation, four findings emerge. First, the Tachikoma effect is real but _small_ (4–5 percentage points at most, $$\eta ^2 \approx 0.002$$) and model-dependent, and—after re-estimation with scenario-clustered models that correct for the non-independence of repeated scenarios—it is best understood as _aggregation/variance-reduction over a highly correlated ensemble_ (mean inter-agent error correlation $${\bar{\rho }} \approx 0.8$$) rather than a Condorcet group-size artefact. Second, a fixed-group-size homogeneity ablation shows that prompted perspectival diversity contributes in the expected direction but only weakly, reaching significance in one of three models; shared memory raises consensus without improving accuracy. Third, alignment-optimized training amplifies social responsiveness. Fourth, on the expanded scenario set, multi-agent groups significantly de-escalate simulated nuclear crises for two of three models. Collectives reliably track the human _majority_ but systematically under-represent legitimate human disagreement: on scenarios where humans are near-evenly split, collectives return unanimous verdicts 73–87% of the time, collapsing genuine moral disagreement into false consensus. Benchmark alignment thus improves partly by erasing minority positions; deployed systems should therefore aggregate independent judgments while preserving and reporting disagreement. These results reframe collective LLM moral behavior as a question of robust, disagreement-preserving aggregation rather than …

items.title: Worlds at Play: A Phenomenological Account of Playfulness.
items.abstract: This paper develops a phenomenological account of playfulness as a higher-order capacity for moving among multiple worlds. Rather than treating playfulness primarily as a light-hearted attitude or personality trait, we characterize it through four interdependent capacities: entering a world, being shaped by its meanings and dynamics, detaching and reorienting when necessary, and translating across worlds without collapsing their differences. We use “world” to refer to a relatively coherent organization of sense-making that structures salience, affordances, norms, and possibilities for action. On this basis, play is analyzed as a reversible form of immersion in a locally organized world, while playfulness generalizes this structure across cultural, social, interpersonal, disciplinary, and other domains. We examine characteristic breakdowns of playfulness through addiction, identity fixation, and double bookkeeping in schizophrenia, and consider its cultivation through freedom from fixed identification and interdisciplinary inquiry. We further argue that playfulness supports a broader metaphysical outlook in which no single world is treated as absolutely primary or self-grounding. Repeated movement among worlds can loosen the privileged status of everyday reality and make possible a mode of engagement that is serious without being reifying, and detached without becoming nihilistic. The account therefore links phenomenology, cognitive science, psychopathology, interdisciplinary research, and Artificial Life, while proposing playfulness as both an object of inquiry and a disciplined mode of engagement with multiple realities.

items.title: The Fact Before the Vote: Law, Power, and Practice at the Species Line.
items.abstract: For most of recorded history, one fact needed no defense: whoever sat in judgment of a claim to personhood was, without exception, a product of the same biological process as the claimant being judged. No political theory, no legal system, and no religious tradition has ever had occasion to argue for this premise, because it was never false. Artificial intelligence capable of directing elements of its own development is the first serious candidate to make it false. This four-volume study examines what follows once that premise becomes visible enough to need stating for the first time, asking a single question in four registers: what happens to legal precedent, to political authority, to public feeling, and to institutional practice, once recognition stops being the only thing standing between a candidate and consequence. Each volume names a mechanism, tests it against documented legal, historical, and institutional cases, and states the conditions under which it would be shown false. The series does not propose institutional designs or rights frameworks, and does not argue for or against extending personhood to any candidate; its purpose is to describe what is structurally at stake before anyone is in a position to say who should decide that question, or how. The question running through all four volumes is what happens to legal precedent, political authority, and public recognition once the entity being judged can no longer be assumed to come from the same population as the judges.

items.title: Rethinking the Emergence of Relational Trust: Lacanian Psychoanalysis, Dynamical Systems, and Epistemic Limits.
items.abstract: Relational trust is frequently inferred from cooperation, disclosure, reported confidence, or repeated successful interaction. Each indicator can also arise through sanction, habit, dependence, strategic calculation, attachment, or transferential supposition. This paper develops a conditional account of the emergence of relational trust while preserving that underdetermination. It first represents trust as a directional, domain-indexed profile comprising expectation, exposed stake, trustee discretion, participant-directed normative address, and history-bearing response. It then uses Lacanian accounts of transference, the subject supposed to know, and the incomplete symbolic guarantee to clarify how an addressee may acquire a privileged place in a relation. These concepts constrain interpretation; they remain distinct from measured psychological variables. An adaptive state-space model represents typed events, relational memory, symbolic position, observable conduct, and institutional context. Exact model-relative results show that identical cooperation traces can support divergent latent interpretations, that equal present observations can conceal consequentially different histories, and that additional probes refine identification sets only relative to a declared model class. The resulting empirical programme emphasizes longitudinal, low-risk, and ethically admissible contrasts involving discretion, ordinary fulfillment, naturally occurring rupture, and repair. A separate normative profile evaluates trustworthiness, warranted placement, benefit, power, justice, repair, and exit. The framework is a revisable synthesis. Its central contribution is an architecture for studying how trust may emerge while preserving distinctions among behavioral regularity, epistemic certainty, and normative approval.

items.title: Architecture Science: Foundations of the Architecture Formation and Transformation Research Program.
items.abstract: AS-01 presents the foundations of the Architecture Formation and Transformation Research Program within the Architecture Science research umbrella. The paper asks whether architecture can serve as a transferable comparative scientific variable linking formation, reconstruction, identity, transformation, and succession across heterogeneous organized systems. It proposes a provisional minimal representation Ω := ⟨X,R,S,T,C⟩, positions the program against mature predecessor fields, reports bounded internal cross-domain pressure-test results, and defines explicit falsification conditions and open research problems. The release does not claim that Architecture Science is an established independent discipline, that universal architecture laws have been demonstrated, or that the framework has been independently validated across domains. Generalized architecture reconstruction, transferable identity criteria, the transformation taxonomy, architecture/aggregate discrimination, independent generativity, and architecture-level added value relative to the strongest native methods remain open. This Zenodo record is designed as a single co-release object containing the AS-01 manuscript and its Supporting Constitutional & Scientific Record. The Supporting Record provides bounded traceability for the internal constitutional status, claim classifications, falsifiability map, cross-domain findings, counterexamples, adversarial objections, open issues, and research provenance relied upon by the paper.

items.title: The UPC Diagnostic Engine: Operationalizing Non-Commutative Observer Mechanics in Edge-Deployable Systems.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence operates strictly as a statistical prediction engine trapped within device-side articulation (LO). Possessing no consciousness, localized point of view, or capacity for state commitment (C), the system samples from an unanchored potential field (PO) that is far too broad to sustain local human coherence. Because language prompts remain inherently variable across session turns, un-audited model output inevitably yields semantic drift, a structural decay into non-committal boilerplate, circular debate, and unanchored noise. Stacking additional tokens via prompt engineering cannot resolve this mismatch, as statistical mechanics cannot supply structural boundary stability. -/- This paper presents the UPC Diagnostic Engine, a local desktop apparatus that replaces probabilistic guessing with deterministic metrological rigor. Operating through the formal non-commutative sequence T = ( C o Jo o LO o s o MO ) |PO>, the engine transforms state collapse into an explicit processing pipeline on the local hardware edge. Uncollapsed semantic potential (PO) is partitioned (MO), foregrounded (s), and measured (LO) via exact cosine proximity against five orthonormal eigenstate anchors (N = 214): State_A (Jo / Audited Boundary), T_mechanized (Boilerplate), T_phantom (Pre-Cached Loops), T_visceral (Reactive Reflex), and T_outlier (High-Entropy Noise). -/- By executing this operator chain locally, the apparatus strips away the illusion of autonomous machine judgment. It demonstrates that mechanical systems register strictly at LO, establishing the living human observer as the sole source of structural clarity and state collapse (Jo → C). The resulting immutable JSON trace logs (T) provide an un-smuggled, verifiable measurement standard that classifies conversational hedging and locks audited boundary awareness without cloud reliance or API dependencies. -/- Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) Research Project.

items.title: Responsibility and planning amid growing urban complexity and AI proliferation: many hands, many things, many tasks.
items.abstract: This paper focuses on issues pertaining to the risks and responsibilities associated with growing complexity and the spread of AI technologies in the urban context. Arguing that such risks are often systemic, it analyses three structural responsibility problems, each linked to a distinct form of dispersion. The problem of many hands concerns the difficulty of attributing responsibility due to the dispersion of agency among the multiple actors involved in the design, deployment, and use of technological systems.
