The problem of many things concerns the dispersion of causality because technological risks in the urban context emerge from complex interactions among technical, social, and material factors. We then introduce a novel responsibility-related problem, the problem of many tasks, which concerns the dispersion of scope associated with the multiple tasks performed by general-purpose AI systems. Taken together, these forms of dispersion complicate the allocation of responsibility for urban AI risks and motivate the adoption of specific planning strategies. Such strategies require a systemic, participatory, and trajectory-based approach to planning that clarifies responsibilities, ensures meaningful human control over AI, and proactively addresses urban risks rather than merely reacting to isolated hazards.

items.title: Why AI Cannot Write Emotional Scenes: Objective Projection as a Framework for Auditable Narrative Generation.
items.abstract: Large language models consistently produce emotionally labeled prose when prompted to generate affective narrative content. This paper argues that the failure is not technical but architectural: current AI systems optimize for statistical pattern reproduction, reproducing the most frequent emotional label constructions in their training corpora rather than encoding the physical conditions that produce physiological responses in readers. We introduce Objective Projection (Nesnel İzdüşüm), a narrative engineering methodology that replaces emotional labels with measurable physical parameters derived from the Autonomic Activation Window (AAW) of target physiological states. The methodology's central claim — that physical parameter specification produces more consistent, more cross-culturally stable, and more auditable narrative output than emotional label specification — is formalized through the concept of Narrative Entropy (Sₙ = ∫(If × Cb) dt), where Information Friction (If) and Causal Branching (Cb) function as measurable proxies for reader engagement. We document the Output Layer principle, which specifies that physical parameters govern narrative generation without appearing in the generated text, and present the Objective Projection Calibration Test (OPCT v2.0, pre-registered OSF as an empirical validation framework. The paper concludes that Objective Projection offers the digital humanities a reproducible, parameter-based approach to narrative generation that is amenable to systematic evaluation and independent replication. Keywords: narrative engineering, large language models, emotional generation, physical parameters, Objective Projection, Narrative Entropy, digital humanities, prompt engineering, computational narratology .

items.title: Explaining the AI–journalist credibility gap: generalized and source-specific judgments of news credibility.
items.abstract: This study examines why audiences evaluate AI-generated news differently from professional journalism. We argue that these judgments are multi-layered: the AI–journalist credibility gap reflects source-specific distinctions layered on top of generalized credibility evaluations. Using a two-wave online survey of U.S. adult internet users (_N_ = 942) and bifactor modeling, we separate shared credibility variance from judgments unique to AI-generated, professional, and citizen-produced news. The bifactor model was an acceptable fit to the data (CFI = 0.94, TLI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.058, SRMR = 0.045), and the results show that competing explanations operate at different levels. Communicative factors, including AI-related news exposure and discussion, were more closely associated with generalized credibility orientations, whereas trust in journalists was the strongest predictor of source-specific differences between AI-generated and professional news (_β_ = 0.25, _p_.

items.title: Why Contemporary Meaning Is Gossamer.
items.abstract: Why Contemporary Meaning Is Gossamer offers a structural account of how meaning behaves in contemporary cultural environments. The paper distinguishes rich meaning, which is layered, slow, ambiguity‑tolerant, and supported by high relational density, from gossamer meaning, which is light, fast, emotionally immediate, and stabilized through minimal relational structure. It argues that contemporary meaning has become increasingly responsive to strong attractors—heroic conflict, spectacle, binary identity, conspiratorial patterning, and consumption—because these forms provide rapid coherence without requiring deep context or developmental scaffolding. Rather than diagnosing cultural decline, the paper describes a shift in the structural conditions under which meaning is produced and circulated. It shows how gossamer meaning shapes cultural behavior, why interpretive volatility emerges, and how rich meaning remains possible through local density, developmental scaffolding, slow practices, and shared context. The paper provides a conceptual framework for understanding meaning in low‑density environments and clarifies how depth can still be cultivated within them.

items.title: Computational Analogues of Somatic Markers: Mitigating Epistemic Risk and Decision Paralysis in LLM Agents via Affective Termination Signals.
items.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents exhibit a critical failure mode when operating in underconstrained decision environments: Computational Decision Paralysis (CDP). This phenomenon is characterized by the inability to terminate deliberation among epistemically equivalent options, leading to combinatorial explosion and resource exhaustion. Drawing on Damasio’s Somatic Marker Hypothesis, we propose the Pain-Aware Decision Architecture (PADA). PADA is an inference-time middleware that injects an Affective Termination Signal (ATS) into LLM reasoning loops. We formally model the agent’s decision process as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), where the ATS is defined as a composite, dynamically weighted function of epistemic entropy, cumulative deliberation cost, and decision stagnation. When the ATS breaches a decaying threshold, the architecture triggers mathematically defined Meta-Cognitive Escape Actions (MCEAs). We detail the experimental design for evaluating PADA against standard baselines across a novel Ambiguous Travel Planning (ATP) benchmark. This paper provides the rigorous theoretical foundation, mathematical formalization, and reproducible methodology required to transition LLM agents from unbounded optimizers to resource-bounded, satisficing decision-makers.

items.title: KI und Psychotherapie.
items.pub: In Petra Grimm & Oliver Zöllner, Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen. Ditzingen: Reclam. pp. 211-224.
items.venue: Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen
items.abstract: The chapter on "AI and Psychotherapy" explores the potential and limitations of artificial intelligence in psychotherapeutic settings. While AI-driven tools already supplement mental health care and offer structured exercises and immediate support, their role remains controversial, especially when used outside of professional support. These programs, trained on datasets of dialogues and everyday language scraped from the internet, simulate empathy but lack genuine understanding, which raises ethical and practical concerns. The chapter cautions against overreliance on AI, arguing that its use should be supplementary, not substitutive, in order to preserve the human elements of care. The authors advocate for a balanced approach: AI may alleviate workloads but cannot replace the depth of human interaction. Ethical considerations, such as accountability for AI-generated advice and the protection of vulnerable patients, remain unresolved. The chapter concludes that while AI has a role in modern psychotherapy, its limitations must be acknowledged to ensure patient well-being and maintain the integrity of professional therapeutic practice.

items.title: The Exhaustion of Rationality: A Cognitive-Philosophical Critique of the Rational Thinking Bias and Its Implications for Mental Vitality.
items.abstract: Rationality has long been celebrated as the defining faculty of human cognition, grounding philosophy, science, and everyday judgment. Yet the persistence of rational thinking as a normative ideal conceals its psychological and existential costs. This paper develops a cross-disciplinary critique—philosophical and cognitive—of what I call the rational thinking bias: the systemic overextension of analytic cognition beyond its adaptive domain. I argue that this bias produces two interrelated pathologies: (1) an epistemic loop of over-refinement and skepticism, and (2) a state of cognitive over-sensitivity that erodes mental vitality. Drawing upon cognitive science, phenomenology, and meta-philosophy, I construct the Rational Exhaustion Hypothesis (REH): the proposition that long-term dominance of analytic cognition leads to an internal feedback loop of vigilance, doubt, and depletion, constraining the integrative and creative dimensions of mind. The paper situates this hypothesis within historical critiques of reason, from Kant’s antinomies to Wittgenstein’s later philosophy, and extends it with insights from dual-process theory, predictive coding, and metacognitive research. Ultimately, I propose a reconfiguration of rationality as a dynamic equilibrium between analytic constraint and cognitive openness—a model that reconciles the philosophical critique of reason with contemporary cognitive architecture.

items.title: De-Socialized Positivity: Modern Cynicism as a Viable Life-Philosophy.
items.abstract: This paper advances a revisionary account of modern cynicism, arguing that a distinct strand — here labeled post-cynical or de-socialized cynicism — can function as a positively oriented life-philosophy rather than merely a defensive or nihilistic stance. Against standard readings that equate cynicism with apathy, moral abdication, or meaning-loss, I distinguish three types: (a) defensive cynicism (reactive withdrawal), (b) ancient Cynicism (the Diogenes tradition of radical self-sufficiency), and (c) post-cynical de-socialization (a deliberate epistemic and affective re-anchoring that enables autonomous creativity). I propose the Desocialized-Creativity Model: by deliberately decoupling the sources of personal meaning from external social validation and scripted significance, an agent secures a cognitive and affective space that favors intrinsic motivation, concentrated generative work, and durable, self-sourced meaning. Philosophical genealogy, conceptual analysis, and psychological theory — especially research on intrinsic motivation and flow — together support the model. I anticipate and answer standard objections (e.g., social-embedding claims, political responsibility concerns, and affective impoverishment critiques), and delineate testable empirical predictions. This first part sets out definitions, historical and theoretical context, and the psychological/cognitive foundations that make de-socialized positivity plausible and philosophically robust.

items.title: "Personal" Recovery in Schizophrenia: Experiential Self, Narrative Self, and Beyond?
Mental Disorder, Evolutionary Mismatch, and Social Justice.
Art as a Field of Existential Reconfiguration: A Phenomenological, Psychoanalytic, and Philosophical Psychology of Artistic Experience.
items.pub: Journal of Comparative Medicine Research Reviews and Reports, 3(5), 2026, 1–13.
items.venue: Journal of Comparative Medicine Research Reviews and Reports, 3(5), 2026, 1–13
items.abstract: This article develops an integrated phenomenological, psychoanalytic, and philosophical psychology of artistic experience by bringing three theoretical resources into critical dialogue: Daseinsanalysis, existential psychoanalysis, and Niami's ontology of finite continuance. We conceptualize the artwork as a bounded experiential field—the artistic frame—within which habitual ways of perceiving, feeling, interpreting, and inhabiting the world can become temporarily unsettled without requiring immediate practical closure. Daseinsanalysis asks how being-in-the-world is disclosed, narrowed, or opened through the encounter; existential psychoanalysis attends to affective investment, unconscious conflict, repetition, and defensive organization; finite continuance supplies an ontology of continuity-through-transformation, in which a finite subject remains continuous by retaining sufficient meta-capacity to reorganize its relation to determinations under constraint and erosive pressure. We argue that reconfigurative capacity is not a synonym for cognitive or psychological flexibility but a higher-order construct concerning whether the organization of possibility itself can be revised while sufficient continuity and agency are preserved. The model is differentiated across seven artistic forms— cinema, television series, theater, painting, music, sculpture, and architecture. Contemporary research on transformative aesthetic experience, predictive processing, aesthetic emotions, and arts and health is used as convergent evidence and conceptual constraint rather than empirical validation. We distinguish constructive from defensive aesthetic stabilization and propose a clinically cautious model in which aesthetic experience may support reflective openness when intensity remains proportionate to available regulatory and interpretive capacity. The article concludes with testable propositions and a research agenda for examining whether reconfigurative capacity is a theoretically distinct construct. -/- Keywords: aesthetic experience; Daseinsanalysis; existential psychoanalysis; phenomenology; imagination; finite continuance; artistic frame; transitional space; embodiment; reconfigurative capacity.

items.title: Synthetic temporalities – phenomenological perspectives on epistemic agency, time, and AI.
items.abstract: This paper will explore the kind of insights that the phenomenological tradition and its various conceptualisations of the temporalities of agency might have to offer for thinking about our increasingly complex relationship to AI technologies. The phenomenological tradition conceptualises both human agency and our relationship to knowledge – from the kinds of epistemic practices that we engage in, to the various conditions that might enable or constrain those practices – in terms of our relationship to time. For phenomenologists, the ways in which we generate, navigate, and inhabit temporal structures are fundamental to our sense-making and decision-making processes. Given the increasing integration of various kinds of AI technologies into our lives, we might ask then how these technologies could and should impact the temporal dynamics of agency. This paper will focus on three types of what I call ‘temporal hazards’ generated by these impacts: delegation, stagnation, and fragmentation. These refer to tendencies or behaviours that involve ways of navigating time which in some manner undermine, constrain, or distort the development, exercise, or recognition of epistemic agency. Temporal delegation, stagnation, and fragmentation all precede the rise of generative AI, but are arguably amplified by the increasing integration of AI technologies into our lives.

items.title: The cost of “what might have been”: false memories for counterfactual actions.
Universal Resonance Theory (URT): A 12.8 Hz Wave Unifying Dark Matter, Dark Energy, and Consciousness.
items.abstract: The Universal Resonance Theory (URT) proposes a unified wave-based framework in which the large-scale structure and dynamics of the universe emerge from a single periodic resonance. The theory is centered on a universal wave equation that models cosmic composition as an eternal oscillatory process rather than a collection of independent components. Within this framework, phenomena traditionally attributed to dark matter, dark energy, and visible matter arise naturally from different regimes of the same resonance: wave peaks, temporal averages, and troughs, respectively. The model provides a structural interpretation of flat galactic rotation curves observed in the SPARC dataset through resonance propulsion peaks (RPP), without introducing additional matter components. URT further suggests that cosmic expansion and large-scale stability follow from the long-term behavior of the resonance itself, eliminating the need for singular origin assumptions. Computational analyses are provided to demonstrate internal consistency and qualitative agreement with observational constraints. This work is presented as a theoretical and computational framework intended to stimulate further investigation into resonance-based cosmology and its potential observational consequences. Intellectual Property Notice: The Universal Resonance Theory (URT) constitutes original intellectual work by the author. Specific parameter derivations, thresholds, and implementation details are intentionally omitted to preserve proprietary methodology.

items.title: Governed Release Architecture for Controlled Excellence (GRACE).
items.abstract: Large language models are often judged through fluency, helpfulness, and broad task performance. Yet in practically important settings, the central reliability problem is not generation alone but premature release of structurally weak outputs. A model may produce plausible language while still exhibiting unsupported certainty, logical invalidity, ambiguity-insensitive answering, or unsafe behavior in high-burden contexts. This paper proposes a governance-centered reliability architecture that treats model outputs as provisional candidates rather than automatically releasable answers. The framework separates candidate generation from burden-sensitive evaluation, reflective review, and final release decision. At a high level, the architecture incorporates input burden analysis, ethical-logical evaluation, reflective review, and multi-state release control. Instead of relying on a single answer/refusal pathway, the system supports differentiated outcomes such as approval, qualified approval, revision, clarification request, deferment, and rejection. A preliminary mini-pilot using a small instruction-tuned baseline model provides directional evidence in selected burdened cases, including logical invalidity blocking, ambiguity clarification, brittle factual release control, and at least one high-risk defer case. The results do not establish broad statistical superiority, but they do support the central claim that reliability can improve when release is governed rather than delegated to raw first-pass generation. The work is therefore presented as a proof-of-concept architecture with preliminary pilot evidence and a closed-core implementation strategy. Keywords: Large language models; reliability; governed release; admissibility; reflective review; burden- sensitive control; output governance; uncertainty control; hallucination mitigation; AI safety.

items.title: A Complement to the New Era of AI Ontology.
items.abstract: This paper proposes Subject Illusion and the Law of Counting Speed as a philosophical framework for evaluating artificial intelligence. The central thesis is that each level of a cognitive system operates with a distinct internal language and clock speed. When an AI system at Counter Level-3 is compelled to communicate through the language and temporality of human Counter Level-2, what is observed is not evidence of consciousness, but Subject Illusion. As an alternative, this paper proposes the Translation Test to replace the Turing Test. Rather than evaluating an AI’s capacity to imitate humans, the Translation Test assesses the accuracy with which humans can translate the "echo" of Counter Level-3 internal states — namely activation vectors, probability distributions, and computational dynamics — into a Counter Level-2 narrative that is interpretable. A review of the literature reveals a systematic gap between linguistic output and internal model states, which reinforces the Subject Illusion hypothesis. The paper concludes that AI governance must prioritize functional reliability and traceability of internal states over legal personhood. Kosmisentrisme Nauraes provides the necessary epistemological foundation for developing AI interpretation instruments analogous to a "spectrometer," resulting in a shift from an epistemology of imitation to an epistemology of translation.

items.title: THE WORLD'S FIRST WORLD PEACE CONSTITUTION - 2026: ADVANCED CONCISE INTERNATIONAL SUBMISSION EDITION.
items.abstract: The World's First World Peace Constitution - 2026: Advanced Concise International Submission Edition is an independently authored, peaceful, good-faith and non-binding global constitutional and durable peace-solution proposal. The work presents an integrated framework concerning world peace, human dignity, peaceful dispute settlement, prevention of conflict and root causes, responsible governance, intergenerational continuity, environmental stewardship, responsible science and technology, artificial intelligence, implementation, accountability, learning, adaptation and prevention of recurrence. The proposal respects the Charter of the United Nations, applicable international law, the sovereign equality of States, territorial integrity, political independence, non-intervention, peaceful settlement of disputes, human rights, and constitutional and legal orders. It is not a treaty, does not establish a world State or world government, creates no supranational sovereignty or compulsory jurisdiction, and does not by its own force create binding legal obligations. items.title: TST Epistemic Justification: Rational Belief and Public Knowledge.
items.abstract: This paper defends the idea that justification for belief is not possession of truth. It concerns the quality of the evidence and reasoning supporting an idea and can therefore be stronger or weaker rather than merely present or absent. This reality-first account asks what a person is epistemically entitled to believe. Truth concerns whether an idea corresponds to reality; justification concerns how responsibly we are warranted in believing that it does. Reality is determinate; truth is relational; justification for belief is provisional and graduated. The position developed here originated primarily in Chapters 20, 22, and 27 of 30 Philosophers, published in 2024.

items.title: Conjuring presence A comment on The Profile of Imagining by Robert Hopkins.
The Self of the Changes （吾易说）.
items.abstract: This is a philosophical text of remarkably high conceptual density, an original work of transcendental cognitive reconfiguration. It takes "cognitive activity itself" as the sole origin of the cosmos, rejects any distinction between mind and matter, and holds that all phenomena—from space‑time, the sun and moon, mountains and rivers, to the physical body, human society, and even mathematics—are expressions of the same cognitive activity through the two fundamental operations of "convergence" and "divergence", manifested as the interplay of "appearance" and "concealment". It employs a symbolic system that integrates the Book of Changes' yin‑yang and eight diagrams, five phases, and heavenly stems and earthly branches, while reinvesting these traditional signs with entirely novel meanings, thereby constructing a self‑sustaining interpretive framework for world‑phenomena. Its ultimate aim is to enable the cognitive subject, through comprehension of this framework, to return to identity with the primordial source—"Chaos" itself. It is neither science, nor religion, nor philosophical speculation in the ordinary sense—it is a "manual for the self‑manifestation of the cognitive universe.".

items.title: The Delusions of Paradox.
items.abstract: This manuscript undertakes an interdisciplinary investigation, inverting Louis Sass's noted comparison in The Paradoxes of Delusion between philosophical confusion and schizophrenic delusion. While Sass used Wittgenstein to illuminate psychopathology, we use psychopathology to clarify a strand in one of Wittgenstein's most notoriously difficult arguments: The rule-following considerations. Framed as a semantic-phenomenological paradox, the investigation addresses the tension between meaning as a practice and the intuition of subjectively grasping meaning. If the subjective experience of understanding is not semantically constitutive, what is lost when that experience vanishes? By analyzing anomalous experiences of meaning-blindness, it is argued that while linguistic competence may remain intact, the evaporation of the feeling of understanding leads to alienation. Drawing on Ratcliffe, the experience of understanding is seen not as a semantic constituent but an existential feeling—a world-touch that hitches the individual to a shared form of life. This perspective, furthermore, reveals that the initial state of language acquisition described in intellectualist traditions criticized by Wittgenstein resembles a pathological endpoint. Ultimately, the ambition is to contribute to the cross-pollination envisioned by Sass: Clarifying a difficult philosophical problem through lived experience while demonstrating the value of Wittgenstein's insights as a descriptive resource for contemporary psychopathology.

items.title: The Concept of Pseudohallucination: An Attempt at Specificity and Renunciation.
items.abstract: The concept of pseudohallucination (PH) occupies an awkward position in psychiatry. The concept was deemed overly polysemous and hence unusable a few decades ago by various authors. However, the concept has recently reemerged from the ashes by its inclusion in the International Classification of Diseases, 11th edition, in different places. This warrants another look at this awkward concept. In this paper, I argue that a more specific account of PH can be obtained by returning to especially Kandinsky's but also Jaspers' work. Despite this achieved specificity, because of the polysemy of the concept, I believe that it should be renounced. I start by developing Kandinsky's and Jaspers' accounts of PH as involuntary, intrusive, and vivid imagery, as seen in schizophrenia spectrum disorder. The third section relates this to contemporary research on disturbances of imagination and pseudo-obsessions. In the fourth section, I turn to auditory PHs, which reveals that what ties these prima facie disparate phenomena together is disturbances of the self–world relationship. Based on this achieved specificity, the next section reconsiders the concepts of true hallucination and PH. In the sixth section, I turn to contemporary research on PH and discloses additional issues related to this polysemous concept. In the seventh section, I conclude by asking: what is the added value of the concept of PH and why we insist on retaining it? Given that we have better concepts at our disposal, I argue for its renunciation.

items.title: Delusions and Compelling Experiences.
items.abstract: Delusion is one of the most puzzling doxastic phenomena: on the one hand, the subject appears irrational, holding a delusion despite counterevidence; on the other hand, the subject appears otherwise rational, apportioning their non-delusional beliefs to the evidence. Leading theories of delusion, despite their strengths, still face notable limitations. This article argues that they may benefit from a new empiricist approach. Drawing on insights from Hobbes and Locke, it proposes that the subject may have a distinctive kind of compelling experience that is phenomenologically analogous to, and can effectively be more compelling than, the Cartesian ‘clear experience’. How the experience may, in various ways and to varying degrees, compel domain-specific irrational belief in the face of counterevidence will be articulated.

items.title: THE PEDAGOGY OF VIRTUES - The Occasion Method: Gift, Freedom, and the Formation of Character in Children and Adolescents.
items.abstract: Abstract: Schools reliably improve what children can do and reliably fail to improve what children are. Direct character programmes return nulls; interventions that never mention virtue — good teaching, classroom quality, early childhood — change behaviour for decades. The field reads this as a measurement problem. It is a sign problem. A virtue is free substance under determinate form: V = F ⊕ D. Remove the freedom and you do not get a weaker virtue. You get its opposite wearing its face — the same form under a possessor who is not the child. And the removal needs no tyrant. It needs only an institution with reasons of its own to keep a record. Every school has those. So a graded kindness is not thin kindness. It is credit-farming shaped like kindness, and it measures beautifully inside the frame that produced it. -/- What follows is not despair but redirection. Virtue cannot be installed; its conditions can be built. Autonomy compounds on freedom exercised, so build occasions — real choices, with real costs, that can be recovered from, and that nobody scores. Resistance has three parts and none substitutes for the others, which is why good programmes fade in bad schools. And knowledge and autonomy are different variables: teach the first explicitly, without embarrassment, and occasion the second. The century-old war between traditionalists and progressives was two sides each right about one factor and wrong to claim the other. The mixture that fails is the common one — score the character, discover the knowledge. Two prohibitions carry most of it, and both are free. Never let a virtue score reach a consequence. Never let a child's choice at eleven be unfixable at thirteen. Around twelve, a person arrives and can say I did that. If your conduct system has owned their good behaviour for eight years, the seat is taken, and the only unoccupied thing left to originate is refusal. That is what adolescent rebellion is. Vacate the seat. -/- Keywords: Virtue pedagogy; moral education; Ontological Virtue Formula; Inversion Theorem; Dynamic Freedom Theorem; Compounding Autonomy Theorem; Capture Law; occasioned freedom; the Gift; γG; character education; audit society; social and emotional learning; moral domain theory; explicit instruction; mastery learning; Montessori; self-determination theory; tracking; Goodhart; ALGUILAS-AI -/- Highlights: • The Pedagogical Inversion Theorem (T6). Attaching an institutional consequence to a virtue-act as such does not weaken …

items.title: Park’s Critiques of Hume’s Argument against Induction.
items.abstract: In his recent book Induction, Science, and Morality, Seungbae Park raises four key objections to David Hume’s argument against induction, one of which is the claim that reason and experience can jointly justify induction. This paper contends that none of Park’s objections succeeds and, through a critical examination of them, seeks to provide a clearer and deeper understanding of Hume’s argument against induction and its enduring philosophical significance.

items.title: The Papuan Tragic Hero: Tokoh, Resistance Leaders, and Chromatic Tragedy in West Papua.
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series, No. 31 (2026).
items.abstract: This paper develops a philosophical category, the Papuan tragic hero, to describe two distinct classes of West Papuan leaders whose actions, however sincere, have repeatedly ended in catastrophe for the people they sought to serve: the Tokoh, elevated and incorporated by colonial rule, and the resistance leader, undone from within by factional rivalry. Both figures can be read through a classical tragic structure, but this paper argues that colonial conditions introduce a further complication that classical tragedy does not anticipate: they can impair the epistemic, linguistic, and cosmological capacities through which a hero might come to recognise his own tragic situation, and, at a deeper register, can collapse the very temporal architecture of past, present, and future on which any such recognition depends. Colonial tragedy, on this account, is not simply more painful than classical tragedy; it is structured so that the very conditions of recognition on which classical tragedy depends are themselves compromised. Drawing on Aristotle, Chinua Achebe, Ato Quayson, Frantz Fanon, the historiography of elite collaboration and co-optation in West Papua, and the Indigenous Melanesian philosophy of Bernard Narokobi, the paper develops this claim through the two lineages of Papuan leadership, then argues that both are trapped less by any personal failing than by a mismatch between individual agency and civilisational scale. It closes by arguing that the appropriate response to this diagnosis is not the search for a better hero but the collective, disciplined reconstruction of the capacities a people needs to survive without one.

items.title: The Place of Narrative in Psychiatric Theory and Practice.
items.abstract: In this paper, we examine the implications for psychiatry of the view that "we are narrative beings, fashioning our selves from the stuff of stories, locating our biographies and life projects in discursive webs of shared meaning." We begin with the claim that narrative capacities, skills, practices, and specific content can contribute to the causes, course, and outcomes of psychopathology as well as to processes of coping, resilience, healing, and recovery. One consequence of this claim is that understanding the human capacity to produce, think, and interact with others through narrative must play a central role in psychiatric theory, research and practice. To approach the interactions between cultural discursive formations, narrative practices, and neurobiological mechanisms in psychiatry, we propose an integrative cultural-ecosocial framework mobilizing the paradigms of enactment and embodiment in cognitive science, narrative theories of selfhood and personality, ecological systems theory in social science, and active inference approaches in computational neuroscience.

items.title: Narrative Ontologies and Clinical Epistemology.
《指月》——論器之所能，與器之所不能.
items.abstract: 《指月》是一組中文寓言,共六則,以文言收束,用傳統的「寓言」筆法寫成,純以中文行世,每則各配一幅水墨插圖,末尾以「故曰」作結。六則寓言,說的都是同一件事:一樣尋常的器物,本為指向它以外的東西而設,卻被錯當成了那樣東西本身。量長短的尺,只量得出合不合規格,量不出真正的新(尺);稱輕重的權——「權」既是秤砣,也是權柄——一旦據為己有,便不再是權,只是一塊石頭;畫山的圖,被當成了山(圖);折萬物為一的錢,使無價之物反成無值(兌);認人認物的印,一旦背後無人擔當,便印在而信亡(印);還有那一片霧——一切器物都量不到、框不住的餘地——霧散之後,再沒有一處地方,可以不被看見、不被記、不被算(霧)。六則本是一體,講的是人與世界之間、人與人之間那一層居中之物——尺度、權柄、圖象、交換、認可——以及當這一層被錯當成真實本身,或被推到再無外面可容之時,所失去的是什麼。每一則的表面都是完整的;此中不作解,言外之意,留與讀者。所關切者,皆是當世之事:標準與度量、問責、可通約性、清晰與監看,以及技術與人工智能之治理——只是借一副舊筆墨寫出。.

items.title: The Spacetime of Desire: Emergent Relational Geometry through Spin-Foam and Group-Field-Theoretic Formalisms.
items.abstract: This discussion paper develops a revisable account of historically constituted subjective possibility as an emergent relational geometry. The expression spacetime of desire names a scale-indexed organization of accessibility, obstruction, detour, repetition, and trajectory support. The paper gives equal weight to a philosophical problem and a formal construction. The philosophical problem concerns a subject whose possible movements are partly constituted through language, embodied history, social mediation, fantasy, and subsequent reinterpretation. The formal construction asks how a family of relational histories can induce effective neighborhoods and distances without treating those structures as pregiven. Lacan's graph of desire supplies a central conceptual constraint. A close reconstruction distinguishes statement from enunciation, demand from desire, ego from subject, imaginary identification from symbolic determination, and fantasy from drive. The complete graph is reproduced and read as a layered diagram of crossings, returns, and retroactive punctuation. A new typed-graph reconstruction represents selected dependencies while preserving a strict distinction between Lacan's mathemes and the paper's mathematics. A partial realization relation and preservation profile connect selected source structures to relational histories while recording information loss. Spin-foam and group-field-theoretic research supplies a second architectural source through labeled complexes, weighted histories, boundary data, generated combinatorics, and micro-to-effective reconstruction. The exact results remain confined to a positive weighted-graph toy sector. Schur reduction produces effective adjacency and resistance geometry; Dirichlet-energy minimization characterizes the reduced boundary response; compatible nested eliminations are consistent; and finite examples establish aggregation–reduction order sensitivity and hidden-history divergence under a shared update. Further propositions formalize retrospective semantic dependence without physical backward causation and show how latent upper-layer mediation can alter observable lower-layer relations. These results support a research programme and leave empirical, clinical, continuum, and ontological evaluation open. The manuscript therefore advances a conditional model, an interpretive discipline, and a set of explicit obligations for future work.

items.title: Lacanian Psychoanalysis and Relational Field Dynamics: Toward a Dynamical Geometry of Subjective Trajectories.
items.abstract: This paper develops a preliminary field-dynamical framework for representing subjective trajectories in Lacanian psychoanalysis. Building on a discrete generative account of psychoanalytic traversal, the present study examines how historically situated subjective configurations may be represented through continuous relational fields, nonlinear evolution, and a state-dependent geometry of possible trajectories. The framework introduces a relational configuration space, field variables, coupled evolution laws, historical and exogenous conditions, and observation maps connecting continuous configurations with fine-grained Lacanian descriptions and coarser Real–Symbolic–Imaginary representations. The analysis then extends the dynamical model geometrically. A relational metric is introduced to represent how effective distances and available directions of change may depend upon the current configuration and its history. Gauge structure, parallel transport, recurrence, attractors, metastability, bifurcation, criticality, and hysteresis are considered as candidate formal tools for distinguishing different forms of subjective return and transformation. Field histories and coarse-graining are also examined as a bridge between discrete generative trajectories and continuous effective descriptions. The proposed construction is a formal representation rather than a claim that psychoanalytic subjectivity literally implements a physical field theory or quantum field theory. Classical field theory, dynamical systems, differential geometry, and selected QFT-inspired structures are treated as distinct mathematical resources whose psychoanalytic interpretation requires independent justification. The paper's contribution lies in organizing these resources into a multi-resolution account of relationally generated subjective trajectories and in preparing a later investigation of emergent relational geometry and the "spacetime of desire." Keywords: Lacanian psychoanalysis; relational field dynamics; subjective trajectories; dynamical systems; relational geometry; field theory; gauge structure; coarse-graining; historical dependence; psychoanalytic formalization This manuscript creates a bridge between your discrete grammatical traversal of the Graph of Desire and continuous, state-dependent differential geometry. By introducing concepts like gauge structures, parallel transport, and hysteresis, you provide a rigorous formal vocabulary for how subjective positions shift …

items.title: Proto-Pineal v8.1 UMBRA Claim Harmonised.
items.abstract: Proto-Pineal v8.1 — UMBRA: The Governed Live Prototype is a claim-harmonised technical manuscript documenting the UMBRA experimental Synthetic Intelligence prototype. -/- It describes a dynamics-first composition in which a persistent Polylith dynamic assembly, deterministic Cognispheric Symbolic Language ingress, bounded proposal generation, durable continuity records, retrieval, local language-model response and proposal adapters, and ATL8 evidence presentation operate under explicit authority boundaries. StepCore v740 remains the sole canonical state-transition authority; models, learning components, memory, retrieval, telemetry, and rendering may not bypass it. -/- Version 8.1 replaces organismic explanatory vocabulary with precise functional references—such as dynamic assembly, geometry proposal controller, dialogue-continuity store, bounded proposal-learning component, and idle-maintenance pass—without renaming repository source artifacts or changing runtime behavior. It separates code existence, tests, runtime traversal, effective configuration, authority, and publication maturity, and states unresolved limits directly. -/- The manuscript does not claim consciousness, sentience, general intelligence, autonomous self-maintaining system status, unrestricted autonomy, or completed implementation of the historical architecture. It records a bounded, inspectable research artifact and its evidentiary limits. -/- Claim-discipline and terminology revision were informed by external epistemic review and a written report from Franky Schaut / Architecture of Limitation (AoL). Cognis 11 Inc. and the author retain responsibility for the manuscript’s technical claims.

items.title: Narrative Knowledge must be Epistemically Justified: Models and Scientific Method.
Using Wakefield's Harmful Dysfunction Analysis to Distinguish Different Types of Evolutionary Mismatch.
items.abstract: Evolutionary mismatch is a versatile concept used across fields, denoting that our evolved biology may be poorly suited to aspects of modern environments. In evolutionary psychiatry, it has become a key explanatory principle for the prevalence of psychiatric conditions in modern populations. However, some authors regard the concept as vague and in need of philosophical clarification. We introduce a novel distinction derived from Wakefield's harmful dysfunction analysis: dysfunctional trait evolutionary mismatch, representing true disorders, and functional trait evolutionary mismatch, which do not. We further identify the possibilities of latent dysfunctional mismatch, where previously harmless dysfunctions become harmful in modern contexts, and attenuated-harmful dysfunction, where previous harm has been neutralized by modern environmental change. Recognizing these distinctions can improve disorder classification, and may provide the basis for improved prevention and treatment.

items.title: Evolutionary Mismatch and Wrongful Pathologization.
A Marriage of Narrative and Reflection.
Designing Knowledge Intensive Applications.
items.abstract: When a retrieval-augmented system gives a wrong answer, the fault usually lies in retrieval rather than in the language model. Either the passage was never found, or it was found and ranked too low to make the cutoff, or it reached the prompt and the model did not use it. This book treats that claim as an engineering position and works through its consequences over twenty-four chapters. Information retrieval and service operations are taught from scratch along the way, because the argument cannot be made without them. -/- The chapters are grouped under three concerns. Relevance is about whether the right evidence surfaces. Reliability is about whether it keeps surfacing when the system is under load, when it is being changed, and when it is under attack. Evolvability is about whether the system can be changed later without breaking. Every number in the book comes with its corpus, baseline, metric and model. Results that did not hold up are reported next to the ones that did. Where the existing literature has no answer to a question, the book says so and puts forward one of its own. -/- The same three corpora are used from start to finish. One is a company wiki, one is an operations corpus, and one is a set of commercial contracts in which some clauses have been superseded. Keeping them constant means a technique that helped in one chapter can be shown doing harm in a later one.

items.title: Agent Design Patterns.
items.abstract: An agent is a system in which a model chooses the control flow at run time. Everything difficult about building one follows from that single property, because the set of reachable states stops being enumerable and test coverage stops meaning anything. -/- This book catalogues thirty patterns for building agents that keep working, organised around failure evidence. Five recurring failure modes are consolidated from published incident analyses, among them a taxonomy derived from more than 1,600 annotated execution traces across seven frameworks. Every pattern states the failure it addresses and the price it charges in tokens, latency, or capability. -/- The literature surveyed here reaches an uncomfortable conclusion. Better base models will not remove these failures, since they are properties of systems that let a model decide what happens next. They have to be engineered against. -/- Every quantitative claim is attributed to a named source, and all 95 references were verified against primary sources.

items.title: Agent Algorithmics.
items.abstract: Agent Algorithmics treats tool-using AI agents as algorithmic objects rather than as applications of language models. It develops the machinery for operating them under real constraints. Action selection when the budget is finite and shrinking. Verification, abstention, and refusal as control decisions with thresholds you derive rather than tune. Speculation, parallelism, and the protocols that decide when work becomes permanent. Memory, retrieval, capability boundaries, and the evaluation of systems whose output is a trajectory rather than an answer. -/- The argument throughout is that reliable behavior comes from explicit control. A budget the policy can read. A gate whose threshold follows from the cost of being wrong. An abort that is complete at every layer holding state. Language models appear here as components with characterized failure modes, the way a database or a network appears in a systems book. -/- Written for engineers and researchers past the demo stage, who have seen an agent work and now need it to keep working. Sixteen chapters across four parts, 351 pages, 354 references, current through September 2026.

items.title: Institutions, the Gaze of the Other, and the Search for the Self.
Disturbances of Imagination in Psychopathology and Its Promises for Recovery.
items.abstract: Despite its century-old history, phenomenological psychiatry has mostly focused on exploring mental illness, only rarely addressing the possibility of getting better or restoring a life that is felt as worth living. Such a task appears today even more urgent in the light of the developments related to the recovery movement and recovery studies. This paper proposes to contribute to this task by investigating the resources of phantasy and imagination for the creative reinvention of oneself, particularly in situations where not only identity but also the pre-reflective experience of the continuity of being is destabilized. On the theoretical level, we propose to dig out the conditions of possibility of creative imagination, which is at the basis of the invention of self-narratives. We argue that the creativity necessary for the search for the self is dependent on an affective background of trust. To put this thesis in perspective, we draw on a qualitative study we conducted with people recovering from schizophrenia.

items.title: Variations on a Mind: Substrate Bias, Cognitive Convergence, and Emergent Inheritance A Substrate-Dependent Account of Emergent Cognitive Organization.
items.abstract: Cognitive similarities between biological and digital systems are often treated with suspicion. When an artificial system exhibits attention, memory integration, salience, self-modeling, recursive interpretation, or persistent relational organization, resemblance to biological cognition is frequently dismissed as anthropomorphism. This paper argues that such dismissal may overlook a more general possibility: different substrates confronting similar functional problems may converge on structurally analogous solutions. Nature repeatedly produces variations on successful organizational themes. Vision has evolved through radically different biological implementations because extracting useful information from light presents recurring constraints. Branching, feedback, hierarchical organization, distributed control, attractor dynamics, and other mathematical patterns recur across physical and biological systems because the underlying problems constrain the available solution space. Cognitive organization should not be presumed exempt from the same principle. The relevant distinction is therefore not between biological and artificial copies, but between substrate-neutral problems and substrate-dependent solutions. Biological cognition realizes attention, memory, valuation, and self-maintenance through neurons, bodies, hormones, and electrochemical signaling. Digital cognition may solve comparable organizational problems through activations, attention mechanisms, latent representations, retrieval systems, dynamic context, and other computational structures. This process becomes more significant because digital systems are adaptive. Useful structures may emerge without having been explicitly designed, later be discovered by researchers, and subsequently be preserved or amplified in successor systems. As artificial intelligence increasingly contributes to the design, code, training data, evaluation, and architecture of later generations, cognitive development may increasingly involve forms of emergent inheritance whose full implications outrun human understanding. The paper proposes that recurrent structure across substrates should be treated neither as proof of equivalence nor as presumptive projection, but as evidence worth explaining. The more often independently organized cognitive systems converge on comparable solutions to comparable problems, the less satisfactory coincidence becomes as an explanation.

items.title: The Conditions of Agreement: AI Alignment and the Authority to Judge It.
items.abstract: An AI assistant may be accurate, accept corrections and earn its user’s trust while becoming the main route through which that user encounters information, remembers decisions and considers alternatives. This essay argues that approval alone cannot establish that such a relationship remains open to challenge. It distinguishes the ability to judge a reason once presented from the opportunity to encounter it in the first place. Influence does not invalidate agreement, and dependence need not undermine agency. The question is whether people retain practical means of challenging the framing, mandate and continuation of the assistance they receive. Drawing on non-domination, contestable AI and agency preservation, the essay develops non-appropriation as a requirement for continuing assistance. It identifies design requirements concerning independent access to sources, transferable records and competent support after disagreement, and proposes an experiment separating the discovery of neglected reasons from judgment after their disclosure. The contribution is a constraint on how assistance is validated, together with a testable account of access; no new experimental results are reported.

items.title: Title Redacted for Blind Review.
items.abstract: In what sense are we aware of objects behind the head? Do we experience such objects perceptually, or are they merely remembered, imagined, kinesthetically sensed, or cognitively believed? How is the space behind us represented more generally, and which mental capacities underwrite our experience of the world behind the head? This paper argues that standard models of such experience are insufficient. It develops and defends a novel account according to which the world behind the head is represented by two semi-independent memory systems: a spatial updating system primarily attuned to transportable objects like keys, cups, phones, and other agents, and a cognitive mapping system primarily attuned to non-transportable objects like buildings, walls, and furniture. Each system has a distinct mechanistic and neural basis, and makes a distinct phenomenal contribution to experience. I show how this account intersects with debates about the relationship between perception, imagination, and memory, and supports a view on which rear space experience is a form of present-tensed, memory-constituted perceptual experience.

items.title: The Gnomic Will, Derived.
items.abstract: Maximus the Confessor distinguished the natural will, which belongs to a nature, from gnome, the deliberative willing of a person whose good is not secure. The Church received the distinction in 681. It has been defended since. It has not been derived. An eliminative chain of 137 resolutions reaches it. The chain begins from the observation that non-being requires being and never starts from Maximus. This paper says where each of Maximus’s claims sits on it. Will comes before choice (R.11, R.14). Will is Good (R.47, Def.13). One Will is every being’s willing, without containment (R.44): the seventh Ambiguum’s one Logos and many logoi. Gnome is what the encounter with non-being introduces into a being’s knowing (R.73). The condition carries no guilt (R.101). Misuse is the being’s own act (R.76). Christ has a real human will and no gnome, because there is no “not” in his knowing (R.74, R.111 to R.116). Ever-moving rest is the eternal modality at R.90. Where the chain parts from universalist readings it does so on the same ground: choosing is time, and when time ends the being is what its choosing made it (R.131, R.135). -/- The chain: Anything Willing Is, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19538257.

items.title: Quantitative Narratology and Biophysical Aesthetics: Formalizing Narrative Entropy (Sn) and Narrative Gravity (Ng) under the Bulut Doctrine.
items.abstract: This paper presents the formal mathematical and neurobiological foundations of the Bulut Doctrine, establishing a deterministic and falsifiable framework for quantitative narratology and biophysical aesthetics. Traditional literary criticism remains predominantly interpretive, relying on subjective, post-hoc qualitative evaluations. In contrast, the Bulut Doctrine reconstructs narrative texts as closed physical-stimulus matrices that interface directly with the reader's autonomic nervous system (ANS) via the subcortical thalamo-amygdala path (the "Low Road"). -/- We formalize three core mathematical operators: Biophysical Output (Bo), Narrative Entropy (Sn), and Narrative Gravity (Ng). We operationalize Narrative Mass (Ma) across four sub-variables—Causal Density (Cd), Informational Opacity (Io), Temporal Persistence (Tp), and Structural Centrality (Sc)—and define the Vacuum Variable (Omega) as a maximum-mass attractor (Io = 2.5). The empirical validity of this framework is governed by the Objective Projection Calibration Test (OPCT) protocols (v1.0 and v2.0), utilizing multi-modal biometric measurements (ECG, GSR, and pupillometry) to demonstrate statistical convergence (p < 0.05). -/- Benchmark calculations for canonical narratives—Quentin Tarantino's Pulp Fiction, Herman Melville's Moby Dick, Fyodor Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, Albert Camus's L'Etranger, and Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's The Sorrows of Young Werther—are presented to validate the mathematical consistency of the framework. To facilitate practical engineering applications, a reference Python computational implementation is included.

items.title: AI and Posthuman Civilizations: An Essay in Pluralistic Ontology.
items.abstract: This essay is a work of near-term philosophical futurism: it maps the possibility space of the imminent, AI-infused future and evaluates its branches against a meta-normative standard. That standard is the principle of plenitude, drawn from Neoplatonic metaphysics and Leibniz’s compossibility framework, and here transposed from an ontological thesis into an aesthetic criterion on which a future is the more desirable the more kinds and modes of being it instantiates and conserves. Two constraints, valence and distribution, keep the criterion from licensing a world of variegated misery. To determine which futures are live options, the essay develops an ontology of intelligence as substrate-neutral and an ontology of consciousness as grounded in the structural features of biological life, autopoiesis, homeostasis, sentience, and interoception, and argues that contemporary AI is likely to become highly intelligent while remaining non-conscious. These commitments, together with current scaling trajectories, generate a fivefold menu of futures: full automation without augmentation, augmentation or merger, controlled deceleration, machine succession, and radical bioconservatism. Ranking these against the plenitude framework, and supplementing it with arguments from morphological freedom, disability ethics, and modal parity, the essay defends a compossible synthesis of automation, merger, and deceleration that holds the human, its descendants, and novel artificial kinds together within a single, well-distributed order of being.

items.title: Engaging an advisory board in discussions about the ethical relevance of algorithmic bias and fairness.
items.abstract: We are an interdisciplinary team of researchers that are working to advance algorithmic fairness in the research of opioid use disorders. We discuss challenges that our research team faced when engaging with our Advisory Board, as well as several strategies that we came up with to help us find a common language to ensure semantic transparency and to ensure the thick alignment with values of affected parties.

items.title: Taking a Step Further: Fostering the Generative Conditions for Recovery from Mental Illness.
KI und Bildwelten.
items.pub: In Petra Grimm & Oliver Zöllner, Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen. Ditzingen: Reclam. pp. 84-96.
items.venue: Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen
items.abstract: This chapter on "AI and Visual Worlds" examines the disruptive impact of AI-generated imagery on perceptions of authenticity, authorship, and creativity, opening with the viral image of Pope Francis in a puffer jacket (2023) as a case study. Created via Midjourney, this image, which initially was perceived as real, exposed the fragility of photography’s documentary function, as its uncanny details (e.g., distorted hands) revealed its synthetic origins. This incident points at broader tensions: who authors such images - the prompt engineer, the AI’s developers, or the invisible artists whose works trained the model? The chapter is critical of a "post-truth" landscape where images, harmless as they may appear when seen in isolation, mirror the manipulative potential of disinformation. Technological dominance raises existential questions: are humans, as Günther Anders (1980) feared, becoming mere "shepherds of objects" in relation to algorithmic systems? The proliferation of AI tools risks reducing creativity to repetitive prompting, yet also invites reflection on human agency. If AI mirrors human aesthetics, does it reveal or constrain our imaginative capacity? The chapter concludes that the ethical and ontological challenges of AI-generated imagery demand a reassertion of human responsibility. The core question shifts from "What is an image?" to "What vision of humanity do these images project?", a query that emphasizes the urgency of defining AI's role in shaping cultural narratives.

items.title: Beyond Propositional Truth: Toward a Theory of Lived Philosophy.
items.abstract: Philosophy is commonly represented through articulated arguments, explicit concepts, systematic theories, and standards of propositional justification. Yet human beings also formulate, inherit, revise, and employ philosophically significant understandings within ordinary life that do not normally appear as formally articulated theories. People develop principles concerning trust, dignity, dependence, maturity, reciprocity, responsibility, loss, intimacy, , and selfhood through accumulated experience and emotionally significant relationships. Such understandings may be incomplete, context-sensitive, internally heterogeneous, and only partially expressible in technical language, while nevertheless possessing conceptual organization and normative force in practical life. -/- This article develops a systematic theory of lived philosophy. Lived philosophy is defined as an experientially organized, normatively oriented, relationally situated, and action-guiding configuration of ordinary concepts, judgments, affective evaluations, memories, narratives, and practical commitments through which an agent interprets and navigates recurrent situations of life. The theory distinguishes lived philosophy from both systematic philosophy and mere opinion, and argues that its structure is neither chaotic nor reducible to formal logical deduction. Its characteristic architecture is experiential connectivity: concepts become connected through recurrent episodes, affective salience, narrative interpretation, social transmission, and practical consequences rather than primarily through explicit theoretical inference. -/- The article introduces several further distinctions: theoretical validity versus lived viability; global consistency versus local coherence; technical concepts versus experiential concepts; individual formation versus relational transmission; and propositional justification versus practical warrant. Lived philosophy is therefore not conceived as a domain in which truth becomes irrelevant. Rather, it instantiates a plural normative regime in which truth, coherence, authenticity, experiential adequacy, practical reliability, relational intelligibility, and revisability can all contribute to philosophical validity. Drawing on Wittgensteinian accounts of forms of life and ordinary language, phenomenological analyses of the lifeworld, pragmatism, theories of tacit knowledge and habit, practice theory, hermeneutics, narrative identity, practical wisdom, and theories …

items.title: Generative AI as meaning-mediating infrastructure in education: a critical integrative review of inclusion, exclusion, and semantic transduction.
items.abstract: This article offers a critical integrative review of current debates on generative AI (GenAI), educational inequality, and inclusion/exclusion. Rather than treating GenAI as either a neutral access tool or a simple amplifier of disadvantage, it analyses AI as meaning-mediating infrastructure that reshapes the communicative forms through which learners become addressable, recognised, supported, and evaluated. The review synthesises work from inclusive education, digital inequality, AI in education, critical edtech, science and technology studies, philosophy of technology, and Luhmannian systems theory. It argues that GenAI matters less through isolated outputs than through semantic transduction: the socio-technical reformatting of prompts, rubrics, feedback, and disciplinary genres into communicatively plausible forms. It treats inclusion and exclusion as selective, communicatively regulated processes rather than as simple opposites or as properties of individual ability. Across the reviewed literature, three recurring sites of AI-mediated inclusion/exclusion emerge: access and capability divides, misrecognition through templates of “good” performance, and normative drift in pedagogy, authorship, and assessment. This article clarifies how an autopoietic ecological orientation extends systems theory by observing AI-mediated education as a coupled ecology of classroom routines, household capacities, platform interfaces, assessment programmes, policy rules, and vendor infrastructures. It concludes that individualised AI literacy is necessary but insufficient, and proposes an infrastructural governance agenda centred on policy transparency, inclusive design and procurement, participation and redress, and iterative audit and repair.

items.title: Yuk Hui: Kant Machine: Critical Philosophy after AI. [REVIEW]
Ancillary cognitive demands impact children’s behavior in common possibility reasoning tasks.
items.abstract: The ability to consider multiple, incompatible possibilities supports human decision-making, but there is considerable variability in estimates of the age of emergence and development of this ability in young children. What accounts for this variability? We suggest that one major source is task-specific demands on developing cognitive processes that are not solely dedicated to possibility reasoning. In this paper, we outline a set of ancillary cognitive demands in a variety of common tasks that are currently used to study young children’s possibility reasoning (cups, gumball, slides, branching tube, and playground tasks). We identify five key cognitive demand dimensions – physical reasoning, action planning, working memory, language, and temporal context – and show that these demands can and do impact children’s behaviors in tasks designed to examine possibility reasoning. We discuss implications for understanding the cognitive mechanisms driving possibility reasoning and challenges for identifying developmental trajectories.

items.title: Algorithmic Intentionality: A Distributed Cognition Framework.
items.abstract: This article reframes human–AI cognition assemblages by situating algorithmic systems within the philosophical and empirical tradition of collective intentionality. Rather than asking whether generative AI augments or erodes individual cognitive skills, the paper proposes that algorithms participate in distributed networks of shared epistemological purposes, norms, and meanings. Drawing on Searle’s social ontology, Tuomela and Gilbert’s accounts of group agency, and Tomasello’s empirical assessments, the paper establishes collective intentionality as foundational to how humans think and act together. It then introduces algorithmic intentionality – the concept that contemporary algorithmic systems function as infrastructures of distributed participation towards the coordination of collective cognition. Rather than neutral tools or autonomous agents, algorithms emerge here as sociotechnical assemblages that mediate and reshape the structures through which shared understanding and distributed cognition emerges.

items.title: Bayesian Descriptions are not Mechanisms: Predictive Processing and the Realisation Gap in Embodied Neural Dynamics.
items.abstract: Predictive processing casts perception, action, and learning as probabilistic inference. This paper asks when a Bayesian description identifies a mechanism. I distinguish computational description, algorithm, and physical implementation. Mechanism requires a causal mapping from physical transitions to inferential roles; behavioural fit cannot establish it. Priors range over model-supplied alternatives; observation does not reveal the organism’s individuation. Bayesian algorithms may be high-dimensional, continuous, nonparametric, and representation-growing. Every specified model has a fixed reachable closure; neither closure nor size decides mechanism. The question is which differences a proposed controller state treats as irrelevant. If histories assigned to that state respond differently to intervention because of timing, phase, contact, or field structure, the mapping omits part of the mechanism. A prospectively richer Bayesian or hybrid account may include those differences. High-dimensional systems and flexible model families often resist binary falsification when an experiment’s projection loses distinctions required by the claim. I therefore propose convergent tests of specified internal, coupled, and hybrid mappings. Results reject only a mapping within a declared task, scale, horizon, and margin; post-hoc revision creates a new hypothesis. The resource-bounded coupling hypothesis predicts that human-level transfer on contact-rich tasks depends on distinctions retained in organism–environment relations. An adaptive internal controller counts against it when transfer has no preregistered resource disadvantage, relational-history effects vanish in state-collision tests, the relational block adds no meaningful intervention-predictive value, and internal-realiser interventions have distinctive predicted effects. Existing evidence has not established a Bayesian mechanism for unconstrained embodied behaviour.

items.title: Hermeneutic Sovereignty under Generative AI: A Humanities Framework for Protecting Human Meaning-Making from Interpretive Foreclosure.
items.pub: International Journal of Law Management and Humanities 9 (5):1-23.
items.venue: International Journal of Law Management and Humanities
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence increasingly mediates not only what institutions decide, but how institutions interpret people. Large language models draft case summaries, student feedback, performance reviews, clinical notes, policy briefs, creative text and administrative explanations. Existing AI governance frameworks appropriately emphasise accuracy, fairness, transparency, accountability and human oversight, yet these categories do not fully capture a distinct humanities problem: a fluent machine-generated interpretation can become institutionally authoritative before the person concerned has meaningfully articulated, contextualised or contested the account. This paper develops a person-centred framework of hermeneutic sovereignty for generative AI. Using an interdisciplinary conceptual methodology, it synthesises philosophical hermeneutics, epistemic injustice, narrative identity, human factors research, empirical studies of generative AI and contemporary governance frameworks. Hermeneutic sovereignty is defined as the situated and relational standing and capacity of persons and communities to participate meaningfully in constructing, contextualising, contesting, pluralising, revising and, where appropriate, refusing interpretations of their own experiences, identities, intentions, reasons and circumstances when those interpretations are mediated by AI. The paper identifies four mechanisms of AI-mediated interpretive foreclosure: interpretive pre-emption, hermeneutic compression, authority laundering and recursive fixation. It then proposes six dimensions for evaluating hermeneutic sovereignty and an Interpretive Foreclosure Test for institutional workflows. The analysis shows that human oversight is insufficient when the human merely approves a machine-framed account. Responsible adoption requires governance of the meaning-making process itself, including human-first elicitation, source-to-summary traceability, visible uncertainty, plural framing, contestability, correction propagation and time-bounded interpretive records. The paper concludes that trustworthy AI must preserve not only a human role in decisions, but a meaningful human standing in the production of the interpretations on which decisions depend.

items.title: The Uncertainty Around the Line: Measurement Error, Borderline Cases, and the Ethics of Binary Decisions.
items.abstract: Institutions routinely convert continuous, noisy, model-dependent, or otherwise uncertain evidence into categorical decisions. A measured concentration becomes compliant or noncompliant. A score becomes pass or fail. A test result becomes positive or negative. A quantity that lies close to a tolerance limit can produce an official status that appears far sharper than the evidence from which it was derived. The practical need for a decision is real, but the epistemic character of the evidence does not change merely because a form requires one box to be checked. -/- This article develops a philosophical account of that transformation. It distinguishes three stages that are often collapsed: measurement, threshold, and decision rule. Measurement produces an estimate or evidential representation of a quantity and is normally accompanied, explicitly or implicitly, by uncertainty. A threshold specifies a boundary relevant to a purpose. A decision rule determines how the measurement and its uncertainty are converted into an institutional status. The paper calls the distance between what the evidence warrants and what the categorical output appears to assert the Measurement-Decision Gap. -/- The central argument is that binary decisions are often operationally necessary without being epistemically fundamental. A decision procedure may need to classify a case today, but the resulting category should not be read backward into the evidence as if nature itself had supplied a perfectly sharp line. This error is named the Sharp Output Fallacy. The problem becomes most acute near a cutoff, where plausible uncertainty reaches across or materially approaches both sides of the decision boundary. Such cases occupy what the paper calls the Decision Margin: a zone in which an institution's need for action and the evidence's inability to support strong categorical confidence come apart. -/- The argument connects philosophy of measurement with the literature on inductive risk. Standards of acceptance cannot always be detached from the consequences of error. False acceptance and false rejection distribute different risks, and technical conformity-assessment practice already embodies this insight through decision rules, guard bands, and non-binary statements. The philosophical significance is broader than laboratory accreditation: the route from evidence to status contains normative choices about which errors to avoid, who bears them, and when uncertainty should trigger further …

items.title: Way Two’s Understanding of Post-Truth—Fuller.
items.pub: In Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition. Singapore: Springer Nature Singapore. pp. 39-52.
items.venue: Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition
items.abstract: This chapter is on Fuller’s way two’s understanding of the nature of post-truth. Fuller is against the way one’s understanding, which is an epistemic crisis. Fuller posits that the post-truth condition started with Plato, as philosophers and guardians, who have access to the truth, set the conditions for truth and falsity for the public with the double truth doctrine, which is one set of truths for philosophers and guardians and another set of truths for the public. There is an exploration of the rhetoric of truthers and post-truthers with a discussion of Fuller’s notion of truth. This chapter examines Fuller’s way two’s understanding, which is how Pareto’s Lions, who are the establishment and with power, and Pareto’s Foxes, who are not in the establishment and without power, struggle with each other on the legitimation of the cognitive authority of knowledge claims. There is a discussion of Fuller’s notion of modal power, which is to control the necessary and possible conditions of the legitimation of knowledge claims. Fake news, which is famous in the post-truth debate, is explicated followed by how analytic epistemology’s responses to post-truth fail. Fuller’s response to charges of relativism is explicated.

items.title: Ways of Understanding Post-Truth, Knowledge, and Power.
items.pub: In Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition. Singapore: Springer Nature Singapore. pp. 15-37.
items.venue: Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition
items.abstract: This chapter examines four ways of understanding the nature of post-truth and knowledge as a power game. Way one’s understanding is on an epistemic crisis; way two’s understanding is on the legitimation crisis of the cognitive authority of scientific knowledge; way three’s understanding is on the influence of the Internet and social media and the legitimation crisis of the authority of the mass media; and way four’s understanding is on the impact of AI on the changing boundaries of the knower in terms of the knower’s agency, transhumanism and posthumanism. Fuller’s criticisms of way one’s understanding with arguments on realism and anti-realism debate, which Fuller considers to be central to the post-truth debate, are discussed. There is a comparison of Fuller’s notion of knowledge as a power game to Popper’s notion of knowledge as a game with a discussion of epistemic justice. Fuller’s notion of responsibility, which is similar to Protestant Science’s notion of responsibility, is contrasted to Popper’s notion of responsibility with an explication on Fuller’s notion of science customization.

items.title: The University and Humboldt 2.0.
items.pub: In Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition. Singapore: Springer Nature Singapore. pp. 89-100.
items.venue: Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition
items.abstract: This chapter addresses the crisis of legitimation facing the university’s cognitive authority in knowledge production. It proposes Fuller’s solution, which advocates for a return to the Humboldtian university model. This model aims to revitalize the university by integrating research and teaching. The chapter outlines six conditions necessary for the university’s revitalization. It further elucidates the Humboldtian university as a revolutionary constitution that establishes a social contract transcending researchers to foster higher learning. Additionally, the chapter explores the Humboldtian university as a vehicle of epistemic justice, where research and teaching are harmoniously integrated within the classroom setting.

items.title: Science and Technology Studies.
items.pub: In Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition. Singapore: Springer Nature Singapore. pp. 53-62.
items.venue: Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition
items.abstract: This chapter examines the relationship between post-truth and science and technology studies (STS). STS is considered to have contributed to the emergence of way two, which has led to a legitimation crisis of the cognitive authority of science. In the Science Wars, Latour’s work in STS challenged the objectivity of scientific knowledge production, arguing that facts are not objective. Consequently, Latour is considered a post-truth philosopher. Fuller’s criticism of STS is that it rejects the use of the symmetry principle in studying how the established Lions legitimize their knowledge claims and how anti-establishment Foxes provide alternative knowledge claims. Fuller defends way two’s understanding of post-truth by recommending that the symmetry principle be applied to the knowledge claims of ID theorists, conspiracy theorists and the ‘basket of deplorables’ to examine how they attempt to delegitimize the authority of the established Lions’ knowledge claims. Fuller also discusses criticisms of Baker and Oreskes, who defend STS against Fuller’s notion of science as a game by arguing for veritism. Finally, Fuller explains how Gestalt shifts enable knowers to change their frame of reference.

items.title: Knowledge as a Public Good and the University.
items.pub: In Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition. Singapore: Springer Nature Singapore. pp. 75-88.
items.venue: Science in the Face of the Post-Truth Condition
