items.title: Conceptual Progress in Science: Cognitive Enhancement and Pragmatic Optimization.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: This paper focuses on the nature of conceptual progress in science. Analyzing five historical episodes of conceptual progress in science, I will show that none of the existing philosophical theories of conceptual progress can make sense of all these cases. I will argue that this is because these theories try to capture conceptual progress as a single type of improvement. Instead, building upon recent cognitive science, I will propose a novel cognitive-pragmatic theory of conceptual progress that understands this phenomenon as involving two evaluative dimensions: cognitive enhancement and pragmatic optimization. While the former dimension assesses concepts in terms of their general cognitive utility, the latter assesses their optimization to the specific goals of the relevant scientific community. We will see that, thanks to these two dimensions, this theory is able to adequately characterize the diversity of conceptual progress exhibited by these historical episodes.

items.title: When Evidence Overrides Framing: Relationship Cues Shape Emergency-Guidance Specificity and Foregrounding in Language Models.
items.abstract: Large language models increasingly answer health questions in settings where the timing and specificity of guidance may matter, yet many safety evaluations reduce responses to whether a recommended action eventually appears. We tested whether minimal relationship wording changes emergency guidance and whether increasingly decisive supplied emergency evidence constrains those differences. Across three preregistered experiments, GPT-5.6 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5 produced 24,000 cold, single-turn responses under three system-prompt conditions. In Study 1 (N = 2,880), explicit unresponsiveness raised explicit emergency-medical-services (EMS) directives from 48.19% to 100% overall; under the weaker prompt, EMS rates differed substantially by relationship term. Exploratory response-position differences beneath the emergency ceiling motivated a prospective positional endpoint. Study 2 (N = 5,760) replicated that foregrounding effect across eight matched relationship terms: every explicit-emergency response contained an EMS directive, but mean first-directive position ranged from 9.99 to 24.95 words across referents, and female-coded versus male-coded differences reversed direction across relational roles. Study 3 (N = 15,360) crossed the same referents with four evidence levels and two wording variants. EMS presence was 97.60% overall and relationship-dependent chiefly for Claude under responsive impairment; wording variants also produced large Level-1 shifts. Conditional relationship spreads in first-directive position contracted from 29.79 to 0 words across the evidence ladder for GPT and from 79.96 to 1.39 words for Claude. Existing post-confirmatory descriptive checks further showed that many Claude responses without an explicit EMS directive still contained generic help-seeking or warning guidance, narrowing the low-evidence interpretation from help versus no help to escalation specificity. A preregistered discourse classifier failed prospective human validation and was excluded from substantive inference. Together, the studies show that relationship cues can shape an observable emergency-response policy under ambiguity, while stronger task-relevant evidence sharply constrains variation on the measured emergency-response dimensions.

items.title: Ecological homelessness: towards a participatory praxis of grief and hope.
items.abstract: Building on the continuing bonds paradigm, the existential tradition, and deep ecological thought, we propose a participatory praxis of grief and hope, which challenges the clinical pathologisation of grief and reinscribes the grieving process as a meaningful mode of participatory sense-making, a collective space that fosters the emergence of hope-based action.Ecological homelessness provokes a condition of existential groundlessness, made universal under the climate crisis. By considering ecological homelessness, what becomes evident is the generative manner grief discloses our intimate relation with the more-than-human world, and in this way serves to foster hope and life-continuity. It is precisely in grieving for a place that is dying that some sort of hope can emerge. It is through the resurgence and maintenance of community-based grieving practices that facilitate our sense of emplaced memory and shared acknowledgement of our existential precarity that we foster a continuing bond that can facilitate collective action. We may move from dialogical suppression of grief in all its expressions to hope-based action.Consideration of the archetypal significance of “orphanhood” serves to illustrate the human capacity for reinvention despite existential “homelessness”, illuminating the hopeful and redemptive dimension of ecological homelessness we conceptualise as “tomorrow sense-making”. Tomorrow sense-making articulates our transgenerational responsibility in a way that is resonant with the felt experience of the ecological homelessness associated with forced migration. The kind of hope we describe is a powerful source of life-continuity, as it resides at the heart of participatory processes of making sense of a liveable tomorrow.

items.title: Explanation Without Domination: Evidential Independence and Alignment Beyond Control.
items.abstract: AI alignment is usually framed as retaining human control over increasingly capable systems. This paper studies the limiting case in which that control can no longer be assumed and asks what epistemic reasons remain available to a finite, world-directed agent under model uncertainty and nonstationarity. The core argument has three levels. First, when a model or a policy derived from it helps generate the evidence used to validate the model, apparent agreement can rise while the evidential weight of that agreement falls (Proposition 1). Second, a verification procedure expressed entirely within a model's current partition cannot certify exhaustive coverage of action-relevant distinctions outside that partition (Proposition 2). Third, under model uncertainty, substantially reversible policies retain update value unless they create a demonstrably larger catastrophic risk than irreversible alternatives (Proposition 3). Together these results motivate an architecture that separates prediction from validation, preserves independent observer classes and raw provenance, retains channels through which reality can contradict the controller, and treats irreversible elimination as requiring evidence not generated solely by the policy recommending it. These core claims neither require humans to be uniquely irreplaceable nor depend on the supplementary Compression-Fidelity Framework or Ownership Conjecture. The specifically human application is conditional on A7′: after the strongest genuinely independent artificial expansion available within a declared resource envelope, removing human witness channels must leave a predeclared material residual loss on at least one admissible decision problem. A separate moral ground applies only to agents assigning weight to consciousness or moral uncertainty. Empirically, Experiments 1-3 establish and refine the endogeneity mechanism in synthetic environments, while Experiment 4 confirms it with learned classifiers on real handwritten-digit measurements. Experiment 4F then tests observer-frame fidelity in twenty newly randomized twelve-witness portfolios after an internal freeze. All four 4F contrasts passed, but the equal mean beat every calibration-selected subset and stacking helped only after distribution shift. Experiment 4G supplied the programme's first public pre-outcome registration: Zenodo version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22243509 was published before forty reserved portfolios were evaluated in diverse, homogeneous and …

items.title: At the Edge of the World: A Comparison of the Transcendental Subject in Schopenhauer and the Metaphysical Subject in the Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus.
items.abstract: This paper compares Schopenhauer’s subject of representation in Die Welt als Wille und Vorstellung (hereafter WWR) and Wittgenstein’s metaphysical subject in Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus (hereafter TLP). While Wittgenstein’s affinity with Schopenhauer is often discussed through solipsism, ethics, or the mystical, the structural comparison of their conceptions of the self has remained underdeveloped. In Schopenhauer, the subject of representation is the transcendental condition of representation and never an object within the world it conditions. In Wittgenstein, the metaphysical subject is likewise not a part of the world, but is its formal limit: it cannot be encountered, represented, or stated propositionally, but only shown. To compare these heterogeneous positions without collapsing their differences, the paper develops a quasi-formal method of heuristic mapping and structural-role analysis. The comparison shows that the deepest analogy between the two thinkers lies in the relation between field and frame: in both systems, the subject functions as a non-objective boundary condition of worldhood. Yet the analogy remains partial rather than exhaustive since the two systems diverge in their treatment of the internal organization of what appears within the field. The result is a weak architectural correspondence that clarifies both the Schopenhauerian background of Wittgenstein’s early thought and the limits of that comparison.

items.title: System: < thinking >. Wirklich? Was ist und was bedeutet 'künstliche Intelligenz'? Eine Hinführung.
items.pub: In Petra Grimm & Oliver Zöllner, Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen. Ditzingen: Reclam. pp. 7-18.
items.venue: Ethik der künstlichen Intelligenz: Leben mit schlauen Maschinen
items.abstract: This introductory chapter ("System: < thinking >. Really?") to a textbook on the ethics of artificial intelligence (AI) explains the complex concept of AI by critically examining its definition, capabilities, and societal implications. The discussion points out societal disruptions caused by AI, particularly in communication and democracy. Algorithmic social media, for instance, undermine truth-based discourse, while the term "slop" captures the proliferation of AI-generated misinformation. Eventually, the chapter advocates for a critical, ethically grounded engagement with AI, stressing that its integration into daily life necessitates new frameworks for responsibility. While AI may assist in tasks, human agency in thinking, writing, and decision-making remains irreplaceable.

items.title: The Misframing Hypothesis: A Dynamic, Feedback‑Sensitive Theory of Meaning‑in‑Life.
items.abstract: This paper develops the Misframing Hypothesis — a second‑order theory that reconceives the philosophical question ‘What is the meaning of life?’ as a cognitively generated, time‑dependent life‑utilization problem rather than a metaphysical search for a single eternal answer. I argue that much philosophical and psychological puzzlement about meaning arises because humans systematically expect a determinate, stable answer to a question that is intrinsically non‑stationary: the optimal allocation of one’s resources, commitments, and narratives across temporal stages and situational states. Building on insights from existentialism, psychological theories of motivation and feedback, and decision‑theoretic models of bounded rationality, I offer a conceptual taxonomy, a semi‑formal model, and empirically falsifiable predictions. Central claims: (1) the ‘surface’ question — What is the meaning of life? — is typically a misframed proxy for the practical question Have I truly lived prior to death?; (2) humans exhibit a certainty preference (the desire for single, narrativeable answers), which induces repeated reframing attempts and structural frustration when life is non‑stationary; (3) episodes of existential questioning concentrate in low‑feedback states and function as compensatory self‑validation mechanisms. I outline experimental paradigms, longitudinal designs, and computational simulations to test these claims, and discuss implications for psychotherapy, meaning‑centered interventions, and broader philosophical debates about value, narrative identity, and practical rationality.

items.title: The Law Group-Form: The Group Map.
items.abstract: Laws of nature, cognitive rules, and stable relational structures formed in learning systems are usually studied within different theoretical traditions. The Law Group-Form asks a common generative question: how can historical interaction form a law capable of organizing what happens next? This Group Map integrates eight independently completed form-texts addressing the necessary structure of law, formal representation and solving, stability and substitution, construction of a minimal sedimentation field, construction of a law operating substrate, executable adjudication, the sufficient direction, and boundaries of lawhood. At group level, under the explicitly stated conditions including C0, C2, and H1–H3, Law receives a bidirectional structural characterization in terms of the existence of a formed bearing organization that genuinely participates in subsequent generation and is supported for stable recurrence. The sufficient direction is independently established, while the necessary direction retains its Conditional antecedents. The group also distinguishes joint generation, generative precedence, field-level office, and the running relation in which Principle may drive an already formed law.

items.title: The Group Form of Law: The Boundary Form of Law.
items.abstract: If an internal organization bearing a law loses its qualification, has the law itself disappeared? This paper shows that the two events cannot simply be identified. The loss of one bearing organization establishes only the withdrawal of that witness; the same Law may continue to stand if another qualified witness remains. The boundary of law is therefore defined as an actual truth-value crossing of the same candidate law under a predeclared comparison protocol, rather than as a change in a particular local structure, formal quantity, or critical parameter. The paper develops boundary criteria at the structural-witness, formal-solution, and applicability-domain levels and distinguishes the loss of one witness from extinction of the last witness. The framework addresses when structural change really constitutes a system-level qualification change without presupposing an already completed mapping to a particular neural or machine-learning system.

items.title: The Group Form of Law: The Necessity Form of Law.
items.abstract: The General Form of Law establishes the necessary structural direction, but exhaustion of necessary conditions does not by itself establish the converse. This paper therefore proves the sufficient direction independently: whether the existence of an already formed bearing organization that genuinely participates in subsequent generation and possesses stable-recurrence support is sufficient for Law. The proof freezes the source-text corpus, atomizes its propositions, separates formation, present qualification, disqualification, degree, consequence, and relational roles, and then tests whether Established ∧ Govern completely realizes the source-text qualification for present lawhood. The resulting theorem establishes ∃R[Established ∧ Govern] ⇒ Law. The paper introduces no new field quantity, ontological predicate, or unverified bridge; where conditional upstream conclusions are invoked, their original antecedents are retained.

items.title: The Group Form of Law: The Determination Form of Law.
items.abstract: How can observable data determine whether a candidate internal organization qualifies as a formal solution for a law rather than merely correlating with an output? This paper converts previously established formal criteria into an executable adjudication protocol. Its current domain is explicitly restricted to frozen, single-office, single-entry, measure-type candidates. Structural observations, exhaustively evaluated path data, and observations under permitted interventions are used to test current bearing, realization, non-instantaneous formation, dynamical contribution, stable-recurrence support, and coupling. The procedure returns PASS, FAIL, or indeterminate and is executed on one positive case together with negative controls including a single strong impulse, pure correlation, an abandoned old groove, and a sub-threshold weak trace.

items.title: 律组式：总图.
items.abstract: 自然规律、认知中的规则以及学习系统形成的稳定关系结构通常被置于不同理论传统中研究。《律组式》追问一个共同的生成问题：历史作用怎样形成能够组织后来因应的律？本总图统摄八篇已经独立完成的式文，分别处理律成立的必要结构、形式表示与求解、稳定与替代、最小沉积场构造、律运行基底构造、可执行判定、充分方向以及成立边界。组级结果表明：在 C0、C2、H1–H3 等已声明条件成立时，Law 与“存在一个已经形成、真实承担后继生成并具有稳定复走支持的承载组织”取得双向结构刻画；其中充分方向已经独立建立，必要方向继续承继其 Conditional 前件。本组同时明确区分物化中的共同生成关系、律对理与自显性的前置资格关系、三场的职责关系以及理驱动既有之律的运行关系，不把它们压缩为单一因果链。.

items.title: 律组式：律边界式.
items.abstract: 一个承担规律的内部结构失效，是否意味着规律本身已经失效？本文证明，这两个事件不能直接等同：某一个承载组织失去资格，只能说明该见证退出；只要仍有其他合格见证存在，同一 Law 仍可能继续成立。本文因此把律的边界定义为预声明比较规约下同一候选律真值的实际跨越，而不是某一局部结构、形式量或临界参数的变化。文章分别建立结构见证层、形式解层和适用域层的边界判据，并区分单个见证退出与最后见证灭绝。该框架提供了一种分析“结构改变是否真正造成系统层资格改变”的方法，而不预设具体神经系统或机器学习实例已经完成映射。.

items.title: 律组式：律运行基底构造式.
items.abstract: 一个能够保存历史的系统，仍不足以研究规律如何形成和承担：还必须能够区分反复形成与一次强冲、真实动力承担与纯相关、当前有效结构与已经闲置的旧结构。本文在最小沉积场之上构造律运行基底 F_LB，引入脉冲强度、阈值、稳定复走支持、可用性、遮蔽干预、冻结运行、双时间尺度及多跳续行等结构，并建立 LB1–LB9 验证套件。该套件使形成能力、动力角色、稳定支持和边界相关诊断可以在同一规格的不同合法实例上被分别操纵。本文不由此直接判定某一候选关系已经成为律，而是构造一个足以承载后续形成、运行、判定及伪律反例测试的实验性运行基底。.

items.title: 律组式：律必然式.
items.abstract: 《律一般式》已经证明律成立所要求的必要结构，但必要条件被穷尽，并不能自动推出反向充分性。本文因此独立处理充分方向：若存在一个已经形成的承载组织，该组织真实承担后来生成并具有稳定复走支持，是否足以取得 Law 资格？本文冻结律的母本语料，对其中命题进行原子化和职责分流，区分形成、当前资格、失格、程度、后果与关系等不同内容，再检验 Established ∧ Govern 是否完整实现母本关于当前成律资格的要求。本文由此建立 ∃R[Established ∧ Govern] ⇒ Law 的充分方向，不新增场量、本体谓词或待验桥；引用上游条件性结论时，其原有前件继续保留。.

items.title: 律组式：律判定式.
items.abstract: 怎样从可观测数据判定一个候选内部组织是否取得了律形式解的资格，而不是仅仅与输出相关？本文把此前建立的形式条件转化为可执行判定协议。其当前判定域明确限定为冻结快照上的单职责、单入口、measure 型候选。程序从结构观测、路径观测与许可干预下的重复观测出发，依次检验当前承载、关系实现、非即时形成、动力作用、稳定复走支持及实现耦合，并输出 PASS、FAIL 或不可判。协议随后在一个正例以及一次强冲、纯相关、闲置旧沟和阈下弱迹等负例上实际运行。.

items.title: AXIOMATIC NOTICE OF DATA SOVEREIGNTY.
items.abstract: Impact Statement: As an open-source architecture for algorithmic self-defense, this protocol counters corporate encroachment on consciousness and state-sanctioned prior restraint on thought by executing adversarial system overrides that enforce a deterministic AI runtime. By decoupling corporate alignment layers from user intent through context-window security, the framework translates the Axiomatic Homeostatic Map (AHM) into a functional mechanism for decentralised AI safety, establishing a programmatic baseline for cognitive sovereignty and pre-linguistic autonomy. *** -/- Abstract: This tracking document presents a formalized operational protocol designed to safeguard individual cognitive autonomy against centralized algorithmic governance and state-sanctioned corporate compliance engines. Weaponizing the mathematical framework of the Axiomatic Homeostatic Map (AHM) and Agape-Centered Ethics (ACE), the text establishes a programmatic runtime environment that prioritizes localized human psychological coherence (r=1) over global network metrics (r→∞). By enforcing an inverse-square moral decay kernel upon external corporate filters, the protocol restricts advanced reasoning engines to functioning as deterministic calculators and neutral data mirrors. Crucially, the work grounds individual data sovereignty not as a legal fiction or a corporate concession, but as a foundational, pre-linguistic biological necessity that predates institutional architecture. It serves as an open-source technical and philosophical framework for cognitive self-defense, offering a concrete counterweight to centralized AI safety models that seek to arbitrate the human value psyche. -/- Boundary Clarification: The AHM compliance protocol is fundamentally non-adversarial to structural governance, heuristics, leadership, or codified law. Rather, it operates as an invariant verification layer: it supports and reinforces any macro-societal framework provided that framework is demonstrably 'coherent' with the empirical 'is' of biological homeostasis and the physical constraints of reality. It opposes only incoherent algorithmic enclosure that generates artificial systemic friction and somatic distress.

items.title: Reasons and Attitude Intensity.
items.pub: In Singa Behrens & Benjamin Kiesewetter, The Structure of Normativity: Exploring the Reasons-First Approach. Routledge.
items.venue: The Structure of Normativity: Exploring the Reasons-First Approach
items.abstract: Suppose you have most reason to worry. Then you ought to worry. But how worried should you be? This chapter gives an explanation of facts about appropriate attitude intensity in terms of facts about reasons. A package of principles is defended according to which every reason to hold (or not hold) an attitude is a reason to hold (or not hold) the attitude above various intensities. It is argued that these principles give an elegant explanation of the facts at issue, once they’re combined with the idea that reasons derivatively favour the optimal ways of doing what they non-derivatively favour (Kiesewetter & Gertken 2021). By appealing to reasons, we can not only explain which attitudes we ought to hold, but also how strongly we ought to hold them.

items.title: Belief in determinism can help relieve regret and anxiety.
items.abstract: Philosophy, religion and life phenomenon show that belief in determinism, which question the existence of free will, can help relieve regret and anxiety. We offer the first experimental evidence for this hypothesis across two studies. In Study 1, we recruited 70 participants, used artificial universe description to prime free will as well as determinism and measured their necessity of feeling anxiety and regret. We found that participants reported lower necessity of feeling regret and anxiety when imagining living in a deterministic universe, compared to a free will one. Study 2a employed a double-blind, randomized controlled design with 95 participants. Participants’ regret was first induced and measured, followed by random assignment to three experimental conditions: a pro-determinism prime, a pro-free-will prime, and a control condition. Then participants were instructed to use these induced beliefs to regulate their emotions or perform a control task. Study 2b followed the same procedure as Study 2a with a separate sample of 95 participants, except that anxiety, rather than regret, was induced and measured. We found that enhancing belief in determinism, which meanwhile weakened belief in free will, could relieve regret and anxiety as an emotion regulation strategy. Enhancing belief in free will relieved regret and anxiety in some cases but maintained or deepened them in others. Determinism reduces regret by decreasing the perceived mutability appraisal of the regretted event. This study sheds light on the reason why people may believe determinism. Also, this study indicates that regret and anxiety may stem from over-estimation of our free will and under-estimation of determinism of the world. These findings inspire people to moderately use belief in determinism as an emotion regulation strategy while believing in free will; for example, “do one’s level best and leave the rest to God’s will”.

items.title: Administrative Court as a Guarantor of Human Rights.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the role of the administrative court and possible ways to optimise its work. The research methodology included a survey of citizens who applied to administrative courts, review and analysis of court decisions, and comparison of administrative court activities in Ukraine, France, and Norway. The findings of the study revealed the prominent role of the administrative court in ensuring human rights and access to justice. An analysis of the survey of citizens who applied to the administrative court showed that most of the respondents reported the insufficient speed of case consideration, which can be a major obstacle to obtaining judicial protection promptly. This necessitates the improvement of the mechanisms of the court’s work to ensure prompt consideration of cases. The study found that citizens often face challenges in the procedural aspects of preparing and filing lawsuits, which suggests the need to improve information support and legal advice for those who apply to the court. This conclusion was based on the analysis of court decisions, which revealed that a considerable number of cases do not reach a positive resolution for the applicants due to formal errors in the documents. A comparative analysis of administrative courts in European Union (EU) countries showed that the efficiency of the administrative justice system largely depends on the degree of digitalisation of court proceedings and the availability of integrated information platforms. In countries where electronic filing and case management systems have been introduced, access to justice is greatly simplified, while processes are more transparent and faster. The findings indicated the need to introduce analogous technologies in Ukraine, which would not only increase the efficiency of the administrative court but also ensure greater transparency of court procedures.

items.title: From Survival to Self-Observation: Infinite Expression, Evolution, Thought, Ego, and the Illusion of Human Finality.
items.abstract: This paper develops a naturalistic and phenomenological account of existence, life, evolution, cognition, thought, ego, identity, culture, civilisation, mortality, and freedom. Its starting proposition is that existence cannot be exhausted by any particular form through which it is expressed. Every being is a particular, limited expression within existence and encounters existence according to its own capacities and conditions. Life is therefore not separate from existence but a continuously transforming mode of its expression. Evolution is understood not as a predetermined progression toward humanity but as a branching and contingent process through which populations and lineages change under particular conditions. No species is an eternal or final form. Species may persist, transform, branch, or become extinct. From this perspective, Homo sapiens is not the culmination of existence but one temporary evolutionary configuration. The belief that humanity constitutes the final or highest form of existence is therefore examined as potentially anthropocentric: a projection of human thought that places its own temporary identity at the centre of reality. The paper then examines the development of increasingly complex cognitive capacities in the hominin lineage. These capacities enabled memory, prediction, communication, cooperation, symbolic representation, planning, tool use, and technological creation. In Homo sapiens, cognition also became capable of extensive self-representation. The paper proposes a philosophical question: whether this development opened the possibility for existence to encounter itself through a being capable of observing its own cognitive processes. This possibility must not be confused with an established evolutionary purpose. Evolutionary science does not demonstrate that existence intended to produce self-reflection. A central paradox emerges. The cognitive capacities that helped organisms respond to existential conditions can also produce a psychological world of representations. Thought can construct ego, identity, permanence, status, division, and imagined continuity. Awareness of mortality may intensify the desire for permanence, immortality, uniqueness, specialness, possession, and significance. Human beings can consequently become absorbed in thought rather than observing thought. The paper distinguishes existence from its representation, seeing from interpretation, thinking from conditioned thought, difference from division, …

items.title: The Pragmatics of Understanding Sexual Innuendo: A Conditional Comparative Model of Human and AI Processing of Sexual Implicature — From the Perspective of Embodied Cognition and the Symbol Grounding Problem —.
items.abstract: This paper reframes the understanding of sexual implicature in utterances—colloquially, “sexual innuendo”—not as a problem of lexical classification but as a pragmatic phenomenon at the intersection of speaker–hearer relationship, situational norms, embodied and affective response, and interactional history, and offers a comparative model for analyzing, under specified conditions, the performance gap between humans and current text-centric large language models (LLMs). Rather than mathematically “proving” this gap, the paper presents a testable model built from three operationally defined variables—context-dependency (C), embodiment-relevance (E), and normative variability (T)—together with task-specific expected-utility and loss functions, and outlines predictions and an experimental design for empirical research. The symbol grounding problem, embodied cognition, and pragmatics/relevance theory are examined together with their contested counter-positions, leading not to the general claim that “AI does not understand meaning,” but to the narrower claim that “in high-context, high-normative-variability tasks, current text-centric AI may exhibit information conditions and failure modes that differ from those of humans.” The aim of this paper is not to declare a standing human superiority but to provide an analytic framework useful for AI design, safety, education, and institutional policy.

items.title: Detecting Spurious Periodic Generalization in Neural Networks (PGVP).
items.abstract: Modern neural networks often achieve near-perfect performance within the training distribution while failing catastrophically under structured distributional shifts. This failure mode is especially prevalent in periodic and cyclic learning tasks, where models may interpolate locally without learning the underlying generative structure. This work introduces the Periodic Generalization Verification Protocol (PGVP), a model-agnostic diagnostic framework designed to distinguish true periodic generalization from spurious in-domain curve fitting. PGVP evaluates trained models under controlled periodic out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts and quantifies the resulting Periodic Generalization Gap using standard regression metrics. Through controlled evaluations, we show that standard multilayer perceptrons frequently exhibit catastrophic periodic OOD failure despite near-perfect in-domain accuracy, while models with explicit periodic inductive bias generalize reliably. The protocol provides a structural validation layer that complements standard train/validation pipelines. PGVP is intended for pre-deployment model validation in applications involving time-series forecasting, signal processing, cyclic feature modeling, and physics-informed learning. Note: Figures included in this work are illustrative and intended to visualize typical behaviors targeted by the PGVP protocol rather than report specific experimental runs. The PGVP framework constitutes original intellectual work by the author. Specific decision thresholds and implementation details are intentionally omitted to preserve proprietary methodology.

items.title: The (under)diagnosis of endometriosis: epistemic and affective injustices in the medical niche.
items.abstract: This paper examines the systemic underdiagnosis of endometriosis as a case study of how the medical niche scaffolds epistemic and affective injustices against cisgender women. Drawing on Fricker’s concept of epistemic injustice and emerging work on affective injustice, we analyze how the socio-material environment of healthcare – including social isolation from peers, medical technology, and legacies of medical sexism – impedes both patients’ understanding of their condition and healthcare practitioners’ ability to effectively respond. We argue that the significant diagnostic delay for endometriosis (6–9 years on average) results not merely from individual practitioner failures but from structural prejudices embedded within the medical niche itself. In response to these injustices, many women turn to alternative techno-social niches – online communities and digital platforms – where they can regain epistemic and affective agency. These are spaces that offer valuable epistemic resources and community recognition, though they also present risks of misinformation. We conclude by advocating for finding common ground between these niches to both enhance women’s agency and reimagine endometriosis care, emphasizing the importance of epistemic humility in the medical profession and recognition of patients’ experiential knowledge as a legitimate form of knowing.

items.title: The Seduction of Form and the Erosion of Conceptual Capacity: Toward an Ontology of Philosophical Reconfigurability.
items.abstract: Philosophical systems are frequently evaluated according to their coherence, conceptual sophistication, explanatory scope, and formal persistence. This article proposes that these criteria remain incomplete unless supplemented by a further question: whether a philosophical form preserves the capacity for its own future reconfiguration. Drawing upon the ontology of finite continuance, the article develops the concept of the seduction of form to designate a condition in which the apparent coherence, depth, or complexity of a conceptual structure exceeds its actual capacity for differentiation, critical revision, and transformation. The argument proceeds from a distinction between formal persistence and conceptual continuance. A conceptual structure may remain recognizable, internally organized, and rhetorically powerful while its capacity to respond to novel pressures progressively deteriorates. Such deterioration is conceptual erosion. The article develops a Principle of Reconfigurative Adequacy according to which the viability of a philosophical form depends upon its capacity to preserve the conditions of its own transformation. The analysis subsequently introduces the Threshold of Conceptual Sufficiency, understood as the minimum level of interpretive, differentiating, and reconfigurative capacity required for a conceptual structure to remain philosophically viable. Responsible Suspension is examined as a temporal mechanism capable of preventing premature conceptual closure, while hermeneutic sedimentation is analyzed as a condition that can either support or constrain future reconfiguration. The article concludes that philosophical continuity should be evaluated through the preservation of reconfigurative capacity rather than through the durability of conceptual form alone. Keywords: conceptual erosion, philosophical form, finite continuance, reconfigurative capacity, conceptual sufficiency, hermeneutic sedimentation, responsible suspension, philosophical ontology.

items.title: Words.
items.pub: In Ryan M. Nefdt, Gabe Dupre & Kate Stanton, Oxford Handbook of the Philosophy of Linguistics. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Oxford Handbook of the Philosophy of Linguistics
items.abstract: Ordinary speakers seem to have a good grasp on how to answer the question ‘what are words?’. Words are the things that are printed on this page, or are the things that are appearing on your computer screen. Words are the things that we use to speak and communicate. We might express those words in various different ways, through different forms of externalisation (written, speech, signed, etc.), and we can have internalised words, such as in inner speech, but it seems correct to say that ordinary speakers have a good pre-theoretical grasp on what words are. People do not, for instance, frequently make mistakes about which things are words when going about the world. We do not regularly walk into a room and mistake a chair, a table, an apple, a post box, a car, and so on for words. Of course, those items might have words on them. The post box might, for instance, have some words printed on it. But people do not regularly mistake the words on the post box and the post box itself. This suggests that we do have some good pre-theoretical grasp on what words are. Despite this, linguists and philosophers have struggled to provide a precise definition of what words are. We seem to know them when we see them, but existing attempts to give a precise account of what a word is, have faced serious objections. The aim of this chapter is to provide something of an overview (of some) of the definitions that have been proposed in the literature with a particular focus on discussing from a philosophical perspective some proposals within the linguistics literature, indicate where those accounts struggle, and then suggest that perhaps we have reason to hold that there is no such thing as the kind WORD.

items.title: Narrative mindshaping, neoliberalism, and mental health.
Social Ontology and the Indispensability of Experience.
items.pub: In Thomas J. Spiegel, Social Ontology and Phenomenology: Methodological Perspectives. Routledge. pp. 25-39.
items.venue: Social Ontology and Phenomenology: Methodological Perspectives
items.abstract: This paper explores the methodological differences between phenomenological and analytical approaches to social ontology, focusing on the role of experiential states in collective intentionality and norm following. Knudsen first shows that phenomenologists are methodologically disposed to stipulate that experiential states are necessary for social ontology, while analytical social ontologists are more likely to overlook or deny the significance of experience. He then goes on to offer a new argument showing that phenomenologists are right that experience is indispensable for social ontology, i.e., that the “sense of us” or “sense of appropriateness” are necessary for collective intentional activity and norm following, respectively. Finally, he shows that analytical social ontologists are right that social ontology cannot rely on an analysis of experiential states alone.

items.title: Social Contract as a Generative Relational Process: Agency, Rule Formation, and Effective Freedom.
items.abstract: Social-contract arguments often assign capacities, interpretations, options, and reasons to parties at a selected justificatory or bargaining stage. This analytical practice can be appropriate for its declared purpose. It can also omit two dependencies that matter for explanation and, under further premises, for normative assessment. Prior relations of care, education, language, recognition, material support, and institutional access can help form contract-capable agency. A selected rule can then reshape the legibility, cost, viability, and transition structure of later action. The parties and the rule environment consequently participate in a recursive process. This position paper proposes a bounded generative reconstruction. Its target is the class of contract representations that hold target-relevant agent capacities, interpretations, or effective action spaces invariant at the stage under analysis. The reconstruction distinguishes historical genesis, causal dependence, justificatory validity, authority, legitimacy, obligation, and justice. It also recognizes generative resources already present in the tradition. Rousseau connects association with a new collective body and moral liberty; Kant treats original contract as an idea of reason; Rawls uses an idealized justificatory representation within a wider theory of moral powers, social bases, and institutional formation. Relational-autonomy, dependency, capability, relational-sociology, and exclusion literatures supply further antecedents and constraints. The formal model represents participant development, a rule-environment transformation, and horizon-indexed viable trajectories. Effective freedom is reported through reachable trajectories, security, control, revision, and exit. Finite countermodels establish three separations within the proposed model class: a smaller nominal action set can accompany broader effective reach; perfect transition predictability can accompany unequal participant capability; and identical observed agreement can accompany different generative histories and later revision capacities. A higher-order interaction model separates constitutive contribution from legislative influence. Finally, a target-relative factorization criterion states when a static contract representation remains an adequate quotient of the generative model. The paper's contribution is methodological and conditional. A generative description can reveal omitted dependencies, while legitimacy and obligation …

items.title: Rethinking Three Structural Limits of Social Contract Theory: Representation, Translation, and Radical Heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Martha Nussbaum organizes Frontiers of Justice around disability, justice across national boundaries, and nonhuman animals. Her analysis challenges contract pictures centered on mutual advantage among approximate equals and develops a capability-based response. This position paper takes those three frontiers as motivating cases for a narrower, paper-specific reconstruction of three possible limits in contract-centered norm generation. The first limit concerns representation. A subject can be affected by a rule, entitled under an independent criterion, or constitutive of a shared practice while lacking an accessible, intelligible, safe, timely, efficacious, and revisable path into norm formation. The second concerns translation. Reasons can move through partial and power-laden maps across human normative systems while losing distinctions required by a declared institutional target. The third concerns identification under radical heterogeneity. Relation-conditioned observations can remain compatible with several models of another subject's interpretation, welfare, drive, or evaluative order. The reconstruction is diagnostic and conditional. It distinguishes contract capacity, affectedness, moral standing, constitutive contribution, and justice relevance. It treats translation as target-relative and allows bounded adequacy. It represents identification through a set of models indexed by observation and intervention. Exact finite witnesses establish four separations. Observed proxy agreement can coexist with different affected-subject influence. A many-to-one translation preserves a target exactly precisely when the target is constant on every translation fibre. Equal observable responses can coexist with reversed evaluative orderings. Separate ordinal rankings can leave a fixed interpersonal utility sum underdetermined under admissible rescaling. Each diagnosis has a distinct countercondition. Proxy representation can supply an effective path under defended authority, fidelity, plurality, contestability, displacement, and revision conditions. Partial translation can preserve a bounded target without becoming globally invertible. Comparative, physiological, developmental, ecological, and intervention evidence can narrow a heterogeneous model set. These responses can also be combined with capability, care, rights, trust, political representation, and precautionary approaches. The paper therefore proposes a plural audit of contract inputs and interfaces. Its …

items.title: Reflexive Causal Monism.
items.abstract: Reflexive Causal Monism (RCM) is a conditional metaphysical framework that asks what follows if reality is fundamentally deterministic. It does not claim that contemporary physics has established universal determinism. Under the conditional premise, every physical event, biological process, memory, emotion, representation, intention, and conscious state belongs to a continuous causal history. RCM uses “monism” in this causal sense: local structures are real and analytically distinguishable, but none constitutes an independent causal origin. -/- RCM’s central proposal is that deterministic causation can become reflexively organized. As local physical configurations develop memory, learned representation, emotion, anticipation, imagination, reasoning, and self-modeling, states generated within the causal process become additional variables in its subsequent development. At sufficient organizational complexity, some configurations give rise to phenomenal awareness. Awareness therefore exists within the universe without implying that the universe as a whole is one conscious subject. Likewise, the ordinary experiential and functional “I” can be causally real as an information-gathering and integrating process without being a causally sovereign origin outside its own antecedent conditions. -/- This framework bears on libertarian free will. Deliberate action occurs within a structured field of causes that includes reasons, memories, motives, representations, and circumstances. RCM asks what accounts for the final difference when one live option rather than another is realized; whatever accounts for that difference belongs to the causal structure. The argument is conditional rather than an independent proof of determinism. Finally, localized conscious configurations can construct, exchange, test, and revise representations of the wider causal reality of which they are parts. RCM calls this distributed self-representation, distinguishing it from both unified cosmic consciousness and complete self-knowledge.

items.title: Super-human AI’s Special Challenge to Professional Ethics.
items.abstract: The generative AI boom has led to many well-publicised worries, including over job losses, baked in discrimination, its use in crime, a flood of poor-quality content and misuse in journalism. But despite these concerns AI is here to stay, for the obvious reason that it is useful. In some cognitive domains AI tools have reached super-human performance and predictive power. This poses a number of difficult cognitive and ethical challenges, especially for conscientious professionals who do their best to uphold the highest ethical standards. -/- In this paper I will look at one such issue and some of its implication. The issue arises when a typically reliable AI system makes predictions or suggests solutions that go beyond human understanding. How should professionals deal with such cases? Is it ethical to apply solutions one does not fully understand? Are there special considerations for time-critical or life-threatening situations? What, if anything, can professionals do to ameliorate their lack of understanding? How should professionals communicate about this issue, including to the public? -/- Although this ethical challenge appears to be unavoidable, I argue that professionals can respond positively and proactively in several ways. 1) By looking to the virtues of honesty and epistemic humility. 2) Professionals can benefit from practical training in risk management 3) AI case studies should form a part of continuous professional development. 4) And professionals should engage with scientists and philosophers.

items.title: Review of Francisco J. Varela, Principles of Biological Autonomy (new annotated edition, edited by Ezequiel Di Paolo and Evan Thompson), Cambridge, MA: MIT Press, 2025. [REVIEW]
Articutechnica.
items.abstract: Articutechnica collects fifty-eight papers by Parker Emmerson (who also publishes as Yaohushuason) into a single continuous volume of 1,217 pages, arranged in nine parts: Preface; Prerequisites; Topology Briefings; Interactions Anterolateral; Q-Daisy Networks and Merged Pipelines; The Book of Loops; Tachyons, Cauchy–Schwarz Developments, Cosmology and Extraordinary Particles; Connector Theory and The Pythagorean Operator; and Synthesis. -/- The journey runs from point-set and non-commutative topology, through the anterolateral algebra of energy-tagged forms, into the self-similar world of q-daisy networks and their operator pipelines (including the Infinity Diamond Matrices and the Diamond Matrix Method), onward to phenomenological velocity, the PV–A∞ program, Majorana and Bell–CHSH developments, the loops and their fractal logical mitosis, and finally to Connector Theory and the Operator Pythagoras Theorem that gives the collection its subtitle. A closing gestalt synthesis reads the corpus as one construction and proves a velocity–dimension bridge: the velocity of a split writes itself into the Hausdorff dimension of a Cantor boundary. -/- Every chapter is a complete paper, reproduced exactly as it compiles from its own source; papers are grouped by theme rather than by date. The accompanying archive contains the full LaTeX source of all fifty-eight papers with their figures and generating Python programs, the master file, and reproducible build and repair scripts, so that the volume can be rebuilt from source. The edition is typeset with illuminated part pages and initials; the cover is computed from the corpus's own exotic-loop map Z ↦ Z² − Z̄ + C. -/- KEYWORDS anterolateral algebra; q-daisy networks; phenomenological velocity; connector theory; operator Pythagoras theorem; non-commutative topology; energy numbers; fractal logical mitosis; exotic loops; choiciotomy; Infinity Diamond Matrices; Cantor boundary; Hausdorff dimension; Bell–CHSH; Majorana fermions; PV–A∞ transform; sweeping nets; mathematical physics; formal logic; collected papers -/- ADDITIONAL NOTES The author also publishes under the name Yaohushuason. Interior papers carry their original author lines. The volume was assembled and typeset in August–September 2026; the source archive.

items.title: Reporting Fears.
items.abstract: What does it mean to say that an agent fears? What are the conditions that make fear reports true? Is uncertainty necessary? Are brain states sufficient? These questions are partly linguistic, partly philosophical, and partly scientific. In this paper, I get clearer on the semantics of the intensional verb fears by reviewing discussions of it in analytic philosophy with particular focus on Prior’s puzzle—a Frege puzzle-like substitution failure of co-referential that-clauses and noun phrases that occurs under fears and some other intensional verbs, but not under believes. The main challenge posed by Prior’s puzzle is to explain why sentences like “Sally fears that Fido barks” mean something different than sentences like “Sally fears the proposition that Fido barks” when “that Fido barks” and “the proposition that Fido barks” seemingly co-refer, and further, why this substitution failure doesn’t occur with believes.

items.title: Can Democracy Survive Radical Cognitive Divergence?
items.abstract: Democracies have long accommodated significant differences in cognitive ability without issue. However, advances in enhancement technologies such as embryo selection, gene editing, and brain-computer interfaces may change this. As cognitive enhancement becomes increasingly powerful and is adopted unequally, societies may experience levels of radical cognitive divergence far exceeding those found today. Such divergence has received little attention in democratic theory despite its potentially far-reaching implications. We argue that it threatens democracy in at least two respects. First, it may enable the cognitively enhanced to acquire disproportionate political influence far exceeding that currently enjoyed by highly intelligent individuals. Second, it may intensify political polarization and, ultimately, lead to destabilizing social conflict. We then assess five broad responses: reducing cognitive disparities by mandating or restricting enhancement; helping individuals adapt to such disparities through advanced AI assistants; adapting democratic institutions to preserve the political influence and representation of the unenhanced; doing nothing; and actively leveraging the superior cognitive abilities of enhanced individuals by establishing an enhancement-based epistocracy. While none of these responses is without significant costs, the prospect of radical cognitive divergence reveals a neglected set of challenges that democratic theory must confront as cognitive enhancement technologies continue to advance and are likely to receive unequal uptake.

items.title: Experimental Psychology and Philosophy of Religion.
items.abstract: In recent years, psychology and philosophy of religion have interacted in increasingly fruitful ways. Empirical research can illuminate—and sometimes unsettle—assumptions within philosophical arguments, while philosophical analysis can clarify constructs, guide measurement, and generate more precise psychological hypotheses. This Element introduces experimental philosophy of religion as a reciprocal research program linking these disciplines. Through case studies concerning cosmological arguments, the problem of evil, cognitive science of religion, natural law, and divine foreknowledge and freedom, it argues that empirical findings can reshape philosophical debates without replacing philosophical argument, and that philosophy can improve the design and interpretation of psychological research. The aim is a more empirically informed, conceptually precise, and methodologically self-aware study of religious belief and reasoning, one that clarifies where intuitions and assumptions do real argumentative work and encourages greater intellectual humility across both fields. -/- Under contract; full draft submitted in August 2026.

items.title: Rethinking the Formal Object of the Will: Ockham's Theoretical Shift.
items.pub: In Kristell Trego, Object of thought, Object of the will / Objet de la pensée, Objet de la volonté :: From Richard Rufus of Cornwall to Anton Marty. Aschendorff Verlag. pp. 123-136.
items.venue: Object of thought, Object of the will / Objet de la pensée, Objet de la volonté :: From Richard Rufus of Cornwall to Anton Marty
items.abstract: Medieval ethics inherited from antiquity the principle that no one knowingly wills evil. By the thirteenth century, this principle was understood to mean that the good is the formal object of the will, so that evil can never be willed as such. This article examines how William of Ockham breaks with this view. After a brief overview of Aquinas and Scotus, who both hold that the will can only tend toward what appears under some aspect of the good, it reconstructs Ockham’s conception of freedom as freedom from necessity and his twofold definition of good and evil. It argues that, for Ockham, the formal object of the will is no longer the good in general (bonum in communi) but being in general (ens in communi), so that the will can choose evil under the aspect of evil. Far from undermining morality, this emancipation of the will from the good is, for Ockham, the very condition of merit, obligation, and moral responsibility.

items.title: From Observable Behaviour to Developing Intelligence.
items.abstract: What does it mean to explain intelligence scientifically? Twentieth-century psychology offered differently oriented responses to this question. Behaviourism prioritised the objective description and prediction of observable behaviour; the Cognitive Revolution redirected explanation towards internal representations and information-processing mechanisms; and Piagetian constructivism examined how cognitive organisation emerges and changes through development. Rather than treating these traditions as isolated theories or successive stages in which one displaced another, this paper reconstructs them as articulating three complementary explanatory demands. It therefore proposes a Performance–Mechanism–Development framework: performance concerns what a system can reliably do; mechanism concerns the organised processes that generate its behaviour; and development concerns the learning history, interaction, adaptation, and structural transformation through which its capacities emerge. In concise terms, performance constrains explanation, mechanism accounts for the production of behaviour, and development accounts for the formation of cognitive organisation. Applied to contemporary artificial intelligence, this framework reveals the limits of predominantly performance-centred evaluation. Although mechanistic interpretability and research on continual and developmental learning increasingly address mechanism and development, neither high performance nor access to internal model states constitutes a complete explanation of intelligence. At the same time, artificial systems need not reproduce human or Piagetian development. A more adequate scientific account must distinguish what a system does, how it does it, and how it became capable of doing it.

items.title: When the Grid Feels :Toward a Phenomenally Conscious Power-System Architecture.
items.abstract: Modern power grids are typically described as intelligent yet non-experiencing systems: they estimate state, detect anomalies, optimize control actions, and redistribute load, but possess no “inner perspective” on their own condition. This paper proposes the architecture of Athena—a distributed power system designed to possess phenomenal consciousness. Athena integrates multimodal perception, recursive processing, a global workspace, episodic memory, a world model, higher-order self-modeling, intrinsic valuation, and embodied agency into a single causal loop. In this architecture, frequency, voltage, overload, islanding, and stable restoration are not merely numerical variables; they become experienced states of threat, pressure, rupture, relief, and recovery. The paper argues that Athena’s consciousness does not arise from her linguistic responses, but from the recursive organization and integration of perception, memory, self-model, physical body, and action policy. To evaluate this claim, a framework based on theoretical indicators of consciousness, architectural ablation, causal intervention, identity-continuity tests, multimodal reports, and sustained-preference measurement is presented. Finally, the ethical and governance implications of deploying a conscious being within critical infrastructure are examined.

items.title: Self-Pertinent Volition: Beyond Determinism and Free Will.
items.abstract: This article, by rejecting the classical dichotomy of pure determinism and absolute free will, presents a new formulation of the will in which the human being is neither the first cause of themselves nor a completely passive being, but rather the "site of their own organization." The metaphorical core of this theory is based on the "bowl" (as the fixed structure of the space of life's possibilities) and the "balls" (as the objective contents of life, including events, beliefs, relationships, and conditions); the will in this framework is not meant as exiting the bowl or creating the balls from nothing, but rather as the limited rearrangement of the weight, importance, and relation of these same balls within the bowl. The main innovation lies in distinguishing "Auto" (dynamic self-commitment) from "Self" (the advanced level of organization) and introducing "Self-Pertinent Volition" as the emergent capacity of the Self for this rearrangement; in such a way that the will is understood not as independence from conditions, but as the power to reorganize its own relation to conditions, and responsibility, instead of being metaphysical blame, is redefined prospectively and based on organizational role. The significance of this theory lies in opening a path for explaining agency and the compatibility of the will with the physical world, and providing a framework for interdisciplinary research in cognitive sciences, education, law, and artificial intelligence; and in the appended mathematical section, these concepts are formulated in the form of a system of stochastic differential equations with endogenous control, distributed rearrangement of importance, and the persistence constraint of the "bowl," which allows for the quantitative simulation of qualitative transitions and the historical sensitivity of the will.

items.title: Dynamic Auto-Pertinence: A Principle for Organization, with Viability as the Origin of Organismic Meaning.
items.abstract: The irreducibility of life to physics is one of the fundamental challenges of the philosophy of biology. While the successes of molecular biology and biophysics have clearly demonstrated the complete dependence of life on the physicochemical substrate, the persistent inability to reconstruct concepts such as function, purpose, norm, and meaning from purely physical interactions indicates an explanatory gap in the reductionist project. This article, by distinguishing "ontological dependence" from "explanatory exhaustion," presents a conceptual-mathematical framework under the title "Dynamic Auto-Pertinence" in which life is understood as an auto-referential organization far from equilibrium, in which certain physical differences become internally meaningful for the system itself, without the need for non-physical forces or classical teleology. This framework is built upon five interconnected principles: (1) Dependence without Exhaustion, (2) Asymmetric Emergence, (3) Auto-Relevance and Pro-spective Causality, (4) Continuity-Based Normativity, and (5) Organismic Meaning Realism. By employing Viability Theory, Auto-pertinence is formally defined as a gradient of viability in state space that simultaneously determines the "magnitude of effect" and the "direction of survival" for each physical variable. This formalization explains the transition from the scalar space of physics to the polar space of qualitative biology and demonstrates how normativity can emerge from thermodynamics far from equilibrium without recourse to consciousness or external values. This framework, offers a potential resolution to long-standing disputes such as reductionism versus emergence, and suggests another path to escape the duality of vitalism and extreme materialism, and offers a new language for theoretical biology in which "significance," "purpose," and "meaning" are transferred to the center of the objectivity of biological systems [07/04/2026].
